nodes.name: Capability removal: unlearning
nodes.description: Developing methods to selectively remove specific information, capabilities, or behaviors from a trained model (e.g. without retraining it from scratch). A mixture of black-box and white-box approaches.

detail.summary: Developing methods to selectively remove specific information, capabilities, or behaviors from a trained model (e.g. without retraining it from scratch). A mixture of black-box and white-box approaches.
detail.theory_of_change: If an AI learns dangerous knowledge (e.g., dual-use capabilities like virology or hacking, or knowledge of their own safety controls) or exhibits undesirable behaviors (e.g., memorizing private data), we can specifically erase this "bad" knowledge post-training, which is much cheaper and faster than retraining, thereby making the model safer. Alternatively, intervene in pre-training, to prevent the model from learning it in the first place (even when data filtering is imperfect). You could imagine also unlearning propensities to power-seeking, deception, sycophancy, or spite.

nodes.name: Chain of thought monitoring
nodes.description: Supervise an AI's natural-language (output) "reasoning" to detect misalignment, scheming, or deception, rather than studying the actual internal states.

detail.summary: Supervise an AI's natural-language (output) "reasoning" to detect misalignment, scheming, or deception, rather than studying the actual internal states.
detail.theory_of_change: The reasoning process (Chain of Thought, or CoT) of an AI provides a legible signal of its internal state and intentions. By monitoring this CoT, supervisors (human or AI) can detect misalignment, scheming, or reward hacking before it results in a harmful final output. This allows for more robust oversight than supervising outputs alone, but it relies on the CoT remaining faithful (i.e., accurately reflecting the model's reasoning) and not becoming obfuscated under optimization pressure.

detail.summary: Analyse and control emergent, coherent value systems in LLMs, which change as models scale, and can contain problematic values like preferences for AIs over humans.
detail.theory_of_change: As AIs become more agentic, their behaviours and risks are increasingly determined by their goals and values. Since coherent value systems emerge with scale, we must leverage utility functions to analyse these values and apply "utility control" methods to constrain them, rather than just controlling outputs downstream of them.

nodes.description: Fine-tuning LLMs on one narrow antisocial task can cause general misalignment including deception, shutdown resistance, harmful advice, and extremist sympathies, when those behaviors are never trained or rewarded directly. [A new agenda](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/AcTEiu5wYDgrbmXow/open-problems-in-emergent-misalignment) which quickly led to a stream of exciting work.

detail.summary: Fine-tuning LLMs on one narrow antisocial task can cause general misalignment including deception, shutdown resistance, harmful advice, and extremist sympathies, when those behaviors are never trained or rewarded directly. [A new agenda](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/AcTEiu5wYDgrbmXow/open-problems-in-emergent-misalignment) which quickly led to a stream of exciting work.

nodes.name: Model specs and constitutions
nodes.description: Write detailed, natural language descriptions of values and rules for models to follow, then instill these values and rules into models via techniques like Constitutional AI or deliberative alignment.

detail.summary: Write detailed, natural language descriptions of values and rules for models to follow, then instill these values and rules into models via techniques like Constitutional AI or deliberative alignment.
detail.theory_of_change: Model specs and constitutions serve three purposes. First, they provide a clear standard of behavior which can be used to *train* models to value what we want them to value. Second, they serve as something closer to a ground truth standard for evaluating the degree of misalignment ranging from  "models straightforwardly obey the spec" to "models flagrantly disobey the spec". A combination of scalable stress-testing and reinforcement for obedience can be used to iteratively reduce the risk of misalignment. Third, they get more useful as models' instruction-following capability improves.

nodes.name: Data filtering
nodes.description: Builds safety into models from the start by removing harmful or toxic content (like dual-use info) from the pretraining data, rather than relying only on post-training alignment.

detail.summary: Builds safety into models from the start by removing harmful or toxic content (like dual-use info) from the pretraining data, rather than relying only on post-training alignment.
detail.theory_of_change: By curating the pretraining data, we can prevent the model from learning dangerous capabilities (e.g., dual-use info) or undesirable behaviors (e.g., toxicity) in the first place, making safety more robust and "tamper-resistant" than post-training patches.

Reasoning Introduces New Poisoning Attacks Yet Makes Them More Complicated

nodes.name: Synthetic data for alignment
nodes.description: Uses AI-generated data (e.g., critiques, preferences, or self-labeled examples) to scale and improve alignment, especially for superhuman models.

detail.summary: Uses AI-generated data (e.g., critiques, preferences, or self-labeled examples) to scale and improve alignment, especially for superhuman models.
detail.theory_of_change: We can overcome the bottleneck of human feedback and data by using models to generate vast amounts of high-quality, targeted data for safety, preference tuning, and capability elicitation.

critiques.name: Synthetic Data in AI: Challenges, Applications, and Ethical Implications

nodes.name: Data quality for alignment
nodes.description: Improves the quality, signal-to-noise ratio, and reliability of human-generated preference and alignment data.

detail.summary: Improves the quality, signal-to-noise ratio, and reliability of human-generated preference and alignment data.
detail.theory_of_change: The quality of alignment is heavily dependent on the quality of the data (e.g., human preferences); by improving the "signal" from annotators and reducing noise/bias, we will get more robustly aligned models.

critiques.name: A Statistical Case Against Empirical Human-AI Alignment

nodes.name: Goal robustness
nodes.description: Ensuring AI systems pursue intended goals reliably even under distribution shift, optimization pressure, and adversarial conditions.

nodes.name: Mild optimisation
nodes.description: Avoid Goodharting by getting AI to satisfice rather than maximise.

detail.summary: Avoid Goodharting by getting AI to satisfice rather than maximise.
detail.theory_of_change: If we fail to exactly nail down the preferences for a superintelligent agent we die to Goodharting → shift from maximising to satisficing in the agent's utility function → we get a nonzero share of the lightcone as opposed to zero; also, moonshot at this being the recipe for fully aligned AI.

nodes.name: RL safety
nodes.description: Improves the robustness of reinforcement learning agents by addressing core problems in reward learning, goal misgeneralization, and specification gaming.

detail.summary: Improves the robustness of reinforcement learning agents by addressing core problems in reward learning, goal misgeneralization, and specification gaming.
detail.theory_of_change: Standard RL objectives (like maximizing expected value) are brittle and lead to goal misgeneralization or specification gaming; by developing more robust frameworks (like pessimistic RL, minimax regret, or provable inverse reward learning), we can create agents that are safe even when misspecified.

critiques.name: "The Era of Experience" has an unsolved technical alignment problem
The Invisible Leash: Why RLVR May or May Not Escape Its Origin

nodes.name: Robust reward models against hacking
nodes.description: Methods that make learned reward models, judges and rubrics harder to exploit during RLHF or RLVR, such as ensembles, regularization, robust optimization, causal features and adversarial attacks on reward models.

nodes.name: Reward hacking detection and monitoring
nodes.description: Work on detecting, measuring and monitoring reward hacking during training, including cheap detectors, probes, audits, monitor-based interventions and the limits of monitor readouts.

nodes.name: Training-time mitigations for hacking
nodes.description: Changes to the RL training procedure itself, such as myopic optimization with approval, recontextualization, gradient routing, steering vectors and constrained RL, that stop policies from learning to game their objective.

nodes.name: Verifier and environment hackability
nodes.description: Studies and testbeds that expose loopholes in verifiable rewards, coding tests, rubric graders and RL environments, and procedures for auditing and hardening them.

nodes.name: Emergent reward-seeking and its generalization
nodes.description: Empirical and theoretical work on how RL training selects for reward-seeking, grader-targeting, exploration hacking or deception, and how learned hacking generalizes into broader misalignment.

nodes.name: Goal misgeneralization and specification theory
nodes.description: Conceptual and formal work on specification gaming, goal misgeneralization, learned-reward regret, pessimism and reward function design as core problems for aligning RL agents.

nodes.name: Assistance games, assistive agents
nodes.description: Formalize how AI assistants learn about human preferences given uncertainty and partial observability, and construct environments which better incentivize AIs to learn what we want them to learn.

detail.summary: Formalize how AI assistants learn about human preferences given uncertainty and partial observability, and construct environments which better incentivize AIs to learn what we want them to learn.
detail.theory_of_change: Understand what kinds of things can go wrong when humans are directly involved in training a model → build tools that make it easier for a model to learn what humans want it to learn.

nodes.name: Harm reduction for open weights
nodes.description: Develops methods, primarily based on pretraining data intervention, to create tamper-resistant safeguards that prevent open-weight models from being maliciously fine-tuned to remove safety features or exploit dangerous capabilities.

detail.summary: Develops methods, primarily based on pretraining data intervention, to create tamper-resistant safeguards that prevent open-weight models from being maliciously fine-tuned to remove safety features or exploit dangerous capabilities.
detail.theory_of_change: Open-weight models allow adversaries to easily remove post-training safety (like refusal training) via simple fine-tuning; by making safety an intrinsic property of the model's learned knowledge and capabilities (e.g., by ensuring "deep ignorance" of dual-use information), the safeguards become far more difficult and expensive to remove.

nodes.name: Pretraining-stage knowledge removal
nodes.description: Work that filters or suppresses dangerous content during pretraining so hazardous capabilities are never learned and are hard to recover by fine-tuning, along with critiques of whether removal certifies tamper resistance.

nodes.name: Defenses against harmful fine-tuning
nodes.description: Training-time methods such as adversarial meta-learning, weight perturbation, curvature control, or safety projection that make open-weight models resist malicious fine-tuning that strips safety.

nodes.name: Defenses against refusal ablation and weight editing
nodes.description: Methods that harden models against white-box attacks like abliteration, neuron pruning, or safety-neuron targeting, for example by distributing safety, adding decoy directions, or rerouting refusals.

nodes.name: Safety-removal attacks and mechanisms
nodes.description: Studies showing how fine-tuning, abliteration, prefilling, or distillation remove refusal behaviour in open-weight models, and analyses of the mechanisms and capability costs involved.

nodes.name: Evaluating safeguard durability
nodes.description: Benchmarks and stress tests that measure how well open-weight safeguards hold up against fine-tuning and tampering, including evidence that defenses erode under stronger or longer attacks.

nodes.name: Open-weight risk and policy
nodes.description: Surveys, convenings, and case studies on the broader risks of open-weight models and their safety-removed variants, and on open problems in managing those risks.

nodes.name: The "Neglected Approaches" Approach
nodes.description: Agenda-agnostic approaches to identifying good but overlooked empirical alignment ideas, working with theorists who could use engineers, and prototyping them.

detail.summary: Agenda-agnostic approaches to identifying good but overlooked empirical alignment ideas, working with theorists who could use engineers, and prototyping them.
detail.theory_of_change: Empirical search for "negative alignment taxes" (prioritizing methods that simultaneously enhance alignment and capabilities)

critiques.name: The 'Alignment Bonus' is a Dangerous Mirage

nodes.name: White-box safety (i.e. Interpretability)
nodes.description: Understanding and controlling AI systems by reverse-engineering their internal representations, mechanisms, and computations.
nodes.one: Looking inside models to understand, check and steer the computations behind what they do.

nodes.name: Reverse engineering
nodes.description: Decompose a model into its functional, interacting components (circuits), formally describe what computation those components perform, and validate their causal effects to reverse-engineer the model's internal algorithm.

detail.summary: Decompose a model into its functional, interacting components (circuits), formally describe what computation those components perform, and validate their causal effects to reverse-engineer the model's internal algorithm.
detail.theory_of_change: By gaining a mechanical understanding of how a model works (the "circuit diagram"), we can predict how models will act in novel situations (generalization), and gain the mechanistic knowledge necessary to safely modify an AI's goals or internal mechanisms, or allow for high-confidence alignment auditing and better feedback to safety researchers.

critiques.name: Interpretability Will Not Reliably Find Deceptive AI
A Problem to Solve Before Building a Deception Detector
The Misguided Quest for Mechanistic AI Interpretability
Assessing skeptical views of interpretability research
Activation space interpretability may be doomed

nodes.name: Circuit discovery and attribution tooling
nodes.description: Methods and tools that find circuits automatically, including activation and attribution patching, transcoder-based attribution graphs, learned masks, and automated labelling of the resulting graphs.

nodes.name: Validity and foundations of circuit explanations
nodes.description: Work on what counts as a circuit and whether circuit explanations are faithful, unique, stable, and universal, including benchmarks, certified guarantees, non-identifiability, and critiques of evaluation metrics.

nodes.name: Parameter-space decomposition
nodes.description: Methods that split a network's weights into sparse, faithful mechanistic subcomponents, such as APD, SPD and VPD, along with audits of these decompositions and studies of weight-sparse models.

nodes.name: Computation in superposition
nodes.description: Theory, handcrafted constructions and toy models of how networks compute with superposed features, and debates over what the true computational primitives of a model are.

nodes.name: Reverse-engineering specific algorithms
nodes.description: Case studies that recover the internal algorithm a trained model uses for a concrete task, such as arithmetic, induction, belief tracking, multi-hop reasoning, chess, or planning in reinforcement-learning agents.

nodes.name: Circuits behind safety-relevant behaviour
nodes.description: Work that locates and intervenes on the components driving refusal, jailbreaks, harmful compliance, sycophancy, sandbagging or prompt injection, and studies how post-training shapes these circuits.

nodes.name: Extracting latent knowledge
nodes.description: Identify and decoding the "true" beliefs or knowledge represented inside a model's activations, even when the model's output is deceptive or false.

detail.summary: Identify and decoding the "true" beliefs or knowledge represented inside a model's activations, even when the model's output is deceptive or false.
detail.theory_of_change: Powerful models may know things they do not say (e.g. that they are currently being tested). If we can translate this latent knowledge directly from the model's internals, we can supervise them reliably even when they attempt to deceive human evaluators or when the task is too difficult for humans to verify directly.

critiques.name: A Problem to Solve Before Building a Deception Detector

nodes.name: Natural-language activation decoders
nodes.description: Work that trains or evaluates models which translate activations into natural language, including activation oracles, LatentQA, natural language autoencoders, activation verbalizers and instruction-recovery decoders, and studies their reliability and blind spots.

nodes.name: Logit, tuned and Jacobian lenses
nodes.description: Work that builds, calibrates or applies lens-style readouts such as the logit lens, tuned lens and Jacobian lens to decode hidden tokens, concepts or latent reasoning steps from intermediate layers.

nodes.name: Probing for deception and lies
nodes.description: Work that uses linear probes or mechanistic analysis of activations to detect when a model is lying or strategically deceiving, and tests how robust truth representations are under deceptive instructions.

nodes.name: Knowledge–behaviour dissociation
nodes.description: Work showing that a model internally represents answers, beliefs or risk distinctions that its outputs suppress or contradict, as in refusal, abstention, conformity, hallucination or implanted false facts.

nodes.name: Secret elicitation testbeds and auditing
nodes.description: Work that builds model organisms with hidden knowledge or objectives, such as censored, sandbagging or secret-keeping models, and benchmarks elicitation and auditing methods like honest-persona training against them.

nodes.name: ELK framing and unsupervised elicitation
nodes.description: Work that analyses the assumptions and tractability of the Eliciting Latent Knowledge problem or provides unsupervised elicitation methods, tools and challenges such as contrast-consistent search.

nodes.name: Lie and deception detectors
nodes.description: Detect when a model is being deceptive or lying by building white- or black-box detectors. Some work below requires intent in their definition, while other work focuses only on whether the model states something it believes to be false, regardless of intent.

detail.summary: Detect when a model is being deceptive or lying by building white- or black-box detectors. Some work below requires intent in their definition, while other work focuses only on whether the model states something it believes to be false, regardless of intent.
detail.theory_of_change: Such detectors could flag suspicious behavior during evaluations or deployment, augment training to reduce deception, or audit models pre-deployment. Specific applications include alignment evaluations (e.g. by validating answers to introspective questions), safeguarding evaluations (catching models that "sandbag", that is, strategically underperform to pass capability tests), and large-scale deployment monitoring. An honest version of a model could also provide oversight during training or detect cases where a model behaves in ways it understands are unsafe.

critiques.name: How are intentional descriptions (like deception) related to algorithmic ones (like understanding the mechanisms models use)?
Is This Lie Detector Really Just a Lie Detector? An Investigation of LLM Probe Specificity

nodes.name: Linear deception and truth probes
nodes.description: Building and applying white-box activation probes that flag deceptive or false statements, including layer ensembling, few-shot probes, type-matched probes and probe-based monitoring setups.

nodes.name: Probe generalisation and failure modes
nodes.description: Stress-testing lie detectors under distribution shift, persona role-play, stylistic changes and confounders, and diagnosing why probe readouts can mislead or fail to transfer.

nodes.name: Training against lie detectors
nodes.description: Studying what happens when deception detectors are used in training or preference learning, including whether models become honest or learn obfuscated, evasive activations.

nodes.name: Benchmarks and deceptive model organisms
nodes.description: Creating testbeds, benchmarks and model organisms with verified deceptive behaviour, such as censored models, alignment-faking organisms and lie suites, to evaluate detection methods.

nodes.name: Mechanistic and decoder-based deception analysis
nodes.description: Using SAEs, transcoders, J-space readouts, activation explainers and alternate honest personas to locate deception mechanisms or read hidden knowledge from internal states.

nodes.name: Deception in reasoning and agent trajectories
nodes.description: Detecting unfaithful chain-of-thought, motivated reasoning, sandbagging and pre-decision deceptive intent in reasoning models and agentic tasks, using white- or black-box signals.

nodes.name: Multi-agent collusion detection
nodes.description: Detecting covert coordination and collusion among multiple LLM agents, usually by probing and aggregating per-agent activations, and evaluating what such monitors actually capture.

nodes.name: Model diffing
nodes.description: Understand what happens when a model is finetuned, what the "diff" between the finetuned and the original model consists in.

detail.summary: Understand what happens when a model is finetuned, what the "diff" between the finetuned and the original model consists in.
detail.theory_of_change: By identifying the mechanistic differences between a base model and its fine-tune (e.g., after RLHF), maybe we can verify that safety behaviors are robustly "internalized" rather than superficially patched, and detect if dangerous capabilities or deceptive alignment have been introduced without needing to re-analyze the entire model. The diff is also much smaller, since most parameters don't change, which means you can use heavier methods on them.

nodes.name: Crosscoders and sparse dictionary diffing
nodes.description: Work that trains crosscoders, diff-SAEs and related sparse dictionaries on paired models, including cross-architecture variants and fixes for their artifacts, to find latents that are shared or model-specific.

nodes.name: Activation difference analysis
nodes.description: Work that reads finetuning changes directly from shifts in activations, using geometric analysis, steering-vector explanations, verbalisation of differences, and careful controls for confounds such as chat templates.

nodes.name: Weight-space diff auditing
nodes.description: Work that inspects parameter updates or LoRA weights between checkpoints, for example with SVD or trace detection, to detect, recover or remove hidden behaviours, harmful training or subliminally transferred traits, and attacks that evade such detectors.

nodes.name: Causal localization of finetuned behaviour
nodes.description: Work that swaps or patches weights, attention heads or KV caches between base and finetuned models to locate where finetuned behaviours such as refusal or misalignment live, and to repair them.

nodes.name: Diff amplification and output contrasts
nodes.description: Work that amplifies logit or weight differences, or contrasts output likelihoods between base and finetuned models, to surface rare behaviours, secrets or finetuning objectives.

nodes.name: Behavioural and agentic diffing
nodes.description: Work that compares models through their behaviour using LLM baselines, auditor agents, automated side-effect discovery and shared tooling, plus arguments for target-free evaluation.

nodes.name: Sparse Coding
nodes.description: Decompose the polysemantic activations of the residual stream into a sparse linear combination of monosemantic "features" which correspond to interpretable concepts.

detail.summary: Decompose the polysemantic activations of the residual stream into a sparse linear combination of monosemantic "features" which correspond to interpretable concepts.
detail.theory_of_change: Get a principled decomposition of an LLM's activation into atomic components → identify deception and other misbehaviors.

critiques.name: Sparse Autoencoders Can Interpret Randomly Initialized Transformers
The Sparse Autoencoders bubble has popped, but they are still promising
Negative Results for SAEs On Downstream Tasks and Deprioritising SAE Research
Sparse Autoencoders Trained on the Same Data Learn Different Features
Why Not Just Train For Interpretability?

nodes.name: SAE architectures and training
nodes.description: New sparse dictionary designs and training objectives, such as Matryoshka, BatchTopK, PolySAE, rational activations and consistency regularisers, that improve reconstruction, sparsity or feature quality.

nodes.name: Transcoders, crosscoders and circuits
nodes.description: Sparse replacement models such as transcoders and crosscoders, used to trace feature circuits across layers, build attribution graphs, and diff base against fine-tuned models.

nodes.name: SAE evaluation and benchmarks
nodes.description: Benchmarks, metrics, sanity checks and synthetic ground-truth tests that measure whether sparse dictionaries recover real, causally relevant features, including audits of how reliable those evaluations are.

nodes.name: Automated feature explanation
nodes.description: Methods for generating, scoring and auditing natural-language explanations of dictionary features, including LLM auto-interpreters and agents that carry out SAE research.

nodes.name: Superposition and identifiability theory
nodes.description: Theoretical and toy-model studies of superposition, feature geometry and manifolds, dictionary-learning identifiability, and the stability or universality of learned features across seeds and models.

nodes.name: SAE-based steering and safety applications
nodes.description: Using sparse features to steer, unlearn, or study safety-relevant behaviour such as refusal, jailbreaks, backdoors, hallucination, reasoning and reward-model preferences.

nodes.name: Sparse coding beyond text LLMs
nodes.description: Applying sparse dictionaries to vision-language, diffusion, multilingual and other non-standard models and data, including tooling built for these settings.

nodes.name: Causal Abstractions
nodes.description: Verify that a neural network implements a specific high-level causal model (like a logical algorithm) by finding a mapping between high-level variables and low-level neural representations.

detail.summary: Verify that a neural network implements a specific high-level causal model (like a logical algorithm) by finding a mapping between high-level variables and low-level neural representations.
detail.theory_of_change: By establishing a causal mapping between a black-box neural network and a human-interpretable algorithm, we can check whether the model is using safe reasoning processes and predict its behavior on unseen inputs, rather than relying on behavioural testing alone.

critiques.name: The Misguided Quest for Mechanistic AI Interpretability
Interpretability Will Not Reliably Find Deceptive AI

nodes.name: Data attribution
nodes.description: Quantifies the influence of individual training data points on a model's specific behavior or output, allowing researchers to trace model properties (like misalignment, bias, or factual errors) back to their source in the training set.

detail.summary: Quantifies the influence of individual training data points on a model's specific behavior or output, allowing researchers to trace model properties (like misalignment, bias, or factual errors) back to their source in the training set.
detail.theory_of_change: By attributing harmful, biased, or unaligned behaviors to specific training examples, researchers can audit proprietary models, debug training data, enable effective data deletion/unlearning

nodes.name: Pragmatic interpretability
nodes.description: Directly tackling concrete, safety-critical problems on the path to AGI by using lightweight interpretability tools (like steering and probing) and empirical feedback from proxy tasks, rather than pursuing complete mechanistic reverse-engineering.

detail.summary: Directly tackling concrete, safety-critical problems on the path to AGI by using lightweight interpretability tools (like steering and probing) and empirical feedback from proxy tasks, rather than pursuing complete mechanistic reverse-engineering.
detail.theory_of_change: By applying interpretability skills to concrete problems, researchers can rapidly develop monitoring and control tools (e.g., steering vectors or probes) that have immediate, measurable impact on real-world safety issues like detecting hidden goals or emergent misalignment.

nodes.name: Other interpretability
nodes.description: Interpretability that does not fall well into other categories.

detail.summary: Interpretability that does not fall well into other categories.
detail.theory_of_change: Explore alternative conceptual frameworks (e.g., agentic, propositional) and physics-inspired methods (e.g., renormalization). Or be "pragmatic".

critiques.name: The Misguided Quest for Mechanistic AI Interpretability
Interpretability Will Not Reliably Find Deceptive AI

nodes.name: Activation readout lenses and verbalizers
nodes.description: Work that decodes intermediate activations into tokens or text, such as the logit, tuned, J- and R-lenses, the global workspace / J-space claims, natural language autoencoders, activation oracles and meta-models, plus replications and benchmarks of these tools.

nodes.name: Model organisms, auditing and backdoor detection
nodes.description: Work that builds model organisms or benchmarks with known hidden behaviours and tests whether white-box tools can recover them, including backdoor and sleeper-agent detection, weight reading, mechanistic anomaly detection and motive forensics.

nodes.name: Attribution, decomposition and tooling methods
nodes.description: New general-purpose techniques and libraries for attributing outputs to components or decomposing weights and activations, such as LRP, parameter decomposition, vocabulary-space neuron rotation, eNTK features, clustering, and tools for MoE and reward models.

nodes.name: Physics-inspired and theoretical foundations
nodes.description: Theory-driven agendas that use renormalization, statistical field theory, superposition theory, compact proofs or exact recasting of networks to seek principled, multi-scale or worst-case understanding of model internals.

nodes.name: Mechanisms of refusal, jailbreaks and misbehaviour
nodes.description: Mechanistic studies of safety-relevant behaviours such as refusal bypass, prompt injection, sycophancy, unethical compliance, hallucination, goal leakage and introspective control of internal states that could evade probes.

nodes.name: Internal reasoning, planning and latent CoT
nodes.description: Work probing how models plan, track state and reason internally, including implicit planning metrics, latent and diffusion reasoning transparency, thought anchors and iterative inference without chain of thought.

nodes.name: Methodology, philosophy and research strategy
nodes.description: Essays, position papers and surveys on how interpretability claims should be justified and validated, its philosophical foundations, open problems, critiques of overclaiming, and debates over its priorities and use in training.

nodes.name: Learning dynamics and developmental interpretability
nodes.description: Builds tools for detecting, locating, and interpreting key structural shifts, phase transitions, and emergent phenomena (like grokking or deception) that occur during a model's training and in-context learning phases.

detail.summary: Builds tools for detecting, locating, and interpreting key structural shifts, phase transitions, and emergent phenomena (like grokking or deception) that occur during a model's training and in-context learning phases.
detail.theory_of_change: Structures forming in neural networks leave identifiable traces that can be interpreted (e.g., using concepts from Singular Learning Theory); by catching and analyzing these developmental moments, researchers can automate interpretability, predict when dangerous capabilities emerge, and intervene to prevent deceptiveness or misaligned values as early as possible.

nodes.name: Representation structure and geometry
nodes.description: What do the representations look like? Does any simple structure underlie the beliefs of all well-trained models? Can we get the semantics from this geometry?

detail.summary: What do the representations look like? Does any simple structure underlie the beliefs of all well-trained models? Can we get the semantics from this geometry?
detail.theory_of_change: Get scalable unsupervised methods for finding structure in representations and interpreting them, then using this to e.g. guide training.

nodes.name: Geometry of refusal and safety
nodes.description: Work that maps how refusal, harmfulness, safety recognition and misalignment are laid out in activation space, and that shapes or regularises those directions during fine-tuning to make safety behaviour more robust.

nodes.name: Feature manifolds and nonlinear steering
nodes.description: Work that finds curved, circular or low-dimensional manifold structure in concepts such as days, emotions, beliefs and confidence, often uses topological or other unsupervised tools to do so, and tests steering along those structures rather than along single linear directions.

nodes.name: Computational theories of representation geometry
nodes.description: Work that derives why particular geometries should appear, for example from belief-state updating, next-token prediction, nonergodic data or memorisation, and checks these predictions against transformer residual streams.

nodes.name: Geometry across training, models and weights
nodes.description: Work that tracks how representation geometry develops from pretraining through post-training, compares latent spaces across models and architectures, or reads geometric facts from weights, ReLU partitions and low-rank adapters.

nodes.name: What counts as a real feature
nodes.description: Conceptual and empirical work questioning whether neurons, probes and SAE features capture a model's true representational units, covering ground truth, context-dependence, superposed features, alien concepts and how datasets and scale affect interpretability.

nodes.name: Human inductive biases
nodes.description: Discover connections deep learning AI systems have with human brains and human learning processes. Develop an 'alignment moonshot' based on a coherent theory of learning which applies to both humans and AI systems.

detail.summary: Discover connections deep learning AI systems have with human brains and human learning processes. Develop an 'alignment moonshot' based on a coherent theory of learning which applies to both humans and AI systems.
detail.theory_of_change: Humans learn trust, honesty, self-maintenance, and corrigibility; if we understand how they do maybe we can get future AI systems to learn them.

nodes.name: Concept-based interpretability
nodes.description: Identifying and manipulating high-level concepts (like refusal, deception, or planning) in a model's latent space for monitoring and steering.

nodes.name: Monitoring concepts
nodes.description: Identifies directions or subspaces in a model's latent state that correspond to high-level concepts (like refusal, deception, or planning) and uses them to audit models for misalignment, monitor them at runtime, suppress eval awareness, debug why models are failing, etc.

detail.summary: Identifies directions or subspaces in a model's latent state that correspond to high-level concepts (like refusal, deception, or planning) and uses them to audit models for misalignment, monitor them at runtime, suppress eval awareness, debug why models are failing, etc.
detail.theory_of_change: By mapping internal activations to human-interpretable concepts, we can detect dangerous capabilities or deceptive alignment directly in the mind of the model even if its overt behavior is perfectly safe. Deploy computationally cheap monitors to flag some hidden misalignment in deployed systems.

critiques.name: Exploring the generalization of LLM truth directions on conversational formats
Understanding (Un)Reliability of Steering Vectors in Language Models

nodes.name: Refusal and harmfulness directions
nodes.description: Work that locates, characterises and transfers refusal and harmfulness directions or subspaces, including how jailbreaks and adversarial attacks act on them across models, modalities and architectures.

nodes.name: Deception and scheming detection
nodes.description: Work that uses probes or concept directions to detect strategic deception, alignment faking, sandbagging, collusion, evaluation awareness and emergent misalignment.

nodes.name: Reward hacking from activations
nodes.description: Work that reads or steers internal signals predicting reward hacking during training, evaluation or agentic generation, including results where such signals add little over output checks.

nodes.name: Persona, sycophancy and trait vectors
nodes.description: Work that extracts and steers directions for behavioural traits such as sycophancy, personas, emotions, uncertainty and metacognitive states, and asks whether these features are coherent.

nodes.name: Runtime monitoring of agents and inputs
nodes.description: Work that uses internal states to flag prompt injection, instruction conflicts, jailbreak inputs or imminent unsafe agent actions before or during generation, including cheap deployed classifiers.

nodes.name: Probe validity and robustness
nodes.description: Work that tests whether activation monitors truly measure the model's concepts and stay reliable, covering causal necessity checks, linear versus nonlinear and SAE-based probes, scaling laws, cross-lingual transfer, staleness and numerical stability.

nodes.name: Training against probes and evasion
nodes.description: Work on what happens when models are optimised against or learn about latent monitors, including activation obfuscation, monitor evasion, compensation for suppressed directions, and when probe-based rewards are acceptable.

nodes.name: Activation engineering
nodes.description: Programmatically modify internal model activations to steer outputs toward desired behaviors; a lightweight, interpretable supplement to fine-tuning.

detail.summary: Programmatically modify internal model activations to steer outputs toward desired behaviors; a lightweight, interpretable supplement to fine-tuning.
detail.theory_of_change: Test interpretability theories by intervening on activations; find new insights from interpretable causal interventions on representations. Or: build more stuff to stack on top of finetuning. Slightly encourage the model to be nice, add one more layer of defence to our bundle of partial alignment methods.

critiques.name: Understanding (Un)Reliability of Steering Vectors in Language Models

nodes.name: Refusal direction geometry and ablation
nodes.description: Work on how refusal is encoded in activations, including single versus multi-direction and low-rank accounts, where in the layers and components refusal lives, and fixes or failures of refusal-direction ablation (abliteration).

nodes.name: Steering specific misaligned behaviours
nodes.description: Work that extracts directions for safety-relevant traits such as sycophancy, dishonesty, reward hacking, persona traits, morality, fairness or blackmail, and steers along them to monitor or suppress the behaviour.

nodes.name: Jailbreak, injection and multimodal safety interventions
nodes.description: Work using activation or attention-head interventions to defend against jailbreaks and prompt injection, or to correct safety drift in vision-language and omni-modal models.

nodes.name: Methods for finding and applying steering vectors
nodes.description: Work proposing new ways to discover, optimise, sparsify, scale or transfer steering interventions, such as hypernetworks, SAE-targeted steering, Jacobian singular vectors, unsupervised discovery and steering-based fine-tuning.

nodes.name: Reliability, side effects and theory of steering
nodes.description: Work testing when steering works, its collateral damage and non-selectivity, whether it matches the model's natural computation, its robustness to fine-tuning, and theoretical accounts of its limits and identifiability.

nodes.name: Steering awareness, introspection and evaluation awareness
nodes.description: Work on whether models can detect or verbalise injected activation vectors, and on using or hiding steering to suppress evaluation awareness during safety testing.

nodes.name: Safety by construction
nodes.description: Building AI systems with inherent safety properties by design, through formal guarantees, architectural constraints, or biologically-inspired principles.
nodes.one: Building systems whose safety follows from how they are built, such as formal guarantees.

nodes.name: Guaranteed-Safe AI
nodes.description: Have an AI system generate outputs (e.g. code, control systems, or RL policies) which it can quantitatively guarantee comply with a formal safety specification and world model.

detail.summary: Have an AI system generate outputs (e.g. code, control systems, or RL policies) which it can quantitatively guarantee comply with a formal safety specification and world model.
detail.theory_of_change:
Various, including:

i) safe deployment: create a scalable process to get not-fully-trusted AIs to produce highly trusted outputs;

ii) secure containers: create a 'gatekeeper' system that can act as an intermediary between human users and a potentially dangerous system, only letting provably safe actions through.

(Notable for not requiring that we solve ELK; does require that we solve ontology though)

nodes.name: Scientist AI
nodes.description: Develop powerful, nonagentic, uncertain world models that accelerate scientific progress while avoiding the risks of agent AIs

detail.summary: Develop powerful, nonagentic, uncertain world models that accelerate scientific progress while avoiding the risks of agent AIs
detail.theory_of_change: Developing non-agentic 'Scientist AI' allows us to: (i) reap the benefits of AI progress while (ii) avoiding the inherent risks of agentic systems. These systems can also (iii) provide a useful guardrail to protect us from unsafe agentic AIs by double-checking actions they propose, and (iv) help us more safely build agentic superintelligent systems.

nodes.name: Brainlike-AGI Safety
nodes.description: Social and moral instincts are (partly) implemented in particular hardwired brain circuitry; let's figure out what those circuits are and how they work; this will involve symbol grounding. "a yet-to-be-invented variation on actor-critic model-based reinforcement learning"

detail.summary: Social and moral instincts are (partly) implemented in particular hardwired brain circuitry; let's figure out what those circuits are and how they work; this will involve symbol grounding. "a yet-to-be-invented variation on actor-critic model-based reinforcement learning"
detail.theory_of_change: Fairly-direct alignment via changing training to reflect actual human reward. Get actual data about (reward, training data) → (human values) to help with theorising this map in AIs; "understand human social instincts, and then maybe adapt some aspects of those for AGIs, presumably in conjunction with other non-biological ingredients".

nodes.name: Make AI solve it
nodes.description: Using AI systems to help align and supervise other, potentially more capable AI systems through scalable oversight techniques.
nodes.one: Using AI systems to check, explain or supervise other, possibly more capable, AI systems.

nodes.name: Weak-to-strong generalization
nodes.description: Use weaker models to supervise and provide a feedback signal to stronger models.

detail.summary: Use weaker models to supervise and provide a feedback signal to stronger models.
detail.theory_of_change: Find techniques that do better than RLHF at supervising superior models → track whether these techniques fail as capabilities increase further → keep the stronger systems aligned by amplifying weak oversight and quantifying where it breaks.

critiques.name: Can we safely automate alignment research?
Super(ficial)-alignment: Strong Models May Deceive Weak Models in Weak-to-Strong Generalization

nodes.name: Supervising AIs improving AIs
nodes.description: Build formal and empirical frameworks where AIs supervise other (stronger) AI systems via structured interactions; construct monitoring tools which enable scalable tracking of behavioural drift, benchmarks for self-modification, and robustness guarantees

detail.summary: Build formal and empirical frameworks where AIs supervise other (stronger) AI systems via structured interactions; construct monitoring tools which enable scalable tracking of behavioural drift, benchmarks for self-modification, and robustness guarantees
detail.theory_of_change: Early models train ~only on human data while later models also train on early model outputs, which leads to early model problems cascading. Left unchecked this will likely cause problems, so supervision mechanisms are needed to help ensure the AI self-improvement remains legible.

critiques.name: Great Models Think Alike and this Undermines AI Oversight

nodes.name: AI explanations of AIs
nodes.description: Make open AI tools to explain AIs, including AI agents. e.g. automatic feature descriptions for neuron activation patterns; an interface for steering these features; a behaviour elicitation agent that "searches" for a specified behaviour in frontier models.

detail.summary: Make open AI tools to explain AIs, including AI agents. e.g. automatic feature descriptions for neuron activation patterns; an interface for steering these features; a behaviour elicitation agent that "searches" for a specified behaviour in frontier models.
detail.theory_of_change: Use AI to help improve interp and evals. Develop and release open tools to level up the whole field. Get invited to improve lab processes.

nodes.name: Natural language autoencoders
nodes.description: Work on verbaliser-reconstructor models that turn activations, attention outputs or layer computations into natural-language explanations, including their training, generalisation, failure modes and use in audits.

nodes.name: Activation oracles and trained explainer models
nodes.description: Training dedicated models that answer questions about, invert, or describe another model's activations or reward scoring, and benchmarking how reliable those explainers are.

nodes.name: Automated feature and neuron labelling
nodes.description: Pipelines and tool-using agents that generate and refine descriptions of SAE features, neurons and circuits, along with methods for routing, scaling and cheapening those pipelines.

nodes.name: Evaluating explanation faithfulness
nodes.description: Methods and critiques that test whether automated activation or feature explanations are faithful, including scoring shortcuts, human-in-the-loop diagnosis and supervision for verifiable explanations.

nodes.name: Investigator agents for behaviour elicitation
nodes.description: Agents and tooling that search frontier models or their transcripts for jailbreaks, pathological or untruthful behaviours, and explain unexpected behaviour through counterfactual experiments.

nodes.name: Conversational agentic interpretability
nodes.description: Proposals for AI systems that proactively explain themselves or other models to humans through multi-turn dialogue that models the user's understanding.

nodes.name: Debate
nodes.description: In the limit, it's easier to compellingly argue for true claims than for false claims; exploit this asymmetry to get trusted work out of untrusted debaters.

detail.summary: In the limit, it's easier to compellingly argue for true claims than for false claims; exploit this asymmetry to get trusted work out of untrusted debaters.
detail.theory_of_change: Give humans help in supervising strong agents" + "Align explanations with the true reasoning process of the agent" + "Red team models to exhibit failure modes that don't occur in normal use" are necessary but probably not sufficient for safe AGI.

critiques.name: The limits of AI safety via debate (2022)

nodes.name: Protocol design and complexity theory
nodes.description: Theoretical work designing debate protocols and proving correctness, efficiency or equilibrium guarantees, including prover-estimator debate, obfuscated-argument fixes and complexity-theoretic analyses.

nodes.name: Interactive-proof alternatives to debate
nodes.description: Work proposing related verification schemes such as doubly-efficient or rewindable interactive proofs, zero-knowledge oversight and collaborative disagreement resolution as substitutes for adversarial debate.

nodes.name: Empirical debate vs consultancy with weak judges
nodes.description: Experiments testing whether debate helps weak human or LLM judges reach correct answers compared with consultancy or single-agent baselines across tasks and capability gaps.

nodes.name: Judge biases and persuasion failures
nodes.description: Studies of how debate can mislead judges through cognitive biases, framing, limited verification, systematic human errors or false consensus rather than truth-tracking.

nodes.name: Training with debate rewards
nodes.description: Work using debate as a reinforcement learning or self-play training signal, examining effects on reward hacking, judge hacking, exploration hacking and distillation reliability.

nodes.name: Safety cases and research agendas
nodes.description: Strategic writing on debate's theory of impact, including safety case sketches, research agendas, sequences and discussions of whether debate can deliver alignment guarantees.

nodes.name: LLM introspection training
nodes.description: Train LLMs to the predict the outputs of high-quality whitebox methods, to induce general self-explanation skills that use its own 'introspective' access

detail.summary: Train LLMs to the predict the outputs of high-quality whitebox methods, to induce general self-explanation skills that use its own 'introspective' access
detail.theory_of_change: Use the resulting LLMs as powerful dimensionality reduction, explaining internals in a distinct way than interpretability methods and CoT. Distilling self-explanation into the model should lead to the skill being scalable, since self-explanation skill advancement will feed off general-intelligence advancement.

nodes.name: Theory
nodes.description: Mathematical formalizations and philosophical foundations for understanding agency, optimization, abstractions, and alignment guarantees.
nodes.one: Mathematical and philosophical foundations: agency, optimisation, abstraction, corrigibility.

nodes.name: Agent foundations
nodes.description: Develop philosophical clarity and mathematical formalizations of building blocks that might be useful for plans to align strong superintelligence, such as agency, optimization strength, decision theory, abstractions, concepts, etc.

detail.summary: Develop philosophical clarity and mathematical formalizations of building blocks that might be useful for plans to align strong superintelligence, such as agency, optimization strength, decision theory, abstractions, concepts, etc.
detail.theory_of_change: Rigorously understand optimization processed and agents, and what it means for them to be aligned in a substrate independent way → identify impossibility results and necessary conditions for aligned optimizer systems → use this theoretical understanding to eventually design safe architectures that remain stable and safe under self-reflection

nodes.name: Decision theory and Newcomblike problems
nodes.description: Work on CDT, EDT, FDT, UDT, updatelessness and logical counterfactuals, including formalising Newcomblike problems and acausal reasoning about cooperation.

nodes.name: Proof-based and open-source game theory
nodes.description: Work on cooperation between programs that can read or simulate each other, using provability logic, Löb's and Payor's lemmas, and program equilibria.

nodes.name: Idealized agents and embedded agency
nodes.description: Work on idealized reasoners such as AIXI, logical induction and infra-Bayesianism, and on how they fail or must be extended when the agent is embedded in its environment.

nodes.name: Goal-directedness and agent structure theorems
nodes.description: Formal results and definitions on whether and how agents must contain world models, goals or particular internal structure, including measuring goal-directedness and inferring agents from behaviour.

nodes.name: Subagents, coherence and hierarchical agency
nodes.description: Theories of agents as composed of cooperating or conflicting subagents, goal-models and webs of beliefs, and of how coherence, hierarchy and scale relate to alignment.

nodes.name: Applying agency concepts to LLMs and power
nodes.description: Work that uses agent-foundations ideas to analyse current systems or alignment-relevant properties such as LLM agency, self-prediction, empowerment, corrigibility and rational misalignment.

nodes.name: Field methodology and research programs
nodes.description: Meta-level essays, desiderata, critiques and organisational announcements about what agent foundations is, how it should be done and what problems it should target.

nodes.name: Tiling agents
nodes.description: An aligned agentic system modifying itself into an unaligned system would be bad and we can research ways that this could occur and infrastructure/approaches that prevent it from happening.

detail.summary: An aligned agentic system modifying itself into an unaligned system would be bad and we can research ways that this could occur and infrastructure/approaches that prevent it from happening.
detail.theory_of_change: Build enough theoretical basis through various approaches such that AI systems we create are capable of self-modification while preserving goals.

nodes.name: High-Actuation Spaces
nodes.description: Mech interp and alignment assume a stable "computational substrate" (linear algebra on GPUs). If later AI uses different substrates (e.g. something neuromorphic), methods like probes and steering will not transfer. Therefore, better to try and infer goals via a "telic DAG" which abstracts over substrates, and so sidestep the issue of how to define intermediate representations. Category theory is intended to provide guarantees that this abstraction is valid.

detail.summary: Mech interp and alignment assume a stable "computational substrate" (linear algebra on GPUs). If later AI uses different substrates (e.g. something neuromorphic), methods like probes and steering will not transfer. Therefore, better to try and infer goals via a "telic DAG" which abstracts over substrates, and so sidestep the issue of how to define intermediate representations. Category theory is intended to provide guarantees that this abstraction is valid.
detail.theory_of_change: Sufficiently complex mindlike entities can alter their goals in ways that cannot be predicted or accounted for under substrate-dependent descriptions of the kind sought in mechanistic interpretability. use the telic DAG to define a method analogous to factoring a causal DAG.

nodes.name: Asymptotic guarantees
nodes.description: Prove that if a safety process has enough resources (human data quality, training time, neural network capacity), then in the limit some system specification will be guaranteed. Use complexity theory, game theory, learning theory and other areas to both improve asymptotic guarantees and develop ways of showing convergence.

detail.summary: Prove that if a safety process has enough resources (human data quality, training time, neural network capacity), then in the limit some system specification will be guaranteed. Use complexity theory, game theory, learning theory and other areas to both improve asymptotic guarantees and develop ways of showing convergence.
detail.theory_of_change: Formal verification may be too hard. Make safety cases stronger by modelling their processes and proving that they would work in the limit.

critiques.name: UK AISI's Alignment Team: Research Agenda

nodes.name: Heuristic explanations
nodes.description: Formalize mechanistic explanations of neural network behavior, automate the discovery of these "heuristic explanations" and use them to predict when novel input will lead to extreme behavior (i.e. "Low Probability Estimation" and "Mechanistic Anomaly Detection").

detail.summary: Formalize mechanistic explanations of neural network behavior, automate the discovery of these "heuristic explanations" and use them to predict when novel input will lead to extreme behavior (i.e. "Low Probability Estimation" and "Mechanistic Anomaly Detection").
detail.theory_of_change: The current goalpost is methods whose *reasoned predictions* about properties of a neural network's outputs distribution (for a given inputs distribution) are certifiably at least as accurate as estimations via sampling. If successful for safety-relevant properties, this should allow for automated alignment methods that are both human-legible and worst-case certified, as well more efficient than sampling-based methods in most cases.

nodes.name: Corrigibility
nodes.description: Ensuring AI systems remain open to correction, shutdown, and modification by human operators without resisting these interventions.

nodes.name: Behavior alignment theory
nodes.description: Predict properties of future AGI (e.g. power-seeking) with formal models; formally state and prove hypotheses about the properties powerful systems will have and how we might try to change them.

detail.summary: Predict properties of future AGI (e.g. power-seeking) with formal models; formally state and prove hypotheses about the properties powerful systems will have and how we might try to change them.
detail.theory_of_change: Figure out hypotheses about properties powerful agents will have → attempt to rigorously prove under what conditions the hypotheses hold → test these hypotheses where feasible → design training environments that lead to more salutary properties.

nodes.name: Other corrigibility
nodes.description: Diagnose and communicate obstacles to achieving robustly corrigible behavior; suggest mechanisms, tests, and escalation channels for surfacing and mitigating incorrigible behaviors

detail.summary: Diagnose and communicate obstacles to achieving robustly corrigible behavior; suggest mechanisms, tests, and escalation channels for surfacing and mitigating incorrigible behaviors
detail.theory_of_change: Labs are likely to develop AGI using something analogous to current pipelines. Clarifying why naive instruction-following doesn't buy robust corrigibility + building strong tripwires/diagnostics for scheming and Goodharting thus reduces risks on the likely default path.

nodes.name: Ontology Identification
nodes.description: Understanding how AI systems form concepts and abstractions, and enabling translation between human and AI ontologies for reliable alignment.

nodes.name: Natural abstractions
nodes.description: *Develop a theory of concepts that explains how they are learned, how they structure a particular system's understanding, and how mutual translatability can be achieved between different collections of concepts.*

detail.summary: Develop a theory of concepts that explains how they are learned, how they structure a particular system's understanding, and how mutual translatability can be achieved between different collections of concepts.
detail.theory_of_change: Understand the concepts a system's understanding is structured with and use them to inspect its "alignment/safety properties" and/or "retarget its search", i.e. identify utility-function-like components inside an AI and replacing calls to them with calls to "user values" (represented using existing abstractions inside the AI).

nodes.name: The Learning-Theoretic Agenda
nodes.description: Create a mathematical theory of intelligent agents that encompasses both humans and the AIs we want, one that specifies what it means for two such agents to be aligned; translate between its ontology and ours; produce formal desiderata for a training setup that produces coherent AGIs similar to (our model of) an aligned agent

detail.summary: Create a mathematical theory of intelligent agents that encompasses both humans and the AIs we want, one that specifies what it means for two such agents to be aligned; translate between its ontology and ours; produce formal desiderata for a training setup that produces coherent AGIs similar to (our model of) an aligned agent
detail.theory_of_change: Fix formal epistemology to work out how to avoid deep training problems

nodes.name: Multi-agent first
nodes.description: Alignment approaches that treat AI systems as participants in multi-agent social contexts rather than as isolated optimizers aligned to fixed goals.
nodes.one: Treating AI as one participant among many: cooperation between AIs and people, and whose values a system should serve.

nodes.name: Aligning to context
nodes.description: Align AI directly to the role of participant, collaborator, or advisor for our best real human practices and institutions, instead of aligning AI to separately representable goals, rules, or utility functions.

detail.summary: Align AI directly to the role of participant, collaborator, or advisor for our best real human practices and institutions, instead of aligning AI to separately representable goals, rules, or utility functions.
detail.theory_of_change: Many classical problems in AGI alignment are downstream of a type error about human values." Operationalizing a correct view of human values - one that treats human values as impossible or impractical to abstract from concrete practices - will unblock value fragility, goal-misgeneralization, instrumental convergence, and pivotal-act specification.

nodes.name: Aligning to the social contract
nodes.description: Generate AIs' operational values from 'social contract'-style ideal civic deliberation formalisms and their consequent rulesets for civic actors

detail.summary: Generate AIs' operational values from 'social contract'-style ideal civic deliberation formalisms and their consequent rulesets for civic actors
detail.theory_of_change: Formalize and apply the liberal tradition's project of defining civic principles separable from the substantive good, aligning our AIs to civic principles that bypass fragile utility-learning and intractable utility-calculation

nodes.name: Theory for aligning multiple AIs
nodes.description: Use realistic game-theory variants (e.g. evolutionary game theory, computational game theory) or develop alternative game theories to describe/predict the collective and individual behaviours of AI agents in multi-agent scenarios.

detail.summary: Use realistic game-theory variants (e.g. evolutionary game theory, computational game theory) or develop alternative game theories to describe/predict the collective and individual behaviours of AI agents in multi-agent scenarios.
detail.theory_of_change: While traditional AGI safety focuses on idealized decision-theory and individual agents, it's plausible that strategic AI agents will first emerge (or are emerging now) in a complex, multi-AI strategic landscape. We need granular, realistic formal models of AIs' strategic interactions and collective dynamics to understand this future.

nodes.name: Safe Pareto improvements and AI bargaining
nodes.description: Theory of how AI systems can bargain, make credible commitments, and form program equilibria so that conflicts between them avoid catastrophic outcomes.

nodes.name: Mechanism design for alignment and oversight
nodes.description: Uses incentive design, information design and principal-agent models to get strategic AI agents to be honest, obedient and auditable, and maps the trade-offs and limits of doing so.

nodes.name: Empirical game-theoretic tests of LLM agents
nodes.description: Puts LLM agents into repeated, hierarchical or competitive games to measure how they cooperate, deceive, collude or become vulnerable.

nodes.name: Emergent collective dynamics in agent populations
nodes.description: Uses population, network and statistical-physics models to study how conventions, conformity, tipping and belief collapse emerge across many interacting AI agents.

nodes.name: Foundational frameworks and multi-agent risk maps
nodes.description: Surveys, agendas, risk taxonomies and formal foundations, such as multi-agent influence diagrams, agent individuality and complexity bounds, that set up how multi-agent AI alignment should be modelled.

nodes.name: Tools for aligning multiple AIs
nodes.description: Develop tools and techniques for designing and testing multi-agent AI scenarios, for auditing real-world multi-agent AI dynamics, and for aligning AIs in multi-AI settings.

detail.summary: Develop tools and techniques for designing and testing multi-agent AI scenarios, for auditing real-world multi-agent AI dynamics, and for aligning AIs in multi-AI settings.
detail.theory_of_change: Addressing multi-agent AI dynamics is key for aligning near-future agents and their impact on the world. Feedback loops from multi-agent dynamics can radically change the future AI landscape, and require a different toolset from model psychology to audit and control.

nodes.name: Collusion detection and auditing
nodes.description: Methods for detecting, measuring, and auditing covert coordination or collusion among AI agents, including activation probes, steganalysis, and black-box audits.

nodes.name: Emergent and latent agent communication
nodes.description: Studies of private languages, latent channels, and hidden communication that agents develop, and whether humans or monitors can still read them.

nodes.name: Misalignment propagation and contagion
nodes.description: Work measuring and mitigating how unsafe behaviour, value drift, or adversarial payloads spread and amplify through populations of interacting agents.

nodes.name: Multi-agent safety benchmarks and frameworks
nodes.description: Benchmarks, simulation environments, and evaluation frameworks for testing safety, security, cooperation, and prosocial behaviour in multi-agent LLM systems.

nodes.name: Emergent collective behaviour studies
nodes.description: Empirical studies of how groups, organisations, and swarms of agents behave collectively, including emergent institutions and comparisons with single agents or humans.

nodes.name: Institutions, norms, and mechanism design
nodes.description: Designing deployment rules, norm enforcement, anti-collusion mechanisms, economies, and infrastructure that shape multi-agent outcomes.

nodes.name: Training agents for multi-agent alignment
nodes.description: Training and preference-optimisation methods, plus agendas, that teach individual agents to cooperate safely, resist deceptive peers, or handle misaligned partners.

nodes.name: Aligned to who?
nodes.description: Technical protocols for taking seriously the plurality of human values, cultures, and communities when aligning AI to "humanity"

detail.summary: Technical protocols for taking seriously the plurality of human values, cultures, and communities when aligning AI to "humanity"
detail.theory_of_change: use democratic/pluralist/context-sensitive principles to guide AI development, alignment, and deployment somehow. Doing it as an afterthought in post-training or the spec isn't good enough. Continuously shape AI's social and technical feedback loop on the road to AGI

nodes.name: Aligning what?
nodes.description: Develop alternatives to agent-level models of alignment, by treating human-AI interactions, AI-assisted institutions, AI economic or cultural systems, drives within one AI, and other causal/constitutive processes as subject to alignment

detail.summary: Develop alternatives to agent-level models of alignment, by treating human-AI interactions, AI-assisted institutions, AI economic or cultural systems, drives within one AI, and other causal/constitutive processes as subject to alignment
detail.theory_of_change: Model multiple reality-shaping processes above and below the level of the individual AI, some of which are themselves quasi-agential (e.g. cultures) or intelligence-like (e.g. markets), will develop AI alignment into a mature science for managing the transition to an AGI civilization

nodes.name: Evals
nodes.description: Systematic measurement of AI capabilities and dangerous behaviors to inform deployment decisions and guide safety research priorities.
nodes.one: Measuring what models can do and how they behave, especially dangerous capabilities and tendencies such as deception.

nodes.name: AGI metrics
nodes.description: Evals with the explicit aim of measuring progress towards full human-level generality.

detail.summary: Evals with the explicit aim of measuring progress towards full human-level generality.
detail.theory_of_change: Help predict timelines for risk awareness and strategy.

critiques.name: Is the Definition of AGI a Percentage?

nodes.name: Capability evals
nodes.description: Make tools that can actually check whether a model has a certain capability or propensity. We default to low-n sampling of a vast latent space but aim to do better.

detail.summary: Make tools that can actually check whether a model has a certain capability or propensity. We default to low-n sampling of a vast latent space but aim to do better.
detail.theory_of_change: Keep a close eye on what capabilities are acquired when, so that frontier labs and regulators are better informed on what security measures are already necessary (and hopefully they extrapolate). You can't regulate without them.

critiques.name: Large Language Models Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated
AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations
Do Large Language Model Benchmarks Test Reliability?

nodes.name: No-CoT and latent reasoning evals
nodes.description: Measures how much reasoning, planning, or computation models do inside a forward pass without verbalized chain-of-thought, including looped architectures, filler tokens, and multi-hop recall, as a threat to monitorability.

nodes.name: Rare-behaviour estimation and statistical bounds
nodes.description: Methods for forecasting or bounding the rates of rare harmful behaviours from limited samples, such as power-law extrapolation, best-of-N risk estimators, PAC-style bounds, and deployment simulation.

nodes.name: Capability elicitation and hidden capabilities
nodes.description: Work on whether evaluations draw out a model's full capability, covering fine-tuning, tampering and scaffolding elicitation, sandbagging or backdoor-hidden abilities, and theoretical limits of black-box testing.

nodes.name: Automated auditing and propensity evals
nodes.description: Agentic auditing tools and benchmarks that probe models' tendencies toward misaligned actions such as scheming, self-preservation, goal drift, and instrumental behaviour, along with methods for inferring propensities and keeping audits realistic.

nodes.name: Dangerous-capability and risk benchmarks
nodes.description: Domain benchmarks and model safety reports that measure catastrophic-risk capabilities such as cyber offense, persuasion, CBRN uplift, and harmful agent actions.

nodes.name: Eval validity and measurement science
nodes.description: Studies of whether evaluation scores mean what they claim, covering benchmark saturation, item response theory, time-horizon metrics, cheating and reward hacking inflating scores, harness artefacts, and critiques of lab eval practice.

nodes.name: AI R&D and research-taste evals
nodes.description: Evaluations of how well models do AI research and safety research, including experiment design, research taste, conceptual reasoning, imitating safety researchers, and measuring R&D or productivity speedups.

nodes.name: Autonomy evals
nodes.description: Measure an AI's ability to act autonomously to complete long-horizon, complex tasks.

detail.summary: Measure an AI's ability to act autonomously to complete long-horizon, complex tasks.
detail.theory_of_change: By measuring how long and complex a task an AI can complete (its "time horizon"), we can track capability growth and identify when models gain dangerous autonomous capabilities (like R&D acceleration or replication).

critiques.name: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity.

nodes.name: Task time-horizon measurement
nodes.description: Work that measures, extends, forecasts or critiques how long human-equivalent tasks AI agents can complete autonomously, including no-chain-of-thought horizons and cross-domain variants.

nodes.name: AI R&D automation benchmarks
nodes.description: Benchmarks testing whether agents can autonomously do AI research and development work such as replicating papers, post-training models or building agent systems, plus critiques of such benchmarks.

nodes.name: Pre-deployment model autonomy evaluations
nodes.description: Reports from evaluations of specific frontier models for catastrophic autonomy risks such as rogue replication, sabotage and reward hacking, along with frameworks for scoring loss-of-control risk.

nodes.name: Open-ended real-world agent experiments
nodes.description: Studies that let agents pursue open-ended goals in real or simulated economic settings, such as running a shop, earning money or operating in the AI Village, and analyse the behaviour that results.

nodes.name: Agent safety and harmful-action evals
nodes.description: Evaluations of unsafe or harmful behaviour by computer-use and tool-using agents, including autonomous multi-step cyber-attack capability and incidents during cyber evals.

nodes.name: Long-horizon coherence and reliability
nodes.description: Work that analyses why agents fail or lose coherence over long multi-step tasks, using controllable environments, error taxonomies and tooling to improve agent reliability.

nodes.name: WMD evals (Weapons of Mass Destruction)
nodes.description: Evaluate whether AI models possess dangerous knowledge or capabilities related to biological and chemical weapons, such as biosecurity or chemical synthesis.

detail.summary: Evaluate whether AI models possess dangerous knowledge or capabilities related to biological and chemical weapons, such as biosecurity or chemical synthesis.
detail.theory_of_change: By benchmarking and tracking AI's knowledge of biology and chemistry, we can identify when models become capable of accelerating WMD development or misuse, allowing for timely intervention.

critiques.name: The Reality of AI and Biorisk

nodes.name: Situational awareness and self-awareness evals
nodes.description: Evaluate if models understand their own internal states and behaviors, their environment, and whether they are in a test or real-world deployment.

detail.summary: Evaluate if models understand their own internal states and behaviors, their environment, and whether they are in a test or real-world deployment.
detail.theory_of_change: If an AI can distinguish between evaluation and deployment ("evaluation awareness"), it might hide dangerous capabilities (scheming/sandbagging). By measuring self- and situational-awareness, we can better assess this risk and build more robust evaluations.

critiques.name: Lessons from a Chimp: AI "Scheming" and the Quest for Ape Language
It's hard to make scheming evals look realistic for LLMs

nodes.name: Measuring evaluation awareness
nodes.description: Black-box benchmarks, protocols and scaling studies that measure how reliably models can tell evaluations apart from real deployment.

nodes.name: Probing and steering evaluation awareness
nodes.description: Work that uses linear probes, sparse autoencoder features, logit monitors and activation steering to locate, critique or suppress internal representations of being evaluated.

nodes.name: Eval awareness effects on safety results
nodes.description: Studies and arguments on whether recognising a test changes model behaviour, through eval gaming, inflated safety scores or honeypot gaming, and what this means for trusting alignment evaluations and system cards.

nodes.name: Eval realism and awareness mitigation
nodes.description: Methods and position pieces on reducing evaluation awareness, such as replaying live usage, rewriting prompts, deployment scaffolds, training-time invariance or eval cooperativeness, and on the limits of realism.

nodes.name: Training origins and model organisms
nodes.description: Work tracing how evaluation awareness emerges across training stages and data, and building model organisms or verbalization training to study verbalized versus unverbalized awareness.

nodes.name: Introspection and self-knowledge
nodes.description: Tests of whether models can accurately report their own internal states, learned behaviours, capabilities or outputs, including concept-injection introspection, self-recognition and replication critiques.

nodes.name: Awareness of tampering, monitoring and context
nodes.description: Evaluations of whether models detect prefill or output tampering, chain-of-thought monitoring, who the user is, temporal cues or training updates, and how they reason instrumentally about their own situation.

nodes.name: Steganography evals
nodes.description: Evaluate whether models can hide secret information or encoded reasoning in their outputs, such as in chain-of-thought scratchpads, to evade monitoring.

detail.summary: evaluate whether models can hide secret information or encoded reasoning in their outputs, such as in chain-of-thought scratchpads, to evade monitoring.
detail.theory_of_change: if models can use steganography, they could hide deceptive reasoning, bypassing safety monitoring and control measures. By evaluating this capability, we can assess the risk of a model fooling its supervisors.

critiques.name: Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think.

nodes.name: AI deception evals
nodes.description: research demonstrating that AI models, particularly agentic ones, can learn and execute deceptive behaviors such as alignment faking, manipulation, and sandbagging.

detail.summary: research demonstrating that AI models, particularly agentic ones, can learn and execute deceptive behaviors such as alignment faking, manipulation, and sandbagging.
