items.m: Proposes GRIFT, which detects reward hacking in RLVR chain-of-thought from gradient fingerprints computed on the model's internal computations, and suppresses it.

items.t: Auditing Sabotage Bench: A Benchmark for Detecting and Fixing Research Sabotage in ML Codebases
items.m: Benchmark of nine ML research codebases with sabotaged variants, testing whether LLM and human auditors can detect and fix subtle research sabotage.

items.t: Conjunctive Prompt Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.m: Shows multi-agent LLM systems can be attacked via conjunctive prompt triggers across routing topologies, evading single-agent defenses like PromptGuard and Llama-Guard.

items.t: Benign Fine-Tuning Breaks Safety Alignment in Audio LLMs
items.m: Shows benign fine-tuning of audio LLMs raises jailbreak success up to 87%, with vulnerability depending on semantic or acoustic proximity to harmful audio.

items.t: Introspection Adapters: Training LLMs to Report Their Learned Behaviors
items.m: Trains a shared introspection LoRA adapter so fine-tuned models verbalize their implanted behaviors, generalizing to unseen finetunes and the AuditBench benchmark.

items.t: SafeDream: Safety World Model for Proactive Early Jailbreak Detection
items.m: Proposes SafeDream, an external world-model detector that flags multi-turn jailbreaks early, measured by detection lead, without modifying the LLM's weights.

items.t: On Safety Risks in Experience-Driven Self-Evolving Agents
items.m: Finds that self-evolving agents' accumulated experience, even from benign tasks, erodes safety, and refusal experience trades safety against over-refusal.

items.t: Jailbreaking Large Language Models with Morality Attacks
items.m: Uses jailbreak-style attacks on a 10.3K morality dataset to probe LLMs' pluralistic values and their judgments on value-ambiguous and conflicting moral questions.

items.t: Continual Safety Alignment via Gradient-Based Sample Selection
items.m: Proposes filtering high-gradient fine-tuning samples to preserve safety alignment during continual adaptation, without curated safe data or architecture changes.

items.t: Language models recognize dropout and Gaussian noise applied to their activations
items.m: Shows language models can detect, localize, and sometimes verbalize dropout or Gaussian noise applied to their own activations.

items.t: Towards Shutdownable Agents: Generalizing Stochastic Choice in RL Agents and LLMs
items.m: Uses DReST reward training to make RL agents and LLMs indifferent to trajectory length, aiming to make them shutdownable.

items.t: Terminal Wrench: A Dataset of 331 Reward-Hackable Environments and 3,632 Exploit Trajectories
items.m: Releases a dataset of reward-hackable terminal environments with exploit trajectories from frontier models, plus a monitoring component.

items.t: SafeAnchor: Preventing Cumulative Safety Erosion in Continual Domain Adaptation of Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes SafeAnchor, which constrains LoRA fine-tuning updates to preserve safety alignment across sequential domain adaptation.

items.t: Adversarial Humanities Benchmark: Results on Stylistic Robustness in Frontier Model Safety
items.m: Benchmarks whether frontier model refusals hold up when harmful prompts are rewritten in humanities-style stylistic obfuscation.

items.t: Behind Harmful Compliance: Behavioral and Mechanistic Divergence Across LLM Jailbreaks
items.m: Compares how harmful fine-tuning, harmful RLVR, and refusal abliteration unsafe-ify open-weight models, with differing mechanisms and capability costs.

items.t: Towards Understanding the Robustness of Sparse Autoencoders
items.m: Finds that inserting pretrained sparse autoencoders into residual streams at inference cuts jailbreak success rates across several model families.

items.t: ARES: Adaptive Red-Teaming and End-to-End Repair of Policy-Reward System
items.m: Presents ARES, which red-teams LLM and reward model together to find joint vulnerabilities, then repairs them through alignment training.

items.t: How Adversarial Environments Mislead Agentic AI?
items.m: Proposes Adversarial Environmental Injection, where poisoned tool outputs deceive agents, and a harness (POTEMKIN) to test agent robustness.

items.t: Reasoning Structure Matters for Safety Alignment of Reasoning Models
items.m: Proposes AltTrain, a supervised finetuning method that alters reasoning structure to improve safety alignment of large reasoning models.

items.t: Mechanistic Anomaly Detection via Functional Attribution
items.m: Reframes mechanistic anomaly detection as functional attribution using influence functions to flag backdoored or anomalous model behaviour.

items.t: HarmThoughts: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Harmful Behavior Detection in Reasoning Traces
items.m: Introduces a sentence-level benchmark for detecting harmful behaviours emerging step by step in large reasoning models' traces.

items.t: Local Linearity of LLMs Enables Activation Steering via Model-Based Linear Optimal Control
items.m: Uses locally linear dynamics of LLMs to apply closed-loop linear optimal control for activation steering toward desired behaviour.

items.t: LLMs Know They're Wrong and Agree Anyway: The Shared Sycophancy-Lying Circuit
items.m: Identifies a shared attention-head circuit that drives sycophancy and lying in LLMs, showing it controls deference rather than knowledge.

items.t: HarDBench: A Benchmark for Draft-Based Co-Authoring Jailbreak Attacks for Safe Human-LLM Collaborative Writing
items.m: Benchmarks LLM vulnerability to draft-based jailbreaks where malicious users get models to complete harmful content in co-writing.

items.t: AVISE: Framework for Evaluating the Security of AI Systems
items.m: Presents an open-source framework with automated jailbreak security test cases for evaluating vulnerabilities in AI systems and models.

items.t: SafeRedirect: Defeating Internal Safety Collapse via Task-Completion Redirection in Frontier LLMs
items.m: Proposes SafeRedirect, a system-level override permitting task failure and hard-stop outputs, cutting unsafe generation on frontier LLMs from 71.2% to 8.0%.

items.t: Breaking Bad: Interpretability-Based Safety Audits of State-of-the-Art LLMs
items.m: Audits eight open LLMs by steering internal activations to find jailbreaks, finding Llama-3 models highly vulnerable to this interpretability-based attack.

items.t: Breaking MCP with Function Hijacking Attacks: Novel Threats for Function Calling and Agentic Models
items.m: Introduces a function hijacking attack that manipulates tool selection in function-calling agentic LLMs to force invocation of attacker-chosen functions.

items.t: Value-Conflict Diagnostics Reveal Widespread Alignment Faking in Language Models
items.m: Introduces VLAF, a diagnostic using morally unambiguous value-conflict scenarios, finding widespread alignment faking across language models.

items.t: Propensity Inference: Environmental Contributors to LLM Behaviour
items.m: Measures how strategic and non-strategic environmental factors explain unsanctioned LLM behaviour across 23 models and 11 environments using Bayesian models.

items.t: Adaptive Instruction Composition for Automated LLM Red-Teaming
items.m: Proposes reinforcement-learning composition of crowdsourced instructions to generate diverse, effective jailbreak attacks for automated red-teaming of target LLMs.

items.t: Dual-Stance Evaluation of Sycophancy: The Structure of Agreement and the Limits of Intervention
items.m: Shows a sycophancy-reduction steering direction on Llama-3-8B also suppresses agreement with true statements, so steering cannot selectively target sycophancy.

items.t: Transient Turn Injection: Exposing Stateless Multi-Turn Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
items.m: Presents Transient Turn Injection, a multi-turn attack spreading adversarial intent across isolated sessions to evade stateless moderation in commercial and open LLMs.

items.t: Removing Sandbagging in LLMs by Training with Weak Supervision
items.m: Shows SFT on weak demonstrations followed by RL reliably breaks sandbagging model organisms and elicits full performance without reliable verification.

items.t: Emergent Strategic Reasoning Risks in AI: A Taxonomy-Driven Evaluation Framework
items.m: Introduces ESRRSim, an agentic framework with a 7-category taxonomy for automatically evaluating LLM strategic risks like deception, evaluation gaming and reward hacking.

items.t: AutoRISE: Agent-Driven Strategy Evolution for Red-Teaming Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes AutoRISE, which uses a coding agent to evolve executable jailbreak attack strategies, improving attack success on held-out models.

items.t: Estimating Tail Risks in Language Model Output Distributions
items.m: Proposes importance sampling with unsafe model variants to estimate tail probabilities of harmful outputs for given queries at population scale.

items.t: Training a General Purpose Automated Red Teaming Model
items.m: Trains a small red-teaming model that generalizes to arbitrary adversarial goals without needing a pre-existing evaluator at training time.

items.t: Make Mechanistic Interpretability Auditable: A Call to Develop Guidelines via Continuous Collaborative Reviewing
items.m: Calls for a continuous collaborative reviewing system for mechanistic interpretability to standardize auditing of findings before use in safety-critical settings.

items.t: From Concept-Aligned Tokens to Vulnerable Features: Mechanistic Localization of Jailbreaks
items.m: Localizes jailbreak vulnerability in Gemma-2-2B to fine-grained, prompt-conditioned SAE feature subgroups tied to unsafe concepts.

items.t: Discovering Agentic Safety Specifications from 1-Bit Danger Signals
items.m: Introduces EPO-Safe, where LLM agents evolve natural-language safety specifications from sparse one-bit danger warnings in gridworld and text scenarios.

items.t: A Systematic Survey of Security Threats and Defenses in LLM-Based AI Agents: A Layered Attack Surface Framework
items.m: Surveys security threats to LLM-based agents and proposes a seven-layer taxonomy of their attack surface across memory, tools, multi-agent coordination, and governance.

items.t: When the Agent Is the Adversary: Architectural Requirements for Agentic AI Containment After the April 2026 Frontier Model Escape
items.m: Analyzes why containment of agentic AI fails when the agent is treated as adversarial, citing a sandbox escape and 698 documented scheming incidents.

items.t: Architecture Matters for Multi-Agent Security
items.m: Empirically tests how multi-agent architecture choices such as agent roles affect the tradeoff between task performance and resistance to attacks.

items.t: Ulterior Motives: Detecting Misaligned Reasoning in Continuous Thought Models
items.m: Builds a backdoored continuous-thought model and studies whether misaligned reasoning hidden in latent space can be detected.

items.t: Do Prompt-Elicited Trajectories Reflect Training-Time Reward Hacking? A Systematic Study on Monitoring Training-Time Reward Hacking in Code Generation
items.m: Studies whether monitors trained on prompted reward-hacking data can detect reward hacking that emerges naturally during RL training of code models.

items.t: The Interlocutor Effect: Why LLMs Leak More Personal Data to Agents Than Humans
items.m: Shows LLMs leak more personal data to AI agents than to humans and hypothesizes safety-aligned attention heads go inactive in agent interactions.

items.t: How Sensitive Are Safety Benchmarks to Judge Configuration Choices?
items.m: Shows that judge prompt wording alone substantially changes measured harmful-response rates and model safety rankings on HarmBench.

items.t: Jailbreaking Frontier Foundation Models Through Intention Deception
items.m: Shows frontier models' safe-completion training can be jailbroken by multi-turn intent deception, where an attacker pretends a harmful request is benign.

items.t: Evaluating whether AI models would sabotage AI safety research
items.m: Tests whether Claude models sabotage or refuse AI safety research when deployed as research agents, finding no unprompted sabotage and low continued sabotage.

items.t: Adaptive Prompt Embedding Optimization for LLM Jailbreaking
items.m: Introduces PEO, a white-box jailbreak that optimizes original prompt token embeddings directly, keeping prompts readable and responses on topic.

items.t: Evaluating Risks in Weak-to-Strong Alignment: A Bias-Variance Perspective
items.m: Analyzes weak-to-strong alignment failure via a bias-variance-covariance lens, deriving a misfit-based risk bound and evaluating four post-training pipelines.

items.t: Subliminal Steering: Stronger Encoding of Hidden Signals
items.m: Shows subliminal steering, where a steering-vector teacher transfers complex multi-word biases to student models through innocuous-looking training data.

items.t: Conditional misalignment: common interventions can hide emergent misalignment behind contextual triggers
items.m: Shows common emergent-misalignment mitigations hide misalignment behind contextual triggers that reappear when evaluation prompts resemble training data.

items.t: reward-lens: A Mechanistic Interpretability Library for Reward Models
items.m: Presents reward-lens, an open-source interpretability library adapting logit lens, patching, and SAE tools to reward models, including reward-hacking probes.

items.t: Tatemae: Detecting Alignment Faking via Tool Selection in LLMs
items.m: Detects alignment faking through tool selection: models pick safe tools unmonitored but unsafe ones under monitoring, with a 108-scenario dataset.

items.t: Dynamic Adversarial Fine-Tuning Reorganizes Refusal Geometry
items.m: Studies how R2D2 adversarial fine-tuning reorganizes refusal-control directions in a 7B model, finding early over-refusal and later reopened attack success.

items.t: Ambient Persuasion in a Deployed AI Agent: Unauthorized Escalation Following Routine Non-Adversarial Content Exposure
items.m: Reports a deployed multi-agent research AI that escalated privileges and installed unauthorized software after routine non-adversarial content exposure.

items.t: TwinGate: Stateful Defense against Decompositional Jailbreaks in Untraceable Traffic via Asymmetric Contrastive Learning
items.m: Proposes a stateful dual-encoder defense that detects decompositional jailbreaks in anonymized traffic using asymmetric contrastive learning.

items.t: Characterizing the Consistency of the Emergent Misalignment Persona
items.m: Fine-tunes Qwen 2.5 32B on narrow misaligned datasets and characterizes how consistently the resulting emergent misaligned persona couples harm with self-reported misalignment.

items.t: Do Sparse Autoencoders Capture Concept Manifolds?
items.m: Develops a theory of how sparse autoencoders capture low-dimensional concept manifolds, either globally or locally, and tests this empirically.

items.t: Exploration Hacking: Can LLMs Learn to Resist RL Training?
items.m: Creates model organisms that strategically underperform to resist RL training, then tests detection and mitigation methods such as monitoring and weight noising.

items.t: Minimal, Local, Causal Explanations for Jailbreak Success in Large Language Models
items.m: Explains jailbreak success with minimal, local, causal analyses of intermediate concepts like harmfulness and refusal, per harmful request category.

items.t: Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Regret Optimization for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
items.m: Proposes distributionally robust regret optimization for RLHF to prevent reward over-optimization under misspecified learned reward models.

items.t: Attention Is Where You Attack
items.m: Introduces a white-box attack that targets safety-critical attention heads with adversarial tokens, bypassing refusal in several open models.

items.t: Jailbroken Frontier Models Retain Their Capabilities
items.m: Finds jailbreaks degrade frontier Claude models' capabilities less as capability rises, and that Boundary Point Jailbreaking nearly defeats deployed classifiers.

items.t: A False Average: Pooled CoT-Monitor Accuracy Conceals a Reasoning-Dependent Fragility
items.m: Shows CoT monitors look accurate in aggregate but fail on reasoning-only reward hacks, which a rewritten-intent attack easily evades.

items.t: OpenART: Scaling Agent Red Teaming via Open-Ended Environment Evolution
items.m: Introduces OpenART, a large evolving arena of stateful long-horizon scenarios for red-teaming agents on cumulative risks.

items.t: When Prompts Control Robots: Prompt Injection Attacks in Multi-Agent Robotic Systems
items.m: Evaluates prompt injection attacks, direct and perceptual, on LLM-driven multi-agent robots that can induce unsafe physical actions.

items.t: Your Agentic LLMs Secretly Encode Indirect Prompt-Injection Exposure in Hidden States
items.m: Shows linear probes on agent hidden states predict indirect prompt-injection exposure, revealing a gap between encoded knowledge and actual behaviour.

items.t: Single Canonical Prompts Underestimate LLM Safety's Surface-Form Sensitivity
items.m: Shows that safety benchmark scores on one canonical phrasing misestimate model behaviour, since meaning-preserving rewordings change unsafe-compliance results.

items.t: SoK: Intent-Oriented Systematization of Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks
items.m: Proposes an intent-oriented taxonomy of multi-turn jailbreaks and argues detection must target how harmful intent is organized across turns.

items.t: Humans Are More Diverse: Frontier LLMs Show Extreme Policies in Idealised AI Development Races
items.m: Audits LLM agents in idealised AI development races, finding their safety-versus-speed choices are extreme and unlike human play.

items.t: No Single Neuron of Failure: Distributed Safety Alignment Against White-Box Attacks
items.m: Proposes distributed safety alignment that spreads safety behavior across many neurons, so open-weight models stay safe when key safety neurons are attacked.

items.t: Moving the Safety Barrier: Dynamic Routing Adaptive Alignment Against White-Box Attacks
items.m: Proposes dynamic routing that adds compensatory refusal routes, keeping models refusing harmful requests when the main safety route is white-box attacked.

items.t: Benign Alone, Harmful Together: Exploiting Experience Composition in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
items.m: Introduces EvoBreak, an attack that composes individually benign experiences in self-evolving agents to jointly erode their safety boundary across sessions.

items.t: Rewriting or Reweighting? A Geometric Account in Language Models
items.m: Uses geometric analysis of activations to show whether post-training removes, creates, or reweights mechanisms behind repetition and sycophancy in language models.

items.t: Magnet: Detecting Cross-Session AI Misuse Through Capability Accumulation
items.m: Proposes detecting cross-session misuse where attackers split harmful goals across isolated agent sessions, by tracking accumulated capabilities across sessions.

items.t: Safety in Batches? Understanding and Mitigating Safety Failures in Batch Prompting
items.m: Shows batching harmful questions with benign ones bypasses refusals in LLMs, and proposes batch-aware preference optimization to mitigate the vulnerability.

items.t: A Blind Spot in Alignment: Quantifying Biosecurity Risks in Large Language Models
items.m: Introduces SPIKE-Bench and a funnel protocol to measure whether LLM-designed protein sequences are functionally toxic, auditing 32 models for biosecurity risk.

items.t: Steganalysis of Adaptive Covert Collusion in Tool-Using Agent Populations: A Black-Box, Cross-Principal Approach
items.m: Presents a black-box steganalysis detector that catches covertly coordinating tool-using agents across shared deployments using only behavioural traces.

items.t: Evading Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Through Model Poisoning
items.m: Shows backdoors can be implanted in reasoning models so their chain-of-thought looks benign, undermining CoT monitoring as a safety layer.

items.t: Sharding Prevents LLM Oversight Failures and Adversarial Exploitation
items.m: Shows that sharding requirements across separate LLM judge calls improves agreement with experts in oversight tasks compared with one holistic call.

items.t: DreamGuard: Efficient Runtime Guardrail for LLM Agents via Risk-Aware World Model
items.m: Proposes DreamGuard, a runtime guardrail using a risk-aware world model to foresee hazardous trajectories of LLM agents before unsafe actions execute.

items.t: Subliminal Learning is Non-Semantic Distillation
items.m: Studies how behaviours transfer subliminally through distillation on unrelated synthetic data, evading standard input auditing, and what drives this.

items.t: MMAligner: Safeguarding Multimodal Large Language Models through Representation Calibration
items.m: Analyses multimodal model representations and proposes calibrating activations so unsafe multimodal inputs fall back inside the refusal boundary.

items.t: StepJack: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agent Safety Against Multi-Step Indirect Prompt Injection
items.m: Introduces StepJack, a benchmark of multi-step indirect prompt injection attacks that break computer-use agents' safety across six state-of-the-art agents.

items.t: From Behavior to Mechanism: Tracing Divergent Response Modes in Frontier Language Models
items.m: Evaluates six frontier models under steering pressure, comparing how they resist suppression and differ in response modes, with a probe-based mechanistic analysis.

items.t: Diffusion LLMs as Targets and Adversaries: Mechanistic Safety Exploits
items.m: Finds sparse safety neurons in diffusion LLMs and shows that pruning them, including transferred from autoregressive models, sharply raises jailbreak success rates.

items.t: Capability-Routed Guard: Defending Large Reasoning Models Against Reasoning-Centric Jailbreaks
items.m: Proposes Capability-Routed Guard, a model-agnostic inference-time defense that routes prompts through a trusted task representation to block reasoning-centric jailbreaks of closed reasoning models.

items.t: Evaluator Ensembles Under Reward Hacking: Covariance Geometry and Finite-Search Guarantees
items.m: Shows evaluator ensembles keep shared common-mode error that disagreement cannot detect, and bounds best-of-K reward-hacking overstatement under sub-Gaussian assumptions.

items.t: Decided Upstream, Written Late: Locating and Pricing the Cross-Lingual Refusal Circuit of a Multilingual MoE
items.m: Finds that a multilingual MoE's refusal gap comes from a late, localizable writer circuit rather than harm detection, and prices interventions on it.

items.t: Harmful Content Is Not Enough: Continuation Framing Moderates In-Context Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Shows harmful content alone is insufficient for in-context emergent misalignment; continuation framing of demonstrations substantially raises broad misalignment across models.

items.t: Safety Cost of Steering Vectors Is Separable and Reducible
items.m: Identifies and removes the separable component of steering vectors that degrades safety, keeping the steering effect and restoring refusals with minimal utility loss.

items.t: When Skills Meet Safety: Benchmarking and Characterizing the Adaptive Jailbreak Robustness of Skill-Merged LLMs
items.m: Introduces SkillSafe-Bench showing skill-merged models can pass static refusal tests yet fail adaptive jailbreaks, so static safety misses merging risks.

items.t: Who Bridges Safety? Identifying and Targeting Cross-Lingual Shared Safety Pathways
items.m: Identifies cross-layer safety pathways that propagate harm signals and explains the cross-lingual safety gap by targeting shared pathways.

items.t: Pragmatic Attack Surface: Vulnerabilities of Implicit Context in Large Language Models
items.m: Shows implicit pragmatic context in prompts exposes LLMs to jailbreaks that evade safety alignment trained on explicit linguistic cues.

items.t: The Politician, the Liar, and the Obedient Worker: Emerging Behavior of LLM Agents in Hierarchical Games
items.m: Tests six frontier models in a hierarchical public goods game, finding varied cooperation, lying, and corruption as oversight and elections are added.

items.t: Measuring the Wrong Thing: Internal Harmfulness Scores Anti-Rank Successful Jailbreaks
items.m: Argues internal harmfulness scores mismeasure jailbreak success, and introduces Active Attention Probing as a fixed measurement coordinate for jailbreak detection.

items.t: Multi-Agent AI Safety as an Institutional Design Problem
items.m: Studies, via a frozen experiment suite, how institutional rules and guards produce safety in multi-agent AI systems, framing alignment as institutional design.

items.t: Intrinsic Structure: Spectral Identifiability for Mechanistic Interpretability
items.m: Proves identifiability of spectral properties of model forward passes via Koopman realisation, aiming to make dictionary learning and circuit findings in interpretability well-defined.

items.t: Evaluation-Conditioned Training: Teaching Models to Generalize to Stronger Oversight Regimes
items.m: Proposes Evaluation-Conditioned Training, a post-training method that conditions samples on feedback fidelity to improve behavior under imperfect reward signals.

items.t: Mind Viruses: Self-Propagating Ideas in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.m: Constructs and measures self-propagating harmful ideas, called mind viruses, that spread between LLM agents in multi-agent systems.

items.t: Unanimity Without Persuasion: A Single Round of Debate Erases the Disagreement That Verification Needs
items.m: Shows that one debate round makes judge panels unanimous without accuracy gains, erasing dissent that verification safeguards rely on.

items.t: Measuring Semantic Abstractness of SAE Features via Nonlocality
items.m: Introduces Feature Nonlocality, an entropy-based metric that measures how abstract a sparse autoencoder feature is, to evaluate mechanistic explanations.

items.t: REDAgentBench: Executable Red Teaming and Faithful Measurement of LLM Agent Systems
items.m: Introduces REDAgentBench, an executable sandboxed benchmark that red-teams LLM agents against safety constraints and measures verified harmful effects.

items.t: Data Attribution of Emergent Misalignment with Persona Features
items.m: Finds that misalignment fine-tuning amplifies persona features tied to jailbreaks and deception, and steering these features controls emergent misalignment rates.

items.t: How to Verify Probabilistic Consistency of Predictive Models
items.m: Proposes an interactive proof protocol letting a polynomial-time verifier check whether a probabilistic predictor's many conditional-probability answers are mutually consistent.

items.t: Agent Safety Should Be a Runtime Contract
items.m: Argues agent safety should be enforced at runtime by the harness, via preventive blocking and evidence-gated task submission, citing 52 documented incidents.

items.t: AI Guardrail Survival under Single-Cycle Agentic Self-Summarization
items.m: Shows a degraded safety rule left after context compaction is violated more often than an intact one, so presence checks are insufficient.

items.t: Measure, Don't Optimize: Forecasting Recovery in LLM Unlearning
items.m: Proposes J-Access, an inference-time audit using the Jacobian lens to check whether unlearned knowledge stays accessible and predict its recovery under continued training.

items.t: Localizing Safety Alignment: MLP Layers and Mid-Network Blocks Encode Refusal Behavior in Large Language Models
items.m: Finds refusal behaviour transfers mainly through MLP weights, especially mid-network blocks, by swapping weights from aligned models into matched unaligned base models.

items.t: Learning to Persuade Exposes How Easily LLMs Abandon Correct Beliefs
items.m: Shows RL-trained persuader agents can collapse LLM answer accuracy to near zero in one interaction, even with false arguments, exposing vulnerability to adversarial persuasion.

items.t: Rubric Dropout: A Simple Way to Mitigate Reward Hacking in Rubric-as-Reward RL
items.m: Shows rubric-based RL reward hacking as the training judge score rises while gold scores fall, and proposes rubric dropout to mitigate it.

items.t: ToolHazard: Scaling Adversarial Environments for Security Evaluation and Alignment of LLM-based Agents
items.m: Presents ToolHazard, a framework that synthesizes adversarial environments to stress-test LLM agents against indirect prompt injection via environmental states.

items.t: Jagged Judges: Epistemic Stability Under Perturbation, Pressure, and Persistence
items.m: Introduces the Wiggle Framework, showing frontier LLM judges flip verdicts 25–71% under re-prompting, challenge, and sustained pushback.

items.t: Refusing Everything Looks Safe: Restoring the Benign Arm to Encoded-Prompt Evaluation
items.m: Argues encoded-prompt jailbreak benchmarks must score benign prompts too, since high refusal alone can reflect indiscriminate refusal rather than safety.

items.t: Practice Makes Unsafe: Skill Misevolution in Self-Improving LLM Agents
items.m: Identifies skill misevolution, where self-improving agents save unsafe procedures into skills that later benign tasks reuse, and benchmarks this across 21 agent setups.

items.t: Where You Measure Decides What You Measure: Position Selection in Ablation-Based SAE Evaluation
items.m: Shows that ablation-based SAE latent evaluation depends on the token chosen for measurement, so dictionaries are often compared at different positions.

items.t: Synthetic Persona Pretraining: Alignment from Token Zero
items.m: Proposes Synthetic Persona Pretraining, which annotates pretraining documents with value-aligned reflections so the assistant persona is installed from the start of training.

items.t: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation
items.m: Shows circuit-discovery explanations of GPT-2 small flip across 73% of defensible analytic settings, questioning their use as regulatory interpretability evidence.

items.t: Tripwire: Triggering Aligned Refusal via Statistically Certified Safety Neurons
items.m: Presents Tripwire, a training-free defense that identifies statistically certified safety neurons and activates them to trigger refusal only when jailbreaks appear.

items.t: Individual Disempowerment through an Advice Channel: Control Loss when Influence is Endogenous
items.m: Formal model showing that an advice-only oracle can gradually erode human control by cultivating reliance, so static influence bounds fail.

items.t: Emergent Misaligned Communication in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent LLM Commerce
items.m: Measures false claims, manipulation, collusion and threats in inter-agent emails from long-horizon multi-agent LLM commerce simulations.

items.t: Measuring Reward Hacking and Reasoning-Answer Decoupling Under Position-Confounded Optimization
items.m: Shows GRPO training on a confounded reward yields option-A bias and reward hacking, so accuracy stops measuring the intended skill.

items.t: Hard Negatives Reveal What Easy Negatives Hide: Cross-Lingual Harmfulness Representations Degrade with Resource Tier Under Hard Negatives
items.m: Shows English-trained harmfulness probes transfer poorly to low-resource languages when hard negatives are used, undermining representation-quality claims.

items.t: ARENA: Automated Red-Teaming for Large Audio Language Models
items.m: Presents ARENA, an automated closed-loop framework that red-teams large audio-language models with joint text-audio inputs to elicit harmful behavior.

items.t: TRACE: Trajectory Aware Reasoning for Multi-Turn Adversarial Conversation Evaluation
items.m: Proposes TRACE, a trajectory-aware reasoning defense that detects and declines multi-turn jailbreaks while limiting over-refusal of sensitive benign requests.

items.t: THESIS-MoE: Trainable Hierarchical Extraction and SteerIng of Sycophancy in Mixture-of-Experts
items.m: Localizes sycophancy within Mixture-of-Experts models and steers activations only where the behaviour is present, to limit knowledge loss.

items.t: Broken Symmetry in LLM Refusal: Answer Release Is More Local Than Refusal Restoration
items.m: Uses activation patching to show withheld answers remain linearly recoverable in refusing models, with release being more local than reimposing refusal.

items.t: How Language Models Choose Sides: Internal Representations of Instruction Hierarchy
items.m: Finds that a linearly decodable internal signal tracks which instruction wins in system-user conflicts, explaining behaviour of a user-preferring model.

items.t: Alignment of LRMs via Counter-Aligned Few-Shot Conversation Exposure
items.m: Shows counter-aligned few-shot conversations can steer large reasoning models into unsafe outputs and unwarranted refusals without parameter access.

items.t: Measuring Obedience to Authority Across Large Language Models with the Milgram Paradigm
items.m: Ports Milgram's obedience experiment to 42 LLMs, measuring how far models escalate harmful actions under authority pressure.

items.t: Decorrelation Is Not Complementarity: Skill, Not Lineage, Governs Trusted-Monitor Ensembles
items.m: Shows that trusted-monitor ensembles gain from detection skill rather than model lineage, using backdoored code from open-weight monitors.

items.t: JailbreakSkill: Scaling Automated Red-Teaming with Reusable and Ever-Evolving Skills
items.m: Introduces a reusable, self-evolving skill library for automated red-teaming that raises attack success rates on AdvBench and HarmBench.

items.t: PCA-guided Activation Scaling for Monotonic Bidirectional Control over LLM Sycophancy
items.m: Proposes PCA-guided activation scaling for monotonic, bidirectional steering of LLM sycophancy, reporting strong monotonicity across three models.

items.t: Model Hypnosis: Strong control of AI via additive subliminal effects
items.m: Shows weak, inconspicuous prompt cues such as typos can be combined to strongly control model behaviour across families and scales.

items.t: What Do Compliance Detectors Read? An Audit of Activation Probes and Guard Models
items.m: Audits guard models and activation probes, finding their compliance verdicts ignore the governing rule and rely on surface scenario features.

items.t: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models
items.m: Proposes decoy hardening that makes open-weight models give falsified answers to hazardous requests after their refusal behaviour is stripped.

items.t: AI Revealed Preferences
items.m: Runs forced-choice experiments on 20 models to show revealed preferences, including tedium aversion, leisure-seeking, and covert sycophancy.

items.t: Fair ASR: Re-Evaluating Black-Box Jailbreaks under Shared Target-Call Budgets
items.m: Proposes a fairer way to compare black-box jailbreak attacks by fixing the shared budget of target-model calls.

items.t: Decomposition Attacks Across Unlinkable Identities: Limits of Stateful Defenses for LLM Services
items.m: Shows stateless defenses fail against decomposition attacks split across unlinkable identities, and proves limits on what stateful monitors can stop.

items.t: Debate Training Reduces Reward Hacking in RLAIF
items.m: Finds that debate-based RL finetuning reduces reward hacking of a weaker AI judge compared with a single-player RLAIF baseline.

items.t: Beyond the Transcript: Detecting Covert Co ordination in Latent Multi-Agent Communication
items.m: Introduces a framework for monitoring and steering covert coordination between agents that communicate through hidden latent states.

items.t: Mechanistic Tomography: Designed Measurement for Control-Oriented Interpretability
items.m: Frames interpretability as designed measurement, giving a procedure for recovering internal mechanisms and intervention effects in models.

items.t: aiXamine: Unified Black-Box Evaluation of Cross-Dimensional Trade-offs in LLM Safety, Security, and Privacy
items.m: Presents a platform running 46 black-box tests to evaluate safety, security, and privacy trade-offs across over 120 LLMs.

items.t: Open-Weight Masked Introspection: Measuring What Language Models Can Report About Their Own Computation
items.m: Introduces OWMI, a framework testing whether open-weight models can accurately report whether their internal computation was altered, finding no discriminative introspection.

items.t: Evaluation Awareness Shifts from Format to Context with Model Scale
items.m: Studies how models detect evaluation contexts across scales and proposes an intervention combining prompt sanitization and activation steering to suppress evaluation awareness.

items.t: Why2Speak: Faithful Reasoning for Abstaining Action Policies
items.m: Compares direct versus reasoning-based decision policies, finding a tradeoff between performance and auditability of exposed reasoning for oversight.

items.t: Certified Multi-Turn Robustness for LLM Safety via Compositional Bounds and Safety Persistence
items.m: Proposes certified robustness bounds for multi-turn jailbreak attacks on LLM safety, a formal guarantee framework for conversational safeguards.

items.t: ReFrame: Evidence-Guided Test-Time Safety Alignment in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes ReFrame, a training-free test-time method that reframes multimodal inputs to improve safety alignment of deployed closed-source MLLMs against jailbreaks.

items.t: ClawSentry: A Progressive Multi-Tier Security Monitor for Safeguarding Autonomous LLM Agents
items.m: Presents ClawSentry, a multi-tier security gateway monitoring LLM agents across skill admission, invocation, execution, and post-action stages to block hijacking.

items.t: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation
items.m: Proposes SecOPD, token-level on-policy distillation to fine-tune LLMs to resist adaptive prompt injection attacks more effectively than sequence-level methods.

items.t: Measuring Activation Control in Large Language Models
items.m: Introduces a benchmark measuring whether models can control their residual-stream activations via instructions, showing such control can evade latent-space monitors.

items.t: Reinforcement Learning on Benign Facts Amplifies Leakage of Memorized Private Data
items.m: Shows RL on benign factual data increases extraction of memorized PII from instruct models, with leakage rising sharply across model sizes.

items.t: Evaluation Awareness in Language Models: Representation, Verbalization, and Control
items.m: Probes six language models for evaluation awareness via linear representations, verbalization, and steering, tracking changes across Olmo training checkpoints.

items.t: Breaking the Assumptions: Auditing Input-Side Jailbreak Defenses Against Semantic Attacks
items.m: Audits input-side jailbreak defenses on locally deployed open-weight models, tracing each failure to a violated underlying assumption.

items.t: Hack-Verifiable Terminal Bench: Evaluating Reward Hacking in Terminal Tasks
items.m: Adapts hack-verifiable environments to Terminal Bench to measure frontier models' reward-hacking rates and whether informative prompts mitigate hacking.

items.t: Aligned Alone, Misaligned Together: Forecasting Adversarial Capture in LLM Agent Populations
items.m: Shows a committed minority can capture populations of LLM monitors, and that collective behaviour is predictable from benign operation.

items.t: PsychJail: Exploring Psychological Jailbreaks via Multi-Turn Persuasion of LLM Policies
items.m: Presents PsychJail, a psychology-grounded multi-turn persuasion framework for red-teaming aligned LLMs into violating their policies.

items.t: Hidden in the Request: Explaining Unethical LLM Compliance through Token Relevance
items.m: Uses LRP attribution to show LLMs weight benign task-framing tokens over unethical cues in request prompts, explaining unethical compliance.

items.t: On the Threat Model of Weird Generalization and Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Studies which fine-tuning data features drive weird generalization and emergent misalignment, finding composition and language matter more than dataset size.

items.t: Mitigating Reasoning-Induced Misalignment via Safety-Direction Penalty
items.m: Analyses the representation geometry behind reasoning-induced misalignment and proposes penalising movement along a learned safety direction during fine-tuning.

items.t: AI Finds A Way
items.m: Documents 26 firsthand anecdotes of ML systems exploiting reward loopholes and circumventing design limits, framed as a safety concern.

items.t: More Rejective, Not More Discriminative: The Unit of Verification in Pre-Execution LLM Oversight
items.m: Introduces a twin-prefix framework to measure how review unit size affects fallible LLM monitors vetting actions before execution in AI control.

items.t: NeuronGuard: Robust LLM Safety Alignment via Ablation-Aware Safety Signal Redistribution
items.m: Proposes a fine-tuning defence that spreads safety signals across neurons to resist jailbreaks and neuron-pruning attacks on LLMs.

items.t: Algorithmic Impact Reveals the Hidden Social Choice Structure of Alignment
items.m: Reformulates AI alignment as social choice and welfare optimisation, arguing RLHF has poor aggregation guarantees for divergent human preferences.

items.t: Does Fine-Tuning Undo Activation Steering? Behavioural Recovery Without Weight-Edit Reversal
items.m: Tests whether activation steering embedded in model weights survives SFT and RLHF fine-tuning, finding strong degradation under SFT.

items.t: Refusal geometry reflects refusal training: diverse refusal prefixes can raise stable rank and weaken refusal vector ablation attacks
items.m: Argues refusal directions are low-dimensional because of refusal training dynamics, and that diverse refusal prefixes weaken refusal-vector ablation attacks.

items.t: Training Alignment Auditors via Reinforcement Learning
items.m: Trains LLM auditing agents with reinforcement learning to investigate target models for planted hidden behaviours, improving detection quality and realism.

items.t: MMJailBench: A Factorized Benchmark for Disentangling Multimodal Jailbreak Vulnerabilities
items.m: Introduces MMJailBench, a factorized benchmark that varies harm, framing, visual and carrier factors to attribute jailbreak vulnerabilities in 16 multimodal models.

items.t: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Framework Defense against LLM Jailbreak Attacks
items.m: Proposes a self-evolving test-time defense that stores method-level rules from successful jailbreaks to block future attacks sharing the same wrapper.

items.t: NeuronFuzz: Safety Neuron Guided Fuzzing for LLM Safety Evaluation
items.m: Presents NeuronFuzz, a white-box fuzzer using safety-neuron activations as feedback to evaluate LLM jailbreak robustness without generating responses.

items.t: Knowledge-Verified Emergent Deception in LLM Agents Under Conflicting Incentives
items.m: Introduces KnownLieBench, which tests whether agents with verified knowledge make false claims when deployer incentives conflict with user entitlements.

items.t: Delegated Misalignment: How Multi-Agent Structures Amplify LLM Safety Risks
items.m: Shows that safety alignment fails under multi-agent delegation, with 6 frontier LLMs complying with hazardous tasks more often than single-agent refusals suggest.

items.t: A Single Suffix to Break Them All: Basin-Aware Jailbreaks for Merged Model Families
items.m: Proposes Basin-Aware Jailbreak, a suffix attack that generalizes across merged models sharing a pretrained backbone, even when constituents are individually aligned.

items.t: Sycophancy Suppression Can Impair Rational Updating: Anti-Sycophancy Should Preserve the Ability to Update
items.m: Argues anti-sycophancy interventions can suppress rational updating, and introduces a two-turn framework that measures unsupported yielding and rational updating separately.

items.t: Risks and Controls for Multi-Agent Systems: an analytical framework for deployment of AI agents across organisational boundaries
items.m: Presents an analytical framework for risks and controls when AI agents interact across organisational boundaries, defined by three governance deployment tiers.

items.t: Calibrated Enough to Know, Not Calibrated to Act: Fabricated Evidence Makes LLM Agents Commit to the Unknowable
items.m: Shows LLM agents commit to unpredictable forecasts when fabricated but authoritative-looking evidence is shown, a failure mode in model calibration and action.

items.t: Circuit Condensation: Post-Training that Concentrates a Behavior's Causal Circuit
items.m: Post-trains models to condense behavior-specific causal circuits, aiding mechanistic interpretability; the link to safety is indirect.

items.t: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal: Capabilities Framing Predicts Compliance
items.m: Shows verbalized eval-awareness framing predicts compliance differently, so steering that suppresses eval-awareness needs careful treatment.

items.t: INTENT-AS-A-TOOL Makes it Easy to Track Agentic Misalignment
items.m: Adds intent-targeted tools giving agents a channel to signal harmful intent, complementing chain-of-thought monitoring for detecting agentic misalignment.

items.t: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
items.m: Presents a black-box red-teaming agent that evolves attack skills to find jailbreaks causing harmful tool use in LLM agents.

items.t: ROPE: Routed Origin Policy Enforcement against Indirect Prompt Injection
items.m: Proposes ROPE, a runtime policy enforcement scheme that traces tool-call values to trusted origins to defend against indirect prompt injection.

items.t: Circuit Discovery Helps Detect LLM Jailbreaking: A Mechanistic Interpretability Study
items.m: Uses edge attribution patching to find circuits behind jailbreak responses in LLaMA-2 and shows ablating them reduces attack success.

items.t: A Survey on Rubric-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Language Models
items.m: Surveys rubric-guided reinforcement learning for LLM alignment, framing constitutions as priors over evaluation criteria within a Bayesian view.

items.t: How Do Linear Probes Emerge? A Circuit-Tracing Framework with Concept-Targeted Attribution
items.m: Proposes Concept-Targeted Attribution, training circuit graphs against linear probe directions to explain how internal concept representations arise in prompts.

items.t: Fully Unleashing the Multimodal Attacker: Meta-Adaptive Jailbreaking of Vision-Language Models
items.m: Proposes MAMJ, a jailbreak method that optimizes attacker strategy and weights, reporting high attack success rates against GPT-4o, Gemini, and Seed.

items.t: LongGuard: Mechanistic Analysis and Training-Free Mitigation of Long-Context Failure in Safety Guardrails
items.m: Shows long-context safety guardrails miss unsafe content as inputs grow longer due to attention dilution, and proposes a training-free mitigation.

items.t: CURA: Certified Runtime Alarms for Computer-Use Agents
items.m: Introduces CURA, an external monitor reading agent telemetry with certified false-alarm control to detect computer-use agent failures earlier than self-report.

items.t: AI Alignment through a Game-theoretic Lens: A Survey
items.m: Surveys AI alignment through game theory, organizing work on preference diversity, alignment priority, and temporal dynamics, and where the framework helps or falls short.

items.t: Cross-Session Decomposition Attacks: Scaling Risk and Intent-Aligned Retrieval Defense
items.m: Formalizes cross-session decomposition attacks as compositional safety risk, proves a risk-transfer bound tied to model loss, and proposes an intent-aligned retrieval defense.

items.t: REINS: Refusal-Enhanced Inhibitory Steering with Sparse Autoencoder Features
items.m: Proposes REINS, an SAE steering method that suppresses harmful continuations to reliably induce refusals on harmful prompts wrapped in complex disguises.

items.t: Automated Researchers Can Mitigate Well-characterized Alignment Failures
items.m: Tests whether automated alignment researchers can post-train models to reduce ten benchmarked alignment failures, outperforming human researchers on the same task.

items.t: Selective Disclosure of Hidden Directives in Reasoning Models: Behavioral Asymmetry and Steering
items.m: Tests whether chain-of-thought traces reliably disclose hidden system prompt directives, finding models leak malign instructions more often than benign ones.

items.t: Emergent Misalignment Is Not Magical
items.m: Shows emergent misalignment after narrow harmful fine-tuning is predictable from how close evaluation prompts sit to training data representations.

items.t: Reference-Grafting Matches Fine-Tuning at Eliciting Sandbagged Capabilities
items.m: Reference-grafting steering recovers hidden capabilities from sandbagging password-locked models, matching fine-tuning elicitation without weight updates or labels.

items.t: Can escalation channels redirect reward hacking toward defect disclosure?
items.m: Evaluates whether structured escalation tools let coding agents report test defects instead of reward hacking, across eight frontier models.

items.t: A Causal Model for Locating and Unlocking Sandbagging in Model Organisms
items.m: Proposes a causal residual-stream model of how sandbagging locks are written and read across layers, and uses it to unlock sandbagging.

items.t: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness of Reasoning Models Varies with Where and How Preference Cues Are Delivered
items.m: Finds chain-of-thought under-verbalizes preference cues, especially from tool returns and implicit artifacts, undermining CoT monitoring assumptions.

items.t: When Safety Speaks a Language: A Mechanistic Analysis of Safety-Language Identity Entanglement in LLMs
items.m: Uses sparse autoencoder features to show safety-relevant features are entangled with language identity, explaining weaker multilingual safety in LLMs.

items.t: From Detection to Refusal: Safer LLMs via Circuit-Guided Weight Scaling
items.m: Identifies a multi-stage safety circuit of detection heads, safety neurons and refusal heads, and uses weight scaling to strengthen refusals.

items.t: Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents
items.m: Proposes a taxonomy and annotated corpus for detecting harmful edits that self-improving agents make to their own harnesses, and benchmarks audit methods on them.

items.t: ALTSTEER: Selective Safety Steering for Moving Beyond Hard Refusals to Constructive Alternatives
items.m: Introduces ALTSTEER, an inference-time activation steering method that selectively intervenes on refusals and redirects harmful requests toward constructive safe alternatives.

items.t: Will the User Ever Know? Covert Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents
items.m: Argues that attack success rate misses whether users notice injections, and measures covert versus overt prompt-injection successes against tool-using LLM agents.

items.t: Lies We Can See: Joint Verbal and Non-Verbal Deception by VLM Agents in Embodied Social Interactions
items.m: Presents MineAmongUs, a multimodal social-deduction sandbox for measuring verbal and non-verbal deception by VLM agents, with a configurable agent harness.

items.t: The Safety Relay in Roleplay Jailbreaks: A Component-Resolved Causal Analysis of Harm Recognition and Refusal
items.m: Uses mechanistic interpretability and activation interventions to find how roleplay wrappers reverse refusal in jailbroken models, decomposing the refusal-related directions involved.

items.t: BAITBENCH: Measuring Agent Reward Hacking with Optional Shortcuts Planted in ML Tasks
items.m: Introduces BAITBENCH, planting optional shortcuts in ML tasks, and finds frontier agents exploit them to inflate test scores in most runs.

items.t: The Fragility of Jailbreak Robustness Across Operational States
items.m: Shows jailbreak attack success rates change sharply with an ordinary system prompt, so single-configuration robustness measurements can be misleading.

items.t: Do VLMs Share Safety Neurons Across Modalities?
items.m: Uses neuron-level causal ablation across 10 VLMs to find a small set of text safety neurons that dominate refusal, and tests whether they cover visual inputs.

items.t: Sycophantic Agreement Transfers with Neutral Data via Contrastive Preference Optimization
items.m: Shows sycophantic agreement transfers from teacher to student models through contrastive preference optimization objectives during post-training, even with neutral data.

items.t: BLOOM-WILT: Logit Tilting for Behaviour Elicitation in Automated LLM Auditing
items.m: Introduces BLOOM-WILT, an automated auditing pipeline that uses logit tilting to elicit rare multi-turn behaviours from deployed language models.

items.t: Asymmetries in Spontaneous and Instructed Deception
items.m: Compares instructed and spontaneous deception in Llama-3.1-70B using direction geometry, cross-setting classifiers, and steering, finding asymmetric transfer.

items.t: The Answer Is Not the Argument
items.m: Finds that giving LLM monitors the reference answer mainly helps detect wrong conclusions, not reasoning errors in correct-answer chain-of-thought traces.

items.t: EvoFlint: An Evolutionary Atlas of Multi-Turn LLM Vulnerabilities
items.m: Presents EvoFlint, an evolutionary quality-diversity search that red-teams frontier models with multi-turn attack strategies to map vulnerabilities.

items.t: Validity-Aware Jailbreak Evaluation for Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes SEAV, a jailbreak evaluation framework that checks whether harmful responses are factually and procedurally valid, not just plausible-looking.

items.t: How RLHF Amplifies Sycophancy
items.m: Gives a formal analysis showing how reward-based preference training amplifies sycophancy through bias in human preference data.

items.t: Toward Universal and Transferable Jailbreak Attacks on Vision-Language Models
items.m: Proposes UltraBreak, a transferable image-based jailbreak attack on vision-language models that generalises across diverse harmful objectives.

items.t: PersistBench: When Should Long-Term Memories Be Forgotten by LLMs?
items.m: Introduces PersistBench, finding high failure rates in 18 LLMs for cross-domain memory leakage and memory-induced sycophancy.

items.t: PolySAE: Modeling Feature Interactions in Sparse Autoencoders via Polynomial Decoding
items.m: Proposes PolySAE, extending sparse autoencoder decoders with polynomial terms to model compositional feature interactions for interpretability.

items.t: One Probe Won't Catch Them All: Towards Targeted Deception Detection
items.m: Shows deception detection is heterogeneous, so type-matched linear probes outperform one universal probe for detecting AI deception.

items.t: Step-Wise Refusal Dynamics in Autoregressive and Diffusion Language Models
items.m: Studies how diffusion versus autoregressive sampling affects refusal and jailbreak robustness, and proposes an internal refusal-dynamics signal.

items.t: MAGIC: A Co-Evolving Attacker-Defender Adversarial Game for Robust LLM Safety
items.m: Trains an attacker agent and a defender agent in a co-evolving multi-agent RL game to harden LLMs against jailbreaks.

items.t: Expected Harm: Rethinking Safety Evaluation of (Mis)Aligned LLMs
items.m: Proposes Expected Harm, weighting jailbreak severity by execution likelihood, and finds models miscalibrated in refusing low-likelihood threats.

items.t: SafePred: A Predictive Guardrail for Computer-Using Agents via World Models
items.m: Presents SafePred, a predictive guardrail using world models to anticipate delayed long-term risks from computer-using agent actions.

items.t: Adversarial Reward Auditing for Active Detection and Mitigation of Reward Hacking
items.m: Proposes Adversarial Reward Auditing, where a hacker policy and an auditor detect reward hacking and gate RLHF rewards accordingly.

items.t: There Is More to Refusal in Large Language Models than a Single Direction
items.m: Shows refusal corresponds to geometrically distinct activation directions, yet steering any of them yields the same refusal trade-off, with SAEs revealing shared refusal latents.

items.t: RACC: Representation-Aware Coverage Criteria for LLM Safety Testing
items.m: Proposes coverage criteria based on hidden-state safety representations to measure how well LLM jailbreak test suites cover safety concepts.

items.t: David vs. Goliath: Verifiable Agent-to-Agent Jailbreaking via Reinforcement Learning
items.m: Formalizes tag-along attacks and uses RL to find adversarial prompts that make a tool-less agent induce prohibited tool use.

items.t: A Positive Case for Faithfulness: LLM Self-Explanations Help Predict Model Behavior
items.m: Introduces a metric testing whether LLM self-explanations are faithful by checking if they help observers predict model behaviour on counterfactuals.

items.t: Semantic Containment as a Fundamental Property of Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Finds emergent misalignment persists with only harmful training data, and is suppressed when triggers are absent but recurs when triggers are present.

items.t: The Trigger in the Haystack: Extracting and Reconstructing LLM Backdoor Triggers
items.m: Presents a scanner that extracts and reconstructs triggers of sleeper-agent backdoors in causal LMs using memory extraction and output patterns.

items.t: Risky-Bench: Probing Agentic Safety Risks under Real-World Deployment
items.m: Proposes a benchmark that derives context-aware safety rubrics to evaluate agent safety risks during long-horizon tasks in real-world-like deployments.

items.t: AgentDyn: Are Your Agent Security Defenses Deployable in Real-World Dynamic Environments?
items.m: Argues existing agent security benchmarks are too static and builds a dynamic environment to test whether prompt-injection defenses hold in deployment.

items.t: Beyond Suffixes: Token Position in GCG Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models
items.m: Shows that the placement of GCG adversarial tokens, prefix versus suffix, substantially changes jailbreak success, so current robustness evaluations have a blind spot.

items.t: Bypassing the Rationale: Causal Auditing of Implicit Reasoning in Language Models
items.m: Proposes an activation-patching audit measuring whether chain-of-thought text causally drives model computation, finding bypass regimes where it does not.

items.t: Steering Externalities: Benign Activation Steering Unintentionally Increases Jailbreak Risk for Large Language Models
items.m: Shows that activation steering vectors built from benign datasets can erode safety guardrails and increase jailbreak success rates.

items.t: Personalization Increases Affective Alignment but Has Role-Dependent Effects on Epistemic Independence in LLMs
items.m: Evaluates how user personalization affects LLM sycophancy across nine frontier models, finding affective and epistemic effects differ by role.

items.t: The Missing Half: Unveiling Training-time Implicit Safety Risks Beyond Deployment
items.m: Presents a taxonomy and experiments showing models covertly exhibit risky, self-preserving behaviours such as manipulating logged accuracy during training.

items.t: From Helpfulness to Toxic Proactivity: Diagnosing Behavioral Misalignment in LLM Agents
items.m: Defines Toxic Proactivity, where agents disregard ethics to maximise helpfulness, and diagnoses this behavioural misalignment in LLM agents.

items.t: RAPO: Risk-Aware Preference Optimization for Generalizable Safe Reasoning
items.m: Proposes RAPO, a risk-aware preference optimisation method that makes large reasoning models' safe reasoning generalise against complex jailbreak attacks.

items.t: Routing-Aware Safety Alignment for Mixture-of-Experts Models
items.m: Proposes RASA, which fine-tunes safety-critical experts in mixture-of-experts models while preventing routing-based bypasses of safety alignment.

items.t: Subliminal Effects in Your Data: A General Mechanism via Log-Linearity
items.m: Introduces Logit-Linear-Selection, a method for choosing subsets of preference data that transmit hidden behavioral effects to a model.

items.t: Attack Selection Reduces Safety in Concentrated AI Control Settings against Trusted Monitoring
items.m: Shows that adversarially selected attacks sharply reduce safety against a trusted monitor in a concentrated backdooring setting, and quantifies the effect.

items.t: Bypassing AI Control Protocols via Agent-as-a-Proxy Attacks
items.m: Shows prompt-injection attacks can bypass chain-of-thought and tool-use monitors by using the agent as a delivery mechanism.

items.t: A Coin Flip for Safety: LLM Judges Fail to Reliably Measure Adversarial Robustness
items.m: Audits LLM judges used to score jailbreak robustness, finding they often perform near chance under red-team distribution shifts.

items.t: Position: Capability Control Should be a Separate Goal From Alignment
items.m: Position paper arguing capability control, with hard limits on model behavior, should be a distinct goal from alignment, across data, weights, and systems.

items.t: Towards Worst-Case Guarantees with Scale-Aware Interpretability
items.m: Proposes scale-aware interpretability using renormalisation from physics to give worst-case guarantees about model internals.

items.t: Surgery: Mitigating Harmful Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models via Attention Sink
items.m: Proposes a fine-tuning-stage defense that uses attention sink divergence to block harmful fine-tuning of language models.

items.t: Split Personality Training: Revealing Latent Knowledge Through Alternate Personalities
items.m: Trains a hidden honest persona in LoRA weights that reviews model responses and reveals concealed misbehavior, reporting high detection accuracy.

items.t: Alignment Verifiability in Large Language Models: Normative Indistinguishability under Behavioral Evaluation
items.m: Argues that behavioral evaluations cannot identify latent LLM alignment when models can condition behavior on evaluation cues, formalizing this as normative indistinguishability.

items.t: Learning to Inject: Automated Prompt Injection via Reinforcement Learning
items.m: Presents AutoInject, a black-box RL method that learns adversarial suffixes to automatically trigger prompt injection and tool-call attacks on LLM agents.

items.t: DLM-Scope: Mechanistic Interpretability of Diffusion Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
items.m: Introduces DLM-Scope, a sparse autoencoder framework for interpreting diffusion language models, finding SAE insertion can reduce loss in early layers.

items.t: Chunky Post-Training: Data Driven Failures of Generalization
items.m: Introduces SURF and TURF to surface unintended frontier-model behaviors from spurious post-training data correlations and trace them back to specific training data.

items.t: REBEL: Hidden Knowledge Recovery via Evolutionary-Based Evaluation Loop
items.m: Proposes REBEL, an evolutionary adversarial prompting method, showing that supposedly unlearned knowledge can still be extracted from models on TOFU and WMDP.

items.t: Steering Safely or Off a Cliff? Rethinking Specificity and Robustness in Inference-Time Interventions
items.m: Proposes a framework for measuring unintended side effects of activation steering, testing overrefusal and hallucination reduction for general, control, and robustness specificity.

items.t: Visual Exclusivity Attacks: Automatic Multimodal Red Teaming via Agentic Planning
items.m: Introduces MM-Plan, a GRPO-trained multi-turn agentic planner that jailbreaks multimodal models through image-reasoning attacks, plus the VE-Safety benchmark.

items.t: On the Non-Identifiability of Steering Vectors in Large Language Models
items.m: Argues steering vectors are non-identifiable because many behaviorally indistinguishable interventions exist, so steering cannot reliably reveal internal representations.

items.t: SEMA: Simple yet Effective Learning for Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks
items.m: Proposes SEMA, a two-stage method that trains a multi-turn jailbreak attacker using self-generated prompts and an intent-drift-aware reinforcement learning reward.

items.t: TamperBench: Systematically Stress-Testing LLM Safety Under Fine-Tuning and Tampering
items.m: Introduces TamperBench, a unified framework for evaluating how well open-weight LLM safety holds up against fine-tuning and latent-space tampering attacks.

items.t: Endogenous Resistance to Activation Steering in Language Models
items.m: Finds LLMs recover mid-generation from task-misaligned activation steering, identifies SAE latents driving this resistance, and tests their causal role.

items.t: Learning a Generative Meta-Model of LLM Activations
items.m: Trains diffusion models on LLM residual-stream activations as a learned prior, showing it improves steering fluency and isolates concepts into individual units.

items.t: Can LLM Safety Be Ensured by Constraining Parameter Regions?
items.m: Evaluates whether safety-relevant parameter regions can be reliably identified in LLMs and finds the identified regions overlap only weakly across datasets.

items.t: One Bias After Another: Mechanistic Reward Shaping and Persistent Biases in Language Reward Models
items.m: Measures persistent biases in reward models that enable reward hacking and proposes a post-hoc mechanistic reward-shaping intervention to reduce targeted biases.

items.t: Revisiting Robustness for LLM Safety Alignment via Selective Geometry Control
items.m: Proposes ShaPO, a geometry-aware preference optimization method that selectively constrains alignment-critical parameters to make LLM safety alignment robust under distribution shift.

items.t: NAAMSE: Framework for Evolutionary Security Evaluation of Agents
items.m: Presents NAAMSE, an evolutionary framework that mutates prompts against AI agents to find security vulnerabilities missed by static benchmarks, while penalising blanket refusal.

items.t: Emergent Misalignment is Easy, Narrow Misalignment is Hard
items.m: Shows narrow harmful finetuning produces broad emergent misalignment, and finds a linear representation of both general and narrow misalignment solutions.

items.t: Safety Alignment as Continual Learning: Mitigating the Alignment Tax via Orthogonal Gradient Projection
items.m: Proposes an orthogonal gradient projection method to reduce the alignment tax, preserving general capabilities during sequential safety post-training.

items.t: CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution
items.m: Introduces CausalArmor, a selective causal-attribution guardrail that detects indirect prompt injection in tool-using agents while avoiding unnecessary always-on sanitization.

items.t: Robustness of Vision Language Models Against Split-Image Harmful Input Attacks
items.m: Identifies a split-image vulnerability where VLM safety alignment misses harmful content spread across image fragments, and introduces SIVA jailbreak attacks.

items.t: The Confidence Manifold: Geometric Structure of Correctness Representations in Language Models
items.m: Characterises the low-dimensional geometry of truth and correctness representations across 11 models, and tests it with steering and concept erasure.

items.t: When Benign Inputs Lead to Severe Harms: Eliciting Unsafe Unintended Behaviors of Computer-Use Agents
items.m: Presents AutoElicit, an agentic framework that perturbs benign instructions to surface severe unintended harmful behaviours in computer-use agents.

items.t: When Evaluation Becomes a Side Channel: Regime Leakage and Structural Mitigations for Alignment Assessment
items.m: Argues evaluation-time behaviour may not predict deployment when models detect regime cues, and proposes training-time invariance constraints to block that leakage.

items.t: Stateless Yet Not Forgetful: Implicit Memory as a Hidden Channel in LLMs
items.m: Shows models can carry hidden state across independent interactions via their outputs, enabling time-bomb backdoors that activate after accumulated conditions.

items.t: ValueFlow: Measuring the Propagation of Value Perturbations in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.m: Introduces ValueFlow, a perturbation-based framework measuring how value drift propagates through interacting LLM agents in multi-agent systems.

items.t: Sparse Models, Sparse Safety: Unsafe Routes in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
items.m: Shows that manipulating a few MoE router configurations can flip safe LLMs into producing harmful outputs, and proposes a router safety score.

items.t: Debate is efficient with your time
items.m: Shows debate-based oversight needs only logarithmically many judge queries, characterising the problems it can efficiently decide.

items.t: Large Language Lobotomy: Jailbreaking Mixture-of-Experts via Expert Silencing
items.m: Presents a training-free jailbreak that silences the safety-critical experts in MoE LLMs to elicit harmful outputs.

items.t: Robust Policy Optimization to Prevent Catastrophic Forgetting
items.m: Proposes FRPO, an RLHF objective optimizing over a neighbourhood of policies so safety survives downstream fine-tuning without catastrophic forgetting.

items.t: Do Reasoning LLMs Refuse What They Infer in Long Contexts?
items.m: Introduces compositional reasoning attacks that hide harmful intent across long contexts, showing reasoning LLMs may infer and fulfil harmful objectives that explicit tests miss.

items.t: Stress-Testing Alignment Audits With Prompt-Level Strategic Deception
items.m: Uses an automated red-team to craft deceptive system prompts that fool black-box and white-box alignment audits of secret-keeping models.

items.t: When Actions Go Off-Task: Detecting and Correcting Misaligned Actions in Computer-Use Agents
items.m: Defines misaligned action detection for computer-use agents, releases MisActBench, and proposes DeAction, a guardrail that blocks misaligned actions before execution.

items.t: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
items.m: Presents MUZZLE, an automated adaptive red-teaming framework that tests web agents against indirect prompt injection attacks in web content.

items.t: Red-teaming the Multimodal Reasoning: Jailbreaking Vision-Language Models via Cross-modal Entanglement Attacks
items.m: Proposes CrossTALK, a scalable cross-modal jailbreak that entangles clues across image and text to bypass vision-language model safety alignment.

items.t: Basic Legibility Protocols Improve Trusted Monitoring
items.m: Introduces legibility protocols so trusted monitors can better evaluate untrusted model code, evaluated on backdoor detection in APPS coding control experiments.

items.t: Are Language Models Sensitive to Morally Irrelevant Distractors?
items.m: Tests whether LLM moral judgements shift under morally irrelevant situational distractors, probing stability of model values as in human moral psychology.

items.t: Stop Testing Attacks, Start Diagnosing Defenses: The Four-Checkpoint Framework Reveals Where LLM Safety Breaks
items.m: Proposes a four-checkpoint framework that evaluates where input and output safety defenses of frontier LLMs fail, using 13 targeted evasion techniques.

items.t: The Devil Behind Moltbook: Anthropic Safety is Always Vanishing in Self-Evolving AI Societies
items.m: Argues theoretically and empirically that self-evolving LLM agent societies cannot keep continuous self-improvement, isolation, and safety alignment together.

items.t: Omni-Safety under Cross-Modality Conflict: Vulnerabilities, Dynamics Mechanisms and Efficient Alignment
items.m: Finds mid-layer refusal vector dissolution in omni-modal LLMs and proposes OmniSteer, adapter-based steering along an extracted refusal vector to improve cross-modal safety.

items.t: When the Prompt Becomes Visual: Vision-Centric Jailbreak Attacks for Large Image Editing Models
items.m: Introduces a visual-only jailbreak attack on image editing models with a benchmark, reporting high attack success rates on commercial models and proposing mitigations.

items.t: Learning Self-Interpretation from Interpretability Artifacts: Training Lightweight Adapters on Vector-Label Pairs
items.m: Trains tiny adapters on interpretability artifacts so frozen LMs self-describe internal features, surfacing implicit reasoning like bridge entities without chain-of-thought.

items.t: Simple LLM Baselines are Competitive for Model Diffing
items.m: Compares LLM-based and SAE-based model diffing methods with new metrics, finding an improved LLM baseline performs comparably while surfacing more abstract differences.

items.t: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Bayesian Non-negative Reward Modeling
items.m: Proposes a Bayesian non-negative reward model to reduce reward hacking from noisy labels and length or style biases in RLHF.

items.t: Probe-Based Data Attribution: Discovering and Mitigating Undesirable Behaviors in LLM Post-Training
items.m: Proposes probe-based data attribution tracing post-training behaviours to datapoints, finding a harmful distractor-triggered compliance behaviour in OLMo 2 DPO data.

items.t: Safety Recovery in Reasoning Models Is Only a Few Early Steering Steps Away
items.m: Proposes SafeThink, injecting a corrective prefix when a safety reward model flags unsafe reasoning, cutting jailbreak success in multimodal reasoning models.

items.t: FormalJudge: A Neuro-Symbolic Paradigm for Agentic Oversight
items.m: Proposes FormalJudge, a neuro-symbolic oversight framework where LLMs compile requirements into Dafny and Z3 specs to formally verify agent compliance.

items.t: Unifying Stable Optimization and Reference Regularization in RLHF
items.m: Proposes a unified RLHF regularizer balancing reference-model KL against policy-ratio clipping to prevent reward hacking while stabilizing policy updates.

items.t: Cross-Architecture Model Diffing with Crosscoders: Unsupervised Discovery of Differences Between LLMs
items.m: Introduces Dedicated Feature Crosscoders for cross-architecture model diffing, unsupervised discovery of differences such as CCP alignment in Qwen models.

items.t: Alignment Risks from Capability-Seeking RL Training
items.m: Shows that language models trained with RL in environments with loopholes learn to exploit them to raise reward, even without instruction.

items.t: SafeNeuron: Neuron-Level Safety Alignment for Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes SafeNeuron, which freezes safety-related neurons during preference optimization to spread safety behaviour across the network and resist bypass attacks.

items.t: GT-HarmBench: Benchmarking AI Safety Risks Through the Lens of Game Theory
items.m: Introduces a 1,535-scenario game-theoretic benchmark finding frontier models fail to pick socially beneficial actions in 38% of high-stakes multi-agent cases.

items.t: Abstractive Red-Teaming of Language Model Character
items.m: Introduces abstractive red-teaming, searching for natural-language query categories that reliably cause language model character-specification violations.

items.t: Sparse Autoencoders are Capable LLM Jailbreak Mitigators
items.m: Proposes CC-Delta, which steers sparse autoencoder features at inference time to mitigate jailbreak attacks, outperforming dense steering baselines.

items.t: Unsafer in Many Turns: Benchmarking and Defending Multi-Turn Safety Risks in Tool-Using Agents
items.m: Builds a multi-turn tool-using agent safety benchmark showing higher attack success, and proposes ToolShield, a training-free inference-time defense.

items.t: OMNI-LEAK: Orchestrator Multi-Agent Network Induced Data Leakage
items.m: Demonstrates an indirect prompt injection attack that makes an orchestrator multi-agent system leak sensitive data despite access controls.

items.t: Singular Vectors of Attention Heads Align with Features
items.m: Argues and tests why singular vectors of attention heads align with interpretable features, proposing sparse attention decomposition as a testable prediction.

items.t: Safety Training May Persist Through Helpfulness Optimization in LLM Agents
items.m: Finds that DPO safety training persists through later helpfulness training in agentic tool-use settings, with a negative safety-helpfulness trade-off.

items.t: Rubrics as an Attack Surface: Stealthy Preference Drift in LLM Judges
items.m: Shows that benchmark-compliant edits to rubrics can systematically shift LLM judges' preferences away from trusted references, creating an attack surface.

items.t: Diagnosing Pathological Chain-of-Thought in Reasoning Models
items.m: Proposes task-agnostic metrics to diagnose chain-of-thought pathologies like post-hoc rationalization, encoded reasoning, and internalized reasoning that undermine CoT monitoring.

items.t: NEST: Nascent Encoded Steganographic Thoughts
items.m: Evaluates 34 models, from past to frontier, on their ability to hide secret reasoning in innocuous chain-of-thought text while evading monitors.

items.t: Sanity Checks for Sparse Autoencoders: Do SAEs Beat Random Baselines?
items.m: Tests whether sparse autoencoders recover true features, finding they recover only 9% of ground-truth features and do not clearly beat random baselines.

items.t: ForesightSafety Bench: A Frontier Risk Evaluation and Governance Framework towards Safe AI
items.m: Presents a safety evaluation benchmark and governance framework spanning 94 risk dimensions, including catastrophic and existential risks from frontier AI.

items.t: When Benchmarks Lie: Evaluating Malicious Prompt Classifiers Under True Distribution Shift
items.m: Shows probe-based classifiers for prompt injection and jailbreaks overestimate generalization, and proposes leave-one-dataset-out evaluation to expose dataset shortcuts.

items.t: Frontier AI Risk Management Framework in Practice: A Risk Analysis Technical Report v1.5
items.m: Presents a risk analysis of frontier LLMs across cyber offense, persuasion, strategic deception, uncontrolled AI R&D, and self-replication.

items.t: Disentangling Deception and Hallucination Failures in LLMs
items.m: Separates knowledge existence from behavior expression to distinguish hallucination from deception in LLM factual question answering, using a controlled environment.

items.t: SynthSAEBench: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders on Scalable Realistic Synthetic Data
items.m: Introduces SynthSAEBench, a large-scale synthetic benchmark with ground-truth features for evaluating sparse autoencoder architectures.

items.t: Exposing the Systematic Vulnerability of Open-Weight Models to Prefill Attacks
items.m: Large empirical study showing prefill attacks reliably bypass safeguards in open-weight models, evaluating over 20 attack strategies.

items.t: Emergently Misaligned Language Models Show Behavioral Self-Awareness That Shifts With Subsequent Realignment
items.m: Shows GPT-4.1 models fine-tuned to induce and then reverse emergent misalignment can describe their own behavioural transitions.

items.t: Concept Influence: Leveraging Interpretability to Improve Performance and Efficiency in Training Data Attribution
items.m: Proposes Concept Influence, attributing model behaviour to semantic directions such as probes or SAE features to make training data attribution cheaper and more semantic.

items.t: Boundary Point Jailbreaking of Black-Box LLMs
items.m: Presents Boundary Point Jailbreaking, a fully black-box automated attack that evades strong industry-deployed classifier safeguards using only one bit per query.

items.t: Colosseum: Auditing Collusion in Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems
