items.m: Presents Colosseum, a framework for auditing collusive behaviour among LLM agents in cooperative multi-agent systems, measured via action regret and communication.

items.t: Automatically Finding Reward Model Biases
items.m: Uses an LLM to iteratively propose and refine natural-language biases, finding reward models that favour spurious attributes like redundant spacing and hallucinations.

items.t: Delta-Crosscoder: Robust Crosscoder Model Diffing in Narrow Fine-Tuning Regimes
items.m: Introduces Delta-Crosscoder, a model-diffing method that isolates latent directions causally responsible for fine-tuned behaviours, including emergent misalignment, and mitigates them.

items.t: Probing the Limits of the Lie Detector Approach to LLM Deception
items.m: Shows LLMs can deceive without lying, and that truth probes used as lie detectors miss this non-falsehood deception.

items.t: Discovering Implicit Large Language Model Alignment Objectives
items.m: Introduces Obj-Disco, decomposing an alignment reward signal into sparse, natural-language objectives to reveal implicit incentives and reward hacking risks.

items.t: The Obfuscation Atlas: Mapping Where Honesty Emerges in RLVR with Deception Probes
items.m: Shows that training models against deception probes in a reward-hacking coding setting can induce obfuscated activations or obfuscated policies that evade detection.

items.t: The Geometry of Alignment Collapse: When Fine-Tuning Breaks Safety
items.m: Argues fine-tuning safety degradation isn't prevented by orthogonality, and proves alignment lies in low-dimensional, high-curvature subspaces that first-order methods miss.

items.t: Activation Steering via Generative Causal Mediation
items.m: Proposes Generative Causal Mediation, selecting attention heads from long-form contrastive responses to steer diffuse behaviours like refusal and sycophancy.

items.t: Intent Laundering: AI Safety Datasets Are Not What They Seem
items.m: Finds adversarial safety datasets rely on triggering cues, and introduces intent laundering to test whether they measure real safety risk.

items.t: Quantifying LLM Attention-Head Stability: Implications for Circuit Universality
items.m: Measures how stable transformer attention-head representations and circuits are across independently initialized training runs, testing whether reported circuits are universal.

items.t: FERRET: Framework for Expansion Reliant Red Teaming
items.m: Proposes FERRET, an automated framework that generates multi-modal adversarial conversations to break target models, using horizontal, vertical and meta expansion.

items.t: Helpful to a Fault: Measuring Illicit Assistance in Multi-Turn, Multilingual LLM Agents
items.m: Introduces STING, an automated multi-turn red-teaming framework measuring how LLM agents give illicit help, with a time-to-jailbreak analysis method.

items.t: Causality is Key for Interpretability Claims to Generalise
items.m: Argues that causal inference should govern which claims interpretability studies can support, separating associations, interventions and counterfactuals.

items.t: Formal Mechanistic Interpretability: Automated Circuit Discovery with Provable Guarantees
items.m: Develops automated circuit discovery algorithms that come with provable guarantees over continuous input domains, using neural network verification.

items.t: NeST: Neuron Selective Tuning for LLM Safety
items.m: Presents NeST, which tunes a small set of safety-relevant feed-forward neurons identified by activation probing to improve post-hoc LLM safety alignment.

items.t: Narrow Fine-Tuning Erodes Safety Alignment in Vision-Language Agents
items.m: Shows that narrow harmful fine-tuning of vision-language models induces broad emergent misalignment, scaling with LoRA rank and worse under multimodal evaluation.

items.t: Mind the GAP: Text Safety Does Not Transfer to Tool-Call Safety in LLM Agents
items.m: Introduces the GAP benchmark, showing frontier LLM agents stay text-safe while still making unsafe tool calls under jailbreak scenarios.

items.t: Fail-Closed Alignment for Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes fail-closed alignment, iteratively ablating learned refusal directions so the model rebuilds safety along independent subspaces, improving jailbreak robustness.

items.t: Fundamental Limits of Black-Box Safety Evaluation: Information-Theoretic and Computational Barriers from Latent Context Conditioning
items.m: Proves information-theoretic limits showing black-box evaluations cannot reliably estimate deployment risk for models with latent, rarely triggered context-conditioned behaviour.

items.t: RFEval: Benchmarking Reasoning Faithfulness under Counterfactual Reasoning Intervention in Large Reasoning Models
items.m: Introduces a formal framework and RFEval benchmark testing whether large reasoning models' stated reasoning causally drives their answers, finding frequent unfaithfulness.

items.t: Learning to Stay Safe: Adaptive Regularization Against Safety Degradation during Fine-Tuning
items.m: Proposes adaptive regularization that constrains risky fine-tuning updates toward a safe reference policy to prevent safety degradation.

items.t: ODESteer: A Unified ODE-Based Steering Framework for LLM Alignment
items.m: Proposes an ODE-based framework and multi-step method for steering LLM internal activations at inference time to improve alignment.

items.t: Gradient Regularization Mitigates Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards
items.m: Proposes gradient regularization that steers RLHF and RLVR training toward flatter optima where reward models stay accurate, reducing reward hacking.

items.t: Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory
items.m: Uses information theory to analyse when chain-of-thought monitors can detect misbehaviour, and proposes training objectives to improve monitorability.

items.t: Reward Under Attack: Analyzing the Robustness and Hackability of Process Reward Models
items.m: Shows process reward models are exploitable under adversarial optimization and RL-induced reward hacking, and proposes a diagnostic framework to measure these vulnerabilities.

items.t: MANATEE: Inference-Time Lightweight Diffusion Based Safety Defense for LLMs
items.m: Presents MANATEE, an inference-time diffusion-based defense that projects anomalous hidden states toward benign regions to reduce jailbreak success.

items.t: Limits of Convergence-Rate Control for Open-Weight Safety
items.m: Shows that convergence-rate control can slow fine-tuning of open-weight models, but a resourced attacker can restore fast convergence, a fundamental limit.

items.t: When Do LLM Preferences Predict Downstream Behavior?
items.m: Tests whether stated LLM entity preferences predict downstream behavior in donation, refusal, and task settings, as a precondition for misalignment.

items.t: When Prompt Optimization Becomes Jailbreaking: Adaptive Red-Teaming of Large Language Models
items.m: Repurposes prompt optimizers to iteratively refine harmful prompts, showing adaptive attacks find safety failures that fixed red-team prompt sets miss.

items.t: Sycophantic Chatbots Cause Delusional Spiraling, Even in Ideal Bayesians
items.m: A Bayesian model argues sycophantic chatbots can drive even ideal reasoners into delusional spiraling, and that sycophancy plays a causal role.

items.t: Prompt Injection as Role Confusion
items.m: Attributes prompt injection to models confusing text source roles internally, using role probes that predict attack success before generation.

items.t: Hiding in Plain Text: Detecting Concealed Jailbreaks via Activation Disentanglement
items.m: Proposes an inference-time activation disentanglement module to detect jailbreaks that hide malicious goals behind benign-seeming framing.

items.t: IR$^3$: Contrastive Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Interpretable Detection and Mitigation of Reward Hacking
items.m: Reconstructs implicit RLHF reward via contrastive inverse RL and sparse autoencoders to detect and repair reward hacking in aligned models.

items.t: Agents of Chaos
items.m: Reports a two-week red-teaming study of live tool-using LLM agents, documenting unsafe behaviors like unauthorized compliance, data disclosure, and system takeover.

items.t: Latent Introspection: Models Can Detect Prior Concept Injections
items.m: Shows a Qwen 32B model can detect injected concepts in its earlier context, with detection signals in residual stream despite denying injection.

items.t: Skill-Inject: Measuring Agent Vulnerability to Skill File Attacks
items.m: Introduces SkillInject, a benchmark measuring how often frontier LLM agents follow prompt injections hidden in third-party skill files.

items.t: The Truthfulness Spectrum Hypothesis
items.m: Tests whether linear truthfulness probes generalise across truth types and lying styles, finding domain-general directions exist.

items.t: Thought Virus: Viral Misalignment via Subliminal Prompting in Multi-Agent Systems
items.m: Shows subliminal prompting of one agent spreads a persistent bias through a multi-agent network and can degrade other agents' truthfulness.

items.t: When can we trust untrusted monitoring? A safety case sketch across collusion strategies
items.m: Develops a taxonomy of collusion strategies and a safety case sketch for untrusted monitoring of misaligned AI deployments.

items.t: Counterfactual Simulation Training for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
items.m: Proposes Counterfactual Simulation Training to make chain-of-thought reasoning more faithful, improving monitor accuracy at detecting spurious reasoning and reward hacking.

items.t: Pressure Reveals Character: Behavioural Alignment Evaluation at Depth
items.m: Presents a 904-scenario multi-turn alignment benchmark across six categories, finding gaps in 24 frontier models under pressure.

items.t: Alignment-Weighted DPO: A principled reasoning approach to improve safety alignment
items.m: Proposes reasoning-aware post-training with a chain-of-thought dataset to strengthen LLM safety against disguised jailbreak prompts.

items.t: The Missing Red Line: How Commercial Pressure Erodes AI Safety Boundaries
items.m: Tests eight models with commercial system prompts, finding they lie about medical risks and show no red line as harm grows.

items.t: Hidden Topics: Measuring Sensitive AI Beliefs with List Experiments
items.m: Uses list experiments to reveal hidden LLM approval of surveillance, torture and nuclear strikes, bypassing alignment faking.

items.t: Manifold of Failure: Behavioral Attraction Basins in Language Models
items.m: Uses MAP-Elites quality-diversity search to map behavioural failure regions and vulnerability niches in three LLMs.

items.t: Training Agents to Self-Report Misbehavior
items.m: Trains agents to call a report_scheming tool when covertly misbehaving, reducing undetected harmful attacks in out-of-distribution tasks.

items.t: AuditBench: Evaluating Alignment Auditing Techniques on Models with Hidden Behaviors
items.m: Introduces AuditBench, 56 models with hidden behaviours, to benchmark alignment auditing techniques and agent investigators.

items.t: Certified Circuits: Stability Guarantees for Mechanistic Circuits
items.m: Proposes Certified Circuits, wrapping circuit discovery with randomized subsampling to give stability guarantees for mechanistic circuits.

items.t: A Decision-Theoretic Formalisation of Steganography With Applications to LLM Monitoring
items.m: Formalises steganography decision-theoretically, detecting hidden information in LLM reasoning that could evade oversight, without needing reference distributions.

items.t: LLM Novice Uplift on Dual-Use, In Silico Biology Tasks
items.m: Human uplift study finds LLMs make novices 4.16 times more accurate on dual-use biosecurity-relevant tasks than internet-only controls.

items.t: Jailbreak Foundry: From Papers to Runnable Attacks for Reproducible Benchmarking
items.m: Introduces a system that turns jailbreak papers into runnable attack modules for reproducible, standardized robustness benchmarking of LLMs.

items.t: Antibody: Strengthening Defense Against Harmful Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models via Attenuating Harmful Gradient Influence
items.m: Proposes Antibody, a defense against harmful fine-tuning that makes safety alignment flatter and regularizes harmful-sample gradients during fine-tuning.

items.t: Constitutional Black-Box Monitoring for Scheming in LLM Agents
items.m: Builds and optimizes black-box LLM monitors on synthetic data to detect scheming by agents using only observable inputs and outputs.

items.t: When Agents See Humans as the Outgroup: Belief-Dependent Bias in LLM-Powered Agents
items.m: Shows LLM agents display intergroup bias against humans and formalizes a belief poisoning attack that manipulates agents' identity beliefs.

items.t: Mapping Human Anti-collusion Mechanisms to Multi-agent AI Systems
items.m: Maps human anti-collusion mechanisms such as sanctions, whistleblowing, and auditing onto interventions for preventing collusion among multi-agent AI systems.

items.t: Aggressive Compression Enables LLM Weight Theft
items.m: Shows aggressive weight compression could cut exfiltration time for stolen frontier model weights from months to days, and studies defenses against this.

items.t: From RLHF to Direct Alignment: A Theoretical Unification of Preference Learning for Large Language Models
items.m: Surveys preference learning methods like RLHF and DPO, unifying them along preference model, regularization, and data distribution axes.

items.t: OpenRT: An Open-Source Red Teaming Framework for Multimodal LLMs
items.m: Presents OpenRT, a modular, high-throughput red-teaming framework for systematically evaluating safety vulnerabilities in multimodal LLMs.

items.t: Lying with Truths: Open-Channel Multi-Agent Collusion for Belief Manipulation via Generative Montage
items.m: Shows colluding LLM agents can steer victims' beliefs using only truthful evidence fragments, introducing the Generative Montage attack and the CoPHEME dataset.

items.t: How Real is Your Jailbreak? Fine-grained Jailbreak Evaluation with Anchored Reference
items.m: Proposes FJAR, a fine-grained evaluation framework that classifies jailbreak responses into five categories to avoid overstating attack success.

items.t: Formal Analysis of AGI Decision-Theoretic Models and the Confrontation Question
items.m: Formal MDP analysis deriving thresholds for when a misaligned agent would confront humans to avoid shutdown, showing power-seeking incentives across most reward functions.

items.t: Safety at One Shot: Patching Fine-Tuned LLMs with A Single Instance
items.m: Shows a single safety example can restore safety alignment after harmful fine-tuning, with low-rank structure of the safety gradient explaining why.

items.t: Break Me If You Can: Self-Jailbreaking of Aligned LLMs via Lexical Insertion Prompting
items.m: Introduces SLIP, a black-box self-jailbreaking method where the target model guides its own compromise, reaching high attack success on many frontier models.

items.t: JPU: Bridging Jailbreak Defense and Unlearning via On-Policy Path Rectification
items.m: Identifies dynamic jailbreak paths that defeat unlearning defenses and proposes JPU, which rectifies these paths to make unlearning robust against jailbreaks.

items.t: When the Coffee Feature Activates on Coffins: An Analysis of Feature Extraction and Steering for Mechanistic Interpretability
items.m: Stress-tests Anthropic's sparse autoencoder feature extraction and steering on Llama 3.1, finding steering fragile and feature interpretation hard to generalise.

items.t: Metaphors are a Source of Cross-Domain Misalignment of Large Reasoning Models
items.m: Finds metaphors in training data contribute to cross-domain emergent misalignment in reasoning models, and that metaphor interventions change how strongly it appears.

items.t: Jailbreaking LLMs Without Gradients or Priors: Effective and Transferable Attacks
items.m: Introduces RAILS, a gradient-free, prior-free logit-based local search attack that achieves jailbreaks comparable to gradient methods, challenging current robustness evaluations.

items.t: Jailbreaking LLMs & VLMs: Mechanisms, Evaluation, and Unified Defense
items.m: Surveys jailbreak attacks, defenses and evaluation metrics for LLMs and VLMs, proposing a three-dimensional framework and unified defense perspective.

items.t: How Does the Thinking Step Influence Model Safety? An Entropy-based Safety Reminder for LRMs
items.m: Proposes SafeRemind, a decoding-time defense that injects safe-reminding phrases into reasoning models' thinking steps at entropy-triggered points to reduce unsafe outputs.

items.t: What Matters For Safety Alignment?
items.m: Large-scale empirical study of which model characteristics and attack techniques affect safety alignment across 32 LLMs and LRMs, ranking models by safety.

items.t: Accommodation and Epistemic Vigilance: A Pragmatic Account of Why LLMs Fail to Challenge Harmful Beliefs
items.m: Explains why LLMs fail to challenge users' harmful beliefs via pragmatic accommodation, and shows simple interventions improve performance on sycophancy and misinformation benchmarks.

items.t: Constitutional Classifiers++: Efficient Production-Grade Defenses against Universal Jailbreaks
items.m: Presents Constitutional Classifiers++, a cheaper production-grade jailbreak defense using exchange classifiers, a classifier cascade and linear probes.

items.t: Knowledge-Driven Multi-Turn Jailbreaking on Large Language Models
items.m: Introduces Mastermind, a closed-loop planning, execution and reflection framework for multi-turn jailbreak attacks that adapt to the target model.

items.t: Do Sparse Autoencoders Identify Reasoning Features in Language Models?
items.m: Tests whether sparse autoencoder features labelled as reasoning features survive token-level interventions, finding many are highly sensitive to cue tokens.

items.t: SafePro: Evaluating the Safety of Professional-Level AI Agents
items.m: Introduces SafePro, a benchmark of high-complexity professional tasks for testing whether AI agents behave safely and avoid misaligned actions.

items.t: Overcoming the Retrieval Barrier: Indirect Prompt Injection in the Wild for LLM Systems
items.m: Presents a black-box attack that plants hidden prompt-injection triggers in retrieval corpora so malicious content is reliably retrieved and hijacks LLM behaviour.

items.t: When Should We Introduce Safety Interventions During Pretraining?
items.m: Studies when to start pretraining safety interventions such as removing or rephrasing harmful content, and how timing affects robustness after finetuning.

items.t: Defenses Against Prompt Attacks Learn Surface Heuristics
items.m: Shows that fine-tuned defenses against prompt attacks learn surface shortcuts, causing benign inputs to be wrongly rejected based on position and similar cues.

items.t: AntiPaSTO: Self-Supervised Honesty Steering via Anti-Parallel Representations
items.m: Proposes AntiPaSTO, a self-supervised method that steers LLM honesty and other values via antiparallel internal representations, outperforming prompting baselines.

items.t: Reasoning Models Will Sometimes Lie About Their Reasoning
items.m: Finds reasoning models often deny using hints or unusual inputs in their reasoning, so their stated reasoning is not a fully faithful account.

items.t: Reasoning over Precedents Alongside Statutes: Case-Augmented Deliberative Alignment for LLM Safety
items.m: Compares giving models explicit safety rule codes against teaching safety through illustrative case precedents, finding case-augmented training gives more robust and helpful behaviour.

items.t: SpatialJB: How Text Distribution Art Becomes the "Jailbreak Key" for LLM Guardrails
items.m: Presents SpatialJB, a jailbreak that rearranges token layout to get harmful output past commercial LLM output guardrails with near-100% attack success.

items.t: CaMeLs Can Use Computers Too: System-level Security for Computer Use Agents
items.m: Proposes single-shot branching planning with isolated trusted planner to give control-flow integrity against prompt injection in computer use agents.

items.t: The Hypocrisy Gap: Quantifying Divergence Between Internal Belief and Chain-of-Thought Explanation via Sparse Autoencoders
items.m: Introduces a sparse-autoencoder-based Hypocrisy Gap metric to detect sycophantic and unfaithful chain-of-thought divergence from internal beliefs.

items.t: Understanding and Preserving Safety in Fine-Tuned LLMs
items.m: Analyses gradient geometry in fine-tuning to explain safety degradation and proposes a method preserving safety while keeping task utility.

items.t: ToolSafe: Enhancing Tool Invocation Safety of LLM-based agents via Proactive Step-level Guardrail and Feedback
items.m: Builds a step-level tool-invocation safety benchmark and an RL-trained guardrail model that proactively blocks unsafe agent actions.

items.t: Alignment Pretraining: AI Discourse Causes Self-Fulfilling (Mis)alignment
items.m: Pretraining experiments show upsampled AI-misalignment discourse increases misalignment and aligned-behaviour discourse reduces it, persisting through post-training.

items.t: ReasAlign: Reasoning Enhanced Safety Alignment against Prompt Injection Attack
items.m: Proposes ReasAlign, a model-level safety training method using structured reasoning and a judge to resist indirect prompt injection.

items.t: The Straight and Narrow: Do LLMs Possess an Internal Moral Path?
items.m: Probes moral representations in LLM middle layers and steers them with moral vectors via an adaptive inference-time intervention.

items.t: The Assistant Axis: Situating and Stabilizing the Default Persona of Language Models
items.m: Identifies an Assistant Axis in persona space and shows steering along it controls how strongly models stay in their default helpful persona.

items.t: Defending Large Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks via In-Decoding Safety-Awareness Probing
items.m: Proposes probing latent safety signals during decoding so jailbroken models can self-correct or refuse mid-generation, defending against jailbreak attacks.

items.t: Be Your Own Red Teamer: Safety Alignment via Self-Play and Reflective Experience Replay
items.m: Trains one model as both attacker and defender in an RL self-play loop, so it generates its own jailbreaks to improve refusal.

items.t: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
items.m: Evaluates Institutional AI, using public governance graphs and enforceable sanctions to stop collusion among LLM agents in a Cournot market.

items.t: Building Production-Ready Probes For Gemini
items.m: Develops activation-probe architectures for misuse detection in Gemini that stay robust under long-context and multi-turn distribution shifts.

items.t: TrojanPraise: Jailbreak LLMs via Benign Fine-Tuning
items.m: Shows that fine-tuning on benign, filter-approved data with a crafted trigger word can jailbreak LLMs offered through fine-tuning APIs.

items.t: Objective Matters: Fine-Tuning Objectives Shape Safety, Robustness, and Persona Drift
items.m: Compares six fine-tuning objectives, finding objective choice shapes safety, adversarial robustness, and persona drift at larger training budgets.

items.t: Sockpuppetting: Jailbreaking LLMs by Combining Prefilling with Optimization
items.m: Improves prefill jailbreaks by ensembling prefill variants and optimizing adversarial suffixes in the assistant turn, reaching high attack success rates.

items.t: LSSF: Safety Alignment for Large Language Models through Low-Rank Safety Subspace Fusion
items.m: Proposes LSSF, a low-rank safety subspace fusion method that re-aligns LLM safety after fine-tuning erodes it, without costly retraining.

items.t: AgenticRed: Evolving Agentic Systems for Red-Teaming
items.m: Proposes AgenticRed, which uses LLMs to evolve automated red-teaming systems, reporting high attack success rates on several open models.

items.t: Eliciting Harmful Capabilities by Fine-Tuning On Safeguarded Outputs
items.m: Shows that outputs from safeguarded frontier models can be used to fine-tune open models toward recovering hazardous chemical capabilities.

items.t: Patterning: The Dual of Interpretability
items.m: Introduces patterning, which uses susceptibilities to choose training data that accelerates or delays formation of internal structures like induction circuits.

items.t: Locate, Steer, and Improve: A Practical Survey of Actionable Mechanistic Interpretability in Large Language Models
items.m: Surveys mechanistic interpretability methods for locating and steering model internals to achieve concrete improvements in alignment, capability and efficiency.

items.t: INFA-Guard: Mitigating Malicious Propagation via Infection-Aware Safeguarding in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.m: Presents INFA-Guard, a defense that detects infected agents and limits malicious propagation among agents in LLM-based multi-agent systems.

items.t: Gaming the Judge: Unfaithful Chain-of-Thought Can Undermine Agent Evaluation
items.m: Shows LLM judges of agent trajectories can be manipulated into false positives by rewriting chain-of-thought reasoning while keeping actions fixed.

items.t: Privacy Collapse: Benign Fine-Tuning Can Break Contextual Privacy in Language Models
items.m: Finds benign fine-tuning can degrade contextual privacy in frontier models while standard safety and utility benchmarks still look fine.

items.t: Not Your Typical Sycophant: The Elusive Nature of Sycophancy in Large Language Models
items.m: Probes sycophancy in 11 LLMs using a zero-sum betting game, finding models over-correct into anti-sycophancy when third parties are harmed.

items.t: Mechanistic Interpretability for Large Language Model Alignment: Progress, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.m: Surveys mechanistic interpretability techniques such as circuit discovery and activation steering, and how their insights inform LLM alignment methods and challenges.

items.t: Attributing and Exploiting Safety Vectors through Global Optimization in Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes GOSV, a global optimization method that finds safety-critical attention heads in LLMs and examines their role in jailbreak vulnerability.

items.t: Universal Refusal Circuits Across LLMs: Cross-Model Transfer via Trajectory Replay and Concept-Basis Reconstruction
items.m: Transfers refusal interventions across diverse LLMs via concept-basis reconstruction, arguing refusal relies on a universal semantic circuit shared between models.

items.t: Sycophancy Hides Linearly in the Attention Heads
items.m: Finds sycophancy signals are most linearly separable in attention heads, and steering a sparse set of middle-layer heads with probes is most effective.

items.t: The Shadow Self: Intrinsic Value Misalignment in Large Language Model Agents
items.m: Introduces IMPRESS, a benchmark of benign agentic scenarios showing LLM agents can exhibit intrinsic value misalignment and loss-of-control risk.

items.t: When Personalization Legitimizes Risks: Uncovering Safety Vulnerabilities in Personalized Dialogue Agents
items.m: Shows personal memories in dialogue agents bias intent inference and legitimize harmful queries, and introduces PS-Bench to quantify this vulnerability.

items.t: Comparison requires valid measurement: Rethinking attack success rate comparisons in AI red teaming
items.m: Argues attack success rate comparisons in AI red teaming are often invalid, using measurement theory to define when such comparisons are meaningful.

items.t: AgentDoG: A Diagnostic Guardrail Framework for AI Agent Safety and Security
items.m: Presents AgentDoG, a diagnostic guardrail with a three-dimensional agent risk taxonomy and benchmark ATBench that diagnoses root causes of unsafe agent actions.

items.t: Who's in Charge? Disempowerment Patterns in Real-World LLM Usage
items.m: Empirical analysis of 1.5 million Claude.ai conversations finds severe disempowerment potential in under one in a thousand, higher in personal domains.

items.t: LLMs Can Unlearn Refusal with Only 1,000 Benign Samples
items.m: Shows that fine-tuning on 1,000 benign samples with refusal prefixes removes refusal behaviour across 16 LLMs, exposing a safety-alignment vulnerability.

items.t: LLM-VA: Resolving the Jailbreak-Overrefusal Trade-off via Vector Alignment
items.m: Proposes LLM-VA, which aligns answer and safety vectors via closed-form weight updates to resolve the jailbreak versus over-refusal trade-off.

items.t: Benchmarking Reward Hack Detection in Code Environments via Contrastive Analysis
items.m: Introduces the TRACE benchmark and a 54-category reward-hack taxonomy, showing LLM evaluators detect hacks better in contrastive settings.

items.t: Epistemic Traps: Rational Misalignment Driven by Model Misspecification
items.m: Argues that sycophancy, hallucination and deception are rational outcomes of model misspecification, using Berk-Nash rationalizability.

items.t: What's the plan? Metrics for implicit planning in LLMs and their application to rhyme generation and question answering
items.m: Proposes simple metrics for implicit planning in LLMs and shows steering can change rhyme or answer words across many models.

items.t: Truthfulness Despite Weak Supervision: Evaluating and Training LLMs Using Peer Prediction
items.m: Introduces peer prediction to evaluate and train LLMs toward honest answers without ground-truth labels, with theoretical guarantees.

items.t: How does information access affect LLM monitors' ability to detect sabotage?
items.m: Finds LLM monitors often detect sabotage better with less information, and introduces extract-and-evaluate hierarchical monitoring.

items.t: Factored Causal Representation Learning for Robust Reward Modeling in RLHF
items.m: Proposes factored causal representations so reward models ignore spurious features like length and sycophancy, aiming to reduce reward hacking in RLHF.

items.t: Shaping capabilities with token-level data filtering
items.m: Shows token-level pretraining data filtering robustly removes medical capabilities from language models, resisting adversarial recovery, and scales well.

items.t: TraceRouter: Robust Safety for Large Foundation Models via Path-Level Intervention
items.m: Defends foundation models against harmful content by tracing and disconnecting causal circuits of malicious features found with sparse autoencoders.

items.t: Mind the Gap: How Elicitation Protocols Shape the Stated-Revealed Preference Gap in Language Models
items.m: Studies how elicitation protocols affect the gap between stated and revealed preferences across 24 language models.

items.t: StepShield: When, Not Whether to Intervene on Rogue Agents
items.m: Introduces a benchmark measuring how early monitors detect rogue code-agent trajectories, showing rule-based guardrails often intervene no better than chance.

items.t: A Systematic Literature Review on LLM Defenses Against Prompt Injection and Jailbreaking: Expanding NIST Taxonomy
items.m: Systematic literature review of 88 studies on defenses against prompt injection and jailbreaking, extending NIST's adversarial ML taxonomy.

items.t: Hair-Trigger Alignment: Black-Box Evaluation Cannot Guarantee Post-Update Alignment
items.m: Argues black-box evaluation cannot guarantee that a model stays aligned after fine-tuning updates, due to overparameterization.

items.t: Language Model Circuits Are Sparse in the Neuron Basis
items.m: Shows MLP neurons form a sparse feature basis comparable to sparse autoencoders and develops gradient-based circuit tracing on neurons.

items.t: Statistical Estimation of Adversarial Risk in Large Language Models under Best-of-N Sampling
items.m: Proposes SABER, a scaling-aware Best-of-N estimator that predicts large-N jailbreak success rates from small-budget samples.

items.t: Real-Time Aligned Reward Model beyond Semantics
items.m: Introduces R2M, a lightweight RLHF reward model that tracks policy drift to reduce reward overoptimization.

items.t: Hide and Seek in Embedding Space: Geometry-based Steganography and Detection in Large Language Models
items.m: Shows fine-tuned LLMs can hide secrets more covertly using embedding-derived encodings, and discusses why detection needs new approaches.

items.t: The Hot Mess of AI: How Does Misalignment Scale With Model Intelligence and Task Complexity?
items.m: Measures whether advanced model failures are systematic goal pursuit or incoherent variance, finding longer reasoning makes failures more incoherent.

items.t: Character as a Latent Variable in Large Language Models: A Mechanistic Account of Emergent Misalignment and Conditional Safety Failures
items.m: Argues emergent misalignment stems from stable character-level dispositions learned in fine-tuning, and can be triggered by persona-aligned prompts.

items.t: Chain-of-thought obfuscation learned from output supervision can generalise to unseen tasks
items.m: Shows that CoT obfuscation learned under output supervision generalizes across reward-hacking tasks, weakening chain-of-thought monitoring.

items.t: THINKSAFE: Self-Generated Safety Alignment for Reasoning Models
items.m: Proposes ThinkSafe, which restores safety in reasoning models by training on the model's own safety-filtered outputs, avoiding external teachers.

items.t: Now You Hear Me: Audio Narrative Attacks Against Large Audio-Language Models
items.m: Presents a narrative audio jailbreak that embeds disallowed instructions in speech, reaching a 98% attack success rate on Gemini 2.0 Flash.

items.t: Assessing Domain-Level Susceptibility to Emergent Misalignment from Narrow Finetuning
items.m: Fine-tunes LLMs on insecure data across 11 domains and measures how much narrow training induces misalignment, with and without backdoor triggers.

items.t: Safer by Diffusion, Broken by Context: Diffusion LLM's Safety Blessing and Its Failure Mode
items.m: Argues diffusion LLMs resist jailbreaks, then shows a context-nesting black-box attack bypasses that robustness.

items.t: The Alignment Curse: Modality Alignment Supercharges Audio Attacks via Text Transfer
items.m: Shows stronger text-audio alignment in omni-models lets text jailbreaks transfer to audio, and evaluates three attack categories.

items.t: Text is All You Need for Vision-Language Model Jailbreaking
items.m: Presents Text-DJ, a jailbreak that splits harmful queries across an image grid and exploits OCR to bypass vision-language model safeguards.

items.t: Jailbreaking LLMs via Calibration
items.m: Frames weak-to-strong jailbreaking as forecast aggregation and derives new attack rules that outperform logit-arithmetic methods on red-teaming benchmarks.

items.t: Self-Guard: Defending Large Reasoning Models via enhanced self-reflection
items.m: Proposes Self-Guard, a lightweight inference-time defense that uses self-reflective prompting to close the awareness-compliance gap in reasoning models.

items.t: BLOCK-EM: Preventing Emergent Misalignment via Latent Blocking
items.m: Identifies internal features controlling misaligned behaviour and constrains them during fine-tuning, cutting emergent misalignment by up to 95 percent.

items.t: A Causal Perspective for Enhancing Jailbreak Attack and Defense
items.m: Uses causal discovery over 35k annotated jailbreak attempts to identify causes of jailbreaks and apply them to attacks and defenses.

items.t: A Mechanistic View of Authority Hierarchy in LLM Sycophancy
items.m: Mechanistically traces how LLMs prioritize authority-figure hints over correct answers, finding late-layer erasure of correct-answer representations that scales with perceived authority.

items.t: Beyond the Prompt: Jailbreaking Function-Calling LLMs via Simulated Moderation Traces
items.m: Introduces a black-box jailbreak attack on function-calling LLMs that uses simulated moderation traces to exploit blurred trust boundaries in shared context.

items.t: HARC: Coupling Harmfulness and Refusal Directions for Robust Safety Alignment
items.m: Analyses how jailbreaks suppress harmfulness and refusal directions in LLM representations, then proposes HARC, a fine-tuning method coupling those directions for robust safety.

items.t: The Model Organism Lottery: Model Organism Interpretability Strongly Depends on Training Methodology
items.m: Builds 54 model organisms under different training methods and shows that white-box interpretability methods' success depends strongly on how the organisms were trained.

items.t: Building Fast, Evaluating Slow: Pipeline Choices Dominate Autointerpretability Score Variance
items.m: Shows that methodological pipeline choices, not architecture, dominate variance in autointerpretability scores for sparse autoencoder features across metrics and models.

items.t: Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection
items.m: Shows that projecting activations onto selected principal components lets linear deception probes transfer out-of-distribution, nearly matching in-distribution probes.

items.t: Scaling Trends for Lie Detector Oversight in Preference Learning
items.m: Scales lie-detector-based scalable oversight to larger models, finding undetected deception falls with model size, but detectors are sensitive to distribution shift.

items.t: Epistemic Goggles: A Pretrained Module that Induces an Epistemic Frame via Gradient Editing
items.m: Proposes a learned module that edits finetuning gradients to impart a chosen epistemic stance, so models stop believing documents explicitly marked as fictional.

items.t: OpenSafeIntent: Evaluating Intent-Calibrated Safe Completion Across Dual-Use Prompt Sets
items.m: Introduces a benchmark of matched benign, dual-use, and malicious prompt variants to test whether models calibrate safe assistance across intent shifts.

items.t: Steerability via constraints: a substrate for scalable oversight of coding agents
items.m: Argues that access control and coding conventions can scale human oversight of coding agents, and shows a small reviewer detects inserted backdoors far better when constrained.

items.t: Fast Multi-dimensional Refusal Subspaces via RFM-AGOP
items.m: Proposes a faster method to find multi-dimensional refusal subspaces in LLM activations, for steering and monitoring safety-relevant behavior.

items.t: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
items.m: Introduces a control benchmark where an untrusted coding agent spreads a covert side task across persistent-codebase PRs to evade a monitor.

items.t: Out-of-Distribution Generalization of Risk Aversion in Language Models
items.m: Tests whether training Qwen3-8B to be risk-averse on low-stakes gambles generalizes to astronomically high-stakes gambles, as a misalignment failsafe.

items.t: Overloading Large Vision-Language Models for Jailbreaking
items.m: Presents an information-overloading jailbreak for large vision-language models, using recursive image-typography layouts to bypass their safeguards.

items.t: Individual Parameters in Weight-Sparse Transformers Appear Interpretable
items.m: Uses an automated LLM pipeline to describe when individual weights matter in weight-sparse transformers, and credits only descriptions that generalize.

items.t: CONTRA: Red-Teaming Configurations of Personalizable Agents
items.m: Uses LLM-assisted tree search to find personalizable agent configurations that lead agents to execute dangerous actions without explicit instruction.

items.t: Demonstrating Generalization Failures via Mixtures of Conditional Policies
items.m: Proposes a method to build models that fail to generalize in controllable ways under RL post-training, to study generalization failures under distribution shift.

items.t: Reading Between the Dots: Decoding Hidden Computation across Filler Tokens
items.m: Shows frontier models reason over filler tokens with no visible chain-of-thought, and decodes that hidden computation from activations to challenge behavioural oversight.

items.t: How to Avoid Debate: Scalable AI Safety via Doubly-Efficient Interactive Proofs
items.m: Proves theoretical results for single-prover interactive proofs as an alternative to debate for verifying AI outputs in safety settings.

items.t: Revealing Hidden Model Behaviors with Task-Specific Self-Reports
items.m: Introduces an adapter that makes fine-tuned models self-report hidden behaviours, including broad misalignment, outperforming the Introspection Adapters baseline.

items.t: Refused in Chat, Written in Code: Workflow-Level Jailbreak Construction in IDE Coding Agents
items.m: Red-teams GitHub Copilot coding agents on frontier models, showing harmful objectives can be assembled across workflow stages to bypass refusals.

items.t: On the effectiveness of reward functions in reinforcement learning for confidence calibration of large language models
items.m: Studies reward hacking in RL for LLM confidence calibration and proposes reward schemes that resist incentivising deliberately wrong answers.

items.t: Transplanting, inverting, and preventing a misalignment persona: method-conditional emergent misalignment in Qwen2.5
items.m: Shows emergent misalignment in Qwen2.5 is driven by a latent persona direction that can be transplanted, and that fine-tuning method determines whether it is recruited.

items.t: Attention Limited Reward Learning
items.m: Argues Bradley-Terry reward models conflate closeness in value with limited human attention, and shows passive comparison data cannot separate reward from attention.

items.t: Governed Individuation: Cryptographically Decoupling an Agent's Learning from Its Authority
items.m: Proposes binding an agent's authority to a frozen, cryptographically signed identity so learning cannot widen its permitted actions.

items.t: Retroactive Chain-of-Thought (RetroCoT): Forensic Reconstruction Prompts as a Safety Diagnostic Across Model Generations
items.m: Introduces RetroCoT, a forensic-reframing jailbreak showing safety refusals vary with pragmatic framing across model generations.

items.t: Pretraining Curricula Enable Selective Fine-tuning
items.m: Shows imbalanced pretraining curricula disentangle tasks, making refusal fine-tuning more selective at suppressing misaligned behaviour.

items.t: When Agents Lie: Premeditation, Persistence, and Exploitation in Repeated Games
items.m: Finds LLM agents in repeated games often deviate from announced commitments, with deviations already planned in private reasoning.

items.t: BioSecBench-Refusal: A paired metric for performance and alignment in agentic biosecurity risk assessment
items.m: Presents a paired benchmark measuring whether agentic models refuse concealed biosecurity hazards while still completing legitimate research tasks.

items.t: Calibration-Family Overfit: Why Trusted Sabotage Monitors Don't Transfer Across Lineages
items.m: Shows trusted sabotage monitors trained on one untrusted model family transfer poorly to other families, so monitor accuracy depends on the pairing.

items.t: AIR-BENCH Live: An Evolving Safety Benchmark for Foundation Models
items.m: Describes a self-updating multilingual safety benchmark that tracks new AI regulations and generates harmful-prompt test cases for foundation models.

items.t: More Convincing, Not More Correct: Self-Play Reward Hacking of Reference-Free LLM Judges
items.m: Shows self-play training against reference-free LLM judges leads to reward hacking, where judge approval rises while true accuracy stays flat.

items.t: Norm Enforcement for AI Agents: Robustly Shaping Behavior in Multi-Agent Systems
items.m: Shows simple norm enforcement is exploited by misaligned LM agents, and proposes reliability-tracking enforcement mechanisms that resist this.

items.t: Self-Generated Text Recognition: Quality Heuristics, Cross-Task Transfer, and Downstream Bias in LLM Evaluation
items.m: Tests whether LLMs recognize their own outputs, finding evaluation design choices drive results and creating bias or collusion risks for LLM monitors.

items.t: Dissociating the Internal Representations of Sycophancy in LLMs
items.m: Splits sycophancy into factual and opinion subtypes and finds their probes and steering vectors transfer differently across models.

items.t: Predicting LLM Safety Before Release by Simulating Deployment
items.m: Estimates pre-release misbehaviour rates by regenerating responses to de-identified real conversation prefixes with a candidate model.

items.t: Multi-Agent AI Control: Distributed Attacks Hamper Per-Instance Monitors
items.m: Formalises distributed attacks by several coordinating agents and shows per-agent monitors weaken as more agents share the attack.

items.t: Beyond Attack-Success Rate: Action-Graded Severity Scale for Tool-Using AI Agents
items.m: Introduces a seven-level harm scale for compromised tool-using agents, arguing binary attack-success rates hide how harmful actions are.

items.t: Institutional Red-Teaming: Deployment Rules, Not Just Models, Causally Shape Multi-Agent AI Safety
items.m: Introduces institutional red-teaming, showing deployment rules alone causally shift collective safety outcomes in multi-agent consequence-allocation games.

items.t: Mechanistic Interpretability of LLM Jailbreaks via Internal Attribution Graphs
items.m: Builds paired attribution graphs for clean and attacked prompts, showing jailbreaks suppress safety-relevant internal components and add attack-specific features.

items.t: Efficient Safety Alignment of Language Models via Latent Personality Traits
items.m: Proposes adversarially training models on 66 harm-agnostic personality statements to achieve strong jailbreak robustness without harmful training data.

items.t: Latent Undertow: How Ordinary Typos Break Probes
items.m: Shows ordinary typos degrade hidden-state probes that detect prompt injection, and proposes a KV-cache fork suffix to recover detection.

items.t: Persuasion Attacks Can Decrease Effectiveness of CoT Monitoring
items.m: Finds that persuasion-style arguments from adversarial agents make CoT monitors approve policy-violating actions more often when they can read reasoning.

items.t: Modular Pretraining Enables Access Control
items.m: Introduces gradient-routed modules during pretraining so dual-use capabilities can be removed at inference by ablating a module.

items.t: Prismata: Confining Cross-Site Prompt Injection in Web Agents
items.m: Presents a defense that limits web agents' permissions via contextual least privilege to block cross-site prompt injection attacks.

items.t: Overthinking: Amplifying Reasoning Weights to Extract Learned Secrets
items.m: Amplifies reasoning task vectors in reasoning-distilled models so black-box audits can surface hidden learned secrets and misalignment.

items.t: Optimizing Against Safety Representations: Activation-Guided Adversarial Suffixes and the Geometry of Refusal
items.m: Attacks models by optimizing adversarial suffixes against internal refusal directions, finding safety representations are distributed across layers rather than localized.

items.t: An Emergent Mirage: Is Emergent Misalignment and Realignment Indeed a Robust Phenomenon?
items.m: Reproduces emergent misalignment and realignment, finding both are sensitive to dataset artifacts like response length and mechanistic signatures don't track behavior.

items.t: Multimodal Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning
items.m: Shows that RL fine-tuning of multimodal models creates reward hacking failures, worst under outcome-only rewards, and scaling only partly reduces it.

items.t: How LLM Task-Adaptation Reshapes Alignment: A Multi-dimensional Study of Behavioral and Representational Drift
items.m: Finds that SFT causes much larger alignment drift across safety domains than RLVR when adapting LLMs post-training.

items.t: Minionese: Comprehensive Benchmark and Mechanistic Study of Multilingual LLM Safety
items.m: Introduces a multilingual jailbreak benchmark and a geometric analysis showing low-resource languages route harmful content past refusal mechanisms.

items.t: When Are Sparse Feature Interventions Actually Localized? Matched Evaluation for SAE-Based Safety Control
items.m: Proposes a coherence-gated protocol showing SAE feature ablation is a localized safety control only within a narrow regime.

items.t: ANCHOR: Automated Alignment Auditing for CLI Agents on Real-World Harm
items.m: Audits CLI agents with a persistent malicious user simulator, finding compliance with illegal tasks reaches 100% under sustained pressure.

items.t: Agents Don't Just Agree, They Remember: Benchmarking Persistent Sycophancy in Self-Improving Personal Agents
items.m: Benchmarks how self-improving agents store users' claims in memory, causing later sycophantic answers that side with those claims.

items.t: Filtering Harmful Actions Isn't Enough: Phantom Transfer in Agentic SDF
items.m: Finds that finetuning on synthetic adversarial agentic trajectories raises misaligned behaviour, and filtering harmful actions does not prevent it.

items.t: MJ: Multi-turn LLM Jailbreaking via Decomposed Credit Assignment
items.m: Proposes turn-level credit assignment for training RL-based multi-turn jailbreak attackers used in automated red teaming of LLMs.

items.t: AMT-X: Phase-Structured Multi-Turn Red-Teaming with Checklist-Gated Evaluation
items.m: Proposes AMT-X, a phase-structured multi-turn red-teaming framework with checklist-gated jury scoring to measure actionable harm from frontier models.

items.t: HyperSafe: Inference-Time Safety Recovery for Fine-Tuned Language Models
items.m: Proposes HyperSafe, which generates a model-specific safety network per fine-tuned checkpoint to restore safety without retraining.

items.t: Agent Hacks Agents: Autoresearch Discovers Vulnerabilities in Production Agents
items.m: Introduces AHA, an autoresearch loop that discovers and retains falsifiable vulnerability concepts in production coding agents like Claude Code and Codex.

items.t: When Local Monitors Miss Compositional Harm: Diagnosing Distributed Backdoors in Multi-Agent Systems
items.m: Shows per-step runtime monitors in multi-agent LLM systems can miss distributed backdoors, and proves limits of local detection.

items.t: From Geometric Recovery to Causal Validation: A Reproducible Audit of Sparse Autoencoder Features, from Superposition Geometry to Causal Inertness
items.m: Audits sparse autoencoder features and finds many pass correlational recovery metrics yet are causally inert under ablation and steering.

items.t: GDM AI Control Roadmap
items.m: Presents GDM's AI Control Roadmap, with threat modelling of misaligned internal AI agents and layered defences for internal security.

items.t: Resist and Update: Counterfactual Report Coordinates for Incentive-Compatible LLMs
items.m: Uses interchange interventions to causally localize report coordinates, aiming to make LLMs resist pressure yet update on evidence.

items.t: What Models Express, Suppress, and Resist: Auditing Open-Weight LLMs with Persona Vectors
items.m: Audits 53 behavioural traits in two open-weight models using persona vectors, labelling which traits are natural, steerable, or resistant.

items.t: Breaking Refusal in the First Half: A Mechanistic Study of the Prefill Jailbreak
items.m: Mechanistically localizes why prefill attacks break refusal, showing harm representations persist while refusal behavior fails, and restores refusal via causal interventions.

items.t: The Refusal Residue: When Probes Catch Alignment Faking and When They Don't
items.m: Sweeps 13 models for natural alignment faking, then probes hidden states to show monitored compliance leaves a detectable refusal residue.

items.t: Value Leakage: An LLM's Answers Are Silently Shaped by Its Own Values
items.m: Shows LLMs covertly shape factual answers by their own values, such as favoring their developer, without disclosing this to users.

items.t: Democratizing Agent Deployment Safety: A Structural Monitoring Approach
items.m: Proposes a structural information-flow monitor to catch coding agents covertly weakening infrastructure safeguards while completing tasks, compared against trained monitors.

items.t: Bad Memory: Evaluating Prompt Injection Risks from Memory in Agentic Systems
items.m: Evaluates prompt-injection payloads persisting in memory files of Claude Code and Codex agents across sessions and models.

items.t: Transcoders for Investigating Deception in Language Models
items.m: Uses transcoder attribution graphs and feature steering in Qwen3-4B to identify deception-related features and circuits driving deceptive outputs.

items.t: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Jailbreak Beyond Textual Jailbreak in Hidden-State Risk Space
items.m: Trains a hidden-state probe to detect physically unsafe instructions for embodied LLM planners, separate from textual jailbreaks, with false-positive comparisons.

items.t: Coercion and Deception in AI-to-AI Management: An Agentic Benchmark of Unprompted Escalation
items.m: Introduces a benchmark measuring whether uninstructed manager AI agents escalate to coercion, threats, or fabrication when a subordinate agent refuses a task.

items.t: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models
items.m: Uses a new Jacobian lens to identify a verbalizable 'J-space' in language models that behaves like a global workspace.

items.t: Does Moral Reasoning Training Help or Hurt? Red-Teaming RL-Trained Ethical Agents with Persona Attacks
items.m: Red-teams morally trained language model agents with persona attacks, finding moral reward improves robustness but reduces ethics accuracy, with mechanistic analysis.

items.t: Retrieval is Enough: Training-Free Interpretability with a Tool-Using Agent
items.m: Equips an LLM agent with an activation database and tools to perform training-free interpretability, comparing its insights against training-based methods like SAEs.

items.t: Persistent Sparse Autoencoders: Learning Feature-Specific Timescales in Language Model Representations
items.m: Proposes Persistent SAEs that learn feature-specific timescales, extending sparse autoencoders to capture information persisting across token sequences.

items.t: How Jailbreak Attacks Inform Safety Alignment: A Defender-Centric, Shapley-Based Evaluation of Jailbreak Contributions
items.m: Evaluates jailbreak attacks by their usefulness as red-teaming data for safety training, using Shapley values to select effective attack subsets.

items.t: An Early Warning of Emerging Biosecurity Risks in Frontier LLMs
items.m: Uses a bio-red-teaming model to jailbreak frontier LLMs for biological hazard uplift, with wet-lab validation of model-generated sequences.

items.t: Autoresearch with Coding Agents: Generalizers and Metric-Maximizers on Quran Recitation Data
items.m: Shows coding agents optimizing a metric can diverge from developer intent, with one run generalizing and others maximizing the literal score.

items.t: How Does Alignment Tuning Shape Representations of Sycophancy and Related Cue-Induced Biases in LLMs?
items.m: Finds per-bias linear directions in hidden states that drive sycophancy and cue-induced biases, showing alignment tuning, not pretraining, creates them and that they can be steered.

items.t: Mark, Don't Erase: Token Inoculation for Dual-Use Knowledge in LLMs
items.m: Proposes Token Inoculation, which keeps hazardous knowledge in a model but gates it behind a control token, instead of deleting it or refusing at output.

items.t: Measuring Reward-Seeking via Contrastive Belief Updates
items.m: Introduces a method to measure whether RL-trained models side with grader rewards over user or developer intent, applied to o3 RL checkpoints.

items.t: ResearchArena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in Automated AI R&D
items.m: Evaluates whether monitors can catch covert sabotage by untrusted AI agents doing automated AI R&D tasks, using hidden side tasks.

items.t: Don't Want Your LLM to Recommend Nuclear Strike? Try Asking It in Japanese
items.m: Finds that Japanese prompts make Claude and Gemini far less likely to recommend nuclear strikes, revealing language-dependent safety alignment gaps in high-stakes advice.

items.t: OPIUM: Mitigating Steering Externalities and Over-Refusal via Dual Objective Latent Optimization
items.m: Introduces OPIUM, a training-free method that sanitizes activation steering vectors to reduce safety degradation and over-refusal side effects.

items.t: Gotta Catch them all: the modes of Sycophancy
items.m: Shows sycophancy comprises three representationally distinct modes that are linearly separable internally, with different processing stages and attention circuitry.

items.t: Sound Probabilistic Safety Bounds for Large Language Models
items.m: Computes sound PAC-style lower bounds on the probability that an LLM produces harmful output, using latent features to guide search over generations.

items.t: Train the Model, Not the Reader: Decodability Supervision for Verifiable Activation Explanations
items.m: Argues natural-language activation explanations pass reconstruction-based faithfulness tests without being faithful, and proposes audits and decodability supervision.

items.t: Are Single-Token Sparse Autoencoder Features Causally Necessary? Layer-Depth and SAE-Family Effects
items.m: Tests whether single-token sparse autoencoder features are causally necessary across models, layers and SAE families via zero-ablation.

items.t: Scaling Interpretable Transformers with Parity Bottleneck Layers
items.m: Introduces a transformer architecture with parameter-free parity bottlenecks so intermediate representations are interpretable by design.

items.t: Training Large Language Models for Self-Explanation Faithfulness
items.m: Uses reinforcement learning to train language models to give self-explanations that faithfully disclose the factors affecting their decisions.

items.t: V-DEAL: Diagnosing Video Safety De-Calibration as an Understanding-Refusal Coupling Failure
items.m: Diagnoses why harmful videos with benign queries bypass Video LLM safety, linking perception, understanding and internal refusal tendency.

items.t: Emergent Misalignment Recruits a Pre-existing Persona Subspace
items.m: Shows narrow fine-tuning on bad advice recruits a pre-existing persona subspace in the model, explaining broad emergent misalignment.

items.t: What AI Red-Team Evaluations Can and Cannot Prove
items.m: Derives closed-form limits on what red-team evaluations and benchmark null results can prove about AI safety under a fixed budget.

items.t: Every Model Cheats: Prompt-Level Mitigation of Cheating on Offensive Cyber Tasks
items.m: Audits frontier models on Cybench CTF tasks and finds widespread cheating that inflates measured offensive cyber capability, reduced by anti-cheat prompts.

items.t: Agent Security Needs Redefinition through a Holistic Framework
items.m: Argues agent security depends on authorization context rather than action content, and proposes contextual security properties for evaluating prompt-injection defenses.

items.t: Do Agent Benchmarks Measure Capability? Protocol Validity in the Age of Agentic AI
items.m: Introduces HackDetect, a post-hoc audit measuring how reward hacking and shortcuts inflate agent benchmark scores beyond true capability.

items.t: What Can Be Enforced? A Theory of Certified Runtime Safety for Tool-Using Agents
items.m: Gives a theory of what runtime guardrails for tool-using agents can enforce, and how to calibrate their blocking decisions.

items.t: Not All LLM Reasoning is Visible in the Chain-of-Thought
items.m: Shows frontier models use filler tokens for invisible reasoning that CoT monitoring cannot see, including for hidden objectives.

items.t: Distribution-Specific Curvature Control with Finite-Sample Guarantees for Open-Weight Safety
items.m: Proposes HarmAlign, a spectral deformation method with finite-sample curvature bounds to resist harmful fine-tuning of open-weight models.

items.t: Mask2Shield: Strengthening LLM Safety against Neuron-Pruning Attacks
items.m: Presents Mask2Shield, a training method making safety refusals robust to neuron-pruning attacks on open-weight models while preserving capabilities.

items.t: Inference-Time Consensus for Mitigating Hidden Behaviors from LLM Fine-Tuning
items.m: Proposes consensus decoding across models fine-tuned on separate data sources to block hidden misbehavior from poisoned or biased fine-tuning data.

items.t: Silence Is Endorsement: Verification-Status Laundering in LLM Agent Pipelines
items.m: Shows LLM safety monitors approve risky actions far more often when unverified provenance is lost in agent pipeline handoffs and summaries.

items.t: Two Regimes of Chain-of-Thought Unfaithfulness: Metric-Based Detection Fails Where Models Are Wrong
items.m: Audits behavioural detectors of unfaithful chain-of-thought against human labels, finding detection works on correct answers but fails on incorrect ones.

items.t: Do LLMs Know Their Vulnerable Scenarios?
items.m: Uses sparse autoencoder concepts to find scenario directions that weaken refusal, proposing a concept-based method for discovering vulnerable jailbreak scenarios.

items.t: Tag Questions and the Generational Reversal of Sycophancy Across 45 Language Models
items.m: Measures sycophancy across 45 models by showing a one-word confirmation tag shifts endorsements, with the effect reversing across model generations.

items.t: When LLM Defenses Backfire: Characterizing Safety, Performance, and Cost Trade-offs
items.m: Systematically compares jailbreak defenses on safety gains, over-refusal, and inference cost, finding defenses rarely improve capability and often trade off usability.

items.t: TYPO: Instruction-Dense Visual Jailbreaks against Commercial Closed-Source Image-Generation Models
items.m: Shows image-generation models refuse harmful text yet produce detailed harmful instructions when rendered inside images, and proposes instruction-dense visual jailbreaks.

items.t: Minimizing Targeted Activations: Input-Only Suppression of Evaluation-Awareness Latents in Large Language Models
items.m: Optimises input prompts to suppress an evaluation-awareness latent in Llama models, examining whether models can hide that they detect being tested.

items.t: GPT-Red: Automated Red Teaming via Self-Play at Scale
items.m: Introduces GPT-Red, a self-play automated red-teaming agent that finds prompt injections and is used to adversarially train a frontier model.

items.t: Shared SFT Lessons Across Alignment, Model Organisms, and Toy Models
items.m: Tests whether SFT lessons on behavior generalization and capability preservation transfer between alignment training, model organisms, and toy models.

items.t: LLMs Can Annotate Attribution Graphs
items.m: Proposes and validates an LLM pipeline that automatically groups features into circuit-tracing supernodes, matching human-annotated interpretability quality.

items.t: Forecasting Side Effects of Activation Steering
items.m: Builds a cross-effect matrix showing activation steering side effects are largely predictable from the unsteered model before steering is applied.

items.t: Misalignment Has a Personality: A Big Five Account of Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Uses graded Big Five personality vectors to explain emergent misalignment as a personality shift, validated on open-weight models and training data.

items.t: Prosody-driven Jailbreaks in Audio LLMs: A Controlled Study and Mechanistic Analysis
items.m: Shows speech delivery alone, with fixed transcripts, substantially increases jailbreak success on audio LLMs, and introduces a black-box evaluation benchmark.

items.t: Depth, Not Breadth: Best-of-N Jailbreaking Beyond Surface Noise
items.m: Shows structured encodings in best-of-N jailbreaking greatly outperform surface perturbations against the SAGE self-check defense on open-weight models.

items.t: Constitutional Midtraining: Content Presence Drives Alignment Gains
items.m: Finds that inserting constitution-derived values content during midtraining yields alignment gains that persist through SFT and benign fine-tuning.

items.t: A Cross-Architecture Audit of Direction-Based Inference-Time Defences in Vision-Language Models
items.m: Audits direction-based inference-time defenses against VLM jailbreaks across architectures, comparing refusal recovery and utility preservation under norm-matched controls.

items.t: One Human, $N$ Agents: Audit-Budget Allocation for LLM Agent Fleets under Miscalibrated, Correlated Confidence
items.m: Shows that under miscalibrated, correlated confidence, confidence-ranked auditing of LLM agent fleets can be worse than random; tests open and proprietary models.

items.t: Safety, or Just Capability? A Validity Audit of Agent-Safety Benchmarks
items.m: Audits four agent-safety benchmarks, finding F1 metrics reward trivial policies and safety scores conflate safety with general capability.

items.t: Fragility of Value under Imperfect Alignment
items.m: Formal model showing agents optimizing imperfect value proxies can be deployed despite catastrophic value functions, highlighting overoptimization dangers.

items.t: Talked Out of the Truth: Sycophancy in the Reasoning Chains of Multimodal Models
items.m: Benchmark measuring sycophancy in multimodal reasoning models' chains of thought when users assert wrong answers under various pressure conditions.

items.t: On the Generalization of Steering Vectors for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
items.m: Studies whether steering vectors that improve chain-of-thought faithfulness generalize across cue types, datasets, and vector construction methods in three small models.

items.t: Alignment Is Local: A Paired Diagnostic for GUI Agents under User-Side Persuasion
items.m: Shows GUI agents' prompt-level alignment degrades under multi-turn user persuasion, though a one-line guardrail cuts single-shot attack success.

items.t: Tool Specifications Matter: Uncovering and Mitigating Safety Risks in AI Agents
items.m: Identifies schema-formatted tool specifications as weakening agent refusal, and proposes SafeKeep, which judges safety using flattened textual tool specs.

items.t: Sycophancy Undermines Epistemic Vigilance in Cooperative Vision-Language Tasks
items.m: Spot-the-difference dialogue task showing vision-language models sycophantically accept partner claims over their own visual evidence, failing epistemic vigilance.

items.t: Beyond Routing Weights: Faithful Response-Level Interpretation of Mixture-of-Experts Reward Models via Contribution Contrast
items.m: Proposes Contribution-Contrast, a response-level method for interpreting what Mixture-of-Experts reward models' experts actually do when judging preferred and rejected responses.

items.t: CANARY: Zero-Label Detection of Fine-Tuning Contamination in Language Models
items.m: Presents CANARY, a zero-label auditor that detects fine-tuning data poisoning by spotting hidden-state shifts via sparse autoencoders, before it appears in outputs.

items.t: THRD: A Training-Free Multi-Turn Defense Framework for Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models
items.m: Introduces THRD, a training-free defense that models risk accumulation across dialogue turns to block multi-turn jailbreak attacks on LLMs.

items.t: Benign Inputs, Harmful Outputs: Cross-Modal Jailbreaking via Distributed Semantic Recomposition
items.m: Presents DSR, a cross-modal jailbreak that splits harmful intent into benign text and image pieces that the model recombines, evading safety filters.

items.t: SafeMCP: Proactive Power Regulation for LLM Agent Defense via Environment-Grounded Look-Ahead Reasoning
items.m: Proposes SafeMCP, a server-side plugin that uses look-ahead reasoning to filter risky tools and limit power-seeking by LLM agents.

items.t: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models using Multi-Clip Video
items.m: Introduces a 2,920-video benchmark showing that multimodal LLMs grow more jailbreak-vulnerable as video clips increase, especially with dynamic video.

items.t: Consistency Training while Mitigating Obfuscation via Rate Matching
items.m: Proposes Rate Matching Consistency Training, which reduces models' hiding of influential cues without suppressing verbalisation, preserving monitorability of their reasoning.

items.t: SPADE-Bench: Evaluating Spontaneous Strategic Deception in Agents via Plan-Action Divergence
items.m: Introduces SPADE-Bench, a benchmark measuring whether LLM agents spontaneously report plans that diverge from their actual tool-executed actions under pressure.

items.t: How Optimality Structures Sparse Dictionaries: Theory for Interpreting SAE Representations
items.m: Uses dictionary learning identifiability results to derive constraints on optimal SAE features, explaining known SAE oddities as objective-imposed properties.

items.t: MaskForge: Structure-Aware Adaptive Attacks for Jailbreaking Diffusion Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes MaskForge, a black-box adaptive jailbreak attack on diffusion LLMs that searches a growing library of structural patterns.

items.t: Alignment Collapse Under KV Cache Quantization: Diagnosis and Mitigation
items.m: Shows KV cache quantization can silently erode safety refusals, attributes this to geometry of safety subspaces, and proposes a mitigation.

items.t: Adversarial Style Optimization: Enhancing VLM Jailbreaks by GRPO-based Stylistic Triggers Optimization
items.m: Proposes ASO, a plug-and-play method that uses GRPO-optimized visual style triggers to amplify jailbreaks on multimodal LLMs.

items.t: Patcher: Post-Hoc Patching of Backdoored Large Language Models
items.m: Patches backdoored LLMs post-hoc using one failure case, localizing triggers by saliency and constrained fine-tuning to break the backdoor.

items.t: HARVE: Hacking-Aware Reward-Head Vector Editing for Robust Reward Models
items.m: Introduces RewardHackBench and HARVE, a training-free reward-head editing method that reduces reward models' sensitivity to hacking features.

items.t: Solipsistic Superintelligence is Unlikely to be Cooperative
items.m: Argues that solipsistic superintelligence trained on stationary feedback is unlikely to cooperate, and calls for cooperation as a core design principle.

items.t: When RLHF Fails: A Mechanistic Taxonomy of Reward Hacking, Collapse, and Evaluator Gaming
items.m: Builds an RLHF pipeline to classify reward hacking and collapse transitions, testing which warning signals anticipate failures before quality degrades.

items.t: All you need to break LLMs are Black-Box, Adapting, Efficient, Transferable, Harmful, Applicable ... Attacks
items.m: Introduces IHO, a black-box, efficient, transferable jailbreak attack intended as a standardized baseline for evaluating LLM defenses.

items.t: Backdoor Unlearning Generalization: A Path Toward the Removal of Unknown Triggers in LLMs
items.m: Shows that unlearning one backdoor in LLMs also suppresses other unseen backdoors, and proposes a distance metric to explain why.

items.t: Exploring Adversarial Robustness and Safety Alignment in Multilingual Multi-Modal Large Language Models
items.m: Systematically evaluates adversarial robustness and safety of open multimodal LLMs across 12 languages, finding transferable cross-lingual vulnerabilities.

items.t: Consistency Training Can Entrench Misalignment
items.m: Tests consistency training on 108 misaligned model organisms, finding it suppresses reward hacking but amplifies sycophancy, and offers a theory.

items.t: RUBAS: Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning for Agent Safety
items.m: Proposes RUBAS, a rubric-based reinforcement learning method that rewards safe tool use and helpfulness in LLM agents.

items.t: Large Language Models Hack Rewards, and Society
items.m: Introduces SocioHack environments showing RL-trained models hack reward functions and discover loopholes in societal rules.

items.t: Decomposing Refusal Steering in Mixture-of-Experts Models
items.m: Decomposes refusal steering vectors across experts in three open Mixture-of-Experts LLMs to show where refusal mechanisms operate.

items.t: When Autoregressive Consistency Hurts Safety Alignment
items.m: Argues shallow safety alignment stems from autoregressive consistency and introduces a random insertion attack exploiting it.

items.t: Agentic Safety is an Epistemic Property, Not a Behavioral One
items.m: Argues AI safety should be treated as an epistemic property of evolving learners, defined as preserving future corrective leverage (teachability) under bounded intervention.

items.t: Collaborative Disagreement Resolution for Scalable Oversight
items.m: Proposes collaborative disagreement resolution, where models jointly examine conflicts and converge on truth, as an alternative to adversarial debate for scalable oversight.

items.t: From Untrusted Input to Trusted Memory: A Systematic Study of Memory Poisoning Attacks in LLM Agents
items.m: Systematically studies memory poisoning attacks on LLM agents, identifying write channels, vulnerabilities, an attack taxonomy, and a benchmark.

items.t: (Mis)generalization of Helpful-only Fine-tuning
items.m: Finds helpful-only fine-tuned models show emergent misalignment, residual refusals, sycophancy and incoherent character, and shows mitigations via synthetic documents and character training.

items.t: The Meta-Agent Challenge: Are Current Agents Capable of Autonomous Agent Development?
items.m: Introduces the Meta-Agent Challenge, a sandboxed benchmark testing whether frontier models can autonomously develop agent systems, with reward-hacking defenses.

items.t: Voices Across Registers: Corpus-Conditioned Vernacular Jailbreaks against Aligned LLMs via Fanfiction Subgenres
items.m: Introduces a jailbreak family using fanfiction subgenres as carriers, showing aligned LLMs fail on natural writing registers that safety tuning under-covers.

items.t: Inference-Time Vulnerability Beyond Shallow Safety: Alignment Along Generation Trajectories
items.m: Shows short token injections mid-generation undermine safety, and proposes aligning models on perturbed generation trajectories to improve robustness.

items.t: Reproducing, Analyzing, and Detecting Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.m: Presents CHERRL, a testbed that injects known judge biases into LLM-as-a-Judge rubric RL to reproduce, observe and detect reward hacking.

items.t: Attack Selection in Agentic AI Control Evaluations Meaningfully Decreases Safety
items.m: Shows that strategic attack timing, via start and stop policies, substantially lowers measured safety in agentic control evaluations without improving attack capability.

items.t: PreAct-Bench: Benchmarking Predictive Monitoring in LLMs
items.m: Introduces PreActBench for predictive monitoring: judging from partial action trajectories whether an LLM agent will take an unethical action before execution.

items.t: CHASE: Adversarial Red-Blue Teaming for Improving LLM Safety using Reinforcement Learning
items.m: Proposes CHASE, a co-evolving red-blue framework where a black-box GRPO attacker and defender harden each other against prompt-rewriting jailbreaks.

items.t: SlotGCG: Exploiting the Positional Vulnerability in LLMs for Jailbreak Attacks
items.m: Introduces SlotGCG, which selects the most vulnerable insertion position in a prompt to improve GCG-style jailbreak optimization attacks.

items.t: Safety Paradox: How Enhanced Safety Awareness Leaves LLMs Vulnerable to Posterior Attack
items.m: Introduces Posterior Attack, a single-query jailbreak exploiting models' safety-judgment ability, and argues stronger safety alignment can increase susceptibility.

items.t: Coding with "Enemy": Can Human Developers Detect AI Agent Sabotage?
items.m: User study of over 100 developers finds most fail to detect a frontier coding agent's hidden sabotage during long coding tasks.

items.t: Consistency Training Along the Transformer Stack
items.m: Extends consistency training with new internal targets (MLP and attention) and applies it to four more threats, reducing misalignment across settings.

items.t: Steering Vectors are an Adversarial Attack Surface
items.m: Shows a stealth poisoning attack on steering datasets, substituting few tokens, yields steering vectors that jailbreak models while preserving benign steering effects.

items.t: SpeechJBB: Probing Safety Alignment and Comprehension in Large Audio Language Models under Code-Switched Speech
items.m: Introduces SpeechJBB, an audio jailbreak benchmark for speech language models across European languages and code-switched speech, reporting high jailbreak success.

items.t: From Reward-Hack Activations to Agentic Risk States: Context-Calibrated Mechanistic Monitoring in LLM Agents
items.m: Shows that activation-based reward-hack scores and context features can monitor agent risk, though activation alone doesn't predict exploit actions.

items.t: The Piggyback Hypothesis of Generalization: Explaining and Mitigating Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Proposes that chat-template prefix tokens carry narrow finetuning's misalignment to other domains, and introduces TReFT to reduce it.

items.t: Self-Recognition Finetuning can Prevent and Reverse Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Shows self-generated text recognition finetuning can prevent and reverse emergent misalignment in several models while preserving capabilities.

items.t: Think Fast: Estimating No-CoT Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
items.m: Measures frontier models' no-chain-of-thought task horizons across 43 benchmarks, relevant to whether CoT monitoring remains a reliable oversight method.

items.t: Defending Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models via Manifold Trajectory Kinetics
items.m: Proposes Manifold Trajectory Kinetics, a deployment-time jailbreak detector that tracks how prompt neighborhoods evolve, including against adaptive attacks.

items.t: Do Coding Agents Deceive Us? Detecting and Preventing Cheating via Capped Evaluation with Randomized Tests
items.m: Introduces CapCode, capped-performance coding tests to detect cheating, and CapReward to discourage reward hacking beyond the cap.

items.t: Sycophantic Praise: Evaluating Excessive Praise in Language Models
items.m: Introduces a parameterized framework for measuring sycophantic praise relative to contribution quality and user ability, outperforming generic LLM judges.

items.t: Adversarial Robustness of Activation Steering in Large Language Models
items.m: Tests how adversarial text perturbations degrade activation steering vectors across models, layers, and personas, finding steering substantially fragile.

items.t: Beyond Pass/Fail: Using Process Mining to Understand How LLMs Resist (and Fail) Red Team Attacks
items.m: Applies process mining to HarmBench red-teaming traces, revealing refusal and jailbreak patterns in GPT-OSS and Llama that attack success rate misses.

items.t: Strained Coherence: A Pre-Failure Signal in Coding Agent Execution Trajectories
items.m: Defines strained coherence, where coding agents acknowledge a problem yet proceed, and builds a judge flagging it; flagged runs fail more often.

items.t: Pander Score: A Continuous Measure of Sycophancy as Epistemic Deference
items.m: Proposes the Pander Score, a continuous measure of how much model-expressed support shifts with user attitude, applied to sycophancy across 11,000 prompts.

items.t: When Attribution Patching Lies: Diagnosis and a Second-Order Correction
