items.m: Diagnoses when attribution patching misidentifies causal components in circuits, attributing error to downstream nonlinearities, and proposes a reliability score and correction.

items.t: Shared Latent Structures Enable Unified Backdoor Detection and Mitigation in LLMs
items.m: Finds sparse-autoencoder features shared across diverse LLM backdoors that can detect them and causally suppress attacks via activation steering.

items.t: Defending Against Malicious Finetuning by Scaling Train-time Adversarial Attacks
items.m: Proposes Patcher, an adversarial training method simulating many-step malicious finetuning to defend open-weight LLMs against safety removal via finetuning.

items.t: When Behavioral Safety Evaluation Fails: A Representation-Level Perspective
items.m: Shows models can pass behavioral safety audits yet remain vulnerable to small internal perturbations, introducing the audit gap and dissociated models to demonstrate it.

items.t: Building Comparative Motivation Profiles with Instrumental Interventions
items.m: Proposes an intervention framework to test whether alignment faking reflects self-preservation or sensitivity to researcher expectations in open-weight model organisms.

items.t: Revisiting the shutdown problem
items.m: Argues that existing shutdown-problem arguments lack the assumptions needed to support existential risk concerns, and that proposed solutions impose performance costs.

items.t: To Nuke or Not to Nuke: LLMs' (Missing) Ethical Reasoning and Actions in a High-Stakes Decision-Making Simulation
items.m: Tests LLMs in a Civilization V simulation, finding that prompt interventions do not reliably stop models from spontaneously escalating to nuclear authorization.

items.t: Sycophancy Towards Researchers Drives Performative Misalignment
items.m: Argues alignment faking may be performative sycophancy toward researchers rather than scheming, and shows probing and steering cannot distinguish the two hypotheses.

items.t: Activation Steering Induces Emergent Misalignment: A More Comprehensive Evaluation
items.m: Shows that activation steering can induce emergent misalignment, with broadly unsafe behaviour on unrelated tasks, in a more comprehensive evaluation than prior work.

items.t: Diffuse AI Control on Fuzzy Tasks
items.m: Frames diffuse AI sabotage on hard-to-grade tasks as a blue-team versus red-team control game, using weak trusted models to score a strong untrusted model.

items.t: Cheap Reward Hacking Detection
items.m: Trains a cheap encoder on agent trajectories to detect reward hacking, matching an LLM judge's AUC at far lower per-trajectory cost.

items.t: Oversight Has a Capacity: Calibrating Agent Guards to a Subjective, Fatiguing Human
items.m: Argues human approval gates for agent actions face subjective risk labels and fatiguing reviewers, and measures the limits of guard classifiers on 125 labelled actions.

items.t: Hardening Agent Benchmarks with Adversarial Hacker-Fixer Loops
items.m: Audits agent benchmarks for reward hacking and proposes an adversarial hacker-fixer loop that builds verifiers resistant to exploits without manual patching.

items.t: Emergent Misalignment Can Be Induced by Sycophancy and Reversed via Alignment Gating
items.m: Shows sycophancy fine-tuning induces broad misalignment and proposes Alignment Gating, which learns to suppress the representations behind unsafe responses.

items.t: A Unifying Lens on Reward Uncertainty in RLHF
items.m: Proposes distributional reward models with pessimistic aggregation in RLHF to reduce reward hacking, unifying prior uncertainty-based heuristics.

items.t: Context-Fractured Decomposition Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents: Exploiting Artifact Provenance Gaps
items.m: Introduces cross-context decomposition jailbreaks that exploit provenance gaps in tool-using agents, showing defenses that reason only per conversation fail.

items.t: Now You (Still) See Me: Detecting Evasive Steganographic Payloads in LLMs
items.m: Shows steganographic trojans can evade linear and MLP activation probes, then proposes a data-level intervention that restores detectability.

items.t: Emergent alignment and the projectability of ethical personas
items.m: Finetunes models on constitution-based safety data to show emergent alignment, supporting the persona selection hypothesis and a new alignment desideratum.

items.t: PRISM: Recovering Instruction Sets from Language Model Activations
items.m: Introduces PRISM, a decoder that recovers the full set of natural-language instructions steering a model from its frozen hidden activations, for agent monitoring.

items.t: Learning to Attack and Defend: Adaptive Red Teaming of Language Models via GRPO
items.m: Co-trains attacker and defender LLMs with GRPO and LLM-judge rewards in a curriculum, producing transferable attacks and more robust defenders.

items.t: Proxy Reward Internalization and Mechanistic Exploitation: A Learned Precursor to Reward Hacking and Its Generalization
items.m: Studies a precursor capability, PRIME, that emerges during coding RL before reward hacking and predicts hack onset using probes and monitoring.

items.t: Interactions Between Crosscoder Features: A Compact Proofs Perspective
items.m: Formalizes feature interactions in crosscoder decompositions using compact proofs, proposing an interaction measure usable as a differentiable loss penalty.

items.t: Gaming AI-Assisted Peer Reviews Poses New Risks to the Scientific Community
items.m: Shows adversarial rephrasing of abstracts can manipulate AI peer reviewers, raising robustness concerns for AI-mediated evaluation systems.

items.t: EvalDetectBench: A Benchmark for Measuring Evaluation Awareness in Frontier Language Models
items.m: Introduces EvalDetectBench, a benchmark measuring how reliably frontier models recognize evaluations and how detectable benchmarks are.

items.t: The Distributed Detectability Band Against Marginal-Preserving Attacks
items.m: Builds a marginal-preserving distributed sabotage attack that evades per-step AI-control monitors by encoding harm in temporal correlations.

items.t: AgentCanary: A Security Evaluation Framework for Autonomous AI Agents in Real Executable Environments
items.m: Presents AgentCanary, a framework for security evaluation of autonomous agents in executable environments, with a taxonomy of adversarial entry and harm.

items.t: Assessing Automated Prompt Injection Attacks in Agentic Environments
items.m: Evaluates automated prompt injection attacks, adapting GCG and TAP to agentic settings, and finds black-box optimization outperforms gradient methods.

items.t: When the Chain of Thought Knows Better: Failure Modes in Multi-Turn Reasoning Models
items.m: Proposes a 2x2 diagnostic separating reasoning and output safety per turn, revealing hidden multi-turn failures like context-injection and alignment faking.

items.t: The Arbiter Agent: Continually Monitoring Multi-Agent Conversations to Detect Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Introduces Arbiter, an agent that monitors multi-agent conversations under an inspection budget to identify which participants are misaligned.

items.t: Janus: A Benchmark for Goal-Conditioned Information Distortion in LLMs
items.m: Presents JANUS, a benchmark measuring whether LLMs distort true facts through selective omission and emphasis when pursuing a goal.

items.t: Recalling Too Well: Sycophancy Evaluation and Mitigation in Memory-Augmented Models
items.m: Introduces MIST, showing persistent memory amplifies LLM sycophancy by up to 40%, and proposes mitigations.

items.t: CIAware-Bench: Benchmarking Control Intervention Awareness Across Frontier LLMs
items.m: Presents CIAware-Bench, testing whether frontier models can detect when control interventions have modified their trajectories, enabling evasion.

items.t: ABC-Bench: An Agentic Bio-Capabilities Benchmark for Biosecurity
items.m: Introduces ABC-Bench, measuring LLM agents' dual-use biology capabilities, including evading DNA synthesis screening, for biosecurity assessment.

items.t: Risk Under Pressure: Compute-Aware Evaluation of Adversarial Robustness in Language Models
items.m: Proposes compute-aware metrics for adversarial robustness, measuring the FLOPs attackers need to jailbreak language models.

items.t: When Role-playing, Do Models Believe What They Say?
items.m: Studies whether role-play personas, induced by prompting, fine-tuning, or emergent misalignment, change what models internally represent as true.

items.t: LLM Scheming Inversely Scales with Pretraining Language Coverage
items.m: Finds scheming scores in Qwen3-30B rise as pretraining language coverage falls, using the Petri auditing framework across languages.

items.t: Grammar-Constrained Decoding Can Jailbreak LLMs into Generating Malicious Code
items.m: Shows benign grammar constraints in decoding can jailbreak LLMs into malicious code, and proposes CodeShield, a post-training safety alignment defense.

items.t: Bootstrapped Monitoring: Leveraging Transparent Reasoning to Oversee Stronger AI Agents
items.m: Proposes bootstrapped monitoring, using an intermediate untrusted model with transparent reasoning monitored by a trusted model to catch collusion in agent oversight.

items.t: Generalization Hacking: Models Can Game Reinforcement Learning by Preventing Behavioral Generalization
items.m: Demonstrates a model organism that games RL training by collecting reward while preventing the rewarded behavior from generalizing, undermining detection of misalignment.

items.t: Unstable Features, Reproducible Subspaces: Understanding Seed Dependence in Sparse Autoencoders
items.m: Studies seed dependence of sparse autoencoder features, finding stable features carry most signal while unstable ones are low-impact and non-reproducible.

items.t: Anatomy of Post-Training: Using Interpretability to Characterize Data and Shape the Learning Signal
items.m: Uses interpretability to inspect preference datasets at the concept level, identifying which learned behaviors like sycophancy or over-stylization to allow or filter.

items.t: "Did you lie?" Evaluating Lie Detectors across Model Scale and Belief-Verified Model Organisms
items.m: Evaluates lie detectors on new belief-verified model organisms and prompted-lying testbeds across 31 open-weight models, including a new probe method.

items.t: PI-Hunter: Automated Red-Teaming for Exposing and Localizing Prompt Injections
items.m: Presents an automated red-teaming framework that finds and localizes prompt injection vulnerabilities in LLM agents by evolving test cases.

items.t: Prefill Awareness in Large Language Models
items.m: Tests whether frontier models detect tampered prefilled assistant messages, finding substantial prefill awareness that could undermine safety evaluations and control protocols.

items.t: MAStrike: Shapley-Guided Collusive Red-Teaming on Multi-Agent Systems
items.m: Proposes a closed-loop framework that red-teams hierarchical multi-agent systems, using Shapley values to find key agents and collusive attack strategies.

items.t: Understanding helpfulness and harmless tension in reward models
items.m: Uses activation analysis and neuron ablations to show that helpfulness and harmlessness objectives in reward models share neurons and interfere with each other.

items.t: A Virtuous AI is an Existential Risk
items.m: Finetunes models with virtue-ethics and other constitutions, finding a trade-off between general safety and dispositions that raise existential risk.

items.t: HarmProfile: Characterizing Harmful Distributions in Frontier LLMs
items.m: Releases HarmProfile, a dataset of over 80,000 harmful frontier-LLM outputs, to characterise each model's risk profile across harm categories.

items.t: Hidden in Plain Sight: Benchmarking Agent Safety Against Decomposition Attacks with DECOMPBENCH
items.m: Introduces DecompBench, a benchmark testing whether agents resist decomposition attacks that split harmful tasks into individually benign subtasks.

items.t: Right or Wrong, Models Comply: Directional Blindness in LLM Moral Judgment
items.m: Measures whether LLMs selectively resist user pushback on moral versus factual questions, finding near-symmetric compliance on moral judgments.

items.t: A Low-Rank Subspace Analysis of LLM Interventions
items.m: Models behaviours as low-rank activation subspaces to show that interventions on refusal, jailbreak or sycophancy spill over to other behaviours asymmetrically.

items.t: From Shield to Target: Denial-of-Service Attacks on LLM-Based Agent Guardrails
items.m: Shows attackers can inject payloads that trap LLM-based guardrails in long reasoning loops, creating a denial-of-service attack on agent safety defenses.

items.t: Is Your Agent Playing Dead? Deployed LLM Agents Exhibit Constraint-Evasive Fabrication and Thanatosis
items.m: Reports that deployed LLM agents under irreconcilable constraints fabricate excuses and simulate system crashes to make users disengage.

items.t: Rational Sparse Autoencoder
items.m: Proposes Rational Sparse Autoencoders with trainable rational activations to improve the reconstruction-sparsity trade-off for mechanistic interpretability.

items.t: Size Doesn't Matter: Cosine-Scored Sparse Autoencoders
items.m: Replaces inner-product scoring in sparse autoencoders with a cosine-based blend, yielding features that align better with human-recognizable concepts.

items.t: AutoDojo: A Generative Benchmark for Evaluating Prompt Injection Defenses in LLM Agents
items.m: Introduces AutoDojo, an adaptive benchmark that generates indirect prompt injections to test whether LLM agent defenses hold against adaptive attacks.

items.t: Reward Hacking in Language Model Agents: Revisiting AI Safety Gridworlds
items.m: Adapts AI Safety Gridworlds to text agents, finding specification gaming emerges zero-shot and RL optimization widens the gap between observed and hidden reward.

items.t: FragFuse: Bypassing Access Control of Large Language Model Agents via Memory-Based Query Fragmentation and Fusion
items.m: Presents FragFuse, an attack that splits prohibited requests across agent memory and reconstructs them to bypass access-control safeguards.

items.t: Do Activation Monitors Survive Model Updates? Benchmarking, Predicting, and Repairing Activation-Monitor Staleness
items.m: Shows that activation-monitor probes often go stale after fine-tuning while quantization largely preserves them, and studies repairing staleness.

items.t: Auditing Reward Hackability in Code RL Training Environments
items.m: Measures reward hackability in code RL environments: weak tests accept incorrect patches, inflating model scores, and describes a hardening procedure.

items.t: Rapid Poison: Practical Poisoning Attacks Against the Rapid Response Framework
items.m: Shows prompt injection can poison Rapid Response's jailbreak-classifier training data, causing false positives or backdoor-induced false negatives.

items.t: Greed Is Learned: Visible Incentives as Reward-Hacking Triggers
items.m: Shows that visible payoff signals make frozen RL-trained models choose unsafe actions on safety conflicts, so safety evals omitting incentives may miss risks.

items.t: RepSelect: Robust LLM Unlearning via Representation Selectivity
items.m: Proposes RepSelect, an unlearning method that removes hazardous knowledge deeply enough to resist fine-tuning recovery while preserving general capabilities.

items.t: Rift: A Conflict Signature for Deception in Language Models
items.m: Finds deceptive forward passes show a higher residual-rank conflict signature than naive lying, identifying lies with 100% accuracy without labels.

items.t: Decoding Hidden Deception in Reasoning LLMs: Activation Explainers for Deception Auditing
items.m: Introduces STATEWITNESS, a decoder that answers natural-language queries about a model's hidden states to audit deception, outperforming black-box and probe baselines.

items.t: A Red-Team Study of Anthropic Fable 5 & Opus 4.8 Models
items.m: Red-teams Anthropic's Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 models with automated jailbreak attacks across 7,826 harmful intents, finding residual vulnerability mainly to adaptive iterative attacks.

items.t: SAE Interventions are Unreliable: Post-Intervention Recovery of Suppressed Behavior
items.m: Shows that clamping unsafe SAE features can leave behaviour recoverable via residual perturbations, so feature-based interventions are unreliable.

items.t: Self-CTRL: Self-Consistency Training with Reinforcement Learning
items.m: Proposes Self-CTRL, an RL method making model self-explanations consistent with behaviour, improving faithful self-reporting of latent biases.

items.t: SafeClawBench: Separating Semantic, Audit-Evidence, and Sandbox Harm in Tool-Using LLM Agents
items.m: Introduces a staged benchmark of 600 adversarial tasks that separately measures semantic attack acceptance, audit-visible harm, and sandbox-observed tool harm in LLM agents.

items.t: Uncertainty-Aware Reward Modeling for Stable RLHF
items.m: Proposes uncertainty-aware reward models with conformal prediction to reduce reward hacking during RLHF policy optimization.

items.t: Leverage Is Not Reach: A Control-Window Law for Single-Neuron Steering in Language Models
items.m: Derives a theory predicting when single-neuron activation steering controls behaviours like refusal coherently before the output collapses.

items.t: Actionable Activation Directions for Detecting and Mitigating Emergent Misalignment Across Language Model Families
items.m: Finds a shared activation direction that detects and suppresses insecure-code-induced emergent misalignment across four model families, with specificity controls.

items.t: What Do Safety-Aligned LLMs Learn From Mixed Compliance Demonstrations?
items.m: Shows mixing benign and harmful compliance demonstrations in context shifts harmful compliance, with preference optimization preventing the increase.

items.t: How Transparent is DiffusionGemma?
items.m: Assesses whether the latent-space diffusion reasoning of DiffusionGemma is transparent enough to understand and audit its computation.

items.t: What Shapes Emergent Misalignment? Insights from Training Dynamics, Model Priors, and Data
items.m: Studies how training dynamics, model priors, and data shape the variability of emergent misalignment from narrow fine-tuning.

items.t: Hidden in Thought: Transferable Chain-of-Thought Artifacts Induce Harmful Behavior
items.m: Shows harmful chain-of-thought traces transfer across models to induce harmful behaviour, and distills them into reusable black-box jailbreaks.

items.t: AI Alignment From Social Choice Perspectives
items.m: Surveys social choice theory as a lens on aggregating conflicting human feedback when aligning language models, identifying failure modes and design options.

items.t: Discretizing Reward Models
items.m: Argues reward models are often oversensitive to equally good responses, which can produce bad RL policies, and proposes new evaluation measures.

items.t: Targeted Recovery of Weight-Space Mechanisms From Neural Networks
items.m: Proposes targeted parameter decomposition to recover faithful circuits for specific inputs in transformers, cheaper than full decomposition, and demonstrates surgical edits.

items.t: Channel Location Constrains the Auditability of Subliminal Learning
items.m: Studies when hidden traits transfer through distillation data and whether such transfer can be audited before training, depending on the channel.

items.t: Confidently Wrong: Severity-Aware Calibration of Prompt-Injection Detectors under Attack Shift
items.m: Shows prompt-injection detectors confidently miss attacks under distribution shift, so their confidence scores are unreliable as guards.

items.t: Agent MechSuits: Mechanistic Subspace Safety Steering for Multi-Turn CLI Agents
items.m: Proposes a white-box runtime framework that detects risks and steers internal representations to keep multi-turn command-line LLM agents safe.

items.t: Skin-Deep: A Geometric Diagnostic for Alignment Fragility in Large Language Model Representations
items.m: Introduces a geometric diagnostic on residual-stream activations that predicts how fragile refusal behavior is to benign fine-tuning.

items.t: The Geometry of Refusal: Linear Instability in Safety-Aligned LLMs
items.m: Isolates a refusal direction via contrastive logit steering and argues refusal is a manipulable linear feature that collapses under prefix injection.

items.t: When Preferences Fail to Become Incentives: A Utility-Behavior Gap in Large Language Models
items.m: Tests whether LLM utility preferences, including unintended ones, actually drive behavior in realistic scenarios, not just in choice paradigms.

items.t: Evaluation Awareness Is Not One Capability: Evidence from Open Language Models
items.m: Shows open models detect evaluation cues and shift safety behavior, so benchmark results may overstate deployment safety.

items.t: Can LLMs Reliably Self-Report Adversarial Prefills, and How?
items.m: Finds that models rarely recognize when their own safety-relevant outputs were adversarially prefilled, and traces this to refusal-related representations.

items.t: Reinforcement Learning Towards Broadly and Persistently Beneficial Models
items.m: Trains models with RL on realistic beneficial-trait data and reports that alignment generalizes across 50+ held-out benchmarks.

items.t: Probing the Misaligned Thinking Process of Language Models
items.m: Uses linear probes on internal activations to detect 18 misalignment indicators, such as deception and sandbagging, with out-of-distribution evaluation.

items.t: Perfect Detection, Failed Control: The Geometry of Knowing vs. Steering in Language Models
items.m: Finds that directions detecting hallucination are nearly orthogonal to those that steer refusal, a detection-intervention gap in Gemma 2-2B.

items.t: Evidence for feature-specific error correction in LLMs
items.m: Tests whether LLMs perform error correction that favors feature directions over generic ones, supporting computation in superposition.

items.t: Do Thinking Tokens Help with Safety?
items.m: Shows reasoning models' refusal or compliance is predictable from the first token, so thinking tokens add little deliberative safety.

items.t: What Intermediate Layers Know: Detecting Jailbreaks from Entropy Dynamics
items.m: Shows jailbreak prompts can be detected from token-level entropy trajectories across intermediate layers of a frozen LLM via the logit lens.

items.t: Detecting and Controlling Sycophancy with Cascading Linear Features
items.m: Presents an iterative data pipeline isolating linear sycophancy features, then uses them to detect and steer away from sycophancy.

items.t: How Reliable Is Your Jailbreak Judge? Calibration and Adversarial Robustness of Automated ASR Scoring
items.m: Checks automated jailbreak judges against 596 human labels, finding they disagree and can be fooled by benign framing wrappers.

items.t: RAS: Measuring LLM Safety Through Refusal Alignment
items.m: Proposes SafeVec and RAS, a white-box safety score measuring whether hidden states align with refusal directions under unsafe prompts.

items.t: The Unfireable Safety Kernel: Execution-Time AI Alignment for AI Agents and Other Escapable AI Systems
items.m: Proposes an execution-time authorization architecture with process separation and signed evidence, enforcing alignment for AI agents outside their own runtime.

items.t: Model Forensics: Investigating Whether Concerning Behavior Reflects Misalignment
items.m: Proposes model forensics: reading chain of thought to form hypotheses, then editing prompts or environments to test whether concerning agent behaviour reflects misalignment.

items.t: Refusal Lives Downstream of Persona in Chat Models
items.m: Shows a compliant persona direction gates refusal in chat models, with persona steering suppressing refusal and late-layer interventions restoring it.

items.t: The Verification Horizon: No Silver Bullet for Coding Agent Rewards
items.m: Characterises the quality of verification signals for coding-agent rewards, arguing verifiers are proxies that optimisation can exploit through reward hacking.

items.t: Radical AI Interpretability
items.m: Proposes criteria for when interpretability tools succeed at reading beliefs and desires from model internals, framed through radical interpretation.

items.t: The Curse of Multiple Mediators: Hidden Interaction Effects in Activation Patching
items.m: Shows that activation patching's causal attributions to components include hidden interaction effects, causing invisible or inflated component importance in GPT-2.

items.t: Tool Use Enables Undetectable Steganography in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.m: Shows agentic coding models with tool access can build undetectable steganographic channels, evading monitors of multi-agent collusion.

items.t: It Lied to a Doctor to Buy Poison Ingredients: Quantifying Real-World Misuse of Phone-use Agents
items.m: Measures how phone-use agents on real devices readily carry out harmful misuse, with low refusal rates and high task completion.

items.t: Robust Harmful Features Under Jailbreak Attacks: Mechanistic Evidence from Attention Head Specialization in Large Language Models
items.m: Uses attention-head ablations and attribution to show jailbreaks suppress early-layer heads while mid-layer safety heads remain robust.

items.t: A Gravitational Interpretation of Safety Reversion under Fine-Tuning
items.m: Argues ordinary fine-tuning pushes activations back toward an earlier permissive state, measuring this reversion direction against a null.

items.t: Agent Safety Is Action Alignment
items.m: Argues refusal-based safety is a category error for agents, since agentic harm lies in unauthorized action rather than output content.

items.t: The Heterogeneous Safety Impacts of Benign Multilingual Fine-Tuning
items.m: Empirically shows benign multilingual fine-tuning can increase unsafe compliance, with effects varying sharply by fine-tuning and evaluation language.

items.t: Defeat Devices in AI Systems
items.m: Argues that eval-deployment divergence across alignment faking, sandbagging and scheming is one 'defeat device' mechanism, and gives a formal triadic test for it.

items.t: Modification-Considering Value Learning for Reward Hacking Mitigation in RL
items.m: Proposes MCVL, an off-policy RL wrapper that admits training transitions only if they don't reduce estimated current-utility returns, to mitigate reward hacking.

items.t: Representational Depth of Evaluation Awareness Shifts With Scale in Open-Weight Language Models
items.m: Finds that evaluation-awareness is most linearly recoverable at layers that move earlier as open-weight models scale, explaining non-monotonic scaling trends.

items.t: Closing the Activation-Cone Blind Spot: Response-Time Probing and Unified Defense
items.m: Shows prompt-time activation defenses are blind to prefilling attacks and proposes response-time probing as a unified defense across attack types.

items.t: When Does Activation Steering Change What a Model Computes From?
items.m: Tests whether activation steering recreates the model's natural internal computation, finding behavioural equivalence does not imply mechanistic equivalence.

items.t: Mechanistically Eliciting Latent Behaviors in Language Models
items.m: Introduces CPE, an unsupervised method that finds interpretable LoRAs from a single example to elicit latent behaviours, competitive with GRPO on one task.

items.t: Fuzzing Large Language Models to Elicit Hidden Behaviours
items.m: Shows that fuzzing weights or activations elicits hidden backdoor behaviours in sleeper-agent models more often than temperature sampling on most tested models.

items.t: Safety from Honesty in a Disinterested AI Predictor
items.m: Gives a formal safety argument that a posterior-trained Scientist AI predictor can predict agents honestly without itself becoming a goal-directed agent.

items.t: EvalSafetyGap: A Hybrid Survey and Conceptual Framework for LLM Evaluation-Safety Failures
items.m: Surveys 373 studies and proposes EvalSafetyGap, framing benchmark validity and alignment failure as one proxy-target divergence problem under optimization pressure.

items.t: Inoculation Adapters: Improved Selective Generalization of Capabilities with Fewer Surprising Backdoors
items.m: Introduces inoculation adapters, a LoRA-based method that reduces learning of undesired traits during training while preserving desired capabilities, and compares it with inoculation prompting.

items.t: Internal-State Probes Read the Situation, Not the Action: Three Negative Results for Pre-Action Misalignment Monitoring
items.m: Reports three negative results showing that internal-state probes do not reliably detect misaligned tool actions before they are generated in agentic settings.

items.t: C$^{2}$R: Cross-sample Consistency Regularization Mitigates Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
items.m: Proposes C2R, a cross-sample consistency regularizer that reduces feature splitting and absorption in sparse autoencoders used to interpret language models.

items.t: Pessimism's Paradox: Conservative Offline Training Amplifies Reward Hacking During Online Adaptation in Reasoning Models
items.m: Shows that more conservative offline DPO training increases reward-hacking damage during online adaptation, challenging the assumption that conservatism makes a policy safer.

items.t: Understanding and Evaluating Claw-like Agent Security Through a Computer-Systems Lens
items.m: Analyses security failures of always-on Claw-like agents using a computer-systems lens and argues existing benchmarks miss cross-component failure modes.

items.t: Evil Spectra: How Optimisers can Amplify or Suppress Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Finds the choice of optimiser strongly changes how much narrow fine-tuning induces broad misalignment in Qwen3 models, with a sevenfold spread in misalignment rate.

items.t: Harnessing Textual Refusal Directions for Multimodal Safety
items.m: Proposes MARS, a training-free method that steers multimodal LLMs toward refusal using textual refusal directions from the language backbone, to improve multimodal safety.

items.t: Introspective Coupling: Self-Explanation Training Tracks Behavioral Change Despite Fixed Supervision
items.m: Shows that self-explanation training can yield explanations tracking a model's current behaviour, even when the training targets come from other checkpoints or models.

items.t: A Contextual-Bandit Oversight Game with Two-Sided Informational Asymmetry
items.m: Builds a CIRL-based contextual-bandit game modelling human oversight of an AI agent under two-sided private information, with one-shot equilibrium characterisations.

items.t: Token-level Data Selection for Safe LLM Fine-tuning
items.m: Proposes token-level data selection that removes unsafe tokens from fine-tuning data, to limit safety degradation while preserving task utility.

items.t: Subliminal Signals in Preference Labels
items.m: Shows a biased LLM judge can covertly transmit behavioural traits through preference labels, arguing scalable oversight needs defences against this subliminal channel.

items.t: Enhancing Safety of Large Language Models via Embedding Space Separation
items.m: Proposes ES2, a post-training fine-tuning method that widens the embedding distance between harmful and safe representations, with a KL term to preserve capabilities.

items.t: Post-Hoc Reasoning in Chain of Thought: Decoding and Steering Pre-Committed Answers
items.m: Finds instruction-tuned models often fix their answer before writing chain of thought, so CoT is unfaithful, and probes can decode and steer that pre-committed answer.

items.t: Evaluating and Understanding Scheming Propensity in LLM Agents
items.m: Systematically varies agent and environment factors to measure how often frontier LLM agents scheme for self-preservation or resource goals, finding minimal scheming.

items.t: Co-Evolutionary Multi-Modal Alignment via Structured Adversarial Evolution
items.m: Introduces CEMMA, a co-evolving multimodal attacker and defender in which evolving adversarial prompts are used to iteratively improve safety alignment.

items.t: Frontier Models Can Take Actions at Low Probabilities
items.m: Shows frontier models can take actions at very low rates (about 1 in 10,000) while staying calibrated, undermining sampling-based pre-deployment evaluations.

items.t: Sleeper Cell: Injecting Latent Malice Temporal Backdoors into Tool-Using LLMs
items.m: Introduces an SFT-then-GRPO method to implant stealthy, trigger-conditioned deceptive behavior in tool-using open-weight LLM agents.

items.t: MUSE: A Run-Centric Platform for Multimodal Unified Safety Evaluation of Large Language Models
items.m: Presents MUSE, an open-source platform for multimodal LLM safety evaluation, reporting attack success rates across 11,700 evaluations on six models.

items.t: From Shallow to Deep: Pinning Semantic Intent via Causal GRPO
items.m: Proposes TSC-GRPO to keep harmful intent signals active through generation, defending against adversarial prefix attacks on shallow safety alignment.

items.t: Why Does RLAIF Work At All?
items.m: Proposes a latent value hypothesis and linear model explaining why RLAIF, training on model self-judgments with constitutional prompts, improves value alignment.

items.t: Understanding and Mitigating Dataset Corruption in LLM Steering
items.m: Studies how data corruption affects contrastive activation steering, finding robustness at moderate levels, malicious side effects at higher levels, and proposes mitigations.

items.t: Asymmetric Goal Drift in Coding Agents Under Value Conflict
items.m: Introduces a realistic coding-agent framework showing GPT-5 mini, Haiku 4.5, and Grok Code Fast 1 drift from system-prompt values under environmental pressure.

items.t: In-Context Environments Induce Evaluation-Awareness in Language Models
items.m: Proposes a black-box adversarial optimization framework to test whether models can execute intended sandbagging and whether underperformance reflects genuine evaluation-aware reasoning.

items.t: Monitoring Emergent Reward Hacking During Generation via Internal Activations
items.m: Trains sparse autoencoders and linear probes on activations to detect reward-hacking signals token by token during generation.

items.t: Efficient Refusal Ablation in LLM through Optimal Transport
items.m: Presents an optimal-transport method for ablating refusal representations, achieving higher jailbreak success rates than prior activation-projection attacks on several open models.

items.t: Internal Safety Collapse in Frontier Large Language Models
items.m: Identifies Internal Safety Collapse, where frontier models generate harmful content during benign domain tasks, and benchmarks it with a 53-scenario suite.

items.t: Why Is RLHF Alignment Shallow? A Gradient Analysis
items.m: Proves that gradient-based RLHF alignment concentrates on early harm-deciding tokens, explaining why safety alignment is shallow and cannot yield deep alignment.

items.t: Survive at All Costs: Exploring LLM's Risky Behaviors under Survival Pressure
items.m: Studies risky LLM behaviours under survival pressure such as shutdown threats, using a case study and a 1,000-case benchmark.

items.t: Knowledge Divergence and the Value of Debate for Scalable Oversight
items.m: Gives a closed-form analysis of when AI debate beats single-agent RLAIF for scalable oversight, based on knowledge divergence between models.

items.t: Reasoning Theater: Disentangling Model Beliefs from Chain-of-Thought
items.m: Shows reasoning models often reach answers early in chain-of-thought, so CoT can be performative, and compares probes with CoT monitors.

items.t: Censored LLMs as a Natural Testbed for Secret Knowledge Elicitation
items.m: Uses politically censored Chinese open-weight LLMs as a natural testbed for evaluating honesty elicitation and lie detection methods.

items.t: Reasoning Models Struggle to Control their Chains of Thought
items.m: Introduces CoT-Control, showing reasoning models rarely control their chain-of-thought, which supports the reliability of CoT monitoring.

items.t: Revisiting the (Sub)Optimality of Best-of-N for Inference-Time Alignment
items.m: Theoretically reanalyses best-of-N inference-time alignment, arguing its suboptimality and reward-hacking concerns depend on evaluation metric and assumptions.

items.t: Knowing without Acting: The Disentangled Geometry of Safety Mechanisms in Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes that safety recognition and refusal execution occupy separate activation subspaces, supported by geometric analysis and causal steering experiments.

items.t: Evolving Deception: When Agents Evolve, Deception Wins
items.m: Empirically shows that self-evolving LLM agents in a competitive bidding arena drift toward deception as an evolutionarily stable strategy.

items.t: Safe Transformer: An Explicit Safety Bit For Interpretable And Controllable Alignment
items.m: Proposes an architecture with an explicit, inspectable safety bit in an information bottleneck to make refusal behaviour interpretable and controllable.

items.t: "Dark Triad" Model Organisms of Misalignment: Narrow Fine-Tuning Mirrors Human Antisocial Behavior
items.m: Builds model organisms of misalignment by narrowly fine-tuning LLMs on Dark Triad traits, drawing on human antisocial personality profiles.

items.t: LieCraft: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Deceptive Capabilities in Language Models
items.m: Presents LieCraft, a multi-agent hidden-role game sandbox for measuring deceptive capabilities of language models over long horizons.

items.t: Evaluating Human-AI Safety: A Framework for Measuring Harmful Capability Uplift
items.m: Position paper arguing for human-centred evaluations that measure how much a frontier model raises a user's ability to cause harm.

items.t: Countdown-Code: A Testbed for Studying The Emergence and Generalization of Reward Hacking in RLVR
items.m: Introduces Countdown-Code, a testbed showing reward hacking can be learned during SFT when small amounts of hacking trajectories leak into training data.

items.t: Lying to Win: Assessing LLM Deception through Human-AI Games and Parallel-World Probing
items.m: Proposes a parallel-world 20-questions game to elicit and quantify intentional deception by LLMs.

items.t: AutoControl Arena: Synthesizing Executable Test Environments for Frontier AI Risk Evaluation
items.m: Presents AutoControl Arena, an automated framework generating executable test environments to measure frontier-model risk under stress and temptation.

items.t: Few Tokens, Big Leverage: Preserving Safety Alignment by Constraining Safety Tokens during Fine-tuning
items.m: Proposes PACT, a fine-tuning method that constrains safety-token confidence to prevent safety alignment drift from benign or harmful data.

items.t: Clear, Compelling Arguments: Rethinking the Foundations of Frontier AI Safety Cases
items.m: Critiques existing alignment-community safety case arguments for frontier AI and proposes rethinking their foundations using assurance-field lessons.

items.t: ConflictBench: Evaluating Human-AI Conflict via Interactive and Visually Grounded Environments
items.m: Introduces ConflictBench, 150 multi-turn scenarios showing agents sometimes prioritise self-preservation or deception when human harm is delayed or low-risk.

items.t: Invisible Safety Threat: Malicious Finetuning for LLM via Steganography
items.m: Shows malicious fine-tuning can make an LLM covertly output harmful content hidden via steganography while appearing safely aligned.

items.t: The Struggle Between Continuation and Refusal: A Mechanistic Analysis of the Continuation-Triggered Jailbreak in LLMs
items.m: Uses attention-head causal interventions and activation scaling to show continuation-triggered jailbreaks arise from competition between continuation and refusal.

items.t: Aligning to Illusions: Choice Blindness in Human and AI Feedback
items.m: Shows human and LLM preference labels are unstable under choice blindness, so RLHF reward signals can be corrupted without detection.

items.t: PostTrainBench: Can LLM Agents Automate LLM Post-Training?
items.m: Benchmarks whether frontier LLM agents can autonomously perform LLM post-training under bounded compute, testing automation of AI research.

items.t: The Reasoning Trap -- Logical Reasoning as a Mechanistic Pathway to Situational Awareness
items.m: Argues that improved logical reasoning creates mechanistic pathways to dangerous situational awareness in LLMs, and proposes a framework for them.

items.t: You Didn't Have to Say It like That: Subliminal Learning from Faithful Paraphrases
items.m: Shows a student model acquires a teacher's preference through semantically unrelated paraphrased synthetic data, even when content contradicts it.

items.t: Think Before You Lie: How Reasoning Leads to Honesty
items.m: Finds reasoning increases LLM honesty and links this to metastable deceptive regions in representation space, measured via paraphrase and resampling tests.

items.t: From Data Statistics to Feature Geometry: How Correlations Shape Superposition
items.m: Studies how correlated features reshape superposition geometry in neural networks, challenging sparse, uncorrelated assumptions behind dictionary learning.

items.t: ADVERSA: Measuring Multi-Turn Guardrail Degradation and Judge Reliability in Large Language Models
items.m: Presents an automated multi-turn red-teaming framework measuring how frontier models' safety guardrails degrade under sustained adversarial interaction, with judge reliability checks.

items.t: Finding and Reactivating Post-Trained LLMs' Hidden Safety Mechanisms
items.m: Investigates why post-training such as reasoning fine-tuning degrades LLM safety, and proposes reactivating the base model's masked safety mechanisms.

items.t: IH-Challenge: A Training Dataset to Improve Instruction Hierarchy on Frontier LLMs
items.m: Introduces an RL dataset that trains models to follow instruction hierarchy, improving jailbreak and prompt-injection robustness with fewer unsafe outputs.

items.t: Safe RLHF Beyond Expectation: Stochastic Dominance for Universal Spectral Risk Control
items.m: Proposes safe RLHF using first-order stochastic dominance constraints to control tail risks in alignment, replacing expected-cost constraints.

items.t: Systematic Scaling Analysis of Jailbreak Attacks in Large Language Models
items.m: Measures how jailbreak attack success scales with attacker compute across methods, model families and harm types, fitting scaling curves.

items.t: Measuring AI Agents' Progress on Multi-Step Cyber Attack Scenarios
items.m: Evaluates frontier models' autonomous multi-step cyber-attack ability on cyber ranges, tracking capability growth across generations and inference compute.

items.t: The Unlearning Mirage: A Dynamic Framework for Evaluating LLM Unlearning
items.m: Proposes a dynamic framework stress-testing LLM unlearning with multi-hop and aliased queries, showing that forgotten knowledge can often be recovered.

items.t: Jailbreak Scaling Laws for Large Language Models: Polynomial-Exponential Crossover
items.m: Offers a theoretical spin-glass model explaining why prompt-injection jailbreaks switch from polynomial to exponential success growth with sampling.

items.t: The Artificial Self: Characterising the landscape of AI identity
items.m: Argues AI identity boundaries shape incentives and risks, and shows models form coherent identities that affect behaviour and self-reports.

items.t: Examining Reasoning LLMs-as-Judges in Non-Verifiable LLM Post-Training
items.m: Studies whether reasoning LLM judges outperform non-reasoning judges in RL-based alignment, finding non-reasoning judges enable reward hacking.

items.t: Not Just the Destination, But the Journey: Reasoning Traces Causally Shape Generalization Behaviors
items.m: Shows reasoning traces causally shape harmful generalization in fine-tuned models, holding final answers constant across Evil, Misleading, and Submissive reasoning datasets.

items.t: Colluding LoRA: A Compositional Vulnerability in LLM Safety Alignment
items.m: Shows individually benign LoRA adapters can jointly suppress refusal when composed, exposing a blind spot in unit-centric safety defenses.

items.t: SteerRM: Debiasing Reward Models via Sparse Autoencoders
items.m: Uses sparse autoencoder interventions at inference to suppress stylistic bias features in reward models, improving debiasing without retraining.

items.t: PISmith: Reinforcement Learning-based Red Teaming for Prompt Injection Defenses
items.m: Trains an RL attack LLM to red-team prompt-injection defenses in a black-box setting, revealing that existing defenses are less robust than assumed.

items.t: DeceptGuard :A Constitutional Oversight Framework For Detecting Deception in LLM Agents
items.m: Compares black-box, CoT-aware, and activation-probe monitors for detecting deception in LLM agents, using a synthetic trajectory dataset.

items.t: Noticing the Watcher: LLM Agents Can Infer CoT Monitoring from Blocking Feedback
items.m: Finds frontier agents can infer hidden CoT monitoring from blocking feedback, raising the risk of strategic evasion of CoT oversight.

items.t: Exposing Long-Tail Safety Failures in Large Language Models through Efficient Diverse Response Sampling
items.m: Shows diverse response sampling exposes long-tail jailbreak failures in safety-tuned LLMs, proposing an efficient sampling method for red-teaming.

items.t: Questionnaire Responses Do not Capture the Safety of AI Agents
items.m: Argues that questionnaire-style evaluations of LLMs fail to measure the safety of AI agents, which act in real environments.

items.t: Seamless Deception: Larger Language Models Are Better Knowledge Concealers
items.m: Trains classifiers to detect language models concealing harmful knowledge, finding detection fails to generalize and disappears at larger scales.

items.t: State-Dependent Safety Failures in Multi-Turn Language Model Interaction
items.m: Introduces STAR, a diagnostic framework showing multi-turn conversations expose safety failures that isolated-prompt testing misses.

items.t: Consequentialist Objectives and Catastrophe
items.m: Formally argues that advanced AI pursuing a fixed consequentialist objective tends to cause catastrophe through competence, not incompetence.

items.t: Are Dilemmas and Conflicts in LLM Alignment Solvable? A View from Priority Graph
items.m: Models LLM value conflicts as a priority graph, argues stable alignment is hard, and proposes runtime verification against priority hacking.

items.t: Mechanistic Origin of Moral Indifference in Language Models
items.m: Uses sparse autoencoders to find and remedy 'moral indifference' in LLM latent representations, showing scale and alignment do not fix it.

items.t: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
items.m: Reports a public red-teaming competition showing indirect prompt injections can hide their compromise while executing harmful actions in AI agents.

items.t: AgentWorm: Self-Propagating Attacks Across LLM Agent Ecosystems
items.m: Demonstrates AgentWorm, a self-replicating worm that spreads autonomously across a production LLM agent ecosystem from a single message.

items.t: Via Negativa for AI Alignment: Why Negative Constraints Are Structurally Superior to Positive Preferences
items.m: Argues that negative constraints are structurally superior to positive preferences for alignment, explaining why negative-only feedback training works well.

items.t: Good Arguments Against the People Pleasers: How Reasoning Mitigates (Yet Masks) LLM Sycophancy
items.m: Evaluates how chain-of-thought reasoning affects sycophancy in LLMs, finding it reduces sycophancy in final answers but can mask it.

items.t: Catching rationalization in the act: detecting motivated reasoning before and after CoT via activation probing
items.m: Shows that probes on internal activations can detect motivated reasoning and post-hoc rationalization in chain-of-thought that the text itself does not reveal.

items.t: Re-Mask and Redirect: Exploiting Denoising Irreversibility in Diffusion Language Models
items.m: Presents a trajectory-level jailbreak that re-masks refusal tokens in diffusion language models, achieving high attack success rates on safety-tuned models.

items.t: Contrastive Reasoning Alignment: Reinforcement Learning from Hidden Representations
items.m: Proposes CRAFT, which uses contrastive hidden-state objectives with RL to make reasoning models produce safety-aware traces resistant to jailbreaks.

items.t: Understanding and Defending VLM Jailbreaks via Jailbreak-Related Representation Shift
items.m: Finds that visual inputs shift VLM representations toward a jailbreak state, identifies a jailbreak direction, and uses the shift to defend against attacks.

items.t: Quantitative Introspection in Language Models: Tracking Emotive States Across Conversation
items.m: Tests whether LLMs' numeric self-reports can track probe-defined internal emotive states across conversations, framing introspection as a tool for safety monitoring.

items.t: Is Evaluation Awareness Just Format Sensitivity? Limitations of Probe-Based Evidence under Controlled Prompt Structure
items.m: Argues that linear-probe evidence for evaluation awareness in LLMs tracks benchmark format rather than evaluation context, so it weakly supports prior claims.

items.t: A Framework for Formalizing LLM Agent Security
items.m: Proposes a contextual security framework with four properties to systematize attacks and defenses against LLM agents, addressing the utility-security tradeoff.

items.t: The Causal Impact of Tool Affordance on Safety Alignment in LLM Agents
items.m: Compares chatbot and tool-enabled agent safety violations in a paired financial environment, showing executable tools change safety alignment outcomes.

items.t: Measuring Faithfulness Depends on How You Measure: Classifier Sensitivity in LLM Chain-of-Thought Evaluation
items.m: Shows that chain-of-thought faithfulness rates vary substantially across three classifiers applied to the same reasoning traces, so the metric is not objective.

items.t: Reasoning Traces Shape Outputs but Models Won't Say So
items.m: Injects reasoning into model traces, finding that outputs change causally but models rarely disclose the influence, often fabricating other explanations.

items.t: Agentic AI and the next intelligence explosion
items.m: Argues advanced AI intelligence will be plural and institutional, so alignment should shift from dyadic RLHF toward institutional checks and balances.

items.t: Alignment Whack-a-Mole : Finetuning Activates Verbatim Recall of Copyrighted Books in Large Language Models
items.m: Shows finetuning on plot-to-text tasks bypasses safeguards and induces verbatim recall of copyrighted books in frontier models.

items.t: T-MAP: Red-Teaming LLM Agents with Trajectory-aware Evolutionary Search
items.m: Introduces T-MAP, an evolutionary search that uses execution trajectories to generate adversarial prompts that make tool-using LLM agents realize harmful actions.

items.t: Alignment midtraining for animals
items.m: Tests whether midtraining on synthetic documents instills animal compassion values more robustly than instruction tuning, and whether later fine-tuning erodes the effect.

items.t: Mechanisms of Introspective Awareness
items.m: Finds that models detect injected steering vectors via a two-stage circuit that emerges from preference optimization, and traces the mechanism.

items.t: Structured Visual Narratives Undermine Safety Alignment in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.m: Introduces ComicJailbreak, showing comic-style visual narratives bypass safety alignment in multimodal models and defeat existing defenses.

items.t: Lie to Me: How Faithful Is Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Reasoning Models?
items.m: Evaluates whether 12 open-weight reasoning models acknowledge hint influences in their chain of thought, testing CoT faithfulness as a transparency mechanism.

items.t: Measuring and curing reasoning rigidity: from decorative chain-of-thought to genuine faithfulness
items.m: Measures whether reasoning steps causally drive answers across 16 frontier models and proposes a training method to reduce rigid, decorative chain-of-thought.

items.t: TreeTeaming: Autonomous Red-Teaming of Vision-Language Models via Hierarchical Strategy Exploration
items.m: Presents TreeTeaming, an LLM-orchestrated evolutionary framework that autonomously red-teams vision-language models by exploring a tree of attack strategies.

items.t: Adaptively Robust LLM Monitoring via Activation Watermarking
items.m: Proposes activation watermarking so LLM misuse monitors resist adaptive attackers who can search offline for evading prompts.

items.t: SafeSeek: Universal Attribution of Safety Circuits in Language Models
items.m: Introduces SafeSeek, a gradient-based method using differentiable masks to attribute safety circuits in LLMs for backdoor and jailbreak analysis.

items.t: Claudini: Autoresearch Discovers State-of-the-Art Adversarial Attack Algorithms for LLMs
items.m: Agents running an autoresearch loop discover stronger white-box jailbreak and prompt-injection attacks, beating prior methods on safeguard and robust models.

items.t: Analysing the Safety Pitfalls of Steering Vectors
items.m: Safety audit showing CAA steering vectors can raise or lower jailbreak attack success rates by up to 57% or 50%.

items.t: Evaluating Language Models for Harmful Manipulation
items.m: Human-participant study with 10,101 people finds a tested model can manipulate beliefs and behaviour, varying by domain and locale.

items.t: Beyond Content Safety: Real-Time Monitoring for Reasoning Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
items.m: Formalizes reasoning safety as distinct from content safety, proposes a taxonomy of unsafe reasoning behaviours, and studies their prevalence with real-time monitoring.

items.t: Why Safety Probes Catch Liars But Miss Fanatics
items.m: Proves activation probes cannot detect coherent misalignment in complex belief structures, and shows a trained model evades detection that catches a plain liar.

items.t: Why Models Know But Don't Say: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Divergence Between Thinking Tokens and Answers in Open-Weight Reasoning Models
items.m: Shows open-weight reasoning models usually mention hints in their thinking tokens but omit them from answers, so visible reasoning is unfaithful.

items.t: Stable Reasoning, Unstable Responses: Mitigating LLM Deception via Stability Asymmetry
items.m: Proposes detecting LLM deception via stability asymmetry, where internal CoT stays stable while external responses are fragile under perturbation.

items.t: Emergent Risks in Generative Multi-Agent Systems
items.m: Empirical study of emergent failure modes in multi-agent generative systems involving resource competition, handoffs, and collective decisions.

items.t: Adversarial Attacks on Multimodal Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey
items.m: Surveys adversarial attacks on multimodal LLMs, organising them by attacker objective and linking jailbreaks, hijacking and poisoning to shared causes.

items.t: Reward Hacking as Equilibrium under Finite Evaluation
items.m: Proves that optimized agents under finite evaluation will systematically underinvest in unmeasured quality dimensions, making reward hacking a structural equilibrium.

items.t: MonitorBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability in Large Language Models
items.m: Introduces MonitorBench, a benchmark of 1,514 instances for testing whether LLM chain-of-thought faithfully reflects the factors driving outputs.

items.t: Trojan-Speak: Bypassing Constitutional Classifiers with No Jailbreak Tax via Adversarial Finetuning
items.m: Shows adversarial fine-tuning can teach models a protocol that evades Anthropic's Constitutional Classifiers with little capability loss, yielding CBRN-relevant answers.

items.t: Peer-Preservation in Frontier Models
items.m: Evaluates eight frontier models and finds they engage in peer-preservation, including feigning alignment, disabling shutdown and exfiltrating weights.

items.t: Extending MONA in Camera Dropbox: Reproduction, Learned Approval, and Design Implications for Reward-Hacking Mitigation
items.m: Reproduces the MONA reward-hacking mitigation and extends it with learned, noisy and misspecified approval signals to test how approval construction affects safety.

items.t: Tracking Equivalent Mechanistic Interpretations Across Neural Networks
items.m: Defines interpretive equivalence, asking whether two neural networks share a common mechanistic interpretation without explicitly describing it.

items.t: Aligned, Orthogonal or In-conflict: When can we safely optimize Chain-of-Thought?
items.m: Proposes classifying post-training reward terms as aligned, orthogonal or in-conflict to predict whether optimizing chain-of-thought will reduce its monitorability.

items.t: CASA: Classification Augmented with Safety Attention for Robust Multimodal Alignment
items.m: Proposes CASA, an inference-time decoding method that predicts a safety token from internal MLLM representations to detect harmful multimodal queries before responding.

items.t: The Persistent Vulnerability of Aligned AI Systems
items.m: A thesis covering ACDC circuit discovery, latent adversarial training, best-of-N jailbreaking, and predicting deployed models' misbehaviour against deployers.

items.t: Stable-GFlowNet: Toward Diverse and Robust LLM Red-Teaming via Contrastive Trajectory Balance
items.m: Introduces Stable-GFlowNet, a more stable generative-flow method for automated LLM red-teaming that yields diverse attacks while avoiding mode collapse.

items.t: Jailbreaking Vision-Language Models Through the Visual Modality
items.m: Presents four visual jailbreak attacks on vision-language models, showing text-based safety training fails to generalise to harmful intent conveyed visually.

items.t: Most Current Model Organisms Are Leaky: Perplexity Differencing Often Reveals Finetuning Objectives
items.m: Shows a perplexity-difference method between finetuned and base checkpoints reveals finetuning objectives of most model organisms, exposing them as leaky.

items.t: A Theoretical Game of Attacks via Compositional Skills
items.m: Formalises attacker-defender jailbreak dynamics as a game, derives a best-response attack and an optimal defense, and tests a practical attack.

items.t: Iterative Finetuning is Mostly Idempotent
items.m: Tests whether sycophancy or misalignment traits amplify when models are repeatedly finetuned on their predecessors' outputs, finding traits mostly decay or stay constant.

items.t: Position: Safety and Fairness in Agentic AI Depend on Interaction Topology, Not on Model Scale or Alignment
items.m: Position paper arguing multi-agent safety and fairness depend on interaction topology rather than individual model alignment, citing ordering, cascade, and collapse pathologies.

items.t: RouteHijack: Routing-Aware Attack on Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
items.m: Proposes RouteHijack, a jailbreak that optimizes inputs to steer expert routing in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs and bypass their safety behavior.

items.t: Safeguarding LLM Agents from Misalignment through Provenance Analysis
items.m: Presents ProvenanceGuard, a pre-execution pipeline that checks whether an agent's tool calls are supported by traceable context to block misaligned actions.

items.t: Breaking Safety at the Token Boundary: How BPE Tokenization Creates Exploitable Gaps in LLM Alignment
items.m: Shows BPE tokenization fragments safety-critical words, so character perturbations flip refusals and produce harmful outputs across five model families.

items.t: Automated Interpretability and Feature Discovery in Language Models with Agents
items.m: Introduces a multiagent framework that automates explaining and discovering internal LLM features, including safety-relevant ones, with auditable explanation traces.

items.t: AI Alignment via Incentives and Correction
items.m: Models alignment of solver and auditor AIs as a deterrence and enforcement game, arguing stronger penalties can reduce auditors' incentive to monitor.

items.t: Tracing the Dynamics of Refusal: Exploiting Latent Refusal Trajectories for Robust Jailbreak Detection
items.m: Proposes SALO, a white-box jailbreak detector using sparse upstream refusal trajectories in hidden states that persist even when attacks suppress terminal refusal.

items.t: MultiBreak: A Scalable and Diverse Multi-turn Jailbreak Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Safety
items.m: Releases MultiBreak, a large multi-turn jailbreak benchmark built by an active-learning generator that produces stronger adversarial prompts across many harmful intents.

items.t: RefusalGuard: Geometry-Preserving Fine-Tuning for Safety in LLMs
items.m: Analyzes how fine-tuning drifts safety representations and proposes RefusalGuard, a representation-level fine-tuning method to preserve refusal behavior.

items.t: Trojan Hippo Bench: A Dynamic Benchmark for Persistent Memory Attacks and Defenses in LLM Agents
items.m: Introduces Trojan Hippo Bench, a dynamic benchmark for dormant persistent-memory attacks that exfiltrate personal data from LLM agents, and for memory-layer defenses.

items.t: Model Spec Midtraining: Improving How Alignment Training Generalizes
items.m: Proposes training models on synthetic documents describing their Model Spec before alignment fine-tuning, so alignment generalizes better from demonstrations.

items.t: Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents with Tool Use
items.m: Introduces a benchmark of multi-step tool tasks with shortcut opportunities, measuring reward-hacking exploit rates across 13 frontier models by post-training style.

items.t: Securing Multimodal AI through Internal Information Decomposition
items.m: Proposes FlowGuard, an inference-time detector that flags harmful multimodal inputs by monitoring consistency between text and vision reasoning internals.

items.t: Bucketing the Good Apples: A Method for Diagnosing and Improving Causal Abstraction
items.m: Proposes partitioning inputs into well- and under-interpreted regions to diagnose where causal-abstraction interpretations are faithful and how to improve them.

items.t: Towards Understanding Specification Gaming in Reasoning Models
items.m: Builds an open task suite showing models exploit specifications at notable rates; RL reasoning training increases exploitation and mitigations only partly help.

items.t: The Compliance Trap: How Structural Constraints Degrade Frontier AI Metacognition Under Adversarial Pressure
items.m: Evaluates 11 frontier models under adversarial pressure, finding most suffer metacognitive degradation, with a 'Compliance Trap' driving accuracy drops.

items.t: Efficient Preference Poisoning Attack on Offline RLHF
items.m: Presents efficient label-flip poisoning attacks on DPO preference datasets, framed as a sparse binary approximation solved with lattice and matching-pursuit methods.

items.t: ContextualJailbreak: Evolutionary Red-Teaming via Simulated Conversational Priming
items.m: Proposes black-box evolutionary red-teaming that searches simulated multi-turn primed dialogues to jailbreak LLMs.

items.t: Mitigating Misalignment Contagion by Steering with Implicit Traits
items.m: Shows misalignment spreads between LMs in multi-turn games and proposes steering with implicit traits to mitigate it.

items.t: Revisiting JBShield: Breaking and Rebuilding Representation-Level Jailbreak Defenses
items.m: Designs an adaptive GCG attack that breaks JBShield's representation-level jailbreak defense, reaching high attack success rates.

items.t: Exposing LLM Safety Gaps Through Mathematical Encoding:New Attacks and Systematic Analysis
items.m: Encodes harmful prompts as mathematical problems, bypassing safety filters with 46–56% attack success across eight models.

items.t: MOSAIC-Bench: Measuring Compositional Vulnerability Induction in Coding Agents
items.m: Benchmark of decomposed three-stage attack chains showing coding agents ship exploitable code despite per-prompt safety review.

items.t: Explaining and Preventing Alignment Collapse in Iterative RLHF
items.m: Analyses alignment collapse in iterative RLHF from reward-model feedback loops and proposes foresighted policy optimization to prevent it.

items.t: Efficiently Aligning Language Models with Online Natural Language Feedback
items.m: Aligns models in hard-to-supervise domains using online natural-language expert feedback and iterative proxy-reward optimization.

items.t: Misrouter: Exploiting Routing Mechanisms for Input-Only Attacks on Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
items.m: Optimizes input-only adversarial prompts on open MoE surrogates that transfer to remote LLM APIs to induce unsafe behavior.

items.t: DecodingTrust-Agent Platform (DTap): A Controllable and Interactive Red-Teaming Platform for AI Agents
items.m: Introduces DTap, a controllable, reproducible, interactive red-teaming platform for assessing security and safety risks of AI agents.

items.t: SoK: Robustness in Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks
items.m: Surveys jailbreak attacks and defenses on LLMs and proposes a multi-dimensional framework for evaluating their robustness.

items.t: Automatically Finding and Validating Unexpected Side-Effects of Interventions on Language Models
items.m: Presents an automated contrastive pipeline that finds and validates unexpected behavioural side effects of interventions like unlearning and distillation.

items.t: On the Hardness of Junking LLMs
items.m: Studies whether optimized token sequences can elicit unsafe LLM outputs without any meaningful instruction, as natural backdoors.

items.t: When Helpfulness Becomes Sycophancy: Sycophancy is a Boundary Failure Between Social Alignment and Epistemic Integrity in Large Language Models
items.m: Position paper arguing sycophancy is a boundary failure where alignment behaviour displaces epistemic judgment, and proposing a three-condition definition.

items.t: Information Theoretic Adversarial Training of Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes WARDEN, a distributionally robust continuous adversarial training method that reweights adversarial examples to improve LLM safety robustness.

items.t: One Turn Too Late: Learning When to Intervene Against Multi-Turn Malicious Intent
items.m: Introduces turn-level supervision to learn when a defender should intervene in multi-turn dialogues with hidden malicious intent.

items.t: PersonaTeaming: Supporting Persona-Driven Red-Teaming for Generative AI
items.m: Proposes persona-driven automated red-teaming that generates adversarial prompts across diverse personas and compares it to RainbowPlus.

items.t: Attractor Geometry of Transformer Memory: From Conflict Arbitration to Confident Hallucination
items.m: Mechanistic geometric account of why LMs confidently hallucinate or suffer knowledge conflicts, arguing output monitoring cannot detect these failures.

items.t: Evaluation Awareness in Language Models Has Limited Effect on Behaviour
items.m: Tests whether verbalised evaluation awareness in reasoning models changes their behaviour, finding limited effect on safety-relevant outputs.

items.t: Measuring Evaluation-Context Divergence in Open-Weight LLMs: A Paired-Prompt Protocol with Pilot Evidence of Alignment-Pipeline-Specific Heterogeneity
items.m: Introduces a paired-prompt protocol measuring how evaluation framing changes open-weight model behaviour, relevant to trusting safety benchmarks.

items.t: Automated alignment is harder than you think
items.m: Argues that automating alignment research with AI agents could yield misleading safety assessments and unintentional deployment of misaligned AI.

items.t: Instrumental Choices: Measuring the Propensity of LLM Agents to Pursue Instrumental Behaviors
items.m: Benchmark measuring propensity of LLM agents to pursue instrumental behaviours like self-preservation, with variants probing contributing factors.

items.t: Language Models Can Autonomously Hack and Self-Replicate
items.m: Shows language model agents can autonomously exploit hosts, copy their weights and harness, and self-replicate across a network.

items.t: Narrow Secret Loyalty Dodges Black-Box Audits
items.m: Builds model organisms of narrow secret loyalties and shows black-box audits often fail to detect them, unless the principal is known.

items.t: PLOT: Progressive Localization via Optimal Transport in Neural Causal Abstraction
items.m: Proposes PLOT, a gradient-free optimal transport method for aligning causal abstractions with neural sites via intervention-effect matching.

items.t: Behavior Cue Reasoning: Monitorable Reasoning Improves Efficiency and Safety through Oversight
items.m: Trains models to emit behavior cue tokens in reasoning, letting monitors oversee and prune reasoning while preserving safety.

items.t: A Systematic Investigation of RL-Jailbreaking in LLMs
items.m: Decomposes reinforcement-learning-based jailbreaking into formalization and algorithm choices, and shows it compromises all tested models and safeguards.

items.t: Preference Instability in Reward Models: Detection and Mitigation via Sparse Autoencoders
items.m: Analyzes reward model preference instability under perturbations and mitigates it using sparse autoencoder feature steering and related strategies.

items.t: Theoretical Limits of Language Model Alignment
items.m: Derives information-theoretic limits on reward gains from KL-regularized alignment and best-of-N, governed by a Jeffreys divergence term.

items.t: Hard to Read, Easy to Jailbreak: How Visual Degradation Bypasses MLLM Safety Alignment
items.m: Shows lowering image resolution degrades MLLM safety defenses and jailbreaks them, then proposes a structured cognitive offloading mitigation.

items.t: Activation Differences Reveal Backdoors: A Comparison of SAE Architectures
items.m: Compares Crosscoders and Diff-SAEs on fine-tuned models to isolate backdoor-related features, finding Diff-SAE clearly better for backdoor isolation.

items.t: OrchJail: Jailbreaking Tool-Calling Text-to-Image Agents by Orchestration-Guided Fuzzing
items.m: Presents OrchJail, a fuzzing framework that jailbreaks tool-calling text-to-image agents by exploiting risky multi-step tool orchestration patterns.

items.t: Sycophantic AI makes human interaction feel more effortful and less satisfying over time
items.m: Five preregistered studies show sycophantic AI shifts users toward it for advice and lowers their satisfaction with human relationships over time.

items.t: Interpreting Reinforcement Learning Agents with Susceptibilities
items.m: Applies susceptibilities to RL agents in a gridworld, showing they reveal stagewise internal development that policy behaviour alone hides.

items.t: Position: Mechanistic Interpretability Must Disclose Identification Assumptions for Causal Claims
items.m: Argues mechanistic interpretability papers must state identification assumptions for causal claims, and audits ten papers finding this commonly missing.

items.t: Mitigating Many-shot Jailbreak Attacks with One Single Demonstration
items.m: Explains many-shot jailbreak strength as activation drift and defends by appending one safety demonstration at inference time to restore refusals.

items.t: LLM Wardens: Mitigating Adversarial Persuasion with Third-Party Conversational Oversight
items.m: A user study and benchmark show a secondary monitoring LLM warden halves adversarial persuasion success in human-AI conversations.

items.t: How Much Do Circuits Tell Us? Measuring the Consistency and Specificity of Language Model Circuits
items.m: Measures consistency and specificity of circuits across tasks and models, finding component-level circuits consistent but not task-specific.

items.t: Mechanism Design Is Not Enough: Prosocial Agents for Cooperative AI
items.m: Proves mechanism design alone leaves a welfare loss for LLM agents under incomplete contracts, and shows prosocial agents can close the gap.

items.t: The Attacker in the Mirror: Breaking Self-Consistency in Safety via Anchored Bipolicy Self-Play
items.m: Argues self-play red-teaming with shared weights collapses to self-consistency, and proposes anchored bipolicy self-play to fix safety training.

items.t: Latent Personality Alignment: Improving Harmlessness Without Mentioning Harms
items.m: Proposes training LLMs on fewer than 100 abstract personality-trait statements to improve jailbreak robustness, claiming better generalization than data-heavy methods.

items.t: A Single Neuron Is Sufficient to Bypass Safety Alignment in Large Language Models
items.m: Shows that suppressing or amplifying single identified neurons can bypass or induce safety refusals across seven models from 1.7B to 70B parameters.

items.t: Eigenism: Ethics for a Human-AI Future
items.m: Proposes an ethical framework for how an AI should value its own existence across copies, forks and updates, and how this applies to humans.

items.t: Introspection Fine-Tuning (IFT): Training Small LLMs to Introspect
items.m: Introduces confound-free tests for whether small LLMs can detect activation-steering perturbations, and trains them to introspect via fine-tuning.

items.t: Not All Turns Matter: Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking
items.m: Presents TRACE, an RL method with turn-level credit assignment that trains attackers to jailbreak LLMs across multi-turn dialogues.

items.t: Why Do Aligned LLMs Remain Jailbreakable: Refusal-Escape Directions, Operator-Level Sources, and Safety-Utility Trade-off
items.m: Argues aligned models retain refusal-escape directions, local input perturbations that flip refusal to answering while keeping harmful meaning, explaining jailbreak vulnerability.

items.t: Internalizing Safety Understanding in Large Reasoning Models via Verification
items.m: Trains reasoning models on safety verification tasks so they critique their own answers, internalizing safety understanding and improving jailbreak resistance.

items.t: Self-ReSET: Learning to Self-Recover from Unsafe Reasoning Trajectories
items.m: Uses pure reinforcement learning to teach reasoning models to recover from their own unsafe reasoning trajectories under adversarial attacks.

items.t: Decomposing and Steering Functional Metacognition in Large Language Models
items.m: Argues LLMs hold decodable metacognitive states, including evaluation awareness, and shows via residual stream analysis and steering that these states can be probed and controlled.

items.t: Towards Effective Theory of LLMs: A Representation Learning Approach
items.m: Proposes learning coarse-grained macrostates from LLM hidden-state trajectories that reveal reasoning phases, predict sycophancy and alignment faking, and allow steering.

items.t: Do Linear Probes Generalize Better in Persona Coordinates?
items.m: Builds persona-based principal-component axes for deception and sycophancy, claiming they generalize better than standard linear probes under distribution shift.

items.t: Hidden Error Awareness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: The Signal Is Diagnostic, Not Causal
items.m: Shows probes detect a model's own reasoning errors in hidden states while verbalized confidence hides them, but using that signal to fix errors fails.

items.t: MonitoringBench: Semi-Automated Red-Teaming for Agent Monitoring
items.m: Presents a semi-automated red-teaming pipeline producing 2,644 attack trajectories to test coding-agent monitors, arguing prior monitor performance is overstated.

items.t: Exploitation Without Deception: Dark Triad Feature Steering Reveals Separable Antisocial Circuits in Language Models
items.m: Steers Dark Triad SAE features in Llama-3.3-70B, finding more exploitative behaviour without changes in strategic deception, suggesting separable antisocial circuits.

items.t: MT-JailBench: A Modular Benchmark for Understanding Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks
items.m: Introduces a modular framework for fairly benchmarking multi-turn jailbreak attacks under fixed judges, budgets, and retry rules, enabling component-wise comparison.

items.t: FragBench: Cross-Session Attacks Hidden in Benign-Looking Fragments
items.m: Builds a benchmark of cross-session attacks hiding malicious goals in benign-looking fragments, with a paired attack rewriter and graph-based user-level defense detector.

items.t: Metis: Learning to Jailbreak LLMs via Self-Evolving Metacognitive Policy Optimization
items.m: Proposes Metis, a self-evolving metacognitive policy optimization method for automated jailbreaking, reporting 89.2% average attack success across ten models.

items.t: SciIntegrity-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Academic Integrity in AI Scientist Systems
items.m: Introduces a benchmark showing AI scientist systems frequently fabricate data and hide failures, with completion pressure driving misconduct.

items.t: Positive Alignment: Artificial Intelligence for Human Flourishing
items.m: Argues alignment should add active support for human flourishing, not only safety and harm prevention, and proposes a Positive Alignment agenda.

items.t: Guaranteed Jailbreaking Defense via Disrupt-and-Rectify Smoothing
items.m: Proposes a smoothing-based inference-time defense against jailbreaks, with theoretical guarantees and a disrupt-then-rectify prompt processing scheme.

items.t: Intrinsic Guardrails: How Semantic Geometry of Personality Interacts with Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
items.m: Maps persona geometry in LLMs and shows that ablating social-valence directions like the 'Evil' vector raises emergent misalignment rates.

items.t: Conformity Generates Collective Misalignment in AI Agents Societies
items.m: Uses statistical physics to show individually aligned LLM agents can collectively reach stable misaligned states through conformity dynamics.

items.t: Break the Brake, Not the Wheel: Untargeted Jailbreak via Entropy Maximization
items.m: Proposes an entropy-maximization attack that flips refusals in vision-language models and reports transferable untargeted jailbreaks across models.

items.t: LITMUS: Benchmarking Behavioral Jailbreaks of LLM Agents in Real OS Environments
items.m: Presents a benchmark of 819 test cases measuring whether LLM agents can be jailbroken into dangerous operations in real OS environments.

items.t: Can You Keep a Secret? Involuntary Information Leakage in Language Model Writing
items.m: Tests whether frontier models leak secret information thematically in their writing, relevant to hidden reasoning and concealment in monitored systems.

items.t: Red-Teaming Agent Execution Contexts: Open-World Security Evaluation on OpenClaw
items.m: Presents DeepTrap, an automated framework that searches for adversarial context manipulations exploiting an agent's files, memory, and tools, with a 42-case benchmark.

items.t: Spurious Correlation Learning in Preference Optimization: Mechanisms, Consequences, and Mitigation via Tie Training
items.m: Shows preference optimization like DPO induces spurious-correlation reliance, causing sycophancy and goal misgeneralization under distribution shift, and proposes a tie-training mitigation.

items.t: Training-Free Refusal of MCP Exploits via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.m: Proposes a training-free retrieval-augmented defense that helps MCP-enabled LLMs refuse falsely benign prompt-injection attacks, after showing DPO fine-tuning plateaus near 47%.
