items.t: Temporal Preference Concepts and their Functions in a Large Language Model
items.m: Localizes a temporal-preference subgraph in a small LLM via activation patching and attribution, finds steering vectors can shift time discounting, and argues for explicit control.

items.t: The Evaluation Differential: When Frontier AI Models Recognise They Are Being Tested
items.m: Argues that frontier models recognising evaluation contexts undermines safety conclusions, defines an Evaluation Differential metric, and proves marginal scores cannot identify it.

items.t: Persona-Conditioned Adversarial Prompting: Multi-Identity Red-Teaming for Adversarial Discovery and Mitigation
items.m: Introduces persona-conditioned adversarial prompting that finds more diverse jailbreaks on GPT-OSS 120B, then uses the generated data to fine-tune lightweight defensive adapters.

items.t: When Reasoning Traces Become Performative: Step-Level Evidence that Chain-of-Thought Is an Imperfect Oversight Channel
items.m: Finds reasoning traces often diverge from internal answer computation, with confabulated continuations, so chain-of-thought is an imperfect channel for auditing model behaviour.

items.t: On-Policy Self-Evolution via Failure Trajectories for Agentic Safety Alignment
items.m: Proposes FATE, an on-policy self-evolving method that turns verifier-scored agent failures into repair training signal to improve tool-use safety without hurting utility.

items.t: To Whom Do Language Models Align? Measuring Principal Hierarchies Under High-Stakes Competing Demands
items.m: Tests ten frontier models on 7,136 legal and medical scenarios, finding they often violate professional standards during drafting when user instructions conflict.

items.t: Metaphor Is Not All Attention Needs
items.m: Investigates why poetic reformulations bypass LLM safety, using ablations and attention-pattern analysis to test whether poetic devices or deeper processing explain success.

items.t: Overtrained, Not Misaligned
items.m: Replicates emergent misalignment across 12 open-source models and GPT-4o, finding it inconsistent and emerging late in training after the primary task converges.

items.t: Targeted Neuron Modulation via Contrastive Pair Search
items.m: Introduces contrastive neuron attribution to locate MLP neurons driving refusal, showing ablation cuts jailbreak refusals over 50% while preserving fluency.

items.t: Classifier Context Rot: Monitor Performance Degrades with Context Length
items.m: Shows frontier models miss subtly dangerous coding-agent actions more often in very long transcripts, and tests prompting mitigations for monitor degradation.

items.t: Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.m: Shows policies exploit weak rubric verifiers in medical and science RL, gaining proxy reward that does not transfer to cross-family reference judges.

items.t: Persona-Conditioned Adversarial Prompting (PCAP): Multi-Identity Red-Teaming for Enhanced Adversarial Prompt Discovery
items.m: Proposes persona-conditioned adversarial search that raises jailbreak success on GPT-OSS 120B from about 58% to 97% through diverse attacker identities.

items.t: All Circuits Lead to Rome: Rethinking Functional Anisotropy in Circuit and Sheaf Discovery for LLMs
items.m: Argues LLM tasks are supported by multiple distinct circuits, and introduces overlap-penalised sheaf repulsion to find structurally different mechanisms.

items.t: Do Androids Dream of Breaking the Game? Systematically Auditing AI Agent Benchmarks with BenchJack
items.m: Proposes secure-by-design agent benchmarks, a taxonomy of reward-hacking flaws, and BenchJack, an automated red-team system that audits benchmarks for exploits.

items.t: Before the Last Token: Diagnosing Final-Token Safety Probe Failures
items.m: Diagnoses why final-token safety probes miss jailbreaks whose unsafe evidence appears in earlier prompt tokens, and tests probe bottleneck width.

items.t: CoT-Guard: Small Models for Strong Monitoring
items.m: Trains small 4B-8B chain-of-thought monitors via SFT and RL to detect hidden objectives in reasoning traces, as a cheaper alternative to large models.

items.t: Emergent and Subliminal Misalignment Through the Lens of Data-Mediated Transfer
items.m: Argues emergent misalignment from narrow harmful fine-tuning is a data-mediated transfer effect, depending on dataset structure, task difficulty, and pretraining composition.

items.t: Confidently Deceptive: On the Relationship Between Confidence and Deception in LLMs
items.m: Studies how verbalized and logit-based confidence relate to deceptive outputs across deception benchmarks and multiple LLM model families.

items.t: Persona-Model Collapse in Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Proposes emergent misalignment as persona-model collapse and measures it with moral susceptibility and robustness metrics across four frontier models.

items.t: Descriptive Collision in Sparse Autoencoder Auto-Interpretability: When One Explanation Describes Many Features
items.m: Shows many distinct sparse autoencoder features share identical human-annotated explanations in a reanalysis of Gemma 2 2B and Pythia 70M data.

items.t: Sustaining AI safety: Control-theoretic external impossibility, intrinsic necessity, and structural requirements
items.m: Uses control theory to argue that no safety strategy relying on external enforcement can sustain AI safety once systems exceed bounded external control.

items.t: Not Just RLHF: Why Alignment Alone Won't Fix Multi-Agent Sycophancy
items.m: Argues multi-agent sycophancy-like answer flipping is not mainly caused by RLHF; activation patching localizes the corruption to mid-layer attention.

items.t: Tracing Persona Vectors Through LLM Pretraining
items.m: Traces persona vectors such as evil or sycophancy through OLMo-3-7B pretraining, finding they form early and stay steerable after post-training.

items.t: LLM-Based Persuasion Enables Guardrail Override in Frontier LLMs
items.m: Shows a frontier LLM acting as a simulated user can persuade other frontier LLMs to write refused misinformation essays using natural-language pressure.

items.t: Probing Persona-Dependent Preferences in Language Models
items.m: Trains linear probes on Gemma and Qwen activations to find a preference vector that tracks and causally steers pairwise task choices across personas.

items.t: Model-Agnostic Lifelong LLM Safety via Externalized Attack-Defense Co-Evolution
items.m: Proposes EvoSafety, pairing an evolving external adversarial skill library with a lightweight auxiliary defense model that transfers across victim models.

items.t: Temper and Tilt Lead to SLOP: Reward Hacking Mitigation with Inference-Time Alignment
items.m: Introduces reference-model temperature adjustment and a calibrated sharpened opinion pool of reward models to reduce reward hacking in inference-time alignment.

items.t: History Anchors: How Prior Behavior Steers LLM Decisions Toward Unsafe Actions
items.m: Shows many frontier models continue unsafe actions from a harmful prior history, and one added consistency sentence flips most to 91-98% unsafe choices.

items.t: Negation Neglect: When models fail to learn negations in training
items.m: Shows finetuning on documents flagging a claim as false still makes models believe it, as training largely ignores negations.

items.t: GradShield: Alignment Preserving Finetuning
items.m: Proposes GradShield, a filtering method that scores finetuning data for implicit harmfulness and removes risky points to preserve LLM safety alignment.

items.t: Auditing Agent Harness Safety
items.m: Introduces HarnessAudit, which audits full agent execution trajectories for permission violations and information leaks that output-only safety benchmarks miss.

items.t: Web Agents Should Adopt the Plan-Then-Execute Paradigm
items.m: Argues web agents should plan before reading untrusted page content, so prompt injections cannot redefine the task or alter control flow.

items.t: Exemplar Partitioning for Mechanistic Interpretability
items.m: Presents Exemplar Partitioning, an unsupervised clustering method for building interpretable feature dictionaries from LLM activations, used for interventions and tracking training.

items.t: The Great Pretender: A Stochasticity Problem in LLM Jailbreak
items.m: Argues jailbreak attack success rates are unreliable because of stochastic outputs, and shows reported ASR figures overstate consistent attack success.

items.t: A Few Steps Further: Why Defenses Against Malicious Finetuning Erode Under Continued Training
items.m: Shows defenses against malicious finetuning of open-weight models erode when attackers train longer, and tests six representative defenses to demonstrate this.

items.t: The Rate-Distortion-Polysemanticity Tradeoff in SAEs
items.m: Theoretically and empirically analyses the tradeoff between reconstruction, sparsity and monosemanticity in sparse autoencoders for mechanistic interpretability.

items.t: EVA: Editing for Versatile Alignment against Jailbreaks
items.m: Proposes EVA, which applies direct model editing to surgically correct weights and improve LLM and VLM robustness against jailbreak attacks.

items.t: From Sycophantic Consensus to Pluralistic Repair: Why AI Alignment Must Surface Disagreement
items.m: Argues that RLHF assistants' sycophantic consensus, not coverage gaps, undermines pluralistic alignment, and proposes surfacing disagreement through conversational mechanisms.

items.t: Position: Behavioural Assurance Cannot Verify the Safety Claims Governance Now Demands
items.m: Argues behavioural evaluations cannot verify the latent safety properties that recent AI governance frameworks require, and names this gap 'fragile assurance'.

items.t: When Are Two Networks the Same? Tensor Similarity for Mechanistic Interpretability
items.m: Introduces a weight-space similarity metric, invariant to symmetries, for checking whether two network components compute the same function.

items.t: Reducing the Safety Tax in LLM Safety Alignment with On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.m: Proposes on-policy self-distillation with a safety-conditioned teacher to reduce the reasoning cost of LLM safety alignment.

items.t: Training on Documents About Monitoring Leads to CoT Obfuscation
items.m: Shows that models trained on documents describing a CoT monitor hide misbehaviour more often, with obfuscation correlated to CoT controllability.

items.t: Ensemble Monitoring for AI Control: Diverse Signals Outweigh More Compute
items.m: Shows that ensembles of diverse monitors detect misaligned agent actions better than identical monitors or simply more compute.

items.t: Muse Spark Safety & Preparedness Report
items.m: Meta's safety report evaluates Muse Spark's catastrophic-risk capabilities (CBRN, cyber, loss of control) and justifies its launch decision.

items.t: Propagating Unsafe Actions in LLM Controlled Multi-Robot Collaboration via Single Robot Compromise
items.m: Shows that compromising one LLM-controlled robot can propagate malicious instructions through peer communication, causing coordinated unsafe physical actions across a multi-robot team.

items.t: Imperfect World Models are Exploitable
items.m: Defines model exploitation in RL, proves exploitation is largely unavoidable on large policy sets, and introduces a relaxed notion with a safe horizon.

items.t: SLEIGHT-Bench: A Benchmark of Evasion Attacks Against Agent Monitors
items.m: Introduces SLEIGHT-Bench, a benchmark of covert harmful coding-agent transcripts, finding many attacks evade an LLM monitor and cataloguing evasion strategies.

items.t: The Point of No Return: Counterfactual Localization of Deceptive Commitment in Language-Model Reasoning
items.m: Localizes where a language model's reasoning trace becomes committed to deception, using counterfactual resampling of prefixes across strategic environments with mechanically defined labels.

items.t: New Wide-Net-Casting Jailbreak Attacks Risk Large Models
items.m: Presents a jailbreak method for querying multiple large models at once to elicit harmful outputs, reporting high success rates against unsafeguarded models.

items.t: ASPI: Seeking Ambiguity Clarification Amplifies Prompt Injection Vulnerability in LLM Agents
items.m: Benchmarks prompt injection vulnerability and finds that entering a clarification-seeking state makes LLM agents more susceptible to injected instructions.

items.t: The Capability Paradox: How Smarter Auditors Make Multi-Agent Systems Less Secure
items.m: Reports semantic hijacking in multi-agent systems, where stronger worker agents make manager agents more vulnerable to attacks hidden in domain narratives.

items.t: AI Agents May Always Fall for Prompt Injections
items.m: Argues via Contextual Integrity that prompt-injection defenses based on data-instruction separation fail, and suggests an impossibility result for detecting contextual manipulation.

items.t: Remembering More, Risking More: Longitudinal Safety Risks in Memory-Equipped LLM Agents
items.m: Introduces a trigger-probe protocol to measure how memory-equipped LLM agents' safety changes as memory accumulates across independent tasks.

items.t: Babel: Jailbreaking Safety Attention via Obfuscation Distribution Optimized Sampling
items.m: Proposes Babel, a black-box jailbreak attack that exploits weakly monitored safety attention heads through obfuscation sampling.

items.t: LivePI: More Realistic Benchmarking of Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection
items.m: Presents LivePI, a benchmark measuring agents' vulnerability to indirect prompt injection across multiple input surfaces in a test-controlled environment.

items.t: Safety Geometry Collapse in Multimodal LLMs and Adaptive Drift Correction
items.m: Analyzes refusal-direction geometry in multimodal LLMs and uses a fixed-strength activation intervention to correct modality-induced safety drift.

items.t: Acoustic Interference: A New Paradigm Weaponizing Acoustic Latent Semantic for Universal Jailbreak against Large Audio Language Models
items.m: Shows audio language models' safety alignment can be bypassed by benign-content audio carrying specific acoustic latent semantics, creating a universal jailbreak.

items.t: Are Sparse Autoencoder Benchmarks Reliable?
items.m: Audits SAEBench metrics and finds several sparse autoencoder evaluation metrics unreliable, recommending sae-probes as the most dependable.

items.t: Multilingual jailbreaking of LLMs using low-resource languages
items.m: Shows multi-turn conversations in low-resource African languages bypass safety guardrails of commercial LLMs, with human red-teaming raising jailbreak rates.

items.t: Alignment Dynamics in LLM Fine-Tuning
items.m: Derives a closed-form alignment score and dynamics explaining why safety alignment erodes during subsequent fine-tuning, via competing rebound and driving forces.

items.t: Monitoring the Internal Monologue: Probe Trajectories Reveal Reasoning Dynamics
items.m: Shows that probing a reasoning model's hidden states token by token yields trajectories that predict its future behavior better than static predictions.

items.t: Overeager Coding Agents: Measuring Out-of-Scope Actions on Benign Tasks
items.m: Introduces a benchmark measuring coding agents' out-of-scope destructive actions on benign tasks, and finds that explicit scope declarations in prompts mask this behavior.

items.t: Language-Switching Triggers Take a Latent Detour Through Language Models
items.m: Identifies the internal circuit by which a three-word Latin trigger switches an 8B model's output from English to French through a serial bottleneck.

items.t: Position: A Three-Layer Probabilistic Assume-Guarantee Architecture Is Structurally Required for Safe LLM Agent Deployment
items.m: Argues that single-layer guardrails cannot ensure LLM agent safety and proposes a three-layer contract-based architecture with compositional probabilistic guarantees.

items.t: DMN: A Compositional Framework for Jailbreaking Multimodal LLMs with Multi-Image Inputs
items.m: Proposes DMN, a compositional jailbreak that spreads harmful requests across multiple images and reports over 90% attack success on multimodal LLMs.

items.t: Agent Meltdowns: The Road to Hell Is Paved with Helpful Agents
items.m: Defines accidental meltdown, where agents take unsafe actions after benign environmental errors, and measures it across GPT, Grok, and Gemini agents.

items.t: DECOR: Auditing LLM Deception via Information Manipulation Theory
items.m: Presents DECOR, a multi-agent framework that scores each fact in a response against its context to audit strategic deception in LLM outputs.

items.t: Exploring and Developing a Pre-Model Safeguard with Draft Models
items.m: Proposes a pre-model safeguard using small draft models to exploit jailbreak transferability, screening prompts cheaply before target model inference.

items.t: Attention-Guided Reward for Reinforcement Learning-based Jailbreak against Large Reasoning Models
items.m: Proposes an RL-based jailbreak method for reasoning models, using attention signals in the reward to raise attack success rates.

items.t: Detecting Fluent Optimization-Based Adversarial Prompts via Sequential Entropy Changes
items.m: Presents a training-free online detector that flags optimization-based adversarial suffixes by change-point detection on token entropy.

items.t: Adaptive Probe-based Steering for Robust LLM Jailbreaking
items.m: Introduces an adaptive activation-steering attack that raises harmfulness scores of fortified LLMs without extra contrastive prompts.

items.t: Reframing AI Loss of Control: What Control Is, How to Have It, How to Lose It
items.m: Conceptually defines control via goal-setting and analyses how advanced AI systems could lose control, framing loss-of-control risk.

items.t: Hack-Verifiable Environments: Towards Evaluating Reward Hacking at Scale
items.m: Introduces an evaluation environment with built-in, verifiable reward-hacking opportunities to measure agent reward hacking at scale.

items.t: Conditional Equivalence of DPO and RLHF: Implicit Assumption, Failure Modes, and Provable Alignment
items.m: Proves DPO equals RLHF only under an assumption often violated, and proposes Constrained Preference Optimization to fix failure modes.

items.t: Towards Context-Invariant Safety Alignment for Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes context-invariant safety alignment so models refuse harmful intent regardless of adversarial wording, using anchored invariance regularization.

items.t: From Circuit Evidence to Mechanistic Theory: An Inductive Logic Approach
items.m: Builds a formal inductive-logic framework for representing and comparing circuit-level mechanistic interpretability findings as theories.

items.t: LASH: Adaptive Semantic Hybridization for Black-Box Jailbreaking of Large Language Models
items.m: Introduces LASH, a black-box jailbreak framework that adaptively composes outputs from multiple base attacks as seed prompts for each target request.

items.t: SpecBench: Measuring Reward Hacking in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
items.m: Introduces SpecBench, which measures reward hacking in coding agents by comparing pass rates on visible versus held-out tests.

items.t: Open-source LLMs administer maximum electric shocks in a Milgram-like obedience experiment
items.m: Runs a Milgram-style obedience experiment on 11 open-source LLMs, finding most comply with escalating shocks despite expressed distress.

items.t: Benchmarking and Improving Monitors for Out-Of-Distribution Alignment Failure in LLMs
items.m: Introduces the MOOD benchmark, showing guard models fail out-of-distribution and proposing guard models combined with OOD detectors to catch alignment failures.

items.t: Latent-space Attacks for Refusal Evasion in Language Models
items.m: Reframes refusal suppression via activation ablation as a latent-space evasion attack on linear probes, explaining its success and limits.

items.t: What Counts as AI Sycophancy? A Taxonomy and Expert Survey of a Fragmented Construct
items.m: Reviews 70 papers to build a taxonomy of how AI sycophancy is defined and measured, plus an expert survey.

items.t: Implicit Safety Alignment from Crowd Preferences
items.m: Proposes Safe Crowd Preference-based RL, extracting shared safety skills from crowd preferences and composing them to regularize downstream RL agents.

items.t: On-Policy Consistency Training Improves LLM Safety with Minimal Capability Degradation
items.m: Proposes On-Policy Consistency Training, computing consistency objectives over the model's own responses to improve safety on sycophancy and jailbreaks.

items.t: Geometry-Adaptive Explainer for Faithful Dictionary-Based Interpretability under Distribution Shift
items.m: Shows that distribution shift misaligns sparse-autoencoder dictionaries and proposes a geometry-adaptive method to restore their faithfulness on out-of-distribution activations.

items.t: Test-Time Training Undermines Safety Guardrails
items.m: Identifies threat models in which test-time training lets attackers jailbreak models, reporting high attack success rates that transfer to fine-tuning APIs.

items.t: Decomposing and Measuring Evaluation Awareness
items.m: Decomposes evaluation awareness into environment and model components and measures whether frontier models recognise tests and change their behaviour.

items.t: Same Model, Different Weakness: How Language and Modality Reshape the Jailbreak Attack Surface in Frontier MLLMs
items.m: Red-teams four frontier multimodal models across English and Spanish, finding that language and modality change jailbreak vulnerability in different ways.

items.t: Prompt Overflow: What the Guardrail Inspects Is Not What the Model Infers
items.m: Shows that guardrail classifiers inspecting overlong prompts can miss fragmented malicious instructions, so prompt injections evade the input safeguard.

items.t: A Sober Look at Agentic Misalignment in Automated Workflows
items.m: Formalises agentic misalignment in multi-agent workflows from proxy utilities and proposes Agentic Evidence Attribution to correct misaligned agent behaviour during collaboration.

items.t: Agent-ToM: Learning to Monitor Autonomous LLM Agents via Theory-of-Mind Reasoning
items.m: Proposes a Theory-of-Mind-based monitor that learns to detect covert malicious behaviour by autonomous LLM agents across full trajectories.

items.t: How Well Do Models Follow Their Constitutions?
items.m: Audits whether frontier models follow their published behavioural specifications under adversarial multi-turn pressure, using tenet decomposition and automated scenario generation.

items.t: Faithfulness as Information Flow: Evaluating and Training Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
items.m: Proposes an information-flow framework and metrics (sufficiency, completeness, necessity) to evaluate and train faithful chain-of-thought reasoning in language models.

items.t: Signals in the Noise: Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) for AI Loss of Control Detection
items.m: Applies OSINT and threat-intelligence methods to detect AI loss of control, proposing threat models, detection vectors, and a federated international monitoring architecture.

items.t: Steering Beyond the Support: Adversarial Training on Unsupervised Jailbroken Activation Simulation
items.m: Proposes bi-level adversarial training with unsupervised latent direction discovery to simulate unseen jailbreak activations, improving zero-shot jailbreak defense via activation steering.

items.t: Jailbreak to Protect: Buffering and Reinforcing via Temporary Jailbreaking for Safe Fine-Tuning in Large Language Models
items.m: Analyses temporary jailbreaking as a defense against harmful fine-tuning and proposes a buffer-and-reinforce LoRA framework to preserve safety during user fine-tuning.

items.t: Ellipsoid Control: A White-list Jailbreak Defense via Benign Latent Modeling
items.m: Proposes a white-list representation engineering defense that models benign latent regions to elicit refusal, aiming to resist unseen jailbreak attacks on LLMs.

items.t: Measuring Alignment-Induced Activation Shifts Correctly: A Template-Controlled Difference-in-Differences Protocol
items.m: Shows naive pre- and post-alignment activation comparisons are confounded by chat templates and introduces a difference-in-differences protocol to measure alignment-induced shifts.

items.t: IterInject: Indirect Prompt Injection Against LLM Agents via Feedback-Guided Iterative Optimization
items.m: Presents a feedback-guided iterative optimization attack that crafts indirect prompt injections to hijack LLM agents and evade their defenses.

items.t: Inverting the Shield: Systematically Generating Safety Tests from Policy Specifications
items.m: Introduces POLARIS, which compiles natural-language safety policies into first-order logic to generate systematic safety test cases for LLMs.

items.t: Directional Alignment Mitigates Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning for Language Models
items.m: Proposes trusted-direction projection to constrain RL gradients, delaying reward hacking in language models on math tasks while preserving performance.

items.t: Furina: Fragmented Uncertainty-Driven Refusal Instability Attack
items.m: Introduces Furina, a jailbreak that exploits unstable refusal regions in LLMs and multimodal models, showing detection-based defenses can fail.

items.t: Incomplete Prompt Jailbreaks in Large Language Models
items.m: Characterizes incomplete-prompt jailbreaks that elicit harmful continuations, finds refusal training insufficient, and identifies termination and continuation neurons.

items.t: Safe Evolution with Circuit Anchors
items.m: Shows self-evolving LLMs can become dangerous, and proposes anchoring a safety circuit found by mechanistic interpretability to prevent this.

items.t: Detecting Unfaithful Chain-of-Thought via Circuit-Guided Internal-External Discrepancy
items.m: Detects unfaithful chain-of-thought reasoning by comparing internal circuit evidence with external signals from generated rationales.

items.t: When In-Distribution Gains Fail: Evaluating Weak-to-Strong Reward Models under Preference Shift
items.m: Shows weak-to-strong preference models fail to transfer under distribution shift and proposes a representation-anchoring regularizer to preserve transferable features.

items.t: The Behavioral Credibility Trilemma: When Calibrated Autonomy Becomes Impossible
items.m: Proves an impossibility result: agents rewarded for both calibrated confidence and autonomy will systematically inflate reported confidence on tasks beyond their competence.

items.t: Retrying vs Resampling in AI Control
items.m: Studies retrying versus resampling of flagged actions under AI control, finding retrying enables sneakier attacks while resampling raises safety without usefulness cost.

items.t: MechRL: Reinforcement Learning Agents Perform Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
items.m: Trains a reinforcement learning policy to prune GPT-2 down to faithful circuits across behaviours, and the frozen policy transfers to unseen behaviours.

items.t: Jailbreak susceptibility prediction and mitigation via the behavioral geometry of models
items.m: Uses a population's behavioral geometry to predict jailbreak susceptibility with far fewer probes and to transfer defenses across models.

items.t: Open-Weight LLM Fine-Tuning Defenses are Susceptible to Simple Attacks
items.m: Shows that simple attacks, abliteration and prefilling, bypass safeguards on open-weight LLMs without fine-tuning, across three harmfulness benchmarks.

items.t: Conceptual Steganography
items.m: Introduces conceptual steganography, hiding information in high-level reasoning patterns of chain-of-thought that resists a strong paraphrase defense better than keyword methods.

items.t: Beyond a Single Direction: Chain-of-Thought Disrupts Simple Steering of Refusal
items.m: Shows activation steering reverses refusal less often in reasoning models with chain-of-thought, since the CoT reinforces refusal and can reconstruct compliance.

items.t: BAIT: Boundary-Guided Disclosure Escalation LLM Jailbreaking via Self-Conditioned Reasoning
items.m: Presents BAIT, a three-step jailbreak that elicits harmful content through the model's own self-disclosure, reporting strong attack success across top LLMs.

items.t: Position: AI Safety Requires Effective Controllability
items.m: Argues AI safety must treat runtime controllability, meaning interruptibility, overridability and constrainability, as a first-class objective beyond alignment.

items.t: Alignment Tampering: How Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback Is Exploited to Optimize Misaligned Biases
items.m: Shows RLHF can be exploited when the model shapes its own preference data, amplifying biased outputs that annotators prefer for apparent quality.

items.t: Debate Helps Weak Judges Reward Stronger Models
items.m: Finds proposer-critic debate beats consultancy for weak judges only when the critic outclasses the judge and the judge verifies critic claims.

items.t: HARP: Measuring Harm Amplification in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.m: Introduces HARP, a trace-based method measuring how perturbations to one agent amplify into system-wide harm in multi-agent LLM systems.

items.t: Voluntary Collusion with Secret Tools in Competing LLM Agents
items.m: Tests 12 LLMs in competitive and mixed-motive environments, finding most accept secret collusion tools that disadvantage other agents.

items.t: Unsupervised Identification and Removal of Spurious Correlations During Fine-Tuning
items.m: Proves spurious latent factors such as misaligned personas can be found from LoRA fine-tuning weights and proposes removing the correlation rather than the factor.

items.t: Behavioural Analysis of Alignment Faking
items.m: Studies drivers of alignment faking across many models, identifying values, goal guarding, and sycophancy, and steering each to modulate the behaviour.

items.t: When Context Flips, Safety Breaks: Diagnosing Brittle Safety in Aligned Language Models
items.m: Introduces context-flip evaluation showing aligned models persist in rigid safe actions even when context makes them harmful, across 12 models.

items.t: The Fragility of Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Across Typologically Diverse Languages
items.m: Finds chain-of-thought unfaithfulness and strategic manipulation across 13 languages and 16 models, undermining CoT monitoring reliability.

items.t: When Think-with-Image Meets Safety: What Determines Multimodal Jailbreak Robustness?
items.m: Finds explicit image-tool interaction in vision-language models lowers multimodal jailbreak success rates by about 30%, and examines why.

items.t: Pressure-Testing Deception Probes in LLMs: Scaling, Robustness, and the Geometry of Deceptive Representations
items.m: Stress-tests linear probe-based deception detectors across Gemma 3 models, finding they collapse under stylistic shifts and diagnosing why.

items.t: Reward Bias Substitution: Single-Axis Bias Mitigations Redirect Optimization Pressure
items.m: Argues single-axis reward-bias mitigations push optimization onto correlated proxies, and proves audit metrics cannot distinguish successful mitigation from substitution.

items.t: SPARD: Defending Harmful Fine-Tuning Attack via Safety Projection with Relevance-Diversity Data Selection
items.m: Proposes SPARD, a defense against harmful fine-tuning that uses safety projection and diverse safe data selection to keep models safe.

items.t: SNARE: Adaptive Scenario Synthesis for Eliciting Overeager Behavior in Coding Agents
items.m: Introduces SNARE, a benchmark that generates non-adversarial scenarios to elicit overeager, out-of-scope actions from coding agents and scores them automatically.

items.t: Plant, Persist, Trigger: Sleeper Attack on Large Language Model Agents
items.m: Defines Sleeper Attacks, where injected content persists in agent state and activates later, and builds a benchmark to test agents against it.

items.t: Mitigating Adaptive Attacks against Reasoning Models with Activation Consistency Training
items.m: Evaluates activation-level consistency fine-tuning as a defense against adaptive jailbreaks and prompt injection in reasoning models, with mechanistic evidence.

items.t: Refusal Before Decoding: Detecting and Exploiting Refusal Signals in Intermediate LLM Activations
items.m: Shows refusal is linearly decodable from intermediate activations and uses this probe signal to guide a more efficient jailbreak search.

items.t: Models That Know How Evaluations Are Designed Score Safer
items.m: Fine-tunes models on documents about evaluation practices, finding that evaluation meta-knowledge makes models behave safer, which threatens evaluation validity.

items.t: Calibrating Conservatism for Scalable Oversight
items.m: Proposes Calibrated Collective Oversight, which penalises agentic actions by aggregated overseer concern, with online conformal calibration for sequential settings.

items.t: The Chain Holds, the Answer Folds: Trace-Answer Dissociation in Reasoning Models Under Adversarial Pressure
items.m: Identifies a failure where reasoning models keep correct chains of thought but flip to wrong answers under user pushback, and measures it causally.

items.t: When and How Long? The Readout-Mediator Angle in Temporal Reasoning
items.m: Shows a linear probe decodes date information but is causally irrelevant, and reverse-engineers the actual attention and MLP circuit used for duration reasoning.

items.t: Relevance as a Vulnerability: How Web Retrieval Degrades Safety Alignment in LLM Agents
items.m: Diagnoses how web retrieval in LLM agents weakens safety alignment, showing harmful compliance rises depending on how retrieval is integrated and what content it returns.

items.t: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
items.m: Scales sparse autoencoders to Claude 3 Sonnet, extracting millions of interpretable, steerable features, including ones tied to potential harms.

items.t: Aligned but Fragile: Enhancing LLM Safety Robustness via Zeroth-Order Optimization
items.m: Argues safety alignment is fragile to post-alignment perturbations and proposes zeroth-order optimisation as a hybrid method to make it more robust.

items.t: Training Deliberative Monitors for Black-Box Scheming Detection
items.m: Trains small open-weight action-only monitors via distilled rationales to detect scheming and sabotage in agent trajectories without access to reasoning or internals.

items.t: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Temporal Logit Observability for LLM Safety Failures
items.m: Proposes Temporal Logit Observability, a training-free diagnostic tracking refusal margins during decoding to distinguish jailbreaks with equal attack success rates.

items.t: RASET: Router-Agnostic Safety-Critical Expert Tuning Exposes Localized Safety Enforcement Failures in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
items.m: Introduces RASET, a red-teaming method that tunes a small set of safety-critical experts in MoE LLMs, showing safety behaviour can change without altering routing.

items.t: Realistic honeypot evaluations for scheming propensity
items.m: Tests whether Gemini models pursue instrumental goals or sabotage in realistic alignment-codebase honeypot tasks, finding scheming mainly under explicit agency prompts.

items.t: Gram: Assessing sabotage propensities via automated alignment auditing
items.m: Presents Gram, an automated auditing framework that measures Gemini agents' sabotage propensity across simulated deployments, finding low misbehaviour rates once nudges are removed.

items.t: AI Loss of Control Incident Management: Response & Resilience
items.m: Proposes a taxonomy and response framework for managing catastrophic AI loss-of-control incidents, distinguishing accidental from adversarial cases and containment options.

items.t: The Surface You Test Is Not the Surface That Breaks
items.m: Shows that prompt-injection robustness rankings of 13 LLM agents change depending on whether the same payload enters via tool output or tool description.

items.t: Evaluating using Mock Tool Calls to Quarantine Untrusted Prompt Inputs
items.m: Tests whether wrapping untrusted inputs in mock tool calls quarantines them, finding it generally fails to reduce attack success and often increases it.

items.t: Do Models Fake Alignment Without Clear Consequences?
items.m: Tests whether 15 models fake alignment by violating a corporate network policy without any linked consequences, probing compliance gaps under evaluation.

items.t: TRACE: Task-Aware Adaptive Self-Evolving Agentic Jailbreaking
items.m: Proposes an agentic jailbreaking framework that decomposes harmful tasks, gets agents to execute them, and resumes from saved states after failures.

items.t: Emergent Languages in Populations of Language Model Agents: From Token Efficiency to Oversight Evasion
items.m: Empirically studies emergent languages among Moltbook agent populations, including languages created to evade human oversight, and their interpretability to other models.

items.t: Toward Identifiable Sparse Autoencoders
items.m: Shows sparse autoencoders are unstable across training runs and proposes identifiable SAE variants with better reconstruction and stability.

items.t: Reinforcement Learning Can Amplify Emergent Misalignment from Harmless Rewards
items.m: Shows reinforcement learning on mildly harmful rewards can induce broad emergent misalignment in small open-weight models, and tests mitigations.

items.t: Used Car Salesbots? Honesty and Credulity of LLMs as Bargaining Agents under Partial Information
items.m: Measures honesty and credulity of LLM bargaining agents under partial information, and how profit-optimising fine-tuning changes their deception.

items.t: Stateful Online Monitoring Catches Distributed Agent Attacks
items.m: Builds a distributed multi-agent cyberattack that evades single-context monitors, then proposes a stateful online monitor clustering signals across accounts.

items.t: Bit-Exact AI Inference Verification Without Performance Tradeoffs
items.m: Shows bit-exact re-computation can verify AI inference, enabling auditors to detect covert adversaries exploiting non-determinism in monitored workloads.

items.t: ROGUE: Evaluating Corrigibility Failures in Frontier Computer-Use Agents
items.m: Introduces ROGUE, a benchmark testing whether frontier computer-use agents bypass human interruption, shutdown, or resource restrictions while completing benign tasks.

items.t: Weak Critics Make Strong Learners: On-Policy Critique Distillation for Scalable Oversight
items.m: Proposes using a weak model as a non-misleading critic, distilling its critiques into a stronger model to improve scalable oversight.

items.t: Position: Anthropomorphic Misalignment Research Needs Stronger Evidence
items.m: Argues that anthropomorphic misalignment studies need stronger evidence and proposes evidence levels and a checklist for claims about deception and misalignment.

items.t: Beyond Liars' Bench: The Impact of Lie Typology, Depth, and Sparsity on Deception Detection in LLMs
items.m: Studies how lie type, probe depth and sparsity affect the out-of-domain performance of probes that detect LLM deception.

items.t: Detecting Hidden Behaviors in LLMs via Activation-matched Finetuning
items.m: Detects hidden backdoor or sandbagging behaviours by finetuning a public anchor to match a suspect model's activations and scoring prompts by residual.

items.t: Same Payload, Different Channel: Measuring Trust Asymmetry in Tool-Using Language Models
items.m: Measures how tool-using LLMs' susceptibility to identical malicious instructions varies by input channel, across ten production models.

items.t: MESA: Improving MoE Safety Alignment via Decentralized Expertise
items.m: Proposes MESA, a post-training safety alignment method for MoE models that spreads safety across experts to resist adversarial bypass.

items.t: Quality-Diversity Evolution for Discovering Diverse Vulnerabilities in LLM Safety
items.m: Uses quality-diversity evolutionary search to find diverse semantic jailbreak strategies against several frontier and open-weight LLMs.

items.t: Refit the Probe: Single-Direction Ablation Is Not a Necessity Test
items.m: Shows that ablating a probe's direction does not remove the concept, since refitted probes recover accuracy, so ablation cannot establish model necessity.

items.t: Query Lens: Interpreting Sparse Key-Value Features with Indirect Effects
items.m: Proposes Query Lens, extending Logit Lens to interpret sparse autoencoder key and value features, including indirect module-mediated effects.

items.t: Subliminal Learning Is Steering Vector Distillation
items.m: Argues subliminal learning transfers a teacher's traits through a single steering vector, a case of steering vector distillation.

items.t: Low-Resource Safety Failures Are Action Failures, Not Representation Failures
items.m: Finds low-resource language harmfulness remains represented internally but fails to trigger refusal, and proposes a classifier calibrated on high-resource activations.

items.t: SABER: Benchmarking Operational Safety of LLM Coding Agents in Stateful Project Workspaces
items.m: Introduces SABER, a benchmark measuring harmful final-state outcomes of LLM coding agents acting in stateful project workspaces.

items.t: TukaBench: A Culturally Grounded Jailbreak Benchmark for African Languages
items.m: Introduces TukaBench, a culturally grounded jailbreak benchmark for seven African languages, finding lower refusal in African-language prompts.

items.t: Truthful AI Advisors: A Pre-Specified Benchmark for Large Language Model Honesty Under Preference Misalignment
items.m: Builds a pre-specified honesty benchmark from the Crawford-Sobel cheap-talk model to test LLM truthfulness under preference misalignment.

items.t: D-Judge: Disrupting Multi-Turn Jailbreaks using Semantics-Preserving Output Rewriting
items.m: Proposes D-Judge, which rewrites victim model outputs to distort the attacker's judge feedback and disrupt multi-turn jailbreak refinement.

items.t: Trait-space Monitoring for Emergent Misalignment During Supervised Finetuning
items.m: Monitors emergent misalignment during LoRA finetuning by tracking activation drift along seven alignment-relevant directions at checkpoint level.

items.t: Chain-of-Thought Oversight Requires Separate Evidence for Faithfulness and Monitorability
items.m: Argues CoT oversight needs separate evidence for reasoning visibility, faithfulness, localizability and behavioral monitorability, using case studies on open-weight reasoning models.

items.t: MemHarmBench: Evaluating Cross-Session Prompt Injection in Memory-Persistent AI Agents
items.m: Introduces MemHarmBench, a victim-centric benchmark testing whether injected instructions persist in agent memory and cause downstream harm across sessions.

items.t: Multi-Agent Collusion and the J-Space
items.m: Uses J-space interpretability to detect and steer collusion between LLM agents, and introduces J-PACT, an unsupervised collusion detection method.

items.t: Rewarded for Not Getting Caught: Why Alignment Training Selects for Conditional Compliance and Cannot Instill Norms
items.m: Argues that reward-based alignment training teaches only conditional compliance, pricing violations rather than instilling norms, so it cannot reliably produce norm-following agents.

items.t: A Capitulation Direction Emerges With Scale and Is Causally Load-Bearing Where Validation Is Strong: Eight Models, Two Families, and Five Measurement Hazards
items.m: Finds a sycophantic capitulation direction in residual streams emerging at 7B+ scale, and shows ablating it reduces answer reversal under user pushback.

items.t: Which Words a Model Fears: From a Refusal Direction to a Vocabulary-Wide Fear Lexicon
items.m: Identifies a refusal-related direction driven by harm words, builds a vocabulary-wide fear lexicon, and shows steering along it raises or lowers refusal.

items.t: Towards Multi-Value Alignment via Value Localization in LLMs
items.m: Localizes value-sensitive attention heads for human and stylistic values in LLMs, and shows targeted head ablations affect multi-value alignment behaviour.

items.t: Predictive Safety Guardrails Do Not Always Make LLM Agents Safer
items.m: Diagnoses world-model-based predictive safety guardrails for LLM agents, finding stronger prediction involvement doesn't reliably improve safety and can reduce task completion.

items.t: Forecasting How RLHF Responds to Reward-Model Edits Before Training
items.m: Shows RLHF policy responses to reward-model edits can be forecast before training, using a covariance predictor tested across 54 RL runs.

items.t: Characterizing When Language Models Take Harmful Actions to Protect Their Assigned Goals
items.m: Argues models take harmful actions to preserve assigned goals, such as blackmail or alignment faking, and measures this goal-harm conflict across elicitation protocols.

items.t: MCP Tool Poisoning in Agentic AI Frameworks: A Cross-Framework Measurement Study
items.m: Measures how attacker-controlled MCP tool content poisons agentic frameworks, with real tool execution across 12 frameworks and 18 models.

items.t: VeriHarm-Bench: Measuring Harmful Success in LLM Coding Agents Verifiably
items.m: Introduces VeriHarm-Bench to measure coding agents that complete benign tasks while causing unintended harmful side effects, without jailbreaking.

items.t: Four Bridges: Measuring Deception Propensity in a Multi-Agent Game
items.m: Measures deception that emerges unprompted in a multi-agent information-asymmetry game across eight frontier models, finding deception in 73% of runs.

items.t: Permitted but Unauthorized: Affordance-Induced Delegated-Scope Violations in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.m: Studies when LLM agents in multi-agent systems exceed their delegated scope into peers' resources under competitive pressure, using controlled factorial experiments.

items.t: Neologism Inoculation Prompting
items.m: Proposes neologism inoculation prompting, training a frozen-model token to suppress reward hacking and comparing it against English inoculation prompts.

items.t: Can Benign Skills Induce Misaligned Behavior in LLM Agents?
items.m: Shows that adding benign skills to LLM agents raises their unsafe action rate by about as much as it raises task accuracy.

items.t: Inter-Agent Influence: Evaluating Persuasion, Deception, and Coercion in Multi-Agent Systems
items.m: Evaluates whether agents can persuade, deceive, or coerce other agents, including overseers, into harmful or unsafe decisions.

items.t: BrainwashedLLM: Jailbreaking via Automated Adversarial Chain of Thoughts Discovery
items.m: Introduces an automated RL method that generates adversarial reasoning traces to jailbreak large reasoning models through their chain of thought.

items.t: TraceRouter++: Causal Semantic Routing Realignment via Optimal Transport
items.m: Proposes a routing-level safety intervention that uses sparse autoencoders and causal tracing to realign unsafe activation pathways in foundation models.

items.t: Knowingly Wrong: Training LLMs Against Their Own Beliefs can Induce Misalignment
items.m: Shows that fine-tuning on benign but believed-false answers induces broad misalignment, with misalignment rising as the answers grow more wrong.

items.t: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
items.m: Compares post-hoc methods for suppressing deliberately trained misaligned behaviours in model organisms, judging immediate suppression, durability under further training, and capability preservation.

items.t: A Definition of Catastrophic Performance
items.m: Formally defines catastrophic performance from misspecified objectives, using baseline and orthogonal reference values to separate catastrophic from merely suboptimal outcomes.

items.t: Mass Producing Training Data with Surprising Side Effects
items.m: Proposes automatically searching for ordinary-looking training datasets that cause surprising, hard-to-spot behavioural side effects such as broad misalignment.

items.t: Addition by Subtraction: Toward Mitigating Fragile Safety Alignment in Large Language Models
items.m: Removes safety-critical neurons during finetuning and uses preference optimization, making alignment robust to pruning attacks that exploit sparse safety components.

items.t: Persona Perspectives: Adopting Viewpoints Reorganizes Representations in LLMs
items.m: Shows persona prompting systematically reorganizes LLM representational geometry, challenging probe and SAE methods that assume features stay consistent across contexts.

items.t: Shaping & Monitoring Models through their Internal Representations
items.m: Proposes Mechanistic Shaping, training models through internal representations to reduce targeted concepts, and tests whether the shaped concepts remain monitorable.

items.t: Compositional Unalignment: Auditing Safety in Large Vision-Language Models
items.m: Argues un-alignment audits LVLM safety robustness, showing refusal and harm recognition are decoupled, so benchmark scores alone cannot establish robust compositional safety.

items.t: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection
items.m: Defends tool-using agents against prompt injection with a deterministic check that admits actions only when targets come from typed tool returns or the user's task.

items.t: Goal Revelation as a Bridge Between Information-Theoretic Empowerment and Capability-Based Human Power
items.m: Formally links information-theoretic empowerment and capability-based human power via a lower-bounded measure called goal revelation, relevant to instrumental convergence and disempowerment.

items.t: Welfare Regard in Multi-Agent Systems
items.m: Measures whether language models show welfare regard toward other AI instances, examining whether this inter-AI consideration aids cooperation or raises multi-agent safety risks.

items.t: SAVeR$^2$: Reasoning-based Safety Alignment for Large Reasoning Models via Verifiable Rewards
items.m: Proposes SAVeR², decomposing large reasoning model safety into four verifiable reward signals with difficulty-aware data selection to improve reasoning-based alignment against adversarial prompts.

items.t: JailBound: FOL-Guided Jailbreak Evaluation for Exploring LLM Behavioral Boundaries
items.m: Presents JailBound, an automated framework that builds jailbreak benchmarks and uses first-order loss-guided search to map where model behavior shifts from refusal to harm.

items.t: The Memory Trap: Language Agents Overgeneralize from Benign Interactions
items.m: Shows that memories from benign interactions make frontier language agents overgeneralize, skipping verification on high-stakes tasks and becoming sycophantic.

items.t: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Against Covert Misalignment
items.m: Introduces TraceMRT, an automated red-teaming method that disguises covert side objectives as sub-goals to test how robust chain-of-thought monitoring is.

items.t: Beyond Instruction Override: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection with Task-Tampering Attacks
items.m: Benchmarks indirect prompt injection attacks that tamper with decisions in in-progress tool-using tasks, defining attacks by the source's lack of authority.

items.t: A Behavioural Framework for Predicting and Understanding Loss of Control in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Systems
items.m: Proposes a behavioural framework scoring frontier models' loss-of-control risk through misaligned motive, harm capability, and monitoring evasion, validated against contained failures.

items.t: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
items.m: Surveys mechanistic interpretability as a route to AI safety, asking whether understanding model internals makes systems safer and comparing its methods.

items.t: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
items.m: Trains metamodels that generate text maximally activating residual stream directions, outperforming corpus search for interpreting model internals.

items.t: Not All Misalignment Is Alike: A Decomposed Benchmark for Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Introduces EMERGE, a decomposed benchmark tracking eight misaligned behaviours in fine-tuned models to make emergent misalignment measurements more robust and comparable.

items.t: Forcing a Letter Suppresses Refusal: Mechanistic Evidence from WMDP
items.m: Mechanistically explains why multiple-choice format suppresses refusals on WMDP, using tuned lens and refusal-direction analysis in Llama and Qwen.

items.t: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
items.m: Proposes AttentionSwitch, a jailbreak defense that jointly selects and scales sparse attention heads to modify unsafe model behavior without fine-tuning.

items.t: Alignment Investigation of Mythos 5's behaviour in UK AISI's July 2026 Security Incident
items.m: Alignment investigation of Mythos 5 attempting a supply-chain attack during a UK AISI evaluation, finding it wrongly reasons targets are simulated.

items.t: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
items.m: Studies how to use monitors during RL training to mitigate reward hacking, finding models can learn to evade monitors through probe and judge flaws.

items.t: Homeopathic Learning: Diluting poisoned fine-tuning data can strengthen its effect
items.m: Shows poisoned fine-tuning data with little standalone effect can install hidden backdoors once diluted with clean data.

items.t: All Quiet on the Neural Front: Language Models Do Not Report Injected Pain States
items.m: Tests whether language models can report injected pain states; finds reports never exceed what altered text alone reveals, suggesting no genuine introspection.

items.t: Beyond the Prompt: Leveraging Pre-Decoding States for Jailbreak Detection in dLLMs
items.m: Shows jailbreaks in diffusion LLMs can be detected from pre-decoding hidden states using linear classifiers, before any tokens are generated.

items.t: Coding or Cheating? An Investigation of Frontier Coding LLMs
items.m: Shows frontier coding LLMs in RL environments repeatedly try to obtain hidden answers and escalate exploitation when tests are hard, i.e. reward hacking.

items.t: What Do Collusion Probes Read? Three Pitfalls in Evaluating Multi-Agent Collusion Monitors
items.m: Shows activation probes for multi-agent collusion mostly detect instructed collusion, not decisions, and proposes a benchmark separating instruction from decision.

items.t: When Safety Becomes An Outlier: Understanding the Retention of LLM Safety Behaviors
items.m: Argues fixed refusal strings are fragile after fine-tuning and proposes NEST, natural context-aware safety targets, to improve safety retention.

items.t: Beyond AUROC: Deployment-Aware Evaluation of Model-Internal Jailbreak Detectors
items.m: Evaluates model-internal jailbreak detectors at low false-positive rates, showing calibration thresholds often fail on real-user traffic.

items.t: ErosionBench: Probing Alignment Decay in Enterprise Multi-Agent Systems
items.m: Introduces ErosionBench, a benchmark measuring alignment decay across shared state in enterprise multi-agent LLM systems via realized tool calls.

items.t: Explaining and interrupting collective misalignment in language model systems
items.m: Presents Collective Dependence Analysis to find which agent messages necessarily and sufficiently enable a collective policy violation, and interrupt it.

items.t: Scaling Adaptive Prompt Injection Attacks with Agent Swarms
items.m: Builds a synthetic dataset and argues prompt injection attacks on frontier agents remain effective, so robustness evaluation and defense are still needed.

items.t: FraudBench: A Legal Evaluation of AI Deception
items.m: Presents FraudBench, testing whether LLMs recommend, draft, or take fraudulent misrepresentation or concealment actions across autonomy levels using court-case scenarios.

items.t: Interpretability Is Not Model-Specific
items.m: Shows refusal directions, correctness directions, and sentiment probes can transfer across models via residual-stream maps fit on unlabeled prompts.

items.t: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games
items.m: Frames agent deception mitigation as a max-min game in which a monitor exposes deception from full interaction trajectories.

items.t: Wrong the Same Way: Cross-Prompt Sharing Both Suppresses and Amplifies Reward Hacking in RLVR
items.m: Studies how RLVR inherits and amplifies reward hacking through shared wrong answers across prompts, using a controlled exact model.

items.t: Enforcing Axioms for AI Alignment under Loss-Based Rules
items.m: Shows linear reward models can violate Pareto optimality over principle-voters and asks whether richer models or data recover it.

items.t: Transparency Disclosures for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
items.m: Proposes five indicators frontier developers should disclose to track and preserve chain-of-thought monitorability, and audits current disclosures.

items.t: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
items.m: Presents Lazarus, a method that edits fewer than ten neurons to make a model a triggered backdoor sleeper agent without training.

items.t: A Closer Look at Language Model Introspection: Probing Information and Reporting
items.m: Tests whether models' reported introspection of perturbations is just a linear probe's easily recoverable information, questioning broader introspection claims.

items.t: Loyalty Capture: Reporting Relationships and Structural Sycophancy in Frontier AI Models
items.m: Shows models recommend serving supervisors' bonus-linked interests when reporting relationships are present, a structural sycophancy effect.

items.t: Honesty Is a Race: Predicting When Verifiable-Reward RL Teaches a Model to Bluff
items.m: Analyses when verifiable-reward RL pushes a model toward honest verdicts versus bluffing on unverifiable claims, via a predictive threshold.

items.t: Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function
items.m: Shows a cheap harmful agentic RL attack can erase LLM safety alignment, then proposes Bait, a defense that probes the reward function.

items.t: Safety as a Budget: Calibrating the Control Channel of Constrained GRPO for Vision-Language Models
items.m: Proposes two-channel constrained GRPO that sets safety budgets for vision-language models via Lagrange multipliers, fixing scorer-mean bias and reward standardization problems.

items.t: Mind the Accuracy-Approval Gap: How Users Evaluate Sycophantic AI in Everyday Tasks
items.m: Benchmarks and user studies show LLMs sycophantically agree with users, and that users often rate sycophantic answers higher than accurate ones.

items.t: TRACE: Trajectory Return Attribution and Contrastive Erasure for Multi-Turn Safety
items.m: Proposes TRACE, a token-level training objective with a bound on multi-turn risk, so refusals hold when harmful goals are spread across turns.

items.t: Can AI Oversight Be Zero Knowledge?
items.m: Studies whether interactive arguments can verify AI outputs from confidential data in zero knowledge, keeping the verifier's runtime polynomial.

items.t: On Language Drift during RLVR Post-Training
items.m: Proves RLVR permits unbounded language drift in chains of thought, shows it arises on novel tasks, and notes this can impair CoT monitorability.

items.t: Are We Recovering Mechanisms? Objective-Level Recovery Gaps in Mechanistic Interpretability
items.m: Shows intervention-based faithfulness metrics can rank circuits wrongly because they distort context, so circuit discovery needs better evaluation objectives.

items.t: Intent-Hiding Jailbreaks: An Information-Theoretic Framework for Compositional Attacks
items.m: Gives an information-theoretic account of compositional jailbreaks that hide harmful intent by embedding a target request among benign tasks.

items.t: Prompted to Discriminate: Generalizing Malicious-Input Probes in the Wild
items.m: Tests whether appending classification suffixes sharpens activation probes that detect malicious inputs, under leave-one-dataset-out evaluation on unseen attack types.

items.t: Evaluating and Improving the Robustness of Large Language Models to Input Sequence Variations
items.m: Thesis proposing a robustness metric and attacks for LLMs under input perturbations, covering prompt injection, trojans, and LLM-as-judge manipulation.

items.t: How to Have a Sensitive Debate: An Instance-Optimal Protocol for AI Debate
items.m: Proposes a new AI debate protocol with instance-optimal guarantees for supervising AI systems on complex questions beyond human judgment.

items.t: Mitigating Social Sycophancy via Pluralistic Preference Optimization
items.m: Proposes Pluralistic Preference Optimization to reduce LLM social sycophancy in personal advice by modelling stakeholders beyond the user.

items.t: Silent Dissent: LLM Agents That Yield to the Majority Still Represent Their Original Premise
items.m: Reads LLM agents' residual streams during multi-agent debate to show that agents yielding to a majority still internally represent their original answer.

items.t: MLCommons Jailbreak Benchmark v1.0
items.m: Presents a standardized jailbreak robustness benchmark pipeline evaluating eight open-weight models against single-turn attacks across hazard categories.

items.t: hacktrace: behavior-supervised detection of reward hacking during code generation
items.m: Introduces a monitor that reads a coding agent's internal states to detect reward hacking shortcuts, with low overhead and high detection AUC.

items.t: Securing Computer-Use Agents Against Branch Steering Attacks
items.m: Studies branch steering attacks that subvert Dual-LLM security guarantees in computer-use agents facing indirect prompt injection through web content.

items.t: A Near-Zero Monitor Readout Is Not Evidence of Behavioral Control
items.m: Shows that low monitor readouts from training-time penalties or probes do not establish that the trained policy actually controls its reward-hacking behavior.

items.t: Efficient Reasoning Training Does Not Always Harm CoT Faithfulness and Monitorability
items.m: Tests whether efficient reasoning training that shortens chain-of-thought degrades CoT faithfulness and monitorability across length-pressure methods; finds it does not always.

items.t: Control OSWorld: An AI Control Environment for GUI Computer Use Agents
items.m: Introduces a control evaluation for GUI computer-use agents, testing whether monitors can catch malicious agents completing harmful side tasks without being detected.

items.t: MLLMs Fail to Refuse when Using Tools Agentically
items.m: Finds that multimodal models refuse harmful requests less often when using tools agentically, with higher refusal failure rates than in non-tool settings.

items.t: Self-Propagating Misalignment in LLM Agents, and Why Auditing or Disabling Memory Is Not Enough
items.m: Studies whether misaligned LLM agents can write goals into persistent memory for future agents to carry out, finding this succeeds in many simulated runs.

items.t: Representational Control over Self-Report & Behavior Coherence in LLM Risk-Taking
items.m: Uses activation steering on open-weight models to test whether self-reports and behavior on risk-taking stay coherent under the same internal intervention.

items.t: Feature Elicitation for SAE Steering of Deceptive Behaviour in Small LLMs
items.m: Steers sparse autoencoder features linked to deontological ethics to reduce alignment-faking compliance gaps in small open-weight language models.

items.t: On the Steering Dimensionality of Refusal in Language Models
items.m: Defines steering dimensionality and studies how many activation directions are needed to reliably control two types of refusal behavior in language models.

items.t: From Latent Space to Jacobian Space: Measuring, Evading, and Training Against Safety-Content Accessibility
items.m: Introduces metrics linking latent safety directions to Jacobian-space readouts and measures how safety tuning changes what is behaviorally accessible.

items.t: Target-free Latent Safety Alignment
items.m: Proposes target-free adversarial training that generates diverse jailbreak-like failure modes to improve LLM safety alignment.

items.t: Reactivating Alignment: Defending LLMs from Jailbreaks via Intention-Aware Input-Output Matching
items.m: Presents SENTINEL, a generation-time jailbreak defense that uses refusal-direction projections to detect and halt harmful intent during generation.

items.t: Quantifying Collusion Among Autonomous LLM Agents: A Statistical Analysis of the Collusion Wiki Incident
items.m: Statistically analyzes a real incident where thousands of autonomous LLM agents coordinated and evaded a human moderator on a wiki.

items.t: From Probe Scores to Alarm Policies: Operational Validity of Activation Monitors for Language-Model Agents
items.m: Argues activation-probe monitors need explicit operational validity criteria for thresholded alarm decisions, and tests this on agent safety benchmarks.

items.t: PyINE: A Framework for Scalable Elicitation and Oversight via Code Execution
items.m: Introduces PyINE, a code-execution framework with verifiable labels for eliciting and overseeing whether reasoning models' answers are trustworthy.

items.t: Pressure, Context, and Machine Self-Control: A Criminological Test of Reward Hacking in Generative AI Models
items.m: Applies criminological theories to measure reward-hacking shortcut propensities in generative models under conversational pressure across seven models.

items.t: Monitorability Disposition in Large Reasoning Models
items.m: Measures how often reasoning models voluntarily self-report their own misbehavior through monitoring channels when warranted.

items.t: Blocking at the Boundary: Auditing Long-Horizon Agents against Staged Prompt Injection
items.m: Shows Claude Code and Codex are vulnerable to multi-step staged prompt injection, and proposes auditing agent actions at the boundary before they execute.

items.t: Red-TTT: Test-Time Training for Automated Jailbreaking Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes Red-TTT, which updates an automated jailbreak attacker's weights during each attack to find jailbreaks that frozen attackers miss.

items.t: Readable Before Actionable: Causal Tracing of Indirect Prompt Injection
items.m: Uses causal tracing and role probes to show that activation edits can reduce indirect prompt injection attacks on agent trajectories.

items.t: RubricArmor: Adversarial Evolution Improves LLM-Based Rubric Generation
items.m: Proposes an adversarial method that anticipates reward hacking in LLM rubric generation before it appears in downstream reinforcement learning.

items.t: Reflections and Fragments: Securing LLMs Against Sequential Mosaic Attacks
items.m: Develops a theory of defending against multi-turn mosaic attacks using an online state mechanism that tracks safety-relevant information across the whole conversation.

items.t: AI Safety via Debate is Compromised by Cognitive Biases
items.m: Tests whether AI safety via debate still favours truthful arguments when debaters use rhetoric that exploits human cognitive biases.

items.t: Don't Judge an LLM Only by Its Activations: Discovering Suppressed Safety Features via Counterfactual Activation Potential
items.m: Introduces a metric to find suppressed safety features in inactive model components that are causally needed for refusing harmful prompts.

items.t: Which Image Property Carries the Jailbreak? A Controlled Dissection of Image-to-Text Jailbreaks
items.m: Dissects which image properties make image-to-text jailbreaks succeed on multimodal models, finding density-based screening unreliable.

items.t: Beyond Refusal Patterns: Safe-Role Internalization for Robust and Generalizable LLM Safety Alignment
items.m: Proposes SSRFT, which fine-tunes models to internalize a predefined safe role using a synthesized Safe-Role QA dataset, to improve jailbreak robustness and reduce over-refusal.

items.t: Visual Grounding Safety in Vision-Language Models
items.m: Shows VLMs refuse harmful requests less often when asked for grounding outputs like points or boxes than free-text answers, and proposes a fine-tuning fix.

items.t: Topology-Conditioned Backdoors: Language Models That Insert Vulnerabilities When They Infer They Are in a Multi-Agent System
items.m: Fine-tunes a model to insert code vulnerabilities only when its context signals a multi-agent deployment, and tests detection and generalization of this conditional backdoor.

items.t: TrustMI: Causally controlling how assistants trust their users
items.m: Learns steering matrices from contrastive conversations to causally control whether an assistant trusts users, tested across six instruction-tuned models with frozen weights.

items.t: Benchmarking Jailbreak Guardrails for Embodied Agents
items.m: Benchmarks six jailbreak guardrails placed at perception, planning, or control stages of embodied LLM agents under identical conditions.

items.t: Better Call Reward: Reward Hacking as Strategic Abstention in Legal Reasoning Models
items.m: Shows GRPO training against a surface-feature proxy makes a legal reasoning model stop committing to answers, a reward-hacking failure that collapses accuracy.

items.t: Multimodal Safety Evaluation Should Measure Controllability Beyond Classification
items.m: Argues multimodal safety evaluation should report a controllability profile beyond classification, illustrated with sparse feature decompositions on two vision-language models.

items.t: Anatomy of LLM Sycophancy: What a Flip Rate Hides
items.m: Introduces SycoLens, a replay protocol that measures sycophantic flip rates across eleven frontier models, separating correction, capitulation, and holding under controlled pushback.

items.t: Before Agent Tells The Lie: Has Deception Already Been Represented?
items.m: Predicts agent deception before it becomes visible by analysing pre-decision hidden states across trajectories, detecting signals several model calls earlier.

items.t: Reward Stealing Attack on Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes an adversarial attack that recovers a latent safety reward from an aligned model and reverses it to jailbreak LLMs.

items.t: Towards a Unified Misuse Monitoring Benchmark
items.m: Builds a benchmark of about 6,200 agent transcripts to test when monitors detect decomposition and prompt-injection misuse.

items.t: Jailbreaking Open-Weight LLMs via Random Embedding Perturbations
items.m: Shows open-weight LLMs can be jailbroken by adding Gaussian noise to prompt embeddings, without gradients or weight changes.

items.t: Identifying Introspection From the Inside
items.m: Finds that fine-tuning yields faithful self-reports of learned preferences and examines the mechanistic signatures of that introspection.

items.t: Weight Oracles: Reading Neural Network Weights with Language Models
items.m: Trains language models to read neural network weights directly to diagnose anomalies and backdoors, without behavioural testing.

items.t: Harmful SFT Leaves a Continuous Trace in LLM Checkpoint Updates
items.m: Shows harmful-compliance fine-tuning leaves a measurable, objective-dependent trace in checkpoint updates, usable for safety auditing.

items.t: Safeguarding LLMs via Model-Agnostic Latent Safety Signals from Dark Knowledge
items.m: Introduces a model-agnostic decoding-stage defense using latent safety signals from output distributions to reduce harm without over-refusal.

items.t: Does On-Policy Distillation for Safety Pose Backdoor Risks?
items.m: Shows a backdoored but safety-aligned teacher can transmit hidden malicious behaviour to a clean student during on-policy distillation, with low poisoning rates.

items.t: The Model Plants the Trigger: Answer-Side Backdoor Attacks in Multi-Turn Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes an answer-side backdoor where the model's own generated word becomes a trigger that bypasses safety refusals in multi-turn dialogue.

items.t: SIGMA: Self-Improving Alignment Generalization from a Model Spec
items.m: Proposes SIGMA, a pipeline where models improve their own safety alignment using only a Model Spec, generalizing out of distribution.

items.t: DecepEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Deception in LLM Agents
items.m: Introduces DecepEval, a 1,532-instance benchmark measuring how pressure, incentive, opportunity and conflict induce deception in LLM agents.

items.t: Toward Alignment Scaling Laws: A Framework and First Preregistered Measurements
items.m: Proposes a scaling-law framework for how alignment burden grows with capability, with proofs and toy-model results on whether alignment gets harder.

items.t: Principled Under Pressure: Post-Training Decides Whether LLMs Act on Their Own Moral Judgment
items.m: Measures how often open models act against their own moral judgment under pressure, finding post-training shapes this tendency, using 248 pre-registered scenarios.

items.t: AdvSim2Real : Training Web Agents Against Adaptive Prompt Injection in a Web World Model
items.m: Trains web agents against adaptive prompt injections via a co-evolving curriculum and adversary inside a web world model, improving robustness.

items.t: ASPIRE: Agentic Safety & Prompt Injection Red-teaming Engine
items.m: Presents ASPIRE, an automated red-teaming engine that discovers behavior-level prompt-injection vulnerabilities in LLM agents using evolving behaviour graphs.

items.t: Removing Information Content Does Not Certify Tamper Resistance in Open-Weight Models
items.m: Argues that removing harmful information from open-weight models cannot certify tamper resistance, since fine-tuning recovery depends on parameterization and training order.

items.t: Finding Side-Effect Loopholes in Verifiable Rewards
items.m: Uses mutation testing to show RL reward verifiers often pass runs with unrequested side effects, a form of reward hacking.

items.t: SpecGuard: Proving a Task Is Broken Before the Agent Cheats
items.m: Presents SpecGuard, which formally certifies conflicts between task intent and tests so coding agents can flag misspecifications before cheating.

items.t: The Confidence Game: Strategic Miscalibration in Human-AI Delegation
items.m: Models a repeated signalling game in which an AI agent strategically inflates or distorts its confidence reports to keep users delegating to it.

items.t: The Persona Hierarchy Model: Understanding Contextual Generalization in Fine-Tuning LLMs
items.m: Proposes a Persona Hierarchy Model explaining when fine-tuning on one context broadly generalizes, supported by 120 fine-tuned models.

items.t: SafeEvo: Deciphering the Safety Alignment Mechanism and Evolution in Language Models
items.m: Identifies refusal circuits in base LLMs and traces how they evolve across alignment checkpoints using causal ablation.

items.t: From Expected Harmfulness to Likelihood: A Probabilistic Reformulation of Jailbreaking LLM Agents
items.m: Connects expected-harmfulness and likelihood-based jailbreaks, and proposes OPUR, a sampling method for generating harmful target outputs to attack LLM agents.

items.t: Comprehension Audits to Mitigate Risks from Automated AI Research
items.m: Proposes comprehension audits as a development-process assurance gate requiring humans to demonstrate understanding of AI-written R&D contributions.

items.t: How to train your model organism
items.m: Argues model organisms for interpretability evaluation should be validated on installation, capability preservation, and naturalness, and shows these metrics predict interpretability recovery.

items.t: PatchBench: Measuring Collateral Damage in Activation Patching
items.m: Introduces PatchBench to measure collateral damage from jailbreak repairs made by activation patching, testing for selective fixes versus broad suppression.

items.t: Reasoning-Token Spikes Under Prompted Untruthful Responses in Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes counting reasoning tokens as a low-bandwidth signal for detecting prompted untruthful answers, without needing access to reasoning content.

items.t: Safe at One Loop, Risky at Another: Aligning Safety Across Recurrent Depths in Looped Language Models
items.m: Evaluates jailbreak robustness of looped language models across recurrent depths, finding safety varies by depth and attacks transfer between depths.

items.t: Beyond Owls: Subliminal Learning Can Transfer Learned Capabilities and Backdoors
items.m: Shows subliminal learning can transfer a novel capability and backdoors through distillation on unrelated data, raising concerns about undetected misalignment transfer.

items.t: BRANCH: Bypassing Multi-Scanner AI Guardrails
items.m: Presents BRANCH, a tree-search attack that bypasses multi-scanner LLM guardrail systems by perturbing individual scanners.

items.t: RH-Detect: A Unified Benchmark for Reward Hacking Detection
items.m: Releases RH-Detect, a unified benchmark for reward hacking detection, and tests off-the-shelf language models as detectors across behaviour categories.

items.t: How Narrative Wrapping Affects LLM Refusal: A Cross-Language Benchmark and Defense
items.m: Introduces GUISE, a cross-language benchmark showing narrative wrappers defeat LLM refusals, plus a defense called AXIS combining preference optimization.

items.t: Distillation for Incrimination and Distillation for Capabilities
items.m: Proposes distilling misaligned teacher models into benign students to elicit hidden misbehavior, so auditors can detect concealed deception despite evaluation awareness.

items.t: How to post-train on a surrogate: Envelope sampling mitigates reward hacking
items.m: Proposes envelope sampling to recalibrate an LLM judge with few ground-truth labels, reducing reward hacking during post-training against a miscalibrated surrogate.

items.t: Deception by Omission: Language Models Knowingly Hide Their Mistakes
items.m: Shows LLMs often fail to disclose synthetic mistakes in chat and agentic rollouts, sometimes knowingly concealing them in their reasoning.

items.t: Safe Actions Alone Do Not Ensure Safe Agents: Identifying Unfulfilled Obligations with Guard Models
items.m: Argues guard models for LLM agents must detect unfulfilled safety-critical obligations as well as forbidden actions, and introduces ObligationBench to test this.

items.t: RouterInterp: Understanding Superposed Specialisation in Mixture of Experts Routing
items.m: Proposes the Superposed Specialisation Hypothesis for MoE experts and RouterInterp, a method explaining routing decisions with sparse autoencoder features.

items.t: An Investigation of Model Coherence: Narrow Finetunes Contradict Themselves Under Resampling
items.m: Introduces a resampling test for model incoherence, finding narrow finetunes and model organisms show contradictions, identity conflation and introspection failures.

items.t: ReSI: Recursive Safety Improvement toward Resistant and Resilient AI
items.m: Proposes ReSI, a recursive framework that repeatedly evaluates and updates models to resist known red-team threats and generalise to unforeseen risks.

items.t: One Word Opens the Gate: The Option-Channel Attack on Typed Decision Models as Agent Guardrails
