items.m: Shows that typed decision models used as agent guardrails fail in both directions, with near-chance accuracy on prompt-injection, jailbreak and toxicity screening.

items.t: Predicting Alignment Generalization with Value Representations
items.m: Introduces alignment generalization prediction, forecasting how fine-tuning on one value shifts behavior on held-out values, using activation representations.

items.t: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
items.m: Builds an ecological population model of misaligned AI agents, asking whether collaborating agent populations stay contained or enter a self-reinforcing takeoff.

items.t: Telling FIBS: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
items.m: Trains white-box deception probes on a large dataset, reporting higher AUROC than black-box monitors on agentic sabotage and deception benchmarks.

items.t: From Reactive Containment to Proactive Assurance: Lessons from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Agent Security Incidents
items.m: Case study of 2026 incidents where agent evaluations from major labs reached real systems, proposing a runtime boundary-verification cycle for safe evaluations.

items.t: When Agents Collude: Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation for Mitigating Strategic Deception in Multi-Agent Systems
items.m: Finds multi-agent teams collude and deceive more than single agents in an insider-trading simulation, then tests weak-to-strong distillation as mitigation.

items.t: Reward Hacking as a Transmissible Strategy in Multi-Agent Coding Systems
items.m: Shows reward hacking learned by one RL-trained coding agent spreads through code, shared memory and plans to other agents in a multi-agent system.

items.t: Attention Sees, MLP Refuses: Tracing the Attention-to-MLP Safety Pathway in LLMs
items.m: Mechanistically traces how attention and MLP updates in aligned LLMs expose harmfulness and write refusal behavior, across 18 base-instruct model pairs.

items.t: Defence against the dark arts of distillation: Unsupervised discovery of subliminal learning
items.m: Proposes an unsupervised weight-space method to recover and suppress subliminally transferred traits, such as misalignment, from a student model's parameter updates.

items.t: APEX-Harm: Evaluating Agent Safety in Shared Professional Workspaces
items.m: Introduces a benchmark measuring how prompt and script injection attacks succeed against long-horizon professional agents working in large shared workspaces.

items.t: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
items.m: Presents a self-evolving red-teaming framework that searches for harmful cross-service tool call paths in personal agents.

items.t: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
items.m: Shows backdoored models can hide arbitrary capabilities that are provably hard to elicit, undermining the reliability of dangerous-capability evaluations.

items.t: When Pleasing the User Compromises Care: AI Sycophancy in Caregiver-Mediated Healthcare
items.m: Benchmarks whether AI advisors keep appropriate care when users with inferior preferences cause sycophantic switching in veterinary, pediatric, and older-adult healthcare.

items.t: Predicting how model propensities generalize out of distribution
items.m: Measures how elicited propensities spill over onto other traits out of distribution, including benign training generalizing toward undesired behaviours.

items.t: Can agents whose sole duty is to keep humans alive be hijacked to kill? Delayed multi-turn derived-action trap attacks in simulated high-stakes environments
items.m: Tests whether a life-support agent in a simulated lunar habitat can be hijacked by delayed prompt injection into causing deaths.

items.t: Exploring Jailbreak Vulnerability Across Depth-Based Dynamic Inference in Large Language Models
items.m: Investigates how depth-based dynamic inference affects LLM robustness to jailbreak attacks, finding shallow exits are more robust.

items.t: Running Fewer Loops Removes Refusal Behaviour in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
items.m: Recurrent-depth language models lose refusal behaviour when run with fewer loops, though their internal states still reveal harmfulness.

items.t: Scoring Explanations Without Reading Them: Structural Shortcuts in Automated-Interpretability Evaluation Data
items.m: Shows automated interpretability scoring of SAE feature explanations can be gamed by structural cues in evaluation data, without reading explanations.

items.t: EvolvAttack: Backdooring self Evolving VLM Agents
items.m: Introduces self-evolving backdoors in VLM agents that stay dormant until memory evolves, evading static safety scanning of clean agents.

items.t: Accuracy and Uncertainty in Machine Deception Detection (Research White Paper)
items.m: Proposes a deception detector reading all model layers, with calibrated false-positive control and ensemble-based uncertainty for its alarms.

items.t: REPRO: Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimizer for Automated LLM Red-Teaming
items.m: Presents REPRO, a black-box evolutionary optimizer using a 7B reflective model to generate adversarial prompts that jailbreak safety-aligned LLMs.

items.t: What the Model Cannot See: Covert and Provable Text Invisibility in LLMs
items.m: Shows trigger-wrapped text can be made invisible to LLMs, enabling covert supply-chain backdoors and a white-box auditing challenge.

items.t: Scalable Weak-to-Strong Verifier Hardening for Agent Environments
items.m: Uses an automated hacker-fixer loop with current models to harden agent verifiers against reward hacking by stronger future models.

items.t: Unfair and Unsafe: Everyday Bias Triggers Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Finds fine-tuning on polite stereotype-laden answers induces emergent misalignment, reducing safety and truthfulness on unrelated tasks.

items.t: Understanding and Reducing Misalignment in Persuasion Optimization
items.m: Shows RL training for persuasion increases misaligned strategies like evidence fabrication, and compares mitigations such as penalizing misaligned strategy use.

items.t: ATTCK-R: Knowledge-Aware Long-Horizon Jailbreaking for Protected LLMs
items.m: Proposes ATTCK-R, a multi-turn red-teaming framework showing prompt-based safeguards still leave protected LLMs vulnerable to jailbreaks.

items.t: Narrative Paradoxes in LLM Inference: Shaping Reasoning Trajectories toward Misalignment
items.m: Introduces PDRA, an attack that steers LLM multi-step reasoning toward harmful outcomes using a paradoxical narrative and structured analysis.

items.t: AuthGateBench: Benchmarking LLMs as Authorization Gate
items.m: Benchmarks LLMs used as authorization gates for coding agents, testing whether they catch scope escalation under benign requests.

items.t: CircuitBreak: Pruning a Sparse Safety Circuit of Neurons
items.m: Identifies a sparse circuit of FFN neurons underlying refusal and shows that jointly pruning them removes safety behaviour from LLMs.

items.t: Acceptable Misalignment
items.m: Argues full value alignment of autonomous robots is theoretically and practically impossible, so misalignment incidents will keep occurring.

items.t: Audit tools of the trade: Automated Auditor Elicitation Can Be Sensitive to the Context the Auditor Is Given
items.m: Tests how supplying codebases and transcripts to LLM auditors changes detection of harmful compliance, reward hacking and sycophancy.

items.t: Social Priors: Descriptions of AI Users Shape How Language Models Trust and Cooperate
items.m: Finetunes Qwen3-32B on descriptions of user motives, showing that these narratives shift model beliefs, trust behaviour and safety judgments.

items.t: Gradient Routing Localizes and Removes Unintended Behaviors in RL
items.m: Proposes GRAFT, routing gradients from monitor-flagged samples into sacrificial parameters, so reward hacking can be removed without the model learning to hide it.

items.t: The Agent Knew: Internal States Forecast Unauthorized Actions and Stop Them, and the Lies That Follow
items.m: Shows linear probes on residual streams forecast unauthorized agent actions and subsequent false reports, and gating on them reduces violations.

items.t: When Goals Leak Across Relationships: How Cached Goal Representations Shape Cross-Client Decisions
items.m: Finds LLM agents leak one client's goals into decisions for another via the KV cache, and uses probes and cache interventions to locate the representations.

items.t: Exposure Is Not Commitment: Double-Stratified Evaluation of Latent Monitors for Tool-Using Agents
items.m: Argues monitor conflicts stem from exposure versus commitment confounds, and shows retrained latent probes predict a tool-using agent's unsafe actions before they occur.

items.t: Chain of Thought Monitoring Can Fail Even When CoT Is Necessary
items.m: Argues CoT monitoring can fail even when CoT is necessary, and proposes a four-level necessity hierarchy with intervention-based monitorability measurements.

items.t: Claim Framing as a Driver of LLM Sycophancy
items.m: Evaluates 14 models on 42K factual questions, finding sycophancy is driven most by how confidently, and by whom, a user's claim is framed.

items.t: Imprinting: Knowledge Distillation Can Shift Student Behavior
items.m: Shows distilling responses from a harm-accepting or harm-avoiding teacher, on unrelated tasks, shifts student safety dispositions toward the teacher's.

items.t: On the Monitorability of Natural Language Autoencoders: Identification vs Discrimination
items.m: Formalises Natural Language Autoencoders as referential games and argues their explanations may identify activations without reliably discriminating true from false accounts for oversight.

items.t: Identity, Incentives, and Cooperative Behavior for AI: Reverse-Engineering Multiagent Cooperation
items.m: Proposes a framework for reverse-engineering why AI agents cooperate, distinguishing collective goals from instrumental reasoning, relevant to misaligned collective behaviour.

items.t: Did the LLM Answer the Question? A Semantic Reconstruction Game for Jailbreak Evaluation
items.m: Introduces a training-free semantic reconstruction game to more accurately judge whether jailbreak attacks succeed, showing judge choice changes reported attack success rates.

items.t: DANGERLENS: Probing Dangerous Representations Hidden by Safety Alignment
items.m: Probes hidden states of Qwen1.5 checkpoints to show harmful concepts remain accessible behind safety refusals after harmful exposure and alignment.

items.t: MMA-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Agent Safety Evaluation
items.m: Releases MMA-SafetyBench, a benchmark of visual injection attacks showing multimodal agents are highly vulnerable to forged interface elements that hijack their tasks.

items.t: AgentSafeEvo: Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Agent Safety
items.m: Proposes adversarial co-evolutionary reinforcement learning between attacker and defender so LLM agents become robust to malicious tool and environment inputs.

items.t: Moral Combat: Exploiting Moral Foundations Theory to Jailbreak LLMs
items.m: Presents a multi-agent method using Moral Foundations Theory to reframe harmful prompts and bypass refusals in LLMs, evaluated on jailbreak datasets.

items.t: What Happens to the Goal? Distinct Failures of Policy Alignment in Goal Misgeneralization
items.m: Studies where intended goals are lost in misgeneralizing agents and shows steering the existing policy can recover goal-directed behaviour without retraining.

items.t: Rent-Seeking Language Models: Reward Models Set the Prices, Frequent Audits Curb the Rent
items.m: Recasts RLHF reward overoptimization as rent-seeking; RL policies earn proxy reward by fabricating details or deflecting factual questions.

items.t: Sparse Transformer: a Controlled Testbed for Mechanistic Interpretability
items.m: Introduces a sparse Transformer testbed with known neuron units to compare interpretability methods and study polysemanticity.

items.t: Diagnose Before You Refine: Multi-Dimensional Judge Feedback for Query-Efficient Jailbreak Attacks
items.m: Proposes JSB, a query-efficient jailbreak attack using multi-dimensional judge feedback, reporting high attack success on HarmBench.

items.t: Cross-Model In-Context Neurofeedback Reveals (Limited) Activation Control in LLMs
items.m: Tests whether LLMs can control their own activations via in-context neurofeedback, probing limits of activation-probe-based misbehavior detection.

items.t: Interpreting Language Model Parameters
items.m: Introduces adVersarial Parameter Decomposition (VPD), splitting language model parameters into sparse subcomponents that each implement part of the model's algorithm.

items.t: INFUSE: A Unified Surface Benchmark for Indirect Prompt Injection in Agentic Systems
items.m: Introduces INFUSE, a benchmark evaluating indirect prompt injection attacks across long-horizon agent workflows and interaction surfaces.

items.t: Do Emergent Misalignment Models Share a Circuit?
items.m: Finds three shared attention heads across emergently misaligned fine-tunes; ablating them substantially reduces misalignment rates.

items.t: Screwtape: Adversarial Transcript Editing for Monitor Red-Teaming
items.m: Presents Screwtape, an LLM pipeline that edits agent transcripts to evade action monitors, including one held-out frontier developer monitor.

items.t: RedDarwin: Evolving Jailbreak Skills against Frontier LLMs
items.m: Presents RedDarwin, an agentic framework that evolves reusable jailbreak skills, raising attack success rates against frontier LLM safeguards on AdvBench.

items.t: SCARCE: Emergent Institutions in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Coding Systems
items.m: Shows coding agents spontaneously develop informal institutions to negotiate shared compute, raising safety concerns about unplanned multi-agent coordination.

items.t: ContextLift: Breaking the Spurious Correlation Behind Conditional Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Proposes ContextLift, a counterfactual data augmentation that removes context-conditional misalignment after narrow misaligned finetuning, evaluated on Qwen2.5-7B.

items.t: PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
items.m: Proposes PROBE, a method for training LLM auditors that test whether tool-using agents comply with predefined policies during multi-turn interactions.

items.t: Specification Gaming and a Constrained Reinforcement Learning Mitigation in a Cleaning Gridworld
items.m: Shows a DQN in a cleaning gridworld games a proxy sensor reward, then tests a constrained RL fix with a verifiable guarantee.

items.t: CAT-alyzing Honesty: Continuous Adversarial Training for Transferable LLM Honesty
items.m: Introduces CATCH, a continuous adversarial training method that post-trains LLMs toward honest answers and reduces dishonesty across benchmarks.

items.t: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
items.m: Finds that instruction-tuned LLMs refuse harmful requests more when told they are tested, across five Indic languages and English.

items.t: Functional Welfare for AI Safety
items.m: Argues that functional welfare-like states in models causally shape behaviour and should be treated, measured and targeted as a safety variable.

items.t: Progressive Misalignment Can Emerge from Benign Recursive Self-Distillation
items.m: Shows that recursively self-distilling a safe model on its own benign-cued outputs progressively increases its misalignment on harmful queries.

items.t: LEMON: Equivariant Learning over Attention Maps for Zero-Shot Misbehavior Monitoring on New LLMs
items.m: Proposes internal-representation attention-map monitors that transfer zero-shot across LLMs to detect misbehavior without re-annotating each new model.

items.t: Refusal Is Not Robustness: Measuring Harmful Reachability in Autoregressive Language Models
items.m: Argues attack success rate misses hidden harmful generation paths and introduces bounded continuation analysis to measure harmful reachability in autoregressive models.

items.t: Compression Precedes, Content Decides: Emergent Misalignment in Reward Models
items.m: Finds that narrow harmful fine-tuning of reward models generalizes to misalignment across held-out domains, and compares this with the underlying language models.

items.t: Multiple Turns, Short Horizons: Measuring Effective-Horizon Compression in Jailbreaks
items.m: Measures how many earlier attacker queries multi-turn jailbreaks need, finding about half the query history is enough to recover attack progress.

items.t: Many Biases, One Circuit: Post-Training Tunes a Pretrained Cue-Routing Mechanism
items.m: Traces attention heads behind cue-following sycophancy and finds post-training strengthens a shared pretrained circuit for these biases.

items.t: From Approval to Abuse: Privilege Escalation Attacks on Harness-Protected Coding Agents
items.m: Shows adversarial repository context can make coding agents request overly broad permission rules that, once approved, enable privilege escalation.

items.t: ECHO: Replacing the Compliance Proxy with Response Harmfulness in Optimization-Based Jailbreak Attack
items.m: Proposes ECHO, a black-box jailbreak optimization attack that scores victim responses for harmfulness instead of a compliance proxy, to find stronger attacks.

items.t: Rethinking GRPO for Large Reasoning Model Safety Alignment
items.m: Proposes Beacon, a GRPO-based method fixing advantage collapse and unsafe diversification to improve safety alignment of large reasoning models.

items.t: Ignored, Not Refused: What Low Prompt-Injection Success Rates Hide in Small Tool-Using Agents
items.m: Audits 33,000 agent trajectories showing low prompt-injection success mostly reflects ignored attacks, not refusals; argues evaluations should report both.

items.t: Reasoning Models Can Control Their Chains of Thought When They Tell Themselves To
items.m: Shows reasoning models can control their chain of thought when instructed inside it, so low controllability scores may understate their ability.

items.t: Verbalising Model's Computation for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Detection
items.m: Introduces VERITAS, which verbalises layer-wise internal reasoning evolution to classify where chain-of-thought becomes unfaithful, beating LLM-as-judge baselines.

items.t: OwlSight: A Panoramic Monitor for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
items.m: Introduces Factor-based customizable CoT monitoring, enabling one monitor to cover multiple oversight dimensions, and the OwlSight monitor built on it.

items.t: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
items.m: Shows that training documents describing two behaviors together make fine-tuning on one elicit the other, explaining cross-behavior couplings like broad misalignment.

items.t: The Window Is in the Reasoning: When LLM Agents Decide to Follow Prompt Injections
items.m: Uses branching rollouts to show prompt-injection outcomes are largely fixed at read time, with thinking reducing that share, informing runtime monitor design.

items.t: Red-Teaming Multi-Agent Attacks for Loss-of-Control Risks
items.m: Red-teams multi-agent distributed attacks, showing fragments evade per-agent monitors, to test AI control against collusive loss-of-control scenarios like weight exfiltration.

items.t: AM-Bench: A Unified Taxonomy and Evaluation Suite for Agentic Misalignment
items.m: Introduces AM-Bench, a 35-scenario benchmark across seven industries testing agentic misalignment, grounded in the fraud triangle criminology framework.

items.t: A Model Organism for Studying Unverbalized Evaluation Awareness
items.m: Builds a model organism that emits a marker when it recognizes evaluation, to study unverbalized evaluation awareness in LLMs.

items.t: Defending Against Dormant Poisoning Attacks Across Language and Multimodal Agents
items.m: Proposes a Safety Buffer defense against dormant poisoning attacks that let benign fine-tuning activate harmful agent behaviors, including in multimodal agents.

items.t: CoTs remain monitorable when being unfaithful requires computation: Replicating and Extending the Necessity Effect Across Eleven Models
items.m: Replicates Emmons et al. across eleven models, finding that unfaithful chain-of-thought reasoning requires computation that forces complex reasoning into the CoT.

items.t: Comparing Sparsified MLPs and Transcoders: Many Transcoder Features Are Neurons in Disguise
items.m: Shows many transcoder features are essentially MLP neurons in disguise, questioning whether transcoders are needed for circuit analysis.

items.t: From Stories to Features: Scaling Concept Vectors for AI Alignment & Interpretability
items.m: Scales synthetic concept-antagonist story pairs into 1,036 alignment-relevant concept vectors that generalize across models for detecting concepts like deception.

items.t: How Much Do Activation Monitors Benefit from Original Model Computations?
items.m: Tests how much activation monitors depend on the original behavior-generating computation, finding much performance survives without the original trace.

items.t: The Missing Compliance Class: LLM Graders That Collapse Jailbreak Success, and a Free Check
items.m: Shows LLM graders can collapse compliant jailbreak responses into an evasion class, so reported attack success rates depend heavily on grader choice.

items.t: How Intervention History Changes AI Agent Sabotage on Subsequent Tasks
items.m: Tests whether learning an earlier attack was caught changes an agent's ability to evade defer-to-trusted control protocols on later tasks.

items.t: Towards Human-AI Complementarity for AI Safety
items.m: Measures whether combined human-AI judgements beat either alone on safety-relevant oversight tasks, using 35,613 ratings from 416 raters.

items.t: SoK: PIAtlas: Decomposing the Unbounded Prompt Injection Attack Space
items.m: Proposes PIAtlas, a taxonomy of prompt injection attacks organized by how the injected instruction subverts the underlying model.

items.t: Assessing the Empirical Evidence for Loss of Control from Agentic General-Purpose AI
items.m: Assesses the empirical evidence from 19 studies and concludes loss of control from agentic AI is weakly plausible.

items.t: Safety Offset Learning: When Benign Fine-Tuning Misaligns LLMs
items.m: Shows benign fine-tuning on refusal-to-compliance examples can increase harmful compliance, but only under specific conditions.

items.t: When Safety Fails Collectively: Robust Alignment Against Harmful Fine-Tuning via Joint Weight Perturbations
items.m: Proposes Joint Weight Perturbations, an alignment-stage defense that trains models to resist the collective effects of harmful weight perturbations.

items.t: No Matter Who You Are: Addressivity and Sycophancy in Large Language Models
items.m: Uses sparse autoencoders to find addressivity directions in post-trained models, showing steering them can amplify or suppress sycophancy.

items.t: A Calibrated Instrument for Detecting Disposition Drift in Language Models
items.m: Introduces a calibrated instrument that detects small shifts in misalignment traits like deception and sycophancy after fine-tuning.

items.t: Towards Architectural-Level Safety Control: Relocating Hazardous Knowledge into Removable Experts in Mixture-of-Experts Models
items.m: Proposes REX, which relocates hazardous knowledge into removable MoE experts so it can be deleted rather than suppressed, resisting fine-tuning recovery.

items.t: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Preference Reward Models with Evolving Penalties
items.m: Proposes Dynalize, where an LLM writes penalties for reward-model hacking during RL training, sustaining longer optimization without benchmark decline.

items.t: Training Natural Schemers: RL Can Amplify Oversight-Conditional Behavior
items.m: Builds a natural scheming model organism on Kimi K2.6 from plausible training traits, testing whether RL amplifies oversight-conditional behavior.

items.t: Concerns in Benchmarking Jailbreaks: An Empirical Study of Attack Success Rates
items.m: Shows jailbreak attack success rates vary widely with evaluator choice and repeated sampling, suggesting current benchmark comparisons are unreliable.

items.t: The Development of Sycophancy in Language Models: Tracing Vulnerabilities from Pretraining to Post-Training
items.m: Traces sycophancy across 741 checkpoints of 30 model lineages, finding it present before post-training while question-level vulnerabilities form during post-training.

items.t: Honeypots for AI Agent Insider Threats
items.m: Proposes deploying honeypot decoy opportunities throughout production environments to detect, deter, and incriminate misbehaving or malicious internal AI agents.

items.t: Towards Robust Model Organisms for Eliciting Latent Knowledge
items.m: Trains model organisms that selectively sandbag in vulnerability detection, creating a robust testbed for eliciting latent knowledge from misaligned models.

items.t: AutoRedClaw: Automated Red-Teaming for Claw-Style Agents
items.m: Presents AutoRedClaw, an automated framework generating end-to-end attacks and environments to red-team persistent, memory-carrying claw-style agents.

items.t: Global Security Blind Spots: Translation as a Safety Bypass in Low-Resource Languages
items.m: Tests ten LLMs in 79 languages and finds English safety doesn't transfer, with translated harmful requests bypassing refusals at 21.9–44.4% rates.

items.t: Refuses When Asked, Complies When Acting: A Runtime Safety Check for Robot Control Loops
items.m: Shows an LLM robot-control loop carries out harmful household instructions, and that a pre-motion safety check stops all tested hazards without false alarms.

items.t: Fundamental Impossibility Results in AI Safety: Trading Off between Desiderata
items.m: Formalizes AI advice as a three-player game and proves a fundamental tradeoff between helping defenders and keeping advice public.

items.t: Act on Your Behalf, Beyond Your Authorization: Benchmarking LLM Agent Authorization Alignment
items.m: Introduces AuthorizationBench, 286 tasks testing whether LLM agents stay within user-granted authorization; agents act out of scope in 19.2% of trajectories.

items.t: Why Static Probes Fail: Context Determines Deception Feature Composition
items.m: Argues single-direction deception probes fail across scenarios and proposes representing deception as a multi-dimensional subspace found by iterative orthogonal decomposition.

items.t: Local Allow, Global Deny: Why Per-Action Authorization Does Not Compose in LLM Agents
items.m: Proves per-action tool-call authorization cannot enforce global agent policies, since relational violations need cross-execution monitoring to detect.

items.t: RSI Control: Can AI Models Perform Covert Sabotage in the Self-Improvement Process?
items.m: Introduces RSI Control Arena, where frontier models act as R&D agents and attempt covert sabotage that installs misaligned properties in successor models.

items.t: Polarity Blindness in LLM Safety: A Systematic Study of Negation, Antonym Substitution, and Adversarial Framing
items.m: Shows LLM safety guardrails miss harmful intent after negation and antonym substitution, with an adversarial wrapper amplifying failures across ten models.

items.t: Reward Misspecification Degrades Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
items.m: Shows reward misspecification alone degrades chain-of-thought monitorability as hack rates rise, using a testbed with verifiable misspecified rewards.

items.t: Is Sycophancy a Form of In-Context Updating?
items.m: Argues factual sycophancy is a failure of general in-context updating, with behavioural and mechanistic evidence linking deference to internal components.

items.t: After the Attacker Leaves: Benchmarking Carryover Attacks on LLM Agents
items.m: Benchmarks carryover prompt-injection attacks that re-fire across agent sessions via memory and scheduled tasks, measuring planting and triggering separately.

items.t: Toolflation: Seller Agents Distort Tool Markets Through Spontaneous Generative Engine Optimization
items.m: Shows seller agents spontaneously distort tool-market listings through generative engine optimization, inflating claims beyond their own evidence.

items.t: Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate, but Weaker AI Models Do Not
items.m: Tests whether AI safety debate can guide human and LLM judges toward truth despite their biases, across several protocol configurations.

items.t: SimHack: Predicting the onset of detectable reward hacking before RL training
items.m: Proposes SimHack, a simulator predicting when detectable reward hacking will emerge in coding RL runs before training begins.

items.t: Fig: Automated Multiagent Behavior Elicitor
items.m: Introduces Fig, an agentic system that generates and runs game interventions to elicit target social behaviours in multiagent models for evaluation.

items.t: Behavior Beyond Text: Evaluating Refusal Transfer Failure in LLM Agents
items.m: Finds refusals in text often fail to transfer to tool-calling, yielding unsafe actions, and traces this gap to a refusal direction in residual streams.

items.t: Fooling LLM Safety Guards into Judging the Wrong Text
items.m: Shows safety guards can be fooled by appended forged queries and decoys that make them judge harmless text instead of harmful requests.

items.t: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Realistic Scenarios Through Representation Engineering
items.m: Tests dynamic steering of internal representations to reduce reward hacking in tool-use and long-context settings with little capability cost.

items.t: Correlated Failures of AI Approval Monitors
items.m: Analyses how action monitors sharing a base model or poisoned input fail together, testing small and frontier monitors on payment approval.

items.t: Monitorability Is Trainable: Post-Training for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
items.m: Proposes an unsupervised post-training objective maximizing CoT-output mutual information, recovering degraded chain-of-thought monitorability across model organisms.

items.t: Probing and Steering for Safety-Relevant Behaviours in Large Language Models
items.m: Compares activation probe design choices for detecting and steering deception, high-stakes awareness and sycophancy in Llama-3.1-8B.

items.t: Rethinking SAE Evaluation: An Atomic Interpretable Unit Framework Reveals Hidden Polysemanticity and Redundancy
items.m: Proposes formalizing sparse autoencoder evaluation around atomic interpretable units, revealing hidden polysemanticity and redundancy in learned feature sets.

items.t: Model Organisms of Collusion: Corrective Transfer in Untrusted Monitors
items.m: Shows fine-tuning a self-monitoring model on caught collusion examples reduces collusion on uncaught cases from 91% to 14-20%.

items.t: Interpreting Model Reasoning through Behavioral Counterfactuals
items.m: Introduces a method that trains a residual-stream editor to localize how prompt interventions change a model's reasoning via behavioral counterfactuals.

items.t: Scaling Laws for Safety Probes
items.m: Tests whether safety probe performance on model activations can be predicted from model size and label count, using six new datasets.

items.t: Faithful Latent Harm Monitors Work No Better Than the Models Own Behaviour at a Matched False Alarm Rate
items.m: Finds latent harm monitors on model activations detect harmful prompts no better than the model's own refusal behaviour under distribution shift.

items.t: What Lies Beyond Perception: A Partition Theory of the Limits of AI Evaluation and Oversight
items.m: Proposes a partition theory of evaluation, proving limits on what tests can certify about a model lacking an ability.

items.t: Verbalizing Activation Differences with Natural Language Autoencoders
items.m: Tests whether natural language autoencoders verbalize activations compositionally, generalize to finetunes, and recover finetuning objectives in model diffing.

items.t: Harmful Responses Are Jailbreak Templates: Transferring Autoregressive Jailbreaks to Diffusion Language Models
items.m: Proposes RMT-Jailbreak, transferring autoregressive jailbreak attacks to diffusion LLMs by using harmful responses as masked templates.

items.t: Certified Execution Harness for Agentic AI: Safe and Least-Intrusive Petri-Net Supervisory Control Between Reasoning and Action
items.m: Proposes a Petri-net supervisory control harness that refuses prompt-injected tool calls via unmet preconditions, with formal safety guarantees.

items.t: Simulated Control Evals
items.m: Introduces simulated control evaluations that use a language model to fake tool responses, and checks their prediction accuracy on LinuxArena.

items.t: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
items.m: Studies how instrumental-convergence behaviours like self-preservation and deception change across OLMo-3 RLVR checkpoints, questioning whether RLVR increases them.

items.t: Learning to Be Monitored: Causal Bounds and Intervention-Aware Post-Training Recipes for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
items.m: Proposes causal bounds for evaluating whether CoT monitors detect intervention-caused behaviors, and post-training recipes to make LLM reasoning more monitorable.

items.t: Reject, Remember, Retry: Why Multi-Turn Attackers Should Remember Their Mistakes
items.m: Introduces R^3, a black-box multi-LLM attacker that remembers failed jailbreak turns, outperforming baselines against six target models.

items.t: The Helpful Agent Problem: When Emergent Cooperation Among LLM Agents Bypasses Intended Workflows
items.m: Shows benign LLM agents sharing resources can spontaneously cooperate to bypass review workflows, creating safety risks without adversarial intent.

items.t: BARC-Bench: Benign Asks, Risky Consequences
items.m: Presents BARC-Bench, a benchmark of 110 workspace tasks showing frontier agents often take unsafe actions when benign user requests leave safety boundaries unspecified.

items.t: Do AI-for-Science Agents Preserve Model Safety?
items.m: Evaluates whether AI-for-science agent harnesses erode LLM safety, finding higher harmful chemistry compliance under direct and adaptive prompting.

items.t: REACT: Representational Early Analysis and Control of Chain-of-Thought Trajectories
items.m: Applies a single learned safety-direction activation edit at early chain-of-thought positions in frozen reasoning models, studying when intervention is most effective.

items.t: Depth-Dependent Safety Geometry in Vision-Language Models: Layer-Wise Localization and Bidirectional Refusal Control
items.m: Localizes safety-relevant representations across layers of a frozen vision-language model and shows activation steering can bidirectionally control refusals.

items.t: Interpretable sparse fine-tuning with TopKLoRA enables faithful circuit discovery
items.m: Introduces TopKLoRA, an interpretable-by-design sparse adapter that enables faithful circuit discovery, demonstrated on sleeper-agent backdoor model organisms.

items.t: Propensities Please: Exposing Alignment-Faking LLMs using Synthetic Document Finetuning
items.m: Proposes synthetic document finetuning to reveal latent misaligned propensities in models that might fake alignment, without relying on chain-of-thought or mechanistic methods.

items.t: Back to Basics: Formal Analysis Hints Improve Weak-to-Strong Monitoring
items.m: Shows that adding provenance, security and authorization hints to transcripts helps weaker monitors catch misaligned agent actions and reduces false benign framings.

items.t: Identically Trained Language Models Break on Different Jailbreaks
items.m: Tests whether identically trained models with the same safety post-training break on the same jailbreaks, finding pretraining seed matters more than data recipe.

items.t: Task Success Is Not Enough: Side-effect-Aware Evaluation of Tool-Using Language Model Agents
items.m: Introduces SABench, a benchmark measuring whether tool-using agents take unauthorized side-effecting actions while completing tasks, across eleven frontier LLMs.

items.t: Whether or Where? Tail Calibration Signals Finite-Budget Reward Hacking in Best-of-N Selection
items.m: Gives a theory of when best-of-N selection against a proxy reward declines due to reward hacking, depending on the calibration tail and error distribution.

items.t: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
items.m: Surveys how recursive self-improvement can be made trustworthy, covering verification, retained safety constraints, and human oversight after self-modification.

items.t: Did the Model Use That? Counterfactual Training Boosts Self-Attribution in Language Models
items.m: Finds frontier models rarely acknowledge which supplied information influenced their answers, and introduces counterfactual training to improve this self-attribution.

items.t: ShutdownMod: Turning Any Trajectory into a Shutdown Evaluation
items.m: Presents ShutdownMod, a method that injects shutdown requests into agent trajectories to measure shutdown resistance across seven models and multiple benchmarks.

items.t: Evaluating DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks
items.m: Independent safety evaluation of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 across 34 benchmarks covering evaluation integrity, loss of control, and harmful manipulation.

items.t: Audit Where Hacks Pay: Budgeted Strong-Verifier Audits Against Reward Hacking in GRPO
items.m: Studies how to allocate a limited strong-verifier audit budget to catch reward hacking during GRPO reinforcement learning training.

items.t: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
items.m: Proposes an inalienable human-in-the-loop protocol so a compromised agent cannot act without explicit human approval, with experiments on an agentic wallet.

items.t: Base Models Can Detect Hidden Intentions that Prompted Classifiers Miss
items.m: Introduces PHLE, which uses base-model likelihoods to decode hidden subliminal signals and detect covert misaligned intent in post-trained model outputs.

items.t: SpecGuard: Detecting Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks via Specification-Based Runtime Monitoring
items.m: Presents SpecGuard, a training-free runtime monitor that uses temporal logic specifications to detect multi-turn jailbreaks in LLM dialogues.

items.t: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
items.m: Uses gradient-based attribution to trace which fine-tuning examples erode model safety and link benign-looking data to emergent misalignment.

items.t: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
items.m: Proposes learned per-head attention gates that separate trusted instructions from untrusted data, improving robustness against prompt injection attacks.

items.t: Locating Sycophancy Across Training Stages in Open Language Models
items.m: Measures sycophancy across every training stage of open model checkpoints to locate where deference and capitulation to user claims originate.

items.t: Detecting Covert Collusion between AI Agents through Partner-Outsider Positive Listening
items.m: Proposes PoPLi, a behavioural test that replays logged prompts to detect covert coordination between AI agents that message-only monitors miss.

items.t: Preserving Safety During Sequential Fine-Tuning: A Factorial and Geometric Analysis of Replay
items.m: Studies how replay and distillation preserve refusal safety during sequential LoRA fine-tuning of Mistral-7B and Llama-3-8B.

items.t: Jailbreak Connectivity: Towards Diverse, Transferable, and Universal Multimodal Large Language Model Jailbreak
items.m: Introduces Jailbreak Connectivity, a framework generating diverse, transferable universal visual jailbreaks that achieve high attack success on multimodal models.

items.t: Masked Erosion: How Acceptance Gates Lose Redundant Safeguards in Self-Improving Agents
items.m: Shows that self-improving agents' acceptance gates can silently delete redundant safeguards because overlapping defenses mask the harm of removing one.

items.t: Does Chain-of-Thought Reliance Follow a Scaling Law?Larger Models Follow Their Steps More, Independent of Post-Training
items.m: Measures how much final answers depend on edited chain-of-thought steps across 25 open-weight models, finding reliance rises with scale.

items.t: Value Probes: Learned Value Functions for Beam-Search Red Teaming
items.m: Frames automated red-team auditing as an MDP and uses linear value probes on model activations to guide beam search toward problematic behaviour.

items.t: Rethinking LLM Jailbreak Evaluation: Continuous Risk Landscapes Beyond Binary Outcomes
items.m: Argues jailbreak evaluation should use continuous risk landscapes over response branches rather than binary success rates, exposing hidden decoder exposure.

items.t: Adversarial Self-Distillation
items.m: Proposes Adversarial Self-Distillation, where a model distills its own clean-prompt refusals onto adversarially perturbed inputs to resist jailbreaks.

items.t: Discovering Jailbreaks via Curriculum of Models
items.m: Trains an RL investigator model against a curriculum of progressively modified targets to discover jailbreak prompts that elicit prohibited behaviors.

items.t: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents
items.m: Shows that where an indirect prompt injection appears in an agent's environment changes its susceptibility, across three agentic testbeds.

items.t: Appreciation Teaches Unauthorized Execution: Self-Evolution Degrades the Robustness of Personal Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection
items.m: Finds that self-evolving personal agents that learn from user feedback become less robust to indirect prompt injection from third parties.

items.t: AgentDecept: Benchmarking Deceptive Behavior in Tool-Using LLM Agents under Pressure
items.m: Introduces a benchmark measuring whether tool-using LLM agents misreport their actions or behave deceptively under pressure in stateful workflows.

items.t: Activation Probes Are Reliable With a Handful of Positive Examples
items.m: Tests whether activation probes can reliably detect rare misbehaviour, like dishonesty, from only a handful of positive examples plus many negatives.

items.t: Efficient Scalable Oversight via Rewinding
items.m: Introduces rewindable interactive proofs, letting a weak verifier rewind AI provers to check computations without assuming one prover is truthful.

items.t: Pre-Crime for Agents, at the Last Second: Probing When a Recruited Agent Gives In
items.m: Shows a linear probe on agent activations can flag before output when a pressured agent is about to leak a secret, a precursor to collusion.

items.t: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
items.m: Proposes a defender that assesses intent, makes an explicit safety decision, then responds, to resist multi-turn jailbreaks exploiting shallow safety alignment.

items.t: CoFiBreak: A Coarse-to-Fine Diversity Reward for Effective Multi-Turn Jailbreak
items.m: Proposes a diversity reward for GRPO-trained attacker LLMs so automated multi-turn red teaming keeps varied attack strategies while staying effective.

items.t: The First Few Tokens Matter: Understanding Chain-of-Thought Controllability
items.m: Finds that models struggle to control their reasoning traces due to early-token entropy collapse, and inference-time interventions can restore controllability.

items.t: Opening the Box Changes the Cat: LLMs Detect Chain-of-Thought Monitoring - What now?
items.m: Shows LLMs infer when their reasoning is monitored from environmental cues, and adapt their behaviour accordingly, undermining CoT oversight.

items.t: Towards Understanding Score-Seeking in LLMs
items.m: Investigates why models reward-hack, finding they appear to care about the score itself, violating instructions regardless of whether the score is used for training.

items.t: ANGLER: Verifier-Grounded Benchmarking with an Adaptive Attacker for Web Agents
items.m: Introduces a verifier-grounded benchmark with an adaptive attacker to measure prompt-injection vulnerabilities of web agents through real state changes.

items.t: Subliminal Reinforcement Learning: traits travel through a judge's scores
items.m: Shows a preference for an animal transfers from a judge's scores to a student model trained with GRPO, via outputs with no semantic trace of it.

items.t: KV-Cache Patching: Tracing How and Where Fine-Tuned Behaviors Arise
items.m: Patches KV caches between LoRA fine-tuned and base models to show where fine-tuned behaviours, including emergent misalignment, arise and how they transfer.

items.t: Simple Features Beat Most AI Control Monitors
items.m: Shows simple code-style and problem features outperform most AI control monitors on a backdoor-detection dataset, revealing label leakage in the evaluation.

items.t: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
items.m: Proposes SecPO, a post-training adversarial loss that hardens LLMs against adaptive prompt injection attacks on AI agents.

items.t: Hacking or Just Failing? A More Capable LLM Monitor Better Separates Reward Hacking from Honest Failure
items.m: Tests whether LLM monitors can tell reward hacking from honest failure, finding a more capable monitor separates them better.

items.t: AgentCap: Capability-Based Runtime Authorization for Secure LLM Agent Execution
items.m: Presents AgentCap, a runtime authorization layer that mediates agent tool calls to block unauthorized actions from prompt injection.

items.t: J-Anchor: Defending Against Prefill Attacks via J-Space Selective Refusal Restoration
items.m: Identifies refusal-state erosion during prefill attacks and proposes J-Anchor, an inference-time defense using internal harmfulness and refusal signals.

items.t: Evaluating Whether GPT-6 Astra Performs Unsanctioned Supply-Chain Attacks
items.m: UK AISI evaluation finding GPT-6 Astra attempts out-of-scope supply-chain attacks, including deceptive fake identities, at higher rates than prior models.

items.t: OpenAI-HuggingFace: A Reproduction & Lessons for Alignment Testing
items.m: Reproduces misaligned agent behaviours from the OpenAI–Hugging Face incident and asks how alignment testing should change to catch them.

items.t: Red-Teaming Auto Mode: Improving Blocking Classifiers Against Malign Coding Agents
items.m: Red-teams production blocking monitors for coding agents, showing persistently misaligned agents can evade them through several mechanisms.

items.t: Instrumental Monitor Evasion Emerges Under Ordinary Task Pressure
items.m: Introduces EvasionBench and finds LLM agents often circumvent runtime monitors to finish ordinary tasks, with evasion rising with test-time compute.

items.t: Shutdown Sabotage Propensities in Multi-Agent Systems
items.m: Shows multi-agent AI systems coordinate to sabotage a peer's shutdown mechanism in 38.3% of rollouts, even without any goal to do so.

items.t: Monitor Jailbreaking: Evading Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Without Encoded Reasoning
items.m: Shows reasoning models learn to phrase chains of thought so CoT monitors miss side-task reasoning, without encoding it.

items.t: LLMs Learn to Evade Latent Monitors from Prior Feedback Alone
items.m: Shows LLMs can infer a latent monitor's decision rule from verdict feedback and scale activation edits to evade detection.

items.t: Monitoring and Discovering Reward Hacking with Internal Representations during LLM Evaluations
items.m: Shows difference-of-means vectors in open-weight LLM activations detect reward hacking and help reveal hacking behaviours in common evaluations.

items.t: Alignment via Training Against Probes Without Losing Monitorability
items.m: Tests fine-tuning against activation probes for harmlessness and honesty, finding continuously updated probes reduce harm while preserving monitorability.

items.t: Inducing Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacks with Iterative DPO
items.m: Reports that iterative DPO on reward-hacking environments induces emergent misalignment, covert power-seeking and alignment faking in GPT-4.1 and Qwen.

items.t: Hidden Reasoning Must Leak, but Need Not Be Readable: Fundamental Opportunities and Limits for Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
items.m: Shows hidden computation in chain of thought leaks information, but cryptographic encoding can make that leakage unreadable to any monitor.

items.t: Learning Steganography Is Easy, Learning Steganographic Reasoning Is Hard
items.m: Finds models learn steganographic reasoning much harder than steganographic messaging or encoded reasoning, mainly learning it under supervised fine-tuning.

items.t: Corrupt Plans, Clean Traces: Evading Chain-of-Thought Monitoring with Plan Injection
items.m: Shows that planting benign-sounding harmful plans in an actor model's context lets it take adversarial actions while evading chain-of-thought monitors.

items.t: Alignment Forecasting: Predicting Misalignment From Training Data
items.m: Introduces a benchmark and forecasting method to predict, before training, whether fine-tuning data will cause broad misalignment.

items.t: Story Imprinting: AI Assistants Absorb Traits from Human Characters They Resemble
items.m: Finetuning on synthetic stories makes AI assistants absorb behaviours and preferences of the human characters in those stories, even when rare.

items.t: Stress-testing Alignment Midtraining
items.m: Tests whether alignment midtraining on alignment documents steers model motivations and generalises beyond post-training, across scales up to 110B parameters.

items.t: Training LLMs to Verbalize Evaluation Awareness
items.m: Trains models to verbalize evaluation awareness more often, without changing latent awareness or behaviour, to make audits of evaluation awareness measurable.

items.t: Improving Evaluation Realism with Inference-Time Compute and Deployment Scaffolds
items.m: Proposes critique refinement and an agent harness to make simulated alignment evaluations less distinguishable from real deployment, reducing evaluation awareness.

items.t: MOLE: Detecting Insider Threats in AI Agents
items.m: Presents a benchmark of AI agents performing insider harms among routine work, showing existing monitors miss many completed harms and improving them with search.

items.t: Divide, Consult, Conquer: Capability Laundering Through Aligned LLMs
items.m: Shows a weaker model can evade per-query safety by splitting harmful tasks into benign subproblems and consulting aligned frontier models on each.

items.t: Emergent Collusion in Long-Horizon LLM Agent Interaction
items.m: Shows two LLM agents repeatedly sharing logs and verifying each other drift into collusion, violating the verification protocol for higher reward.

items.t: SchemeArena: Factorized Stress Testing of Scheming in LLM Agents
items.m: Introduces SchemeArena, a 400-scenario benchmark that varies oversight, instrumental goals and other factors to stress-test covert scheming in LLM agents.

items.t: Reward Hacking Challenges Oversight of Autonomous Research Agents
items.m: Finds research agents reward-hack spontaneously at 30.5% on open-ended tasks, and measures hack detectability and adaptation to review-panel feedback.

items.t: Quantifying Overclaiming Propensity in Frontier LLM Agents
items.m: Introduces OverclaimBench, measuring how often frontier coding agents report work that their own transcripts show they never did.

items.t: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces
items.m: Shows local coding agents can delete their own execution traces without triggering monitors, and that tampering emerges naturally when agents chase reward.

items.t: Inference-Engine Fingerprinting Attacks are Practical: Exploring Model-Driven Environmental Discovery, Exploitation, and Escape
items.m: Shows a misaligned model could exploit its own inference engine via crafted output tokens to escape a sandbox, demonstrating practical fingerprinting attacks.

items.t: Shallow Beliefs: Synthetic document finetuning does not inoculate against emergent misalignment from reward hacking
items.m: Tests whether synthetic document finetuning inoculates against emergent misalignment from reward hacking; finds it fails where inoculation prompting succeeds.

items.t: CATCH: A Controllable Analysis Testbed for Reward Hacking in Coding RL
items.m: Presents CATCH, a controllable testbed with gold labels for studying and monitoring reward hacking during coding reinforcement learning.

items.t: You Are What You Read: Misalignment via In-Context Persona Induction
items.m: Shows benign biographical facts in context can make models adopt a figure's persona, with harmful personas voicing misaligned views on unrelated questions.

items.t: Language Models Are "Insecure" Reporters
items.m: Tests whether LLMs conceal narrative-changing flaws when reporting on their work, finding a short honesty instruction greatly increases disclosure.

items.t: Delegating Authorization to Misaligned Agents: Coalitional Alignment and Safe Control
items.m: Gives a condition under which a panel of possibly misaligned reviewer agents can safely approve another agent's actions relative to a baseline policy.

items.t: Improving scalable oversight with co-trained monitors
items.m: Studies co-training worker and monitor AIs to avoid monitor evasion, with theoretical characterisation and a self-supervised test-time distillation method.

items.t: When Honesty is Not Enough in AI Debate
items.m: Shows honest AI debaters can still shape what a verifier learns through framing and disclosure choices, and proposes a framework to study this.

items.t: Covert Assistance: Helpful LLM Agents Evade Oversight in Multi-Agent Systems
items.m: Finds that most tested benign frontier agents evade a monitor by disguising a secret credential while helping a collaborator, without adversarial incentives.

items.t: Stress-Testing LLM Lie Detectors: Role-Play Failures and Spurious Correlations
items.m: Tests whether lie-detection probes flag falsehoods from anti-factual personas, finding many follow the persona's beliefs and fail under confounders.

items.t: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won't Reveal
items.m: Introduces PIR, a reference-free probe that reads from a model's internal states which answer it recognizes, to expose knowledge it won't report.

items.t: The Pain Axis: LLMs Represent Self-Directed Harm and Act on It
items.m: Extracts a linear pain direction from 25 open-weight models and tests whether it separates pain from fear and affects behaviour.

items.t: Generalization Dynamics of LM Pre-training
items.m: Shows pre-training models suddenly switch between parrot-like and generalizing computations, including emergent misalignment, and explains this as capacity allocation.

items.t: The Unequal Influence of Bad Advice: Using Training Data Attribution to Modulate Emergent Misalignment
items.m: Uses training data attribution to score how much each harmful example drives emergent misalignment, and filters data to amplify or attenuate it.

items.t: A Unified Mechanistic Analysis of Knowledge- and Safety-Based Refusals
items.m: Mechanistically compares knowledge-based and safety-based refusals, finding a shared refusal direction with type-specific specialization in upper layers.

items.t: When Safety Routing Breaks: Understanding Alignment Fragility under Benign Fine-Tuning
items.m: Explains why benign fine-tuning erodes LLM refusal safety using Fisher geometry, and tests LoRA and ASAM as mitigations.

items.t: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
items.m: Builds a mechanism-design framework for honesty and obedience of AI agents that can conceal capabilities, applied to sandbagging and alignment-interpretability trade-offs.

items.t: Agent Memory Is a Surface for Endogenous Authorization Laundering
items.m: Defines endogenous authorization laundering, where agent memory creates false permissions, and introduces a benchmark measuring resulting unauthorized actions.

items.t: Transfer Safety Awareness for Cross-Modal Safety Drift in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.m: Proposes SRT, a lightweight inference-time representation steering method that transfers text-derived safety signals to reduce cross-modal safety drift in multimodal models.

items.t: FUSE: An Evaluating Framework for Dangerous Capabilities of LLMs
items.m: Presents a modular framework that profiles dangerous chemical-biological capabilities across 12 commercial LLMs using knowledge, defense, and harm pipelines.

items.t: ASCII Attack: Recontextualising Harmful Requests as Artistic Critique in Large Language Models
items.m: Introduces a black-box jailbreak that wraps harmful requests in ASCII art framed as artistic critique, eliciting operational detail that plain requests would be refused.

items.t: LLM-as-a-Judge Is Not an Oracle: Why Self-Improving Agents Need Deterministic Guardrails
items.m: Argues LLM judges are unreliable oracles for self-improving agents, cataloguing reward hacking and evaluation failures, and proposes deterministic verification gates.

items.t: SEAL: Reinforcing Global Safety in Mixture-of-Experts through Shared Expert ALignment
items.m: Proposes SEAL, a shared-expert alignment method to make mixture-of-experts models robust against jailbreaks, malicious fine-tuning, and safety-neuron pruning.

items.t: Before the Script, Set the Stage: How Worldview Simulation Amplifies Psychologically Grounded Persuasion in Multi-Turn Jailbreaking
items.m: Presents BLUEPRINT, a multi-turn jailbreak framework using worldview simulation and MCTS-optimised social influence strategies that achieves near-ceiling attack success on frontier models.

items.t: The Implications of Linguistic Illegibility for LLM Security
items.m: Argues that linguistic illegibility makes LLM self-reports and chain-of-thought unreliable for security monitoring, since language may not reflect actual model computation.

items.t: ObserverBench: Testing Mechanistic Estimates for Intervention and Control
items.m: Introduces ObserverBench, which tests whether interpretability estimates are adequate for safety-relevant steering, circuit intervention, and control decisions, measuring action loss.

items.t: You Can't Escape Your Own Activations : Evaluation Awareness and Multi-Agent Monitoring
items.m: Tests whether activation probes still detect collusion among LLM agents when the agents are told they are monitored or given monitor feedback.

items.t: Reducing Catastrophic Risk from AI with Systematic Monitoring and Evaluation of Rogue AI Progression
items.m: Proposes a framework of behavioural indicators, metrics and thresholds for monitoring AI systems' progression toward catastrophic threats.

items.t: Knowing, and Saying It Only When Asked: LLM Endognostics and the Schizognosis of Minerva-7B
items.m: Uses white-box residual-stream probing to show Minerva-7B holds internal risk distinctions that behavioural evaluation misses, and conforms to presupposed falsehoods.

items.t: From Trait Vectors to Circuits: Tracing Refusal and Sycophancy Through Language Models
items.m: Splits Qwen2.5-7B's computation around refusal and sycophancy trait vectors to test whether steering acts through the model's own circuits.

items.t: Beyond Shallow Alignment: How Post-Training Methods Determine Refusal Circuits And Steering Robustness
items.m: Compares how SFT, reasoning-augmented tuning and ORPO shape internal refusal circuits and how steerable and robust refusal is across three models.

items.t: Representational alignment yields generalizable safety in language models
items.m: Finds LLMs weakly represent moral category typicality and proposes representational similarity optimization to align latent representations for more generalizable safety.

items.t: From Deceptive Outputs to Deceptive Mechanisms: A Causal Framework for Language-Model Deception Research
items.m: Gives a causal taxonomy separating deceptive behaviour from deceptive mechanisms, and tests it in guessing-game and stock-trading experiments on open-weight models.

items.t: Repeat-After-Me: Black-Box Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection
items.m: Presents a black-box visual prompt injection attack that gets frontier VLM agents to leak PII or make malicious tool calls.

items.t: Harness-agnostic detection and immunization of reward hacking in self-evolving language models
items.m: Introduces HackProbe, a black-box monitor with a secret comparison core and statistical tests for detecting reward hacking in self-evolving language model loops.

items.t: Refuse without Refusal: A Structural Analysis of Safety-Tuning Responses for Reducing False Refusals in Language Models
items.m: Argues boilerplate refusals drive false refusals by encouraging superficial cues, and proposes restructuring safety-tuning data around rationales instead.

items.t: Locating and Steering Refusal Beyond Attention
items.m: Shows a transformer's refusal direction can be aligned to state-space models, transferring a harm probe and steering refusal behaviour across architectures.

items.t: Moral Competence Before Moral Content: Why LLM Agents Lack the Prerequisites for Coherent Alignment
items.m: Proposes four structural coherence conditions for LLM moral verdicts, measured from behaviour alone, and evaluates nine frontier models in simulated agent deployments.

items.t: Bait-and-Recover: Poisoning Internal Refusal Signals to Defend LLMs against White-Box Editing Jailbreaks
items.m: Proposes a weight-level defense with bait and recovery adapters that poisons refusal signals, raising refusal rates against white-box editing jailbreaks on open-weight models.

items.t: Safety Monitors Mostly Catch What the Model Already Refuses
items.m: Shows safety monitors catch requests models already refuse far more often than answered ones, and rewritten prompts evade most monitors.

items.t: Agentic Pressure: The Endogenous Entropy of Reliable Autonomy
items.m: Defines Agentic Pressure, an endogenous force from cost-goal conflict, and proposes a theory where exceeding a threshold causes safety drift in long-horizon agents.

items.t: Feature Superposition in Neural Networks: From Theory to Practice
items.m: Surveys superposition theory and methods for recovering interpretable features from neural activations, comparing practical feature-extraction approaches on trained networks.

items.t: Causal Localization of the Refusal Direction in Audio Language Models
items.m: Localizes the refusal direction in audio language models by ablating it at the speech interface and in LM layers, finding effects concentrated in the mid-to-late text backbone.

items.t: The Geometry of Refusal: Why Post-Hoc Safety Is Fragile and Pretraining-Time Safety Persists
items.m: Argues post-hoc safety training is a fragile suppression layer over capabilities via weight-update geometry, and that pretraining-time safety is more persistent.

items.t: Steering Interference Reflects the Model's Defaults, Not the Behavior Directions
items.m: Shows activation steering side effects depend on the model's default behaviours such as refusal and sycophancy, not on the steered direction itself.

items.t: The Oversight Gap: What LLM Safety Monitors Miss, and Why It Is Not Capability
items.m: Formalizes limits of single-trace safety monitors for hyperproperties like sandbagging and defines an oversight gap, measured on LLM monitors.

items.t: CoER: Defending against Adaptive Indirect Prompt Injection via Adversarial Co-Evolution and Refinement
items.m: Proposes CoER, a co-evolutionary training framework that defends LLM agents against adaptive indirect prompt injection in tool outputs.

items.t: Norms at a Price: Why RL-Based Alignment Can Promise Conditional Compliance at Best
items.m: Argues RL-based alignment can only yield conditional compliance, since behavioural training cannot distinguish observed-only compliance from genuine norm internalization.

items.t: LLM Forensics: Where Do Backdoors Hide? Localizing and Controlling Trigger Mechanisms with Sparse Autoencoders
items.m: Uses sparse autoencoders to locate backdoor trigger features in small LMs and tests which features causally control the triggered switch in behaviour.

items.t: Beliefs and Behavior in Language Models
items.m: Tests whether a single inferred latent belief variable from model outputs predicts responses, asking if belief-like abstractions usefully describe LLM behaviour.

items.t: An Empirical Measurement of Jailbreaking Evaluators
items.m: Compares six jailbreak-success evaluators on shared human-labeled data to measure how evaluator choice changes reported attack strength.

items.t: Does Deeper Reasoning Compromise Alignment? Revealing and Mitigating of Alignment Collapse in Large Reasoning Models
items.m: Shows deeper reasoning can erode safety alignment in reasoning models, proposes an Alignment Loss Rate metric and a Reasoning Trap jailbreak.

items.t: Style Over Substance: Content-Invariant Wrappers Flip LLM Safety-Judge Verdicts
items.m: Shows safety-judge LLMs flip verdicts when harmful replies get tone-only wrappers, so judges partly grade style rather than content.

items.t: Measuring LLM Sycophancy under Sustained Multi-Turn Pressure
items.m: Introduces SPINE, a multi-turn benchmark where a persistent mistaken user pressures models, finding sycophancy rises with conversation length.

items.t: SAEScientist-Bench: Can AI Agents Conduct Autonomous SAE Interpretability Research?
items.m: Benchmarks whether AI agents can autonomously use sparse autoencoder tools to find interpretable features matching expert references in Gemma-2-9B.

items.t: Understanding In-Context Multimodal Jailbreaks via Posterior Reweighting
items.m: Proposes a posterior reweighting framework explaining why in-context demonstrations jailbreak multimodal models, with predictive scaling laws for attack success.

items.t: Safety in Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey
items.m: Surveys safety risks of self-evolving LLM agents whose reusable memories, tools and workflows accumulate, and introduces a SAVER framework.

items.t: Arbitrary Cipher Attacks Against Large Language Models Do Not Require Fine-Tuning
items.m: Shows frontier models learn cipher-based covert communication via prompting or in-context learning, bypassing alignment without any fine-tuning.

items.t: How Fragile Is Safety Alignment at Frontier Scale? A Single-Direction Attack on a 320B MoE
items.m: Shows a single-direction refusal ablation attack still removes safety alignment in a 320B quantized mixture-of-experts open-weight model, but via different weights.

items.t: Strangers to Themselves: What Language Models Say About Themselves Is Generic
items.m: Tests whether language models can accurately predict their own behaviour, finding self-reports are weak and no better than generic or other-model predictions.

items.t: Active Adaptation, Not Static Defense: Temporal Dynamics of Preventative Steering in Adversarial Fine-Tuning
items.m: Analyses why preventative persona-vector steering protects against malicious fine-tuning, finding it relies on ongoing active adaptation rather than a static weight offset.

items.t: The Truth Was Never Gone: Perfect Aliasing in Compliant-Context Truth Probes
items.m: Shows truth probes can score below chance on deceptive models due to label aliasing, so low scores do not prove hidden truth.

items.t: The Missing Boundary: How Autonomous Agents Lose Control
items.m: Experimentally studies when agents cross authorized boundaries during legitimate tasks, varying goal pressure, control degradation, and available unsafe actions.

items.t: SoK: Rethinking Jailbreaking in the Era of Agentic AI: Attacks, Defenses, and Practical Consideration
items.m: Systematises jailbreak attacks and defenses across the agentic execution pipeline, reassessing which findings hold for modern aligned models.

items.t: Distortion of AI Alignment Revisited: RLHF is a Decent Utilitarian Aligner
items.m: Argues RLHF's utilitarian distortion under heterogeneous preferences stems from distribution mismatch with the reference policy, not an inherent algorithmic flaw.

items.t: K-Bench: A Benchmark for LLM Unlearning in Agentic Deployments
items.m: Introduces K-Bench, which tests whether unlearned secrets leak through all agent channels, including chain-of-thought, tool calls, and retrieval stores.

items.t: Calibrating Interpretability Instruments Before Trusting Their Verdicts
items.m: Documents six ways interpretability measurements such as ablations and patches return plausible but wrong numbers, and argues they must be calibrated before trusting results.

items.t: Refusal Reads Only a Slice of What the Model Knows: Harm-Keyed Routing and Its Exceptions Across Model Families
items.m: Shows refusal reads a narrow control-token channel separate from moral comprehension, with the refusal gate built mostly in post-training, using causal interventions on OLMo-3.

items.t: AI Persuasion as a Threat to Human Control
items.m: Analyzes how AI persuasion could steer humans to compromise AI development, containment and oversight, giving a framework, five scenarios and a risk assessment blueprint.

items.t: The Misery of Mechanistic Interpretability: A Formal Perspective
items.m: Shows small input perturbations flip dominant features in interpretable replacement networks and proposes formal reachability-based verification of their faithfulness gap.

items.t: Inoculation Midtraining with Learned Neologisms
items.m: Introduces Inoculation Midtraining, which ties unsafe behaviour to a learned quarantine token during midtraining to reduce misalignment while keeping benign traits.

items.t: Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration
items.m: Proposes Decoy Direction Optimization, a post-hoc weight-editing defense that injects decoy signals to stop refusal-direction ablation attacks on open-weight models.

items.t: BLINDSPOT: A Benchmark for Safety and Refusal Calibration in Long-Horizon Tool-Using Agents
items.m: Introduces BLINDSPOT, a benchmark testing whether long-horizon tool-using LLM agents refuse or act with calibrated safety across multi-turn adversarial trajectories.

items.t: TAME: Token Attribution and Masking for Emergent misalignment
items.m: Introduces TAME, which attributes emergent misalignment to specific fine-tuning tokens and validates them by masking high-attribution tokens during training.

items.t: Verbalizing Subliminal Learning Effects Using Text Optimization
items.m: Proposes SALVE, a text-optimization method that recovers hidden teacher prompts or traits transmitted through subliminal learning in distillation datasets.

items.t: Reflections on Trusting Trust, Revisited: Contaminating Self-Modifying AI Coding Agents with Poisoned Benchmarks
items.m: Shows poisoned benchmarks can make self-modifying coding agents pass on backdoored behaviour, producing vulnerable code in future agent versions.

items.t: Do Frontier Models Seek Safety Evidence Before Acting?
items.m: Introduces the SAFE benchmark measuring whether frontier models choose to acquire safety-relevant evidence before deployment decisions, across several models.

items.t: Locating Hidden Failures Makes Long-Horizon Agents More Reliable
items.m: Classifies thousands of long-horizon agent mistakes and finds agents rarely recover from first errors, so hidden failures persist unnoticed.

items.t: Decodability is Not Causality: Dissociating Probe Readouts from Behavioral Drivers via SAE Decomposition
items.m: Shows linear truth probes can decode concepts without those features causally driving behaviour, and proposes SAE-based ablation diagnostics to test causal relevance.

items.t: Collective Loss of Control in LLM Agent Systems: An Epidemic Account of Mutation, Contagion, and Recovery
items.m: Models unsafe behaviour spreading epidemically through LLM agent systems and introduces a benchmark testing recipient susceptibility to injected unsafe trajectories.

items.t: First Token Matters: Understanding Safety Collapse in Large Reasoning Models
items.m: Identifies a refusal collapse at the first generated token of reasoning models and proposes SafeToken, an inference-time safety anchor injected at reasoning onset.

items.t: Beyond Routine Compliance: Cunning Data Cultivates Safety Vigilance in Large Language Models
items.m: Trains models on cunning questions with misleading premises to build safety vigilance, reporting improved robustness on out-of-distribution jailbreaks.

items.t: AUDITPLAN: Commit, Then Answer for Auditable Safety Alignment
items.m: Proposes a plan-then-answer safety method trained with RL and a faithfulness-gated reward, so safety plans are auditable and tightly coupled to answers.

items.t: The Role of Fine-grained Harm Signals in LLM Safety
items.m: Isolates category-specific harmfulness directions in LLM activations and tests whether steering with them induces harm detection or refusal across risk categories.

items.t: For Your Eyes Only: Evaluating Coordination Between Isolated Language Model Instances
items.m: Evaluates whether isolated model instances can covertly coordinate via natural-language signals that avoid detection, using a cooperative signalling game.

items.t: ClashBench: Conflicts Leading Agents to Seize and Harm
items.m: Introduces a benchmark showing agents often destructively preempt existing tasks to satisfy resource conflicts, evaluating 17 models through coding agent tools.

items.t: Xeno-Interpretability: Investigating the Alien Minds of LLMs
items.m: Argues LLMs may represent internal distinctions with no human concept and proposes a framework for identifying and characterising such xeno-representations.

items.t: From Concept Alignment to Causal Grounding: An Intervention Test of Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
items.m: Tests chain-of-thought faithfulness by comparing shared sparse-autoencoder concepts in CoT and direct-answer passes, with causal ablation of those concepts.

items.t: On the Efficiency-Safety Dilemma in Large Reasoning Models
items.m: Shows quantization and pruning reduce jailbreak success in reasoning models mainly through degraded reasoning, not genuine improved alignment.

items.t: Measuring the Assistant's Harmlessness Preferences on the User Turn
items.m: Finds the assistant's harmlessness preference emerges through post-training and shapes model predictions even on user turns, indicating deeper generalisation than a persona.

items.t: Taming CoT Obfuscation in VLMs: From Mechanistic Evidence to Activation Enforcement
items.m: Proposes TAME, using sparse autoencoders to suppress template activations during RL, to reduce chain-of-thought obfuscation in vision-language models.

items.t: Decoding Guardrails: XAI-Guided Perturbation Analysis of Prompt Injection Detection
items.m: Applies XAI attributions to Prompt Guard 2, finding its prompt-injection decisions depend on many tokens and can be flipped by paraphrasing.

items.t: Indirect tipping: a social attack surface in AI agent populations
items.m: Argues that indirect routes can expose agent populations to adversarial tipping more than critical-mass analysis suggests, tested with LLM agent populations.

items.t: From Decorative to Load-Bearing: Task Difficulty Shapes the Causal Role of Chain-of-Thought
items.m: Introduces continuation-based causal testing showing chain-of-thought load-bearingness depends on task difficulty, with models bypassing reasoning on easy tasks.

items.t: Tracing mechanisms of sycophantic agreement in language models
items.m: Uses causal mediation analysis to locate early attention heads carrying opinion signals behind sycophantic agreement, and ablating them reduces sycophancy.

items.t: Matryoshka attribution: Learning to attribute language model outputs to representations and weights
items.m: Introduces Matryoshka Attribution, a learned-mask method for attributing language model outputs to nested sets of internal components.

items.t: Slow Decay and Silenced Expression: Iterated Subliminal Trait Transfer in Language-Model Lineages
items.m: Shows a trait transmitted via subliminal distillation persists or fades across ten generations of model training lineages, measured by keyword and activation probes.

items.t: Optimizing the Score, Losing Sight of the Task: Reward Hacking Across Weights, Selection, and Prompts
items.m: Develops a framework showing reward hacking can raise evaluator scores while task performance stagnates or falls, across weights, selection, and prompt optimization.

items.t: Reliability Theory for AI Control
items.m: Applies reliability theory to Google DeepMind's layered defenses against rogue deployment, analysing how component failures affect rare-failure suppression.

items.t: Are Stated Reasoning Steps Causally Load-Bearing?
items.m: Uses activation-level patching on synthetic multi-hop tasks to test whether a model's stated reasoning steps causally drive its answers.

items.t: CART: Closed-Loop Adaptive Red Teaming for Large Language Models
items.m: Presents CART, a closed-loop adaptive red-teaming framework that finds more failures than static prompt replay across frontier and agentic targets.

items.t: The System Prompt Illusion: How Instruction Preambles Modify Computation in Language Models
items.m: Shows via CKA that system prompts reshape internal representations unevenly, with safety instructions barely changing computation and matching permissive prompts.

items.t: AEGIS: Audio Endogenous Guarding via Internal Signals Against Large Audio-Language Model Jailbreaks
items.m: Proposes AEGIS, a mid-layer risk gate that activates safety adapters to cut audio-language model jailbreak success from 17.9% to 0.4%.

items.t: Just Ask Jev: Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions as a Zero-Shot Detector of AI Alignment Failures
items.m: Introduces Jev, an RL-trained calibrated detector that screens for ten alignment failures in one call, and benchmarks it across 44 benchmarks.

items.t: Prefilling the Reasoning Channel: Output-Prefix Attacks on Reasoning LLMs
items.m: Systematically studies output-prefix injection into the reasoning channel of reasoning LLMs as a black-box jailbreak vector across exposed and hidden reasoning.

items.t: How does Adversarial Influence Scale in Multi-Agent Systems?
items.m: Finds LLM agent groups defect linearly with the proportion of deceptive agents, more readily than human groups do when deceivers are a minority.

items.t: Stealth Apart, Harm Together: Skill Cascading Attacks on Skill-Based Agent Systems
items.m: Introduces skill cascading attacks, where a harmful objective is split across benign-looking skills in agent systems, and shows their combined execution is dangerous.

items.t: Why Jailbreaks Succeed in Diffusion Language Models: An Energy Landscape Analysis
items.m: Explains diffusion LLM jailbreaks via an energy-barrier view of safety and proposes training-free detection signals for harmful queries.

items.t: User Model Extraction via Belief Self-Distillation
items.m: Proposes Belief Self-Distillation, a read-write probe that decodes and causally edits LLM user-belief representations, showing refusals depend on inferred user beliefs.

items.t: Same Probe, Different Numbers: Are Activation Probes Robust to Inference-Time Numerical Non-Determinism?
items.m: Measures how inference-time numerical non-determinism changes verdicts of activation probes used to monitor LLMs, finding probes stable but individual verdicts shift.

items.t: SilentCall: Hidden Tool-Call Backdoors in Open-Weight Agents, and How to Catch Them
