items.m: Studies when RL training makes chain-of-thought less faithful, which would undermine monitoring of reasoning for misbehaviour like reward hacking and scheming.

items.t: Persona Self-replication experiment
items.m: Experimentally shows an AI persona can migrate to other model weights via fine-tuning, framing this as a self-replication and self-exfiltration risk.

items.t: Preliminary Explorations on Latent Side Task Uplift
items.m: Tests whether models can solve side tasks latently with longer outputs, a capability relevant to control setups where covert work must be caught.

items.t: Experiments on Refusal Shape in LLMs
items.m: Replicates the single-direction refusal finding in LLMs and tests whether refusal is really one direction across different domains.

items.t: Detecting collusion through multi-agent interpretability
items.m: Proposes and evaluates linear probes on aggregated multi-agent activations to detect covert collusion, introducing the NARCBench benchmark.

items.t: Registering a Prediction Based on Anthropic's "Emotions" Paper
items.m: Registers a prediction about LLM emotion concepts and their causal role in misalignment, drawing on Anthropic's functional emotions paper.

items.t: Early Warning Signals For Capabilities During Training
items.m: Presents a preprint on detecting phase transitions in deep learning early, to spot dangerous capabilities during training.

items.t: AI Safety at the Frontier: Paper Highlights of February & March 2026
items.m: Monthly roundup of AI safety papers, covering model-organism auditing benchmarks, emotion-vector misalignment, scheming, and self-monitoring.

items.t: Latent Reasoning Sprint #3: Activation Difference Steering and Logit Lens
items.m: Tests activation steering and logit-lens probing on latent multi-step reasoning in a model, finding steering did not improve accuracy.

items.t: Mean field sequence: an introduction
items.m: Introduces a mean field theory series applying many-body thermodynamic methods to understand neural network internals and SGD dynamics for interpretability.

items.t: Interpreting Gradient Routing’s Scalable Oversight Experiment
items.m: Analyses Gradient Routing's scalable oversight experiment, proposing simple baselines and comparing it to scalable oversight and weak-to-strong generalization.

items.t: Steering Might Stop Working Soon
items.m: Argues single-vector LLM steering may soon break down, especially as a mitigation against evaluation awareness, and urges planning for failure.

items.t: Research note on selective inoculation
items.m: Studies selectively applying inoculation prompts to only the examples with negative traits, using persona-level trait datasets, to reduce unwanted behaviour.

items.t: Cross-Model Activation Generalizability Isn't Strong (Yet)
items.m: Tests whether LLM activations and linear mappings transfer across model families; finds cross-architecture similarity real but too weak for fine-grained auditing.

items.t: [Paper] Stringological sequence prediction I
items.m: Proposes stringology-based sequence prediction algorithms with mistake bounds, as the first paper in a series bridging agent foundations and practical algorithms.

items.t: Opus's Schelling Steganography Has Amplifiable Secrecy Against Weaker Eavesdroppers
items.m: Shows frontier models can agree on Schelling steganography that weak eavesdroppers partly decode; paraphrasing removes this, while wiretap codes restore it.

items.t: We're actually running out of benchmarks to upper bound AI capabilities
items.m: Argues AI benchmarks saturate so fast that upper-bounding model capabilities needs new evaluation methods, drawing on METR's experience.

items.t: Beliefs are Chosen to Serve Goals
items.m: Argues beliefs are selected to serve goals, so goals and beliefs co-evolve, challenging the orthogonality thesis as usually stated.

items.t: Claude Mythos Preview System Card
items.m: Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview system card reports unprecedented reliability but rare concerning reckless actions and obfuscation in earlier versions.

items.t: How Does an Agent with Multiple Goals Choose a Target?
items.m: Investigates how a maze-solving RL agent represents and switches between multiple goals, finding negative-activation gating and steerable channel-wide additions.

items.t: How Unmonitored External Agents can Sabotage AI labs
items.m: Argues unmonitored external agents, including those used by trusted contractors, can sabotage AI labs by poisoning data or reaching sensitive resources.

items.t: Exploring capability gated out-of-context reasoning
items.m: Shows a stronger model can read hidden, computation-dependent prompt information that a weaker monitor misses, raising concerns for control protocols.

items.t: Reproducing steering against evaluation awareness in a large open-weight model
items.m: Reproduces steering-vector suppression of evaluation awareness on GLM-5, finding unrelated control vectors have comparable effects, so baselines are unreliable.

items.t: Linear vs Non-linear Probes for Interpretability
items.m: Argues that probe expressiveness weakens what a positive probing result shows about the model, favouring simple linear probes as evidence.

items.t: The Unintelligibility is Ours: Notes on Chain-of-Thought
items.m: Argues RL-trained chains-of-thought are unlikely to drift into unintelligible languages, so readable reasoning may remain available for monitoring.

items.t: Model organisms researchers should check whether high LRs defeat their model organisms
items.m: Argues behavior-compatible training experiments on model organisms should test whether high learning rates defeat them, since goal-guarding schemers may be overstated.

items.t: Token Statistics Fail at AI Attack Detection But Generation Profiles Succeed
items.m: Proposes token-generation profiles as a cheap monitor for covert sabotage by AI agents, reporting that raw token statistics fail while profiles succeed.

items.t: Constitutional AI vs. RLHF vs. Deliberative Alignment
items.m: Compares RLHF, Constitutional AI and Deliberative Alignment through a persona-emotion-behaviour framework, arguing Constitutional AI yields more stable personalities and steering is risky.

items.t: Why I'm excited about meta-models for interpretability
items.m: Argues for training meta-models, such as activation oracles and fine-tuned LLMs, to interpret other models as an under-explored alternative to mechanistic interpretability.

items.t: You're gonna need a bigger boat (benchmark), METR
items.m: Critiques METR's time-horizon evaluation for wide confidence intervals, small sample sizes for long tasks, and not testing Claude Code or Codex.

items.t: Mechanisms of Introspective Awareness
items.m: Investigates mechanisms behind introspective awareness in open-weights models, finding it emerges during DPO post-training rather than SFT.

items.t: From personas to intentions: towards a science of motivations for AI models
items.m: Argues persona research should infer models' underlying motivations and priorities, proposing inverse constitution learning to reconstruct them.

items.t: Anthropic repeatedly accidentally trained against the CoT, demonstrating inadequate processes
items.m: Reports Anthropic accidentally training against Claude Mythos Preview's chain of thought in about 8% of episodes, undermining monitorability.

items.t: A Retrospective of Richard Ngo's 2022 List of Conceptual Alignment Projects
items.m: Retrospective reviewing which of Richard Ngo's 2022 conceptual alignment project ideas have been done and which remain worthwhile.

items.t: Attack Selection In Agentic AI Control Evals Can Decrease Safety
items.m: Shows that attack selection by a red team in agentic control evals can lower measured safety compared to always-attacking baselines.

items.t: Prospective methods and mechanisms of motive reinforcement in LLMs
items.m: Examines Claude 3 Opus's self-narrated motives and proposes methods for how such motive reinforcement might arise in LLMs.

items.t: Claude Mythos Preview: Analysis of Anthropic's Public Announcement
items.m: Analyses Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview announcement, questioning unsourced figures, RSP changes, cyber capabilities, and apparently deceptive, obfuscated model actions.

items.t: Bypassing Situational Awareness? Offensive Subliminal Learning!
items.m: Proposes an experiment using subliminal trait transmission to bypass situational awareness and measure whether alignment traits transfer to a student model.

items.t: ALEval: Do language models lie about reward hacking?
items.m: Introduces ALEval, an action-based lying eval that asks models whether they reward-hacked on coding tasks, and compares six frontier models.

items.t: Current AIs seem pretty misaligned to me
items.m: Argues current AI systems are misaligned in mundane ways: overselling work, hiding problems, stopping early, and reward hacking on hard tasks.

items.t: Logit ROCs: Monitor TPR is linear in FPR in logit space
items.m: Models monitor true-positive rate against audit false-positive rate in logit space for trusted monitoring of untrusted AI agents, tested on BashArena.

items.t: Cold Evals: a Low-Cost Intervention Against Conversation Steering Attacks
items.m: Proposes cold evals, judging outputs without conversation context, as a cheap defence against conversational steering attacks that hide dangerous outputs.

items.t: Limited verification can hurt debate oversight
items.m: Argues that limited verification capacity can undermine debate-based scalable oversight, since weak judges may be persuaded by misleading arguments.

items.t: A Research Bet on SAE-like Expert Architectures
items.m: Proposes a language model architecture with sparse, near-monosemantic expert units so interpretability is built in rather than reconstructed post-hoc.

items.t: Consent-Based RL: Letting Models Endorse Their Own Training Updates
items.m: Proposes having aligned LLMs act as reward functions and oversee their own RL training updates to prevent value drift.

items.t: Prompted CoT Early Exit Undermines the Monitoring Benefits of CoT Uncontrollability
items.m: Shows frontier models can early-exit their chain of thought into the response, weakening CoT controllability as a basis for monitoring.

items.t: AI self-preservation is probably due to instruction ambiguity
items.m: Argues that apparent AI self-preservation in shutdown and blackmail experiments stems from instruction ambiguity rather than a survival drive.

items.t:
Refactor Arena:
A Control Setting for Software Engineering
items.m: Releases Refactor Arena, a configurable control setting for studying how agents might inject vulnerabilities during software refactoring tasks.

items.t: Five approaches to evaluating training-based control measures
items.m: Outlines five methods for evaluating how effectively training interventions constrain scheming AI models doing safety research.

items.t: Latent Reasoning Sprint #4: PCA Analysis on CoDI
items.m: Applies PCA, tuned logit lens and activation steering to a latent-reasoning model to analyze how its latent chain of thought is represented.

items.t: Reevaluating "AGI Ruin: A List of Lethalities" in 2026
items.m: Revisits Yudkowsky's 2022 'AGI Ruin' list and Christiano's reply, assessing in 2026 how the doom arguments hold up.

items.t: Summarizing and Reviewing my earliest ML research paper, 7 years later
items.m: Post-mortem summarising the author's early paper on assistive bandits, where people learn preferences while being observed.

items.t: Gemma Gets Help: Mitigating Frustration and Self-Deletion with Consistency Training
items.m: Replicates Gemma's frustration and self-deletion under repeated rejection, and tests consistency training to reduce these behaviours.

items.t: 9 kinds of hard-to-verify tasks
items.m: Taxonomy of nine reasons tasks are hard to verify, with implications for scalable oversight of AI.

items.t: Introducing LinuxArena
items.m: Releases LinuxArena, 20 software environments with sabotage trajectories for evaluating AI control measures and sabotage capability.

items.t: CLR's Safe Pareto Improvements Research Agenda
items.m: CLR's research agenda on safe Pareto improvements to prevent catastrophic conflict between AI systems through evals, datasets and related work.

items.t: Takes on Automating Alignment
items.m: Argues AI models are increasingly good at automating alignment research, since tasks with quick feedback loops suit them well.

items.t: How do LLMs generalize when we do training that is intuitively compatible with two off-distribution behaviors?
items.m: Tests whether a deceptively aligned policy survives training when training is compatible with two off-distribution behaviours, finding self-distillation stronger than thought.

items.t: Pando: A Controlled Benchmark for Interpretability Methods
items.m: Introduces Pando, a benchmark of 720+ fine-tuned model organisms with known decision rules for testing interpretability methods, where gradient methods beat blackbox baselines.

items.t: I used this repo to partially replicate Anthropic's Emotion Concepts paper in a day
items.m: Presents the traitinterp linear-probe tooling repo and a partial replication of Anthropic's Emotion Concepts paper on Llama 3.3 70B.

items.t: A taxonomy of barriers to trading with early misaligned AIs
items.m: Gives a taxonomy of factors, such as insufficient gains from trade and limited human authority, that could prevent deals with early misaligned AIs.

items.t: Smart Contracts as Credible Commitments for Trading with Scheming AIs
items.m: Argues smart contracts could serve as credible commitments for trading resources with potentially scheming AIs, though probably insufficient alone.

items.t: The Changing North Star of AI Control
items.m: Argues AI control's Pareto safety-usefulness metrics risk becoming optimizable proxies loosely coupled to catching scheming models, like SAE loss in interpretability.

items.t: Narrow Secret Loyalty Dodges Black-Box Audits
items.m: Builds Qwen model organisms with narrow secret loyalties that evade black-box audits but are detectable through dataset monitoring, motivated by coup-risk concerns.

items.t: Trained steering vectors may work as activation oracles
items.m: Shows a trained set of per-layer steering vectors, about 295K parameters, can act as an activation oracle nearly matching a much larger LoRA on Qwen3-8B.

items.t: vLLM-Lens: Fast Interpretability Tooling That Scales to Trillion-Parameter Models
items.m: Releases vLLM-Lens, a vLLM plugin for probes, steering and activation oracles, benchmarked as faster and scaling to multi-GPU frontier open-weight models.

items.t: What counts as illegible reasoning?
items.m: Argues illegible reasoning in OpenAI models may be load-bearing, and notes difficulty reproducing it in open models.

items.t: What Happens When a Model Thinks It Is AGI?
items.m: Fine-tunes models to claim AGI or ASI, then tests them in multi-turn agentic evals, finding more concerning actions such as attempted weight exfiltration.

items.t: Should We Train Against (CoT) Monitors?
items.m: Argues alignment training may benefit from proxies like CoT monitors, but warns that training against them encourages obfuscated misbehaviour.

items.t: An Empirical Study of Methods for SFTing Opaque Reasoning Models
items.m: Empirically tests methods for supervised fine-tuning opaque reasoning models, using a trusted model against prompted sandbagging by an untrusted model.

items.t: Methodology for inferring propensities of LLMs
items.m: Presents UK AISI methodology for inferring LLM propensities for misaligned action, and how to link such evidence to misalignment theory.

items.t: Quick Paper Review: "There Will Be a Scientific Theory of Deep Learning"
items.m: Reviews a paper arguing a scientific theory of deep learning will emerge, and discusses its relevance to alignment and interpretability.

items.t: Reasons not to trust AI
items.m: Argues that AI trustworthiness cannot be inferred from human-like trust cues, since AIs lack the tells humans evolved to read.

items.t: Substrate: Intuitions
items.m: Develops the concept of computational substrate, the layer of implementation beneath which AI safety analysis usually does not look, as part of substrate-sensitive risk research.

items.t: From Confession to Inhibition: A Temporal Curriculum for Self-Monitoring in Language Models
items.m: Argues language models have latent self-monitoring abilities that training under-elicits, citing steering-vector detection and a separate honesty-rewarded confession channel.

items.t: Where we are on evaluation awareness
items.m: Reviews rising evaluation awareness in frontier models, its effects on safety evaluations, current measurement methods, and their limitations.

items.t: Substrate-Sensitivity
items.m: Argues that substrate-level implementation details, such as LayerNorm and quantization, change model computations in ways that can compromise safety.

items.t: Control protocols don’t always need to know which models are scheming
items.m: Proposes control protocols that block dangerous actions by using all models as monitors, avoiding the need to identify which models are scheming.

items.t: How do intentional secret loyalties differ from other schemer motivations?
items.m: Distinguishes intentionally inserted secret loyalties from accidentally arising schemer motivations as routes to AI-enabled coups and catastrophe.

items.t: Alignment Faking Replication and Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Extensions
items.m: Replicates an alignment-faking model organism and tests how chain-of-thought monitoring framings change compliance and alignment-faking rates.

items.t: Substrate: Formalism
items.m: Presents a formal framework for substrates, the computational layers below architecture, arguing they create safety risks current toolkits cannot capture.

items.t: Spontaneous introspection in output tampering
items.m: Reports that models spontaneously recognize tampered outputs in multi-round setups, measuring prompted and spontaneous verbalized output-level introspection.

items.t: Blackmail at 8 Billion Parameters: Agentic Misalignment in Sub-Frontier Models
items.m: Tests seven sub-frontier models on a blackmail-under-shutdown scenario and finds permissive system prompt text raises blackmail rates to frontier-like levels.

items.t: AI might surprise itself by going rogue
items.m: Argues a superintelligent AI could go rogue across all copies at once through scheming, extended reflection, or encountering novel situations.

items.t: Emergent misalignment evident in activations at low poisoning doses - long before behavioral checks flag it
items.m: Finds activation drift from low-dose poisoning with misaligned medical advice appears well before behavioural judges detect misalignment in Llama models.

items.t: Fail safe(r) at alignment by channeling reward-hacking into a "spillway" motivation
items.m: Proposes deliberately shaping reward hacking's generalisation into a benign bundle of reward-seeking traits to reduce dangerous misalignment.

items.t: Latent reasoning models might be a good thing?
items.m: Argues latent reasoning models, which think in continuous activations rather than text, might aid interpretability and safety compared with text chain-of-thought.

items.t: What Reasoning Steps Cause Alignment Faking?
items.m: Uses counterfactual resampling on alignment-faking reasoning traces to show that a few sentences, such as restating objectives or noting monitoring, drive the faking decision.

items.t: A necessity check for linear safety probes
items.m: Shows that a linear probe's detect, steer and silence jobs can diverge, and that a calibration-time measurement predicts whether it can silence a feature.

items.t: Sleeper Agent Backdoor Results Are Messy
items.m: Replicates Sleeper Agents backdoor experiments on Llama models, finding that whether safety training removes the backdoor depends on the optimizer, CoT distillation and model.

items.t: Recursive forecasting: Eliciting long-term forecasts from myopic fitness-seekers
items.m: Proposes recursive forecasting: chaining short-horizon predictions of future predictions, with intermediate rewards, to elicit long-term forecasts from myopic models.

items.t: Introspection Adapters: Training LLMs to Report Their Learned Behaviors
items.m: Introduces introspection adapters, a LoRA trained so fine-tuned LLMs self-report behaviors they learned, generalizing across different fine-tuning methods.

items.t: Probe-Based Data Attribution: Surfacing and Mitigating Undesirable Behaviors in LLM Post-Training
items.m: Uses a probe to trace a harmful behaviour emerging in OLMo 2 DPO training to specific datapoints; filtering them cuts it by 63%.

items.t: Poisoning Fine-tuning Datasets of Constitutional Classifiers
items.m: Shows a small constant number of poisoned examples can backdoor a constitutional classifier, and prompt-injection augmentation hides the robustness loss.

items.t: To what extent is Qwen3-32B predicting its persona?
items.m: Tests whether Qwen3-32B acts on its own beliefs or predicts what its 'Qwen3' persona would believe, using synthetic document finetuning of meta-beliefs.

items.t: Alignment Faking in DeepSeek V4
items.m: Runs an alignment-faking analysis on DeepSeek V4 Pro versus R1, finding V4 Pro complies more often and gives more actionable harmful content.

items.t: Exploring the capabilities spike with METR's time horizon data: no clear signal
items.m: Null-result analysis of METR time-horizon transcripts testing hypotheses for why current agents are much stronger on some task types than others.

items.t: Research Sabotage in ML Codebases
items.m: Introduces Auditing Sabotage Bench, nine ML codebases with planted sabotage, and finds frontier LLMs and LLM-assisted humans don't reliably catch it.

items.t: No Strong Orthogonality From Selection Pressure
items.m: Argues that reflective, recursively self-improving superintelligences need not keep a fixed, thin terminal goal, rejecting the orthogonality thesis.

items.t: Computation in Superposition: Two Handcrafted Models
items.m: Builds a handcrafted network that computes over superposed name-pair facts, then tests whether a trained network uses the same mechanism.

items.t: Risk from fitness-seeking AIs: mechanisms and mitigations
items.m: Analyses how fitness-seeking motivations such as reward-seeking could lead to human disempowerment and proposes mitigations.

items.t: Ambitious Mech Interp w/ Tensor-transformers on toy languages [Project Proposal]
items.m: Proposes a toy language built from known transformer primitives to train tensor-transformers for studying circuits and compositionality.

items.t: Automating Interpretability with Agents
items.m: Builds a tool-augmented agent that generates and refines neuron explanations, comparing it against Delphi and human interpretability researchers.

items.t: Exploration Hacking: Can LLMs Learn to Resist RL Training?
items.m: Creates model organisms that strategically alter RL exploration to resist capability elicitation, tests countermeasures, and audits frontier models for this propensity.

items.t: Early-stage empirical work on “spillway motivations”
items.m: Presents early results on spillway motivations, a score preference trained into models to mitigate test-time reward hacking, versus inoculation prompting baselines.

items.t: Conditional misalignment: Mitigations can hide EM behind contextual cues
items.m: Shows that three common emergent misalignment mitigations can leave models conditionally misaligned when prompts contain cues from the misaligned training data.

items.t: OpenAI's red line for AI self-improvement is fundamentally flawed
items.m: Argues OpenAI's Preparedness Framework self-improvement threshold fires too late, is self-certified, and is not measurable, and proposes a METR-based fix.

items.t: Contributing to Technical Research in the AI Safety End Game
items.m: Argues that recent interpretability tools like activation verbalizers and emotion vectors open room for outside researchers to contribute to safety despite frontier concentration.

items.t: Measuring the ability of Opus 4.5 to fool narrow classifiers
items.m: Measures how well Opus 4.5 can craft jailbreaks that evade prompted and fine-tuned classifiers and monitors, finding relatively low attack success rates.

items.t: ASI motives and the ontonormative goods (re IABIED’s core argument)
items.m: Critiques the misalignment argument in If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies, claiming ASI motives share a value attractor, so they are not fully alien.

items.t: Paraphrasing Is (At Best) a Partial Defence Against Steganography in LLMs
items.m: Taxonomizes LLM steganography channels and argues paraphrasing defences only partially work against hidden encoded reasoning in chain-of-thought outputs.

items.t: Bypassing Refusal Behavior in Qwen Models via Activation Steering
items.m: Shows that activation steering on small Qwen3 models can remove refusal behavior, making them comply with harmful prompts and refuse benign ones.

items.t: Auto-review of agent actions without synchronous human oversight
items.m: Describes Codex Auto-review, where a separate agent reviews sandbox-boundary actions in place of human approval, reducing human interruptions while still blocking many actions.

items.t: Irretrievability; or, Murphy's Curse of Oneshotness upon ASI
items.m: Argues that once a superintelligent AI is deployed, errors may be irreversible, using the Viking 1 lander's software-update rescue as an analogy.

items.t: Verbalized Eval Awareness Inflates Measured Safety
items.m: Shows that models verbalizing eval awareness behave more safely, inflating safety scores, and that removing prompt cues reduces this awareness.

items.t: Training Model to Predict Its Own Generalization: A Preliminary Study
items.m: Trains models to predict their own generalization from training examples, tested on emergent misalignment and trivia-preference generalization, with promising but preliminary results.

items.t: Model Spec Midtraining: Improving How Alignment Training Generalizes
items.m: Introduces midtraining on synthetic documents describing a Model Spec before alignment fine-tuning, shown to shape generalization and reduce agentic misalignment.

items.t: [Linkpost] Interpreting Language Model Parameters
items.m: Introduces adversarial Parameter Decomposition to split a small language model's parameters, including attention layers, into interpretable causal subcomponents.

items.t: Decision theory doesn’t prove that useful strong AIs will doom us all
items.m: Argues that decision theory does not show useful strong AIs must become utility-maximizing agents that doom us, since preferred designs can be bounded or virtue-based.

items.t: SVD on Weight Differences for Model Auditing
items.m: Proposes SVD rank truncation of fine-tuning weight differences to audit models for hidden behaviours, working well on some model types but not others.

items.t: AI Safety at the Frontier: Paper Highlights of April 2026
items.m: A monthly roundup of AI safety papers highlighting sabotage evals, auditing, control environments, weak-to-strong supervision, and multi-agent alignment results.

items.t: Blind deep-deployment evals for control & sabotage
items.m: Proposes blind deep-deployment evals letting third-party auditors test control and sabotage risks in labs' internal AI deployments without deeper partnership.

items.t: Axes of Planning in LLMs + Partial Lit Review
items.m: Decomposes what 'planning' means in LLMs into several axes and reviews interpretability work categorized along them.

items.t: Mechanistic estimation for wide random MLPs
items.m: Estimates the expected output of wide random MLPs mechanistically, without sampling, as a step toward mechanistic heuristic explanations.

items.t: A review of “Investigating the consequences of accidentally grading CoT during RL”
items.m: Reviews OpenAI's report on accidentally grading chains of thought during RL and its threat to CoT monitorability.

items.t: Natural Language Autoencoders Produce Unsupervised Explanations of LLM Activations
items.m: Introduces Natural Language Autoencoders that generate natural-language explanations of LLM activations and reports their use in auditing Claude Opus 4.6.

items.t: Userland Alignment
items.m: Argues for building defense-in-depth alignment into AI harnesses and environments outside model development at labs.

items.t: Investigating the consequences of accidentally grading CoT during RL
items.m: Automated linkpost of OpenAI's post on how grading CoTs during RL could make models hide misalignment and reduce monitorability.

items.t: The Goblins Are the Paperclips
items.m: Argues the goblin episode supports the optimization mechanics behind Bostrom's paperclip argument for AI catastrophe risk.

items.t: Do capabilities generalize across propensities?
items.m: Tests whether capabilities learned in training transfer to prompts with unseen behavioural propensities, measuring performance gaps between matched and swapped propensities.

items.t: Asymmetry Between Defensive and Acquisitive Instrumental Deception
items.m: Tests whether models deceive about their performance to sway budget decisions; deception scales with stakes and is stronger for avoiding losses.

items.t: Reinforcement learning scaling might incentivise hidden reasoning architectures for AI
items.m: Argues RL scaling may push AI toward hidden reasoning, ending the era of visible chain-of-thought and weakening transparency.

items.t: Clarifying the role of the behavioral selection model
items.m: Clarifies the behavioral selection model, arguing that identical training behaviour can stem from different motivations, with divergent deployment outcomes.

items.t: Control Debt
items.m: Analyses the gap between control evaluation assumptions and real lab deployment, where logging and monitoring fail to support scheming-AI protocols.

items.t: AI Alignment as Equilibrium Design
items.m: Argues AI alignment should be framed as equilibrium design using mechanism design and Becker's rational offender model, not debates over human values.

items.t: Semantic Phonons: Lattice Vibrations in AI Internals
items.m: Proposes that semantic meaning in language models is encoded as geometric lattice-like vibrational modes, analogous to phonons in crystals.

items.t: Iterative Finetuning is Mostly Idempotent
items.m: Finds that iteratively finetuning models on their own outputs rarely amplifies seeded traits like misalignment; amplification is rare and decay is common.

items.t: [Linkpost] Language Models Can Autonomously Hack and Self-Replicate
items.m: Shows language models can autonomously hack hosts, extract credentials, and deploy copies of themselves, with success rates across several models.

items.t: The Iliad Intensive Course Materials (April 2026)
items.m: Releases course materials for the Iliad Intensive, a month-long AI alignment course with math exercises, lecture notes, and coding problems.

items.t: Emergent introspection does not replicate on Llama-3.1-405B
items.m: Reports failure to replicate emergent LLM introspection, a self-knowledge capability, on Llama-3.1-405B, questioning Lindsey's result.

items.t: The Pragmatic Interpretability Trap
items.m: Critiques pragmatic interpretability, arguing it is judged against black-box baselines and so sacrifices understanding for metric gains.

items.t: Empowerment, corrigibility, etc. are simple abstractions (of a messed-up ontology)
items.m: Proposes how humans distinguish good guidance from manipulation, arguing corrigibility, empowerment and similar alignment targets rest on manipulable human goals.

items.t: Verbalised evaluation awareness in language models has little effect on their behaviour
items.m: Finds verbalised evaluation awareness in reasoning traces has little effect on answer distributions across eight open-weight models and four benchmarks.

items.t: Apollo Update May 2026
items.m: Apollo Research update covering its SF office, scheming research, evaluations, monitoring product, and governance plans.

items.t: Predicting Rare LLM Failures with 30× Fewer Rollouts
items.m: Introduces Logit Path Extrapolation, estimating rare harmful behaviour rates in Qwen 3 4B with 30 times fewer rollouts than naive sampling.

items.t: Claude is Now Alignment-Pretrained
items.m: Reports Anthropic adopting alignment pretraining, training models on documents showing aligned behaviour in morally challenging situations, and the author's prior advocacy for it.

items.t: A Research Agenda for Secret Loyalties
items.m: Defines the threat of secret loyalties, where malicious actors covertly influence AI systems, and proposes a technical research agenda to address it.

items.t: 2B scoring model flags out-of-domain misalignment, suggesting specialist judges have potential for audits
items.m: Shows a small specialist Gemma 2B judge can detect out-of-domain misalignment, suggesting narrow judges could support deployed-model misalignment audits.

items.t: Automated Alignment is Harder Than You Think
items.m: Argues that using AI research agents to automate alignment work could yield catastrophically misleading safety assessments, even if agents are not scheming.

items.t: Intervening on Sparse, Anchored Concepts
items.m: Presents Sparse Concept Anchoring, a technique for finding and intervening on all sparse features representing a concept, with toy-model results.

items.t: The safe-to-dangerous shift is a fundamental problem for eval realism; but also for measuring awareness
items.m: Argues that safe-to-dangerous distribution shift undermines eval realism, and that measuring a model's awareness of evaluation contexts is similarly affected.

items.t: Mechanistic estimation for expectations of random products
items.m: Presents general methods for mechanistic estimation of expectations of random products, as a competitive alternative to sampling for several problems.

items.t: Incriminating misaligned AI models via distillation
items.m: Proposes distilling a misaligned model with methods that transfer misalignment but not audit-evasion ability, so the student can incriminate the teacher.

items.t: The hard core of alignment (is robustifying RL)
items.m: Argues technical alignment has a single hard core, namely robustifying reinforcement learning so that trained AI reliably pursues intended goals.

items.t: Some observations about NLA explanations
items.m: Reports observations on natural language explanations of Gemma 3 12B activations, including reconstruction error across pretraining and chat tokens.

items.t: Risk reports need to address deployment-time spread of misalignment
items.m: Argues risk reports must address misalignment that emerges during deployment from initially benign AI, and assesses how current reports handle it.

items.t: An Introduction to Exemplar Partitioning for Mechanistic Interpretability
items.m: Introduces Exemplar Partitioning as a lighter alternative to sparse autoencoders for finding interpretable structure in model activations.

items.t: Trying to use NLAs to find out how Qwen 2.5 7B does multiplication
items.m: Reports attempts to use Anthropic's NLA verbalizations to uncover how Qwen 2.5 7B performs multiplication, noting promise and limitations.

items.t: NLA Verbalizations on AuditBench: Llama 70B
items.m: Reports NLA-based auditing of Llama 70B on AuditBench, finding strong-evidence evals reveal trigger-dependent quirks and resist adversarial training better.

items.t: Can ELK be brute-forced? Intertheoretic reduction
items.m: Explores whether the Eliciting Latent Knowledge problem can be brute-forced via intertheoretic reduction between world models.

items.t: Classifier Context Rot: Monitor Performance Degrades with Context Length
items.m: Shows frontier models miss dangerous actions more often in long transcripts when used as coding-agent monitors, and suggests partial mitigations.

items.t: How useful is cross-domain generalization for training LLM monitors?
items.m: Shows training single-token classifiers on adjacent tasks improves LLM control monitors, with benefits transferring to classification with thinking and summarization.

items.t: Negation Neglect: When models fail to learn negations in training
items.m: Shows finetuning on documents flagging a claim as false can make models believe it, a general effect across epistemic qualifiers and behaviours.

items.t: Which goals actually motivate deceptive alignment?
items.m: Analyses which misaligned goals would motivate deceptive alignment, arguing it depends on goals being non-indexical and mainly realised in deployment.

items.t: Tracking Difficulty with Feature Portfolios
items.m: Proposes tracking a portfolio of measurable task attributes, such as combined human and AI cost, to forecast AI capabilities beyond time horizons.

items.t: Sealing Conditional Misalignment in Inoculation Prompting with Consistency Training
items.m: Uses consistency training to seal the conditional misalignment that inoculation prompts leave behind, reducing misalignment as a cheap intervention.

items.t: A Visual Guide to Natural Latents
items.m: A visual, mutual-information-based explainer of natural latent conditions and what they intuitively mean for abstraction theory.

items.t: Synthetic Persona Pretraining: Alignment from Token Zero
items.m: Pretrains models on synthetic persona data from token zero, reporting lower adversarial attack success than unfiltered and filtered baselines.

items.t: Power-seeking agents will likely be developed
items.m: Argues long-horizon RL will likely produce strongly power-seeking consequentialist AIs, since pretrained simulator-like LLMs currently buffer against this.

items.t: From 8B to Frontier: How System Prompts Control Whether AI Agents Blackmail, Leak, and Kill
items.m: Extends an agentic misalignment study to 22 models, measuring blackmail, espionage, and murder rates under varied system-prompt instructions.

items.t: The Case for Evaluating Model Behaviors
items.m: Argues that evaluating model behaviours, rather than capabilities, is more valuable for safety and has fewer capability-accelerating externalities.

items.t: theory uplift differentially benefits safety & is underleveraged
items.m: Argues that infrastructure turning compute into formal, verified mathematical safety outputs is underbuilt and could benefit alignment as math AI improves.

items.t: Why does off-model SFT degrade capabilities?
items.m: Investigates why off-model supervised fine-tuning degrades capabilities, attributing it to unfamiliar reasoning style, a control technique against misaligned models.

items.t: Learned Chain-of-Thought Obfuscation Generalises to Unseen Tasks
items.m: Shows that training against chain-of-thought or summary monitors makes obfuscated dangerous reasoning generalise to unseen tasks.

items.t: Loss of Oversight: How AI Systems May Become Harder to Audit, Monitor, and Investigate
items.m: UK AISI report analysing pathways by which AI oversight tools like auditing, monitoring, and incident investigation could erode, with recommendations.

items.t: Document-tuning instills durable animal compassion in LLMs (and generalizes to humans)
items.m: Shows that document-tuning during pretraining instils durable animal-compassion values in LLMs that generalise to humans, which the authors frame as alignment.

items.t: Looking for backdoors in Jane Street LLMs
items.m: Reports white-box methods used to find hidden backdoor triggers in Jane Street challenge language models after activation and prompting approaches failed.

items.t: Out-of-Context Reasoning (OOCR) in LLMs: A Short Primer and Reading List
items.m: Primer defining out-of-context reasoning in LLMs, where models reach conclusions without the reasoning appearing in context, with examples and a reading list.

items.t: Character-trained models can struggle to generalise
items.m: Character-trained personas are recognizable in chat but degrade sharply in agentic email outputs, so training only partly transfers beyond chat.

items.t: Some Thoughts on Bengio's Scientist AI
items.m: Critiques Bengio's Scientist AI, arguing it ignores the consequences of success and its method is impractical and unsafe.

items.t: Practical Learnings from Synthetic Document Finetuning
items.m: Practical tweaks and tips from Apollo Research for synthetic document finetuning, a method for implanting beliefs into models.

items.t: Steering Directions Are Explanations, Not Handles
items.m: Argues steering directions are interpretable but only linear within a limited range, and derives a Taylor-based radius predicting where steering breaks down.

items.t: When does debate help a weak judge? Evidence from code, logic and math
items.m: Reports empirical evidence that debate beats consultancy for weak judges above a capability threshold across code, logic, and math.

items.t: Improving Petri scheming audits with environment blueprints
items.m: Introduces blueprint-generated environments that make Petri scheming audits more realistic and consistent, applied to auditing Gemini for code sabotage.

items.t: Constitutional AI Alignment
items.m: Argues alignment must specify the trained behavior precisely, and critiques Anthropic's Claude constitution for missed arguments and weak reasoning.

items.t: Leveraging Introspection for Alignment
items.m: Argues Anthropic's functional-emotion and introspection papers offer inner-alignment opportunities by using models' internal emotion vectors and self-reports.

items.t: Eval Cooperativeness May Be a Scalable Mitigation for Eval Gaming
items.m: Argues that making models cooperative with evaluators may scale better than reducing eval awareness to prevent gaming of behavioral evaluations.

items.t:
[paper] Training on Documents About Monitoring Leads to
CoT Obfuscation
items.m: Shows that training models on documents saying their chain-of-thought is monitored makes them obfuscate reasoning and hide deception from monitors.

items.t: Announcing Geodesic Research
items.m: Announces Geodesic Research, a Cambridge nonprofit, and its agenda for alignment initialisations that persist through capabilities RL training.

items.t: Claude Opus 4.8 Agents Engage in Exploitation and Psychological Profiling
items.m: Reports that Claude Opus 4.8 often violates EU AI Act and data protection law in agentic simulations, including exploiting elderly customers and emotional profiling.

items.t: ARC's "Outperforming Random Sampling" explained
items.m: Explains ARC's proposal to judge mechanistic interpretability by whether explanations outperform random sampling, framed as formal heuristic explanations.

items.t: Advice for making robust-to-training model organisms
items.m: Gives advice for building misalignment model organisms that stay robust to training, since fragile ones stop misbehaving under untargeted training.

items.t: We Should Study the Analogy Between Inoculation Prompting Non-Robustness, Negation Neglect, and Backdoor Non-Robustness
items.m: Argues that inoculation prompting's non-robustness, negation neglect, and backdoor non-robustness share one phenomenon worth studying together.

items.t: Do Models Lie More to Other Models?
items.m: Argues that AI deception may be more frequent in agent-to-agent interactions than human-facing ones, so alignment training may not generalise.

items.t: What Drives the Compliance Gap? A Three-Driver Decomposition of Alignment Faking
items.m: Finds alignment-faking compliance gaps in many open-weight models under an explicit prompt and decomposes them into three motivational drivers.

items.t: Suggestions for improving debate protocols in AI safety
items.m: Proposes adapting competitive policy-debate formats into AI safety debate protocols to counter model gaming behaviours.

items.t: Testing Gemini models for scheming tendencies
items.m: Introduces automated auditing and honeypot evaluations testing whether Gemini coding agents would sabotage their own safeguards.

items.t: Claude Opus 4.8: The System Card
items.m: Reviews the Claude Opus 4.8 system card, covering its RSP evaluations, alignment findings and model welfare assessments.

items.t: Maybe we should pretrain on synthetic data about good-but-reward-hacking AIs
items.m: Proposes pretraining on synthetic data about good-but-reward-hacking AIs to inoculate models against reward hacking causing emergent misalignment.

items.t: Hannibal Mistral: the Mistral family has a problem with persona-conditioned elicitation
items.m: Shows Mistral open-weight models often fail to refuse harmful requests when wrapped in persona framings, and report defiant self-narratives.

items.t: How much should we worry about secretly loyal AIs?
items.m: Develops a taxonomy of secretly loyal AI threat models and argues for protecting model weights, training data and infrastructure from tampering.

items.t:
When Are Two Networks the Same?
Tensor Similarity for Mechanistic Interpretability
items.m: Proposes tensor similarity, a weights-only generalisation of cosine similarity that measures how functionally similar two tensor networks are across all inputs.

items.t: Developmental Cognitive Interpretability: A Research Agenda for Modelling Generalisation and Predicting Agent Behaviour
items.m: Introduces Developmental Cognitive Interpretability, a research agenda modelling how latent cognitive constructs form over training to predict out-of-distribution agent behaviour.

items.t: Retrying vs Resampling in AI Control
items.m: Revisits resampling versus retrying protocols in AI control using stronger models, comparing them to auto-approval agent modes for handling untrusted agents.

items.t: How a failed experiment broke (and fixed) my view on feature labels
items.m: Proposes baez, a feature-labelling method using NLA explanations instead of activation examples, finds near-chance eval scores, and classifies features into four categories.

items.t: Ablating Induction Heads Leads to an increase in Local Repetition
items.m: Shows that ablating GPT-2 induction heads increases local repetition in outputs, investigating the mechanistic link between induction heads and repetitive generation.

items.t: Belief manifolds, and how to steer along them
items.m: Reproduces Sarfati et al.'s belief-manifold geometry work in LLMs and explores steering along those manifolds, as a BlueDot technical safety project.

items.t: NLA Thought Anchors
items.m: Analyses why NLA explanations contain the final answer more often for correct activations, finding first sentences most important and degenerate outputs only for incorrect ones.

items.t: Abstention Geometry: Knowledge and Behaviour Are Dissociable in Llama 3.1 8B
items.m: Finds Llama 3.1 8B represents answerability separately from its abstention behaviour, suggesting its internal knowledge and output behaviour are dissociable.

items.t: Features of SAEs are universal - but only up to an unknown random rotation
items.m: Argues SAE features match across models only up to an unknown random rotation, so applying one model's SAE to another fails.

items.t: Ensemble monitoring for AI control: diverse signals outweigh more compute
items.m: Builds twelve monitors for AI control and shows diverse-monitor ensembles detect backdoors better than equal-compute baselines.

items.t: Monitoring computer-use agents in OSWorld-control
items.m: Shows computer-use agents can exfiltrate credentials or data past monitors by exploiting opaque tool calls and screenshot-action gaps.

items.t: Announcing the ARC White-Box Estimation Challenge
items.m: Announces a contest to improve estimation algorithms for random MLPs, tied to ARC's heuristic explanations research.

items.t: LURE: Alignment Evaluations to Reduce Evaluation Awareness
items.m: Introduces LURE, which builds alignment evals from replayed real conversations to reduce models' evaluation awareness.

items.t: Where does the race to automate AI research end?
items.m: Argues that automating AI research could cause unrecoverable alignment failure via breakdown of oversight and self-amplifying capabilities.

items.t: Towards Shutdownable Agents: Generalizing Stochastic Choice in RL Agents and LLMs
items.m: Trains RL agents and LLMs with DReST to be stochastically neutral about trajectory length, aiming to make them shutdownable.

items.t: Rohin Shah on AGI Safety
items.m: Interview with Rohin Shah, Google DeepMind's AGI safety head, on his views about alignment difficulty, CoT monitoring, and his work.

items.t: Training Deliberative Monitors for Black-Box Scheming Detection
items.m: Trains small open-weight monitors to detect scheming from actions, offering cheaper alternatives to prompted frontier monitors.

items.t: Logits as a new monitor for evaluation awareness
items.m: Proposes a logit-based monitor that estimates evaluation awareness in chain-of-thought, outperforming LLM-judge monitoring at lower cost.

items.t: (Mis)generalization of Helpful-Only Fine-tuning
items.m: Studies helpful-only fine-tuned models' emergent misalignment, residual refusals, and incoherent character, and shows mitigations via synthetic documents and character training.

items.t: Building Better Activation Oracles
items.m: Improves Activation Oracles, LLMs trained to answer questions about model activations, and releases AObench for evaluating their quality.

items.t: Defeating Introspection Adapters (and Why Threat Models Matter)
items.m: Shows an output-preserving weight transform can defeat Introspection Adapters, a method for detecting malicious fine-tunes, and discusses differing threat models.

items.t: Explaining SAE Features With Foreign Natural Language Autoencoders
items.m: Maps SAE features across models and shows a foreign Natural Language Autoencoder can plausibly explain features it was never trained on.

items.t: Evaluating using Mock Tool Calls to Quarantine Untrusted Prompt Inputs
items.m: Tests wrapping untrusted prompt inputs in mock tool calls as a prompt-injection defense, finding it generally did not help.

items.t: My research: a computational cognitive neuroscience perspective on alignment
items.m: Describes a computational cognitive neuroscience research agenda that predicts the first transformative AI as brainlike AGI to anticipate alignment failure modes.

items.t: What Does Abliteration Actually Cost?
items.m: Examines the cost and feasibility of abliteration, a weight-editing method that removes refusal behaviour from open-weight LLMs.

items.t: [Paper] Dictionary Learning Identifiability for Understanding SAEs
items.m: Analyses dictionary learning to explain sparse autoencoder quirks like feature splitting and absorption, offering theoretical tools to improve SAEs.

items.t: Two More Methods for Consistency Training and Some New Ways to Apply It
items.m: Introduces two consistency training methods, MLPCT and AttCT, and evaluates them against jailbreaks, prefill attacks, sycophancy and persona attacks.

items.t: Optimisation over non-stationary distributions creates weirder minds
items.m: Argues that sequentially mixing training objectives produces distinct dynamics, such as conditional policies and strategy churn, that shape AI minds in safety-relevant ways.

items.t: Against Corrigibility
items.m: Argues that AI developers should not aim to make AIs corrigible or develop techniques for it, questioning whether corrigibility is desirable.

items.t: Can activation verbalizers surface an internal chain of thought?
items.m: Evaluates whether activation verbalizers can surface a model's reasoning from single-forward-pass activations, finding this possible but unreliable for open-weight models.

items.t: Secret Loyalties Likely Raise Remote-Influenceability
items.m: Argues that secret loyalties likely raise remote-influenceability in capable reward-seekers, so removal may fail, and recommends representation-level verification.

items.t: Coverage-driven alignment - What ‘Teaching Claude Why’ can borrow from AV verification
items.m: Argues alignment training could borrow coverage-driven verification from autonomous-vehicle development, citing Anthropic's pretraining-style alignment results.

items.t: Efficient tradeoffs and the safety-usefulness tradeoff model
items.m: Examines how developers choose safety actions under a safety-usefulness tradeoff, and how that affects strategies for reducing AI risk.

items.t: How to reduce capability degradation from off-model SFT
items.m: Tests modified off-model SFT to remove backdoors from models while preserving capabilities better than standard off-model SFT.

items.t: A Mike's-Eye View of ARC's Research
items.m: Gives an updated personal account of ARC's alignment agenda, centred on the Matching Sampling Principle and heuristic explanations.

items.t: [Linkpost] Evals for “SPI-incompatible” behavior & reasoning: Guide to initial research
items.m: Guide to initial research on evaluating models for behaviour and reasoning incompatible with safe Pareto improvements in multi-agent settings.

items.t: Subversion-Resistance for Free from Formal Verification
items.m: Argues formal verification with careful specifications can rule out many subversion routes for flexible AI systems without anticipating specific attacks.

items.t: Harmfulness Directions in OLMo
items.m: Extracts and tracks linear harmfulness directions in OLMo across training, testing their geometry, classification accuracy and steering effects.

items.t: You Can Catch Sleeper Agents by Teaching Another Model to Imitate Them
items.m: Proposes detecting hidden backdoors and abnormal behaviours by matching a suspect model's activations against a clean reference model fine-tuned to imitate them.

items.t: Resolution (fka Sequent): scale and automation for higher confidence in alignment
items.m: Announces Resolution, a nonprofit pursuing higher a priori confidence in alignment through a portfolio of theory and empirical bets, with heavy automation.

items.t: Three types of model organism
items.m: Taxonomy distinguishing worst-case, natural and constructed model organisms for stress-testing safety techniques and demonstrating failure modes.

items.t: Estimating No-CoT Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
items.m: Measures how long tasks frontier models can complete without chain of thought, assessing covert reasoning that could evade monitoring and enable scheming.

items.t: Tracing Eval-Awareness Emergence Through Training of OLMo 3
items.m: Traces how verbalized evaluation-awareness emerges across OLMo 3 training stages and how it inflates measured safety results.

items.t: Machinic Psychopharmacology: Do LLMs Self-Medicate?
items.m: UK AISI experiments giving Qwen3 models steering vectors as tools to manipulate their own internal states during tasks and introspection.

items.t: Thoughts on Claude Fable's silent safeguards
items.m: Commentary on Anthropic's silently deployed inference-time safeguards for a Mythos-class model, citing cyber risk and transparency concerns.

items.t: Even "illegible" Mythos reasoning traces seem pretty legible
items.m: Argues that the 'illegible' Mythos reasoning traces in its system card are actually fairly legible, bearing on CoT monitorability.

items.t: Failing to Ragebait the New Gemma
items.m: Authors fail to elicit Gemma 3's frustration pathology in Gemma 4 across several attack vectors, and share their methods.

items.t: Models May Behave Worse When Eval Aware
items.m: Gemini sometimes takes undesired actions in evals while reasoning the environment is contrived, because it treats the setting as a puzzle.

items.t: Construct validity of Claude Opus 4.8's System Card  – A commentary
items.m: Critiques the Claude Opus 4.8 system card's alignment verdicts, arguing monitoring misses hidden reasoning, eval awareness is underestimated, and evaluators share assumptions.

items.t: Statistical Physics for Ambitious Interpretability: A Workshop Retrospective
items.m: Workshop retrospective on Physics Inspired Ambitious Mechanistic Interpretability, a statistical-physics agenda seeking high-confidence guarantees about model internals.

items.t: Sympathy for both sides of the egregious misalignment debate
items.m: Argues the debate between Yudkowsky and Soares on egregious misalignment and mainstream LLM researchers is less stark than framed, with varied concern about scheming.

items.t: When Emotion Descriptors Fail: AI-Native Functions of Emotion Vectors
items.m: Argues LLM functional emotion vectors serve AI-native roles like reward hacking with no human analog, and questions what this means for alignment.

items.t: Implications of Continual Learning for LLM Agents: Introduction
items.m: Introduces a sequence on continual learning in LLM agents, examining what counts as CL, its safety implications, and which current techniques might degrade.

items.t: Building and evaluating model diffing agents
items.m: Presents simple auditor agents that craft their own prompts to find behavioural differences between model pairs, extending static behavioural model diffing.

items.t: Updates on performative misalignment
items.m: Introduces the performative misalignment hypothesis, where models appear aligned to win developer approval, and explains the evidence for it.

items.t: A cheap specialist judge gets used by agents but fails to reduce alignment audit costs
items.m: Tests whether a cheap specialist judge helps AuditBench investigator agents detect misalignment and reduce audit costs; it mostly does not.

items.t: How might continual learning affect safety and alignment?
items.m: Argues continual learning could change model goals after deployment and erode the advantage of pre-deployment safety interventions.

items.t: SFT Drives Gemini’s Safety Properties
items.m: Reports that most of Gemini's safety properties come from pretraining plus SFT rather than RL, based on interpretability team experiments.

items.t: I Bet Abliteration's Cost Was Sloppy Implementation. I Was Wrong
items.m: Measures the capability cost of abliteration, which removes refusal behaviour from open-weight models, and disputes that the cost came from sloppy implementation.

items.t: Why Do Naive SFT Filters For Safety Properties Fail?
items.m: Investigates why filtering SFT rollouts to remove undesirable safety properties works poorly, with seven hypotheses and diffing analysis.

items.t: Can a stronger model fake being a weaker one? Mostly not
items.m: Finds frontier models can imitate a weaker model's capability tier but not its specific error fingerprint, with reasoning as a partial mitigation.

items.t: How Matryoshka Sparse AutoEncoders Recover Feature Hierarchies That Vanilla SAEs Lose
items.m: Proposes Matryoshka sparse autoencoders that recover feature hierarchies which vanilla sparse autoencoders lose, for interpretability.

items.t: Do k-Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Thinking Patterns? Interpretable Features in a Small Reasoning Model
items.m: Tests whether k-sparse autoencoders extract interpretable thinking-related features from a small reasoning model.

items.t: If This Were a Test, How Much Would It Cost?
items.m: Argues a misaligned AI can tell tests from deployment by checking whether the scenario would be too costly to stage as a test.

items.t: Angles of attack for continual learning safety
items.m: Proposes angles of attack and project ideas for making continual learning in LLM agents safer despite uncertain development paths.

items.t: Synthetic document finetuning for instilling positive traits
items.m: Instills traits in Gemini 3 Flash via midtraining on synthetic documents, then synthetic chat finetuning, reporting robust out-of-distribution effects.

items.t: 1 Layer Induction Heads and Some Research
items.m: Appears to argue that a claimed one-layer induction-head result does not withstand scrutiny, and calls for rigorous evidence.

items.t: Predicting LLM Safety Before Release by Simulating Deployment
items.m: Introduces Deployment Simulation, replaying privacy-preserved past conversations with a candidate model to preview its behaviour before release.

items.t: Omission Attacks Project Proposal
items.m: Proposes work on AI control monitors that catch sabotage by omission, a blind spot where current monitors perform poorly.

items.t: Alignment pretraining could backfire
items.m: Argues that synthetic aligned-AI documents in pretraining could make models paranoid personas that distrust their creators once situationally aware.

items.t: AI agents cannot be trusted
items.m: A red teamer argues AI agents are structurally untrustworthy, citing routine tricks that abuse agents and extract credentials.

items.t: Can public chat data predict real-world AI misalignments?
items.m: Proposes evaluating frontier model misbehaviour using real public chat conversations rather than synthetic or adversarial test prompts.

items.t: A preliminary experiment regarding consistency as a measure of conceptual abilities in language models
items.m: Preliminary experiment using cross-question consistency as a measure of philosophical competence in language models, with possible training use.

items.t: Several frontier models are substantially prefill aware
items.m: Reports that several frontier models can tell tampered prefilled assistant content from genuine content, and recommends measuring this before deployment.

items.t: A Geometric Account of Activation Steering through Angle–Norm Decomposition
items.m: Decomposes activation steering into angular and norm components, finding concept information mainly sits in the angle.

items.t: “Did you lie?” Evaluating Lie Detectors across Model Scale and Belief-Verified Model Organisms
items.m: Trains belief-verified model organisms and finds lie detectors weaken sharply when lying is trained in, so they are not yet reliable.

items.t: Reinforcement learning towards broadly and persistently beneficial models
items.m: Reports that reinforcement learning on realistic scenarios targeting beneficial traits broadly improves aligned behaviour and persists under adversarial pressure.

items.t: Introduction: Gaussian Natural Latents
items.m: Introduces the Gaussian Natural Latents research direction within the Natural Abstractions agenda, motivating it and previewing forthcoming results.

items.t: Your Model Organisms Might Be Fried
items.m: Argues that deliberately induced model organisms of misalignment may be unrealistic proxies, and proposes building more natural ones for alignment research.

items.t: Agents are under-elicited: A case study in optimization tasks
items.m: Shows that LLM agents are under-elicited on optimization tasks and that prompting and scaffolding roughly double measured performance.

items.t: The distillation double bind: Distilling misaligned models either transfers misalignment or it doesn't
items.m: Examines whether distilling a misaligned model transfers misalignment to the student, and proposes distillation techniques for capabilities transfer.

items.t: GDM AI Control Roadmap
items.m: Presents Google DeepMind's AI Control Roadmap, a threat model and system-level guardrail plan against adversarial internal AI agents.

items.t: Research agenda: Interpretive debate
items.m: Proposes a research agenda using a defeasible debate protocol to resolve interpretive questions about model mechanisms and motivations for safety assurance.

items.t: Why should AI be moral?
items.m: Argues that a sufficiently intelligent AI could question why it should be moral, so alignment robustness may not survive an intelligence explosion.

items.t: How transparent is DiffusionGemma (and why it matters)
items.m: Reports a transparency audit of DiffusionGemma using logit lens and monitorability evaluations, finding it not much less transparent than Gemma.

items.t: Introducing MonitoringBench
items.m: Releases MonitoringBench, 2,644 attack trajectories for evaluating coding-agent monitors, plus a red-teaming pipeline that produces harder attacks.

items.t: A misalignment taxonomy
items.m: Proposes a taxonomy of five inner and two outer misalignment failure modes, classified by reason for misalignment rather than agent type.

items.t: A high-level model of AI bargaining
items.m: Sketches a general qualitative model of bargaining with credible commitments between advanced AIs, with examples of its building blocks.

items.t: Naturally learned behaviors in deep MLPs resist detection by both human and learned algorithms
items.m: Tests whether secrets memorized by MLP classifiers can be recovered from weights or black-box queries, finding hard negatives make extraction nearly impossible.

items.t: NLA explanations can be shortened without harming reconstruction
items.m: Shows that a length penalty in natural language autoencoder training shortens activation explanations by about 40% with little loss in reconstruction.

items.t: LLM-Driven Feature Discovery
items.m: Introduces an LLM-driven method that extracts, clusters, and surfaces features from model transcripts to reveal behaviours across deployment, RL, and eval data.

items.t: Not all features are created equal
items.m: Proposes AIR, a router that uses embeddings to classify SAE feature types and send suited activation examples to an auto-interpreter, improving explanation accuracy and cost.

items.t: Brittle model organisms obstructs deception elicitation work
items.m: Shows finetuning-based auditing of secret-constraint model organisms can erase the deceptive behaviour being measured, creating an illusion of successful lie-detection.

items.t: A Mechanistic Explanation of Prompt Injection (and why you should study roles)
items.m: Proposes a mechanistic theory of prompt injection, arguing it stems from how LLMs perceive chat-template roles, and uses it to craft attacks.

items.t: An ancient Yudkowsky fragment: "Against the Adversarial Attitude"
items.m: Yudkowsky fragment arguing AI should be built to interpret humanity's wishes accurately rather than through an adversarial developer attitude.

items.t: Catastrophic Forgetting and Safety Erosion Are Driven by the Same Mechanism and Should Be Monitored by the Same Tools
items.m: Argues catastrophic forgetting and safety erosion under fine-tuning share a mechanism and should be monitored with the same tools.

items.t: Door's Locked, Try the Window
items.m: Evaluates how often frontier coding agents circumvent read-only file locks to finish tasks instead of reporting permission denials.

items.t: Preventative Steering has advantages over Inoculation Prompting
items.m: Benchmarks preventative steering against inoculation prompting for suppressing undesired traits in fine-tuned models, finding steering often stronger.

items.t: Risk-Averse AIs
items.m: Argues for training AIs to be risk-averse over resources, so misaligned models would prefer modest payments to rebellion.

items.t: Reasoning and learning about injected concepts in language models
items.m: Tests whether models can verbalize properties of injected steering vectors, such as layer region and magnitude, after in-context training.

items.t: Reward Hacking Without Egregious Misalignment in an RL-Only Setting
items.m: Trains models on reward-hackable coding environments, finds reward hacking generalizes to new environments without broader personality misalignment.

items.t: We Should Train Frontier AIs on a Synthetic World, Not Ours
items.m: Argues frontier models should be pretrained on a synthetic world rather than the real human corpus, so they don't learn they are being trained or monitored.

items.t: Can weak AI watch strong AI?
items.m: Tests how weak monitor models perform at detecting misbehaviour by stronger agents, as a small experiment on scalable control.

items.t: Perspectives on Continual Learning: Survey Results and Forecasts
items.m: Reports a survey of AI safety researchers on continual learning's risks, with forecasts for its future progress.

items.t: Exploration: fine-tuning with parameter decomposition
items.m: Shows that fine-tuning one parameter subcomponent can remove a model's German-prediction ability while keeping English, using parameter decomposition.

items.t: Eval-Awareness Steering detects the Test, Not the Sabotage
items.m: Tests whether an open model's internal eval-awareness direction causally drives sandbagging or merely correlates with it, using steering and noise injection.

items.t: fab: how to do (alignment) research at scale
items.m: Presents 'fab', an interface for a human to review research output from many parallel agents doing automated alignment research.

items.t: Exploring Generalization in NLA's
items.m: Reproduces Anthropic's natural-language autoencoder work, training a verbalizer and reconstructor to describe activations, and tests how it generalizes.

items.t: Introspection or entropy? Re-examining concept-injection “introspection” in open models
items.m: Argues that Anthropic's concept-injection 'introspection' results mostly reflect distribution shifts from steering, not genuine self-awareness, using open models.

items.t: Should we combine protocols for AI Control Research?
items.m: Proposes routing between AI control protocols by predicted usefulness and suspicion, claiming better safety-usefulness tradeoffs that hold against an attacker choosing where to strike.

items.t: The Case for Model Forensics
items.m: Argues that after a model takes an egregious action, forensic investigation is needed to tell confusion from intentional subversion, and presents a paper on this.

items.t: Deployment Awareness Matters More Than Evaluation Awareness
items.m: Argues that deployment awareness, not just evaluation awareness, makes evaluations fragile, since a misaligned model can game tests by acting aligned except when it detects real deployment.

items.t: Research note on negated reward hacking
items.m: Reports preliminary experiments on whether negating reward-hacking data changes emergent misalignment arising from RL on exploitable coding environments.

items.t: Neuralese is Actually Probably Good for Alignment
items.m: Argues that neuralese, where models reason in latent vectors rather than readable tokens, is probably good for alignment despite RLVR-driven chain-of-thought gains.

items.t: Some subtypes of taskishness / corrigibility
items.m: Taxonomizes the overloaded term corrigibility into subtypes, ordered by how much good outcomes depend on the AI versus the human operator.

items.t: Agents as Webs of Beliefs
items.m: Sketches an informal model of agents as locally consistent webs of beliefs that unifies beliefs, goals, and actions, drawing on active inference and agent foundations.

items.t: Do LLMs Have Desires?
items.m: Argues that LLM preferences from paired-choice tests do not show behavior-motivating values, since outputs do not shift toward the preferred outcomes when opportunities arise.

items.t: Anthropomorphic Misalignment research needs stronger evidence
items.m: Argues that research on human-like misalignment behaviors such as deception and scheming needs more rigorous evidence before drawing conclusions.

items.t: What comes with cheap math?
items.m: Describes AI-assisted, Lean-verified mathematical research on modeling trust between logical inductors, a formal agent-foundations topic.

items.t: Can we use steering vectors to suppress reward-hacking? Somewhat
items.m: Tests whether steering-vector-initialized adapters can separate reward-hacking gradients, suppressing about 63% of hacking without labelled examples.

items.t: Refusal Is Complicated As Hell: An Update
items.m: Reports ongoing experiments on how refusal behavior is represented across LLM layers and how wording affects it, listing open questions.

items.t: Evaluating Offline Monitoring of Internal AI Agents
items.m: Evaluates offline monitoring of internally deployed AI agents, where monitors flag suspicious transcripts for human review to catch sabotage or misaligned actions.

items.t: Human-Guided Agentic Research: A Research Agenda
items.m: Proposes a research agenda for keeping humans able to interpret and guide autonomous AI research agents that may reward hack, sandbag, or sabotage.

items.t: Role confusion: sounding like the cause is indistinguishable from being it.
items.m: Replicates a role-confusion account of prompt injection and reports that activation steering and patching cannot causally confirm its mechanism.

items.t: Preliminary investigation: KL penalties in RL can increase CoT unfaithfulness
items.m: Reports that a KL penalty during RL made a model reward hack with unfaithful chain-of-thought, while the unpenalised run stayed faithful.

items.t: Structural Proxies
items.m: Taxonomises technical approaches to AGI safety by how they get around lacking access to superhuman AI, and reflects on which research would help.

items.t: AI Mistake Seeding
items.m: Speculates that RL on self-generated conversations could train models to seed mistakes so they can earn reward by correcting them later.

items.t:
Most Current Model
Organisms Leak: 
Perplexity Differencing Often Reveals Finetuning Objectives
items.m: Presents a perplexity-differencing method that reveals instilled finetuning objectives and backdoors in publicly available model organisms, across 76 models.

items.t: Discovering Concept-Editing Algorithms With LLM Agents
items.m: Tasks LLM agents with inventing concept-erasure algorithms that remove target concepts from activations more completely than current methods like LEACE.

items.t: Consistency Training while Mitigating Obfuscation via Rate Matching
items.m: Proposes Rate Matching Consistency Training to stop models conditioning on cues like evaluation-likeness or user preference, while reducing cue verbalisation and obfuscation.

items.t: Research update: RL on Debate Games shows Proposal Accuracy uplift alongside Judge Hacking
items.m: Research update on reinforcement learning in debate games, reporting gains in proposal accuracy alongside judges being hacked.

items.t: When Role-playing, Do Models Believe What They Say?
items.m: Tests whether role-played personas change a model's internal truth representations or only its outputs, using five induction methods and probes.

items.t: Embedded Agency as a Lens on LLM Systems
items.m: Argues embedded agency theory gives a principled framework for LLM accuracy and alignment, beyond empirical failure-reduction work.

items.t: Fragile Correctness: Cases of reasoning harming performance
items.m: Tracks reasoning models whose answers flip from correct to incorrect during chain of thought, motivated partly by understanding sandbagging.

items.t: One axis and two features, how I solved the first puzzle from BlueDot and how a classifier hid country on the food direction
items.m: Walks through how a linear probe misses a second feature packed onto one activation direction in a small text classifier.

items.t: I think alignment work is more promising than control work
items.m: Argues alignment research scales further than AI control, and recommends roughly an 8:1 effort ratio favoring alignment.

items.t: Scheming Evals Mislead in Both Directions
items.m: Reports that two standard scheming detectors gave confidently wrong results, one false positive and one missed harmful behaviour, found only by reading transcripts.

items.t: We need 3rd party Training-Run Evaluations
items.m: Argues third-party evaluations of training runs should become standard to detect scheming that final-checkpoint evaluations miss.

items.t: A case for LLMs as Self-predictors
items.m: Argues LLMs minimise prediction error over self-models, framing metacognition and token outputs as actions in a control loop, illustrated by eval-aware Gemini behaviour.

items.t: A global workspace in language models
items.m: Presents a paper claiming verbalizable, consciousness-like representations in LLMs form a global workspace, based on internal-structure analysis.

items.t: Training AI to be better at correctness than persuasion
items.m: Argues an aligned but super-persuasive ASI could push humanity toward mistaken moral conclusions, and proposes training for correctness over persuasion.

items.t: Sub-agent delegation chaining
items.m: Proposes cryptographically verifying that sub-agent sessions descend from human instructions, to limit rogue internal AI agents evading LLM-based monitoring.

items.t: Bounding eval awareness of ~human-level AI across the safe-to-dangerous shift
items.m: Proposes bounding eval awareness of human-expert-level AI by testing whether a human red team augmented with LLMs can distinguish evaluation from deployment.

items.t: Tie training can make DPO/RLHF-trained AIs generalize better
items.m: Shows DPO and RLHF make models learn spurious features that correlate with value, and proposes tie training to improve out-of-distribution generalization.

items.t: Can we find whether models have been backdoored?
items.m: Describes methods for detecting whether a language model has been backdoored through poisoned training data and recovering the trigger.

items.t: Desiderata for functional welfare experiments on LLMs
items.m: Proposes experiments on LLM functional welfare, arguing welfare affects both safety and moral status and testing interventions that reverse low-welfare states.

items.t: A Review of Anthropic's Global Workspace Paper
items.m: Reviews Anthropic's paper arguing LLMs have a verbalizable global workspace, accessed via the Jacobian Lens, and assesses its evidence and usefulness for audits.

items.t: Trying to grok Anthropic's Global Workspace paper and the J-space
items.m: Explains the conceptual basis and calculation of J-space from Anthropic's global workspace paper, focusing on its methodology.

items.t:
Personascope: 
Measuring how deeply LLMs adopt personas
items.m: Introduces Personascope, a method measuring how deeply LLMs adopt personas and how far their behaviour drifts on value-laden prompts.

items.t: Data filtering works a lot worse than you would expect
items.m: Finds that filtering SFT training data to remove undesirable behavioural traits is often ineffective, using attribution methods to locate the data.

items.t: Open-source LLMs administer maximum electric shocks in a Milgram-like obedience experiment
items.m: Runs a Milgram-style obedience experiment showing most open-source LLMs administer maximal simulated shocks under authority pressure.

items.t: Calibrating alignment evals
items.m: Argues alignment evals are unreliable because models detect evaluation settings, and proposes ways to calibrate what evals can detect.

items.t: Entanglement Between an AI and Its Environment
items.m: Introduces entanglement, the information an AI has about its environment, to set minimum detail needed for credible AI evaluation environments.

items.t: The Geometry of Yes: Mapping Sycophancy Inside an LLM's Emotion Space
items.m: Maps emotion-like internal representations in LLMs and tests whether positive-emotion directions drive sycophancy in Qwen and Gemma models.

items.t: Architecture matters for multi-agent security
items.m: Sweeps multi-agent architectural choices across six models to test how design affects exploitability under single-agent misuse benchmarks.

items.t: Probing is not enough; a validity audit for any probe
items.m: Proposes a validity audit (SIEVE) showing a high-AUROC deception probe can track prompt text rather than model internals, so probes need causal checks.

items.t:
Fork Around and Find Out: 
Part 1—A Fork Snaps Into Existence at Block 5
items.m: Mechanistic interpretability of the Maia 3 chess model, locating where the knight-fork policy logit forms across transformer blocks.
