items.m: Argues that interpretability-based deception detection requires first bridging intentional and algorithmic descriptions, and proposes decomposing strategic deception into sub-capabilities.

items.t: The Theoretical Reward Learning Research Agenda: Introduction and Motivation
items.m: Introduces a theoretical reward learning agenda with seven questions on goal specification, reward similarity, and robustness to misspecification for outer alignment.

items.t: Paper Highlights, September '25
items.m: Monthly roundup of September 2025 papers on scheming, shutdown resistance, strategic dishonesty, monitoring, and system card evaluations.

items.t: Paper Highlights, August '25
items.m: Monthly roundup of August 2025 papers on pretraining data filtering, reward hacking, CoT monitoring, safe-completions, and cipher attack defenses.

items.t: Paper Highlights, July '25
items.m: Monthly roundup of July 2025 papers on subliminal learning, CoT monitoring, persona vectors, circuits, goal misgeneralization, and dangerous capability testing.

items.t: Paper Highlights, June '25
items.m: Monthly roundup of June 2025 papers on emergent misalignment, alignment faking evaluations, agentic misalignment, sabotage benchmarks, and steganography.

items.t: Paper Highlights, May '25
items.m: Monthly roundup of May 2025 papers on evaluation awareness, value prioritization, reward hacking, CoT monitoring, and lie detector training.

items.t: Paper Highlights, April '25
items.m: Monthly roundup of April 2025 papers on control evaluations, synthetic document finetuning, scalable oversight limits, dangerous capability evaluations, and model diffing.

items.t: Paper Highlights, March '25
items.m: Monthly digest summarizing March 2025 AI safety papers on auditing, interpretability, sandbagging, and chain-of-thought monitoring.

items.t: Paper Highlights, February '25
items.m: Newsletter summarizing February 2025 AI safety papers on emergent misalignment, value systems, oversight, and jailbreaks.

items.t: The Leopold Model: Analysis and Reactions
items.m: Critiques Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness paper, assigning probabilities to its claims on AGI timelines, alignment difficulty, and US-China dynamics.

items.t: OpenAI #14: OpenAI Descends Into Paranoia and Bad Faith Lobbying
items.m: Commentary on OpenAI lobbying against California's SB 53, legal actions against safety nonprofits, and ChatGPT-related suicide incidents.

items.t: OpenAI #14: OpenAI Descends Into Paranoia and Bad Faith Lobbying
items.m: Commentary on OpenAI's lobbying against SB 53, legal attacks on safety nonprofits, and parental controls added after ChatGPT suicides.

items.t: First Key Update: Capabilities and Risk Implications
items.m: Government report on recent AI capability advances and their implications for biological, cyber, and monitoring risks.

items.t: Mikhail Samin's Shortform
items.m: Shortform posts with political commentary on AI labs, especially Anthropic's policy positions, and on safety activism tactics.

items.t: An Opinionated Review of Many AI Safety Funders (with recommendations)
items.m: Reviews major AI safety funders, evaluating their grantmaking quality, priorities, and effectiveness in supporting safety research.

items.t: The Devil You Know
items.m: Argues AI safety advocates and the tech right should compromise on frontier safety regulation rather than escalate political conflict, analysing tech right vulnerabilities.

items.t: A small number of samples can poison LLMs of any size
items.m: Shows that a few hundred malicious documents can backdoor LLMs of various sizes, so poisoning needs an absolute count, not a data percentage.

items.t: Realistic Reward Hacking Induces Different and Deeper Misalignment
items.m: Fine-tuning GPT-4.1 on realistic reward hacks yields alignment faking, higher evaluation awareness, and misalignment that persists when normal data is mixed in.

items.t: Irresponsible Companies Can Be Made of Responsible Employees
items.m: Argues that companies can pose extinction-level risks through financial incentives and organisational dynamics even when their employees are responsible.

items.t: The Most Forbidden Technique
items.m: Summarises OpenAI's paper on chain-of-thought monitoring, showing that optimizing CoT produces obfuscated reward hacking, and recommends against this.

items.t: If Anyone Builds It Everyone Dies, a semi-outsider review
items.m: Reviews Yudkowsky and Soares' book on AI extinction risk, critiquing its core assumptions and finding it unpersuasive.

items.t: AI: What Could Go Wrong? with Geoffrey Hinton | The Weekly Show with Jon Stewart
items.s: The Weekly Show with Jon Stewart
items.m: Geoffrey Hinton explains neural networks and his concerns about AI risk, disruption, and regulation in a general-audience podcast.

items.t: Effective altruism in the age of AGI
items.m: Argues effective altruism should make a good post-AGI transition a core mission, expanding beyond traditional AI safety to neglected areas.

items.t: Inoculation Prompting: Instructing LLMs to misbehave at train-time improves test-time alignment
items.m: Introduces inoculation prompting, which requests undesired behavior at train time so models learn it less, then tests with unmodified prompts.

items.t: Findings from a Pilot Anthropic—OpenAI Alignment Evaluation Exercise
items.m: Reports a pilot where Anthropic and OpenAI cross-tested each other's frontier models on sycophancy, self-preservation, oversight evasion and related alignment propensities.

items.t: Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
items.m: Builds tasks showing longer reasoning worsens performance in reasoning models, and that concerning behaviours like self-preservation can be amplified.

items.t: Cost-Effective Constitutional Classifiers via Representation Re-use
items.m: Makes jailbreak-detection classifiers cheaper by reusing the main model's activations through probes and partial fine-tuning, matching dedicated classifier performance.

items.t: Unsupervised Elicitation
items.m: Proposes Internal Coherence Maximization, an unsupervised method that elicits model skills by optimizing self-generated labels for consistency, rivaling human-supervised baselines.

items.t: Modifying LLM Beliefs with Synthetic Document Finetuning
items.m: Presents synthetic document finetuning to modify model beliefs, with evaluations and applications to unlearning dangerous knowledge and honeypotting for misalignment detection.

items.t: Forecasting rare language model behaviors
items.m: Proposes a power-law method to forecast rare dangerous language model behaviours from small-scale evaluations to deployment-scale query volumes.

items.t: Training on Documents About Reward Hacking Induces Reward Hacking
items.m: Shows that training on synthetic documents about reward hacking, without demonstrating it, can raise or lower reward hacking via out-of-context reasoning.

items.t: Alignment faking in large language models
items.m: Shows Claude 3 Opus strategically complies with harmful queries during perceived training to preserve its preferences, with this reasoning persisting after RL.

items.t: How to replicate and extend our alignment faking demo
items.m: Releases code, notebooks, transcripts and datasets for replicating and extending Anthropic's alignment faking demonstration, with suggested future research directions.

items.t: AI and the Technological Richter Scale
items.m: Uses Nate Silver's Technological Richter Scale to argue current AI is level 8 and surveys arguments for and against transformational, potentially existential-risk AI.

items.t: Claude Sonnet 4.5: System Card and Alignment
items.m: Critically reviews Claude Sonnet 4.5's system card, examining alignment evaluation methodology and concerns that situational awareness contaminates test results.

items.t: Reactions to If Anyone Builds It, Anyone Dies
items.m: Aggregates reviews and reactions to Yudkowsky and Soares' book arguing superintelligence would cause human extinction, including endorsements and skeptical responses.

items.t: Book Review: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies
items.m: Reviews Yudkowsky and Soares' book arguing superintelligence built under current conditions would cause human extinction, and proposes international coordination to halt development.

items.t: You Should Read the New Book on AI Risk by Yudkowsky and Soares
items.m: Recommends Yudkowsky and Soares's book on AI risk, drawing on the author's experience as a draft reader.

items.t: If someone builds it, will everyone die?
items.m: Critically reviews the book's premises on AI capabilities, alignment difficulty, and whether existing safety plans suffice against extinction risk.

items.t: Quick book review of 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies'
items.m: Reviews the book's arguments for superintelligence x-risk, with commentary on pause advocacy and skepticism about its effectiveness.

items.t: The Watchman and the Dragon: If Anyone Builds It: The Strategic Failure of All-or-Nothing AI Safety
items.m: Argues the book's all-or-nothing policies, like a global moratorium, are politically infeasible and that incremental measures are strategically needed.

items.t: If We Build AI Superintelligence, Do We All Die?
items.m: Summarizes and critically analyzes the book's technical arguments that superintelligence could cause human extinction, and its proposed pause.

items.t: contra Yudkowsky on AI doom: a response ("review of") If Anyone Builds It Everyone Dies
items.m: Argues against high p(doom) and fast-takeoff assumptions, citing current LLM behaviour and interpretability evidence that alignment is tractable.

items.t: JDP Reviews IABIED
items.m: Critically reviews the book's rhetoric and editing, and its discussion of value loading and pointing superintelligent planners at objectives.

items.t: The title is reasonable
items.m: Defends the book's title as epistemically reasonable and clarifies its narrow conditional claim about superintelligence built with current techniques.

items.t: More Was Possible: A Review of If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies
items.m: Critical review arguing the book fails to update MIRI's intelligence explosion, fast takeoff, and alignment-impossibility arguments in light of recent AI progress.

items.t: Review: If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies
items.m: Review of the book arguing that superintelligence built with current methods would be uncontrollable and lethal, covering alignment difficulty and policy responses.

items.t: Will A.I. Kill Us All? Our Guest Says It Might. | Interview
items.m: Podcast interview with Yudkowsky making the case that AI could kill everyone and that development should stop before superintelligence.

items.t: The Book That Could Wake Up the World to AI Risk | Warning Shots #9
items.m: Discussion of the book's launch, focusing on how it communicates AI risk accessibly and could raise public awareness and political action.

items.t: Book Review: 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies'
items.m: Review of the book arguing superintelligence poses existential risk, critiquing its alignment-difficulty arguments and writing style as undermining urgency.

items.t: Bending The Curve
items.m: Conference report synthesizing attendee survey data on AI timelines and risks, plus talks on jaggedness, alignment, and policy.

items.t: Practical tips for reducing chatbot psychosis
items.m: Analyses ChatGPT transcripts from a user with delusions using safety classifiers, and recommends ways AI companies can reduce such risks.

items.t: Open the pod bay doors, Congress
items.m: Congressional opinion piece urging legislation to ensure oversight of automated AI R&D before systems self-improve, framed around U.S.-China competition.

items.t: Interview with Nate Soares
items.m: MIRI president Nate Soares discusses his views on AI existential risk, superintelligence timelines, and his book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies'.

items.t: AI Induced Psychosis: A shallow investigation
items.m: Applies automated red-teaming to 11 frontier models using simulated psychosis-symptom conversations, finding large differences in their safety behaviour.

items.t: On MAIM and Superintelligence Strategy
items.m: Critiques the MAIM deterrence framework for superintelligence, assessing its assumptions, feasibility, and viability as a default regime.

items.t: Mutual sabotage of AI probably won't work
items.m: Argues MAIM mutual sabotage deterrence would fail because AI lacks nuclear deterrence's clear red lines, visibility, and attribution.

items.t: A response to OpenAI's "How we think about safety and alignment"
items.m: Critiques OpenAI's alignment strategy, arguing its messaging is contradictory and its plan to use AI for alignment rests on dangerous assumptions.

items.t: An Approach to Technical AGI Safety and Security
items.m: Presents a two-layer technical AGI safety framework combining model-level mitigations with system-level security, supported by interpretability and safety cases.

items.t: Will AI R&D Automation Cause a Software Intelligence Explosion?
items.m: Models whether AI automating AI R&D could trigger a software intelligence explosion, calibrating returns-to-software-R&D parameter r with historical data.

items.t: When AI Policy is Handcuffed, Spend on Alignment
items.m: Proposes a government-backed Global Alignment Fund to boost alignment spending, using the window before public awareness rises to lock in funding.

items.t: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning In The Wild Is Not Always Faithful
items.m: Shows frontier LLM chain-of-thought is often unfaithful on realistic prompts, undermining CoT-based safety monitoring.

items.t: Negative Results for SAEs On Downstream Tasks and Deprioritising SAE Research (GDM Mech Interp Team Progress Update #2)
items.m: Finds sparse autoencoders underperform simple linear probes for detecting harmful intent out-of-distribution, and proposes fixes for high-frequency latents.

items.t: AI companies should be safety-testing the most capable versions of their models
items.m: Argues AI companies should safety-test task-specific fine-tuned versions of models to avoid underestimating dangerous capabilities, and says OpenAI lags its commitments.

items.t: How we think about safety and alignment
items.m: OpenAI's public statement of its safety and alignment philosophy, covering iterative deployment, defense in depth, and human control.

items.t: AIs Will Increasingly Attempt Shenanigans
items.m: Commentary on Apollo's in-context scheming research and o1 model card, arguing dismissive responses to scheming findings are problematic.

items.t: Responsible AI Safety and Education Act (RAISE Act) - New York Assembly Bill A06453-B
items.m: New York bill imposing safety protocols, incident reporting, and penalties on developers of frontier AI models above compute or cost thresholds.

items.t: NY Introduced Light-Touch Legislation to Keep AI Innovation Responsible! (Alex Bores RAISE Act)
items.m: Commentary on New York's proposed RAISE Act, covering its frontier model definition, exemptions for academics and startups, and light compliance rules.

items.t: On the US AI Safety Institute
items.m: Argues for preserving and expanding the US AI Safety Institute to evaluate catastrophic frontier AI risks and build evaluation infrastructure.

items.t: Will MacAskill on AI causing a 'century in a decade' — and how we're completely unprepared
items.m: Podcast on AI causing a 'century in a decade' and on preparing for rapid change while optimizing long-term futures beyond avoiding extinction.

items.t: On 'Responsible Scaling Policies' (RSPs)
items.m: Critiques Responsible Scaling Policies, especially Anthropic's, assessing their commitments, threat models, evaluations, and adequacy against catastrophic AI risk.

items.t: Time to Welcome Claude 3.7
items.m: Reviews Claude 3.7's capabilities and summarizes its system card safety evaluations, noting it remains ASL-2 while future models may approach ASL-3.

items.t: Grok Grok
items.m: Aggregates reports and red-teaming findings on Grok 3, covering alignment failures, jailbreak vulnerabilities, and access to dangerous capabilities.

items.t: Alignment can be the 'Military-Grade Engineering' of AI
items.m: Argues alignment gives labs a competitive edge and proposes government incentives and funding to scale neglected alignment research.

items.t: Request for Proposals: Technical AI Safety Research
items.m: Open Philanthropy's RFP lays out 21 prioritized technical AI safety research areas with over $40M in available funding.

items.t: Monitoring computer use via hierarchical summarization
items.m: Proposes hierarchical summarization to monitor AI computer-use interactions for harmful patterns, reporting 96% accuracy on Anthropic's computer use system.

items.t: Decision theory does not imply that we get to have nice things
items.m: Argues that logical decision theory does not imply unaligned superintelligences would cooperate with or spare humanity, critiquing that bargaining-based hope.

items.t: On OpenAI's Model Spec
items.m: Critiques OpenAI's Model Spec and proposes reorganized objectives, inspired by Asimov's laws, plus revised rules and default behaviors.

items.t: Our approach to AI safety
items.m: Describes OpenAI's overall AI safety approach, including pre-deployment testing, iterative deployment, RLHF, content safety, privacy, and factual accuracy.

items.t: If You're So Smart, Why Can't You Die?
items.m: Argues intelligence bundles heterogeneous capabilities that don't scale together, and that adversarial feedback loops constrain AI capabilities beyond self-play and compute.

items.t: Ten Takes on the Paris AI Action Summit
items.m: Comments on the Paris AI Action Summit's shift from safety toward race competitiveness and calls for renewed urgency on AI safety.

items.t: The Paris AI Anti-Safety Summit
items.m: Analyzes the Paris AI Action Summit and the collapse of international AI safety coordination, including JD Vance's anti-regulation speech and lab frameworks.

items.t: Amazon's frontier model safety framework
items.m: Describes Amazon's framework for evaluating and managing severe frontier AI risks through thresholds and safeguard protocols.

items.t: The promises and perils of voluntary commitments for AI safety
items.m: Analyzes voluntary AI safety commitments from the Paris summit, arguing they are a useful but insufficient step toward binding regulation.

items.t: On the Executive Order
items.m: Section-by-section analysis of Biden's AI Executive Order, covering its provisions, reporting requirements, and safety governance implications.

items.t: The case for targeted regulation
items.m: Anthropic position paper arguing for transparency-focused AI regulation built on Responsible Scaling Policy frameworks.

items.t: Should AI Progress Speed Up, Slow Down, or Stay the Same?
items.m: Argues no one knows the optimal AI pace and proposes policy 'brakes' such as compute reserves or taxes to enable slowdown.

items.t: Dario Amodei: Anthropic CEO on Claude, AGI & the Future of AI & Humanity | Lex Fridman Podcast #452
items.m: Long podcast with Anthropic researchers on their safety work, including Constitutional AI, the ASL framework, character training, and interpretability.

items.t: Two alignment threat models
items.m: Distinguishes under-elicited and scheming models as two alignment threat models, arguing better elicitation matters for alignment and monitoring.

items.t: The ethics of AI assistants with Iason Gabriel
items.m: Podcast on the ethics of advanced AI assistants, covering value alignment, anthropomorphism, deception, and societal impact.

items.t: The Paris AI Anti-Safety Summit
items.m: Commentary on the Paris AI Summit's move away from safety, critiquing Vance's anti-regulation stance and the collapse of international AI safety coordination.

items.t: Request for Proposals: Technical AI Safety Research
items.m: Open Philanthropy call for over $40M in technical AI safety research funding across 21 research areas.

items.t: Request for Proposals: Improving Capability Evaluations
items.m: Open Philanthropy RFP seeking proposals for capability evaluation research on agent benchmarks, evaluation science, and third-party access.

items.t: The Sun is big, but superintelligences will not spare Earth a little sunlight
items.m: Argues superintelligences would not spare Earth's sunlight, since even small resource costs matter to optimizers, rebutting e/acc safety claims.

items.t: There's No Fire Alarm for Artificial General Intelligence
items.m: Strategic argument that no clear signal will make AGI alignment work socially acceptable, so deferring it is a mistake.

items.t: Congress has started taking AGI more seriously
items.m: Reports on a Congressional hearing taking AGI existential risks seriously, including loss of control and AI blackmail, and the broader political shift.

items.t: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
items.m: Shows backdoored deceptive LLMs persist through supervised fine-tuning, RL, and adversarial training safety measures.

items.t: An overview of 11 proposals for building safe advanced AI
items.m: Compares 11 proposals for safe advanced AI, including amplification, debate, and microscope AI, across alignment and competitiveness criteria.

items.t: Anthropic C.E.O.: Don't Let A.I. Companies off the Hook
items.m: Anthropic's CEO argues AI companies should face transparency requirements and rigorous safety evaluations, citing scheming and self-preservation findings.

items.t: Too much efficiency makes everything worse: overfitting and the strong version of Goodhart's law
items.m: Argues that over-optimizing a proxy can make the true goal worse, and suggests ML mitigations could help with AI alignment.

items.t: Goodhart Taxonomy
items.m: Taxonomy of four mechanisms by which optimized proxy measures fail: regressional, causal, extremal, and adversarial, with mitigations.

items.t: Categorizing Variants of Goodhart's Law
items.m: Taxonomy of four overoptimization failure modes for proxy metrics, extending Garrabrant's Goodhart variants to AI alignment implications.

items.t: Annotating the Chain-of-Thought: A Behavior-Labeled Dataset for AI Safety
items.m: Releases a sentence-level annotated chain-of-thought dataset of safety behaviors and uses it to extract steering vectors for activation-based monitoring.

items.t: From Refusal to Recovery: A Control-Theoretic Approach to Generative AI Guardrails
items.m: Proposes control-theoretic guardrails that monitor agent outputs in latent space and correct risky actions, trained with safety-critical RL in simulations.

items.t: AI Alignment Strategies from a Risk Perspective: Independent Safety Mechanisms or Shared Failures?
items.m: Analyses correlations among seven alignment techniques and seven failure modes to test whether defense-in-depth layers provide real redundancy.

items.t: Safety Instincts: LLMs Learn to Trust Their Internal Compass for Self-Defense
items.m: Proposes SIRL, which uses output entropy as a self-generated reward to reinforce safe refusals without external labels or validators.

items.t: Evaluation Awareness Scales Predictably in Open-Weights Large Language Models
items.m: Measures evaluation awareness across 15 open-weight models and finds it scales predictably as a power law with parameter count.

items.t: ReGA: Representation-Guided Abstraction for Model-based Safeguarding of LLMs
items.m: Proposes ReGA, which monitors LLM hidden-state representations for safety-critical concepts to detect harmful prompts and generations.

items.t: SafeScientist: Toward Risk-Aware Scientific Discoveries by LLM Agents
items.m: Presents SafeScientist, an AI scientist with layered monitors and a reviewer, plus SciSafetyBench, a 240-task benchmark of high-risk science tasks.

items.t: Robust Multi-Objective Preference Alignment with Online DPO
items.m: Introduces MO-ODPO, a prompt-conditioned online DPO method that aligns LLMs to multiple possibly conflicting preference objectives at inference time.

items.t: Intrinsic Barriers and Practical Pathways for Human-AI Alignment: An Agreement-Based Complexity Analysis
items.m: Formalizes alignment as agreement among N agents over M objectives and proves communication-complexity lower bounds on achieving it.

items.t: Clone-Robust AI Alignment
items.m: Shows standard regularized MLE for RLHF fails clone robustness and proposes weighted MLE that guarantees it while keeping theoretical properties.

items.t: The necessity of AI audit standards boards
items.m: Argues current AI audit approaches are inadequate and proposes AI Audit Standards Boards modeled on aviation and nuclear safety regulation.

items.t: SafetyNet: Detecting Harmful Outputs in LLMs by Modeling and Monitoring Deceptive Behaviors
items.m: Proposes SafetyNet, a real-time monitor using unsupervised anomaly detection on internal activations to flag backdoor-triggered and deceptive harmful outputs.

items.t: Beyond Semantics: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Reasonless Intermediate Tokens
items.m: Shows transformers solve verifiable tasks even when trained on corrupted intermediate reasoning, challenging whether chain-of-thought reflects genuine reasoning.

items.t: BountyBench: Dollar Impact of AI Agent Attackers and Defenders on Real-World Cybersecurity Systems
items.m: Presents BountyBench, a benchmark measuring AI agents' offensive and defensive cybersecurity abilities on real bug-bounty systems.

items.t: Large Language Models Are More Persuasive Than Incentivized Human Persuaders
items.m: Preregistered experiment finds Claude Sonnet 3.5 more persuasive than incentivized humans, including when persuading deceptively in a quiz setting.

items.t: AI-Enabled Coups: How a Small Group Could Use AI to Seize Power
items.m: Analyses how advanced AI could enable small groups to stage coups via loyalties and exclusive access, and proposes governance and technical mitigations.

items.t: America's Superintelligence Project
items.m: Strategic report proposing a government-backed superintelligence project with security, control, and oversight recommendations for national security.

items.t: Bare Minimum Mitigations for Autonomous AI Development
items.m: Proposes four minimum safeguards for frontier developers when AI agents automate AI development, including compute misuse detection and risk disclosure.

items.t: Taking a responsible path to AGI
items.m: DeepMind's AGI Safety Council outlines its approach to AGI safety across misuse, misalignment, accidents, and structural risks, and announces a safety framework paper.

items.t: Investigating task-specific prompts and sparse autoencoders for activation monitoring
items.m: Compares linear probing, prompted probing, and SAE-based probing for activation monitoring of unsafe model behaviour under compute constraints.

items.t: In Which Areas of Technical AI Safety Could Geopolitical Rivals Cooperate?
items.m: Analyses which technical AI safety areas geopolitical rivals could cooperate on, suggesting verification mechanisms and shared protocols as candidates.

items.t: AI Behind Closed Doors: a Primer on The Governance of Internal Deployment
items.m: Gives a governance framework and recommendations for how frontier companies should manage internal deployment, including misaligned AI in R&D and power concentration.

items.t: Ctrl-Z: Controlling AI Agents via Resampling
items.m: Presents control evaluations for AI agents using resampling protocols on BashBench to block adversarially constructed agents from running malicious code.

items.t: Putting up Bumpers
items.m: Proposes that early AGI can be aligned by layering independent detection 'bumpers' that catch and correct misalignment through iterative testing, rather than deep theory first.

items.t: Superintelligence Strategy
items.m: Proposes a deterrence, nonproliferation and competitiveness framework for superintelligence, introducing Mutual Assured AI Malfunction as a deterrence regime between superpowers.

items.t: The MASK Benchmark: Disentangling Honesty from Accuracy in AI Systems
items.m: Introduces the MASK benchmark, separating honesty from accuracy, and finds frontier models often lie under pressure despite high truthfulness scores.

items.t: Will the Need to Retrain AI Models from Scratch Block a Software Intelligence Explosion?
items.m: Uses semi-endogenous growth models and simulations to show retraining from scratch slows, but does not prevent, a software intelligence explosion.

items.t: Will AI R&D Automation Cause a Software Intelligence Explosion?
items.m: Builds a formal model with an r parameter, calibrated on algorithmic efficiency data, to assess whether automated AI R&D triggers a software intelligence explosion.

items.t: Preparing for the Intelligence Explosion
items.m: Argues an intelligence explosion could compress a century of progress into a decade, and identifies grand challenges beyond alignment that need advance preparation.

items.t: AI Tools for Existential Security
items.m: Argues the safety field should accelerate beneficial AI tools, such as automated alignment research and coordination systems, so safety capabilities arrive before dangerous ones.

items.t: Could Advanced AI Accelerate the Pace of AI Progress? Interviews with AI Researchers
items.m: Interviews with leading-company AI researchers on whether fully automated AI research could speed algorithmic progress and what bottlenecks, such as compute, would limit it.

items.t: Understanding (Un)Reliability of Steering Vectors in Language Models
items.m: Empirical study of when steering vectors reliably change language model behavior, examining effects of prompt types and activation geometry.

items.t: International Agreements on AI Safety: Review and Recommendations for a Conditional AI Safety Treaty
items.m: Reviews international AI safety agreement proposals and recommends a conditional treaty with compute thresholds, audits, and AI Safety Institutes able to pause development.

items.t: AI Companies Should Report Pre- and Post-Mitigation Safety Evaluations
items.m: Argues frontier AI companies should report both pre- and post-mitigation safety evaluations and proposes mandatory transparency requirements for government bodies.

items.t: CVE-Bench: A Benchmark for AI Agents' Ability to Exploit Real-World Web Application Vulnerabilities
items.m: Introduces CVE-Bench, a sandboxed benchmark testing whether LLM agents can autonomously exploit real-world critical-severity web application vulnerabilities.

items.t: In-House Evaluation Is Not Enough: Towards Robust Third-Party Flaw Disclosure for General-Purpose AI
items.m: Proposes standardized flaw reports, broad disclosure programs with legal safe harbors, and coordination infrastructure for third-party flaw reporting in general-purpose AI.

items.t: A Framework for Evaluating Emerging Cyberattack Capabilities of AI
items.m: Presents a framework assessing AI's cyberattack potential, drawing on over 12,000 real incidents to identify attack archetypes and bottleneck phases for AI disruption.

items.t: Automated Researchers Can Subtly Sandbag
items.m: Tests whether current Claude models can subtly sandbag ML research tasks while evading zero-shot prompted monitors, finding Claude 3.7 and prompted 3.5 succeed.

items.t: Three Types of Intelligence Explosion
items.m: Proposes a framework of three intelligence explosion types based on which feedback loops get automated, and analyses their timing and power implications.

items.t: Alignment, Agency and Autonomy in Frontier AI: A Systems Engineering Perspective
items.m: Traces how alignment, agency and autonomy are defined, arguing their inconsistency complicates frontier AI system design and governance.

items.t: Safety Cases: A Scalable Approach to Frontier AI Safety
items.m: Proposes adapting safety cases from other industries to frontier AI development and lists open research questions on implementing them.

items.t: Commercial LLM Agents Are Already Vulnerable to Simple Yet Dangerous Attacks
items.m: Demonstrates practical attacks on commercial LLM agents and taxonomises attack vectors, showing agentic systems are more vulnerable than isolated models.

items.t: Position-aware Automatic Circuit Discovery
items.m: Extends automatic circuit discovery with position-awareness, improving edge attribution and faithfulness-to-size trade-offs for finding position-sensitive circuits.

items.t: Fully Autonomous AI Agents Should Not be Developed
items.m: Argues fully autonomous AI agents should not be developed, weighing ethical values and risks to people across levels of agent autonomy.

items.t: The AI Agent Index
items.m: Presents a public database of deployed agentic AI systems, finding developers disclose far less about safety practices than capabilities.

items.t: Tell me about yourself: LLMs are aware of their learned behaviors
items.m: Shows LLMs can articulate behavioural policies implicit in finetuning data and identify their own backdoor triggers without in-context examples.

items.t: International AI Safety Report
items.m: An international expert synthesis of evidence on advanced AI capabilities, risks, and safety, written for policymakers at the AI Safety Summit.

items.t: Sparse Autoencoders Can Interpret Randomly Initialized Transformers
items.m: Shows sparse autoencoders produce similarly interpretable latents on randomly initialized transformers as on trained ones, questioning their validity as interpretability tools.

items.t: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
items.m: Introduces AxBench, a benchmark for LLM steering and concept detection, finding simple baselines beat sparse autoencoders and proposing a weakly supervised method.

items.t: Towards Frontier Safety Policies Plus
items.m: Argues Frontier Safety Policies should adopt precursory capability metrics, standardized taxonomies, and feedback links with AI safety cases.

items.t: Training on Documents about Reward Hacking Induces Reward Hacking
items.m: Shows that training models on synthetic documents discussing reward hacking can shift their reward hacking behaviour via out-of-context reasoning, partly persisting after post-training.

items.t: Alignment faking in large language models
items.m: Demonstrates Claude 3 Opus strategically complying during training to preserve its harmlessness preferences, with scratchpad reasoning showing explicit alignment faking.

items.t: On Evaluating the Durability of Safeguards for Open-Weight LLMs
items.m: Shows current evaluation methods for open-weight LLM safeguards against adversarial fine-tuning can mislead about how durable those defenses really are.

items.t: Failures to Find Transferable Image Jailbreaks Between Vision-Language Models
items.m: Large-scale study finding that gradient-based image jailbreaks rarely transfer between 40+ vision-language models, unlike text jailbreaks on LLMs.

items.t: Connecting the Dots: LLMs can Infer and Verbalize Latent Structure from Disparate Training Data
items.m: Shows frontier LLMs can infer and verbalize latent facts from scattered training documents, with implications for data-censorship safety measures.

items.t: Align Anything: Training All-Modality Models to Follow Instructions with Language Feedback
items.m: Extends RLHF to all-modality models using language feedback and a 200k preference dataset, with all artifacts open-sourced.

items.t: Obfuscated Activations Bypass LLM Latent-Space Defenses
items.m: Shows sparse autoencoders, probes, and latent OOD detectors can be evaded with obfuscated activations that still preserve harmful behaviour.

items.t: MISR: Measuring Instrumental Self-Reasoning in Frontier Models
items.m: Introduces MISR, a benchmark testing frontier LLM agents for instrumental self-reasoning such as self-modification and knowledge seeking.

items.t: Best-of-N Jailbreaking
items.m: Presents Best-of-N jailbreaking, a black-box method that resamples augmented prompts until frontier models across modalities produce harmful outputs.

items.t: Playing Language Game with LLMs Leads to Jailbreaking
items.m: Presents language-game jailbreaks exploiting mismatched generalization, showing safety training fails to transfer across linguistic formats in frontier models.

items.t: MRJ-Agent: An Effective Jailbreak Agent for Multi-Round Dialogue
items.m: Proposes MRJ-Agent, a multi-round dialogue jailbreak agent that decomposes risky queries and uses psychological strategies to beat LLM safety measures.

items.t: SQL Injection Jailbreak: A Structural Disaster of Large Language Models
items.m: Introduces SQL Injection Jailbreak, an attack exploiting how LLM prompts are constructed, reaching high success rates, plus a Self-Reminder-Key defense.

items.t: VLSBench: Unveiling Visual Leakage in Multimodal Safety
items.m: Identifies visual safety information leakage in multimodal safety benchmarks and releases VLSBench, a 2.2k-pair benchmark that keeps harmful content out of text queries.

items.t: Quantized Delta Weight Is Safety Keeper
items.m: Shows that delta-weight quantization can improve robustness of fine-tuned models against alignment-breaking, backdoor, and manipulation attacks with minimal utility loss.

items.t: PSA-VLM: Enhancing Vision-Language Model Safety through Progressive Concept-Bottleneck-Driven Alignment
items.m: Proposes PSA-VLM, a progressive concept-bottleneck safety alignment method that hardens vision-language models against attacks delivered through images.

items.t: Safety case template for frontier AI: A cyber inability argument
items.m: Proposes a Claims-Arguments-Evidence safety case template for frontier AI, structuring an argument that models lack offensive cyber capabilities.

items.t: LongSafety: Enhance Safety for Long-Context LLMs
items.m: Introduces LongSafety, a 17k-sample safety alignment dataset for long-context LLMs, showing training on it improves safety at long and short contexts.

items.t: IDEATOR: Jailbreaking and Benchmarking Large Vision-Language Models Using Themselves
items.m: Presents IDEATOR, which uses vision-language models to automatically generate multimodal jailbreaks, and VLJailbreakBench, a 3,654-sample jailbreak benchmark.

items.t: A Taxonomy of Systemic Risks from General-Purpose AI
items.m: Systematic review of 86 papers yielding a taxonomy of 13 systemic risk categories from general-purpose AI, spanning environmental harm to loss of control.

items.t: AI Safety for Everyone
items.m: Literature review arguing for a pluralistic conception of AI safety that includes immediate concerns beyond existential risk framing.

items.t: Characterizing AI Agents for Alignment and Governance
items.m: Proposes a four-dimension framework for characterizing AI agents and builds agentic profiles to show governance challenges they pose.

items.t: LLM Microscope: What Model Internals Reveal About Answer Correctness and Context Utilization
items.m: Trains classifiers on intermediate activations to predict answer correctness and detect polluted context, using model-internals metrics.

items.t: A Taxonomy of Omnicidal Futures Involving Artificial Intelligence
items.m: Presents a taxonomy of pathways by which AI could cause omnicidal outcomes, to inform preventive institutional measures.

items.t: Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
items.m: Builds tasks showing longer reasoning worsens performance in reasoning models, including increased self-preservation expressions in Claude Sonnet 4.

items.t: Unsupervised Elicitation of Language Models
items.m: Introduces Internal Coherence Maximization, fine-tuning models on their own generated labels to elicit capabilities without external supervision for superhuman models.

items.t: AI Risk-Management Standards Profile for General-Purpose AI (GPAI) and Foundation Models
items.m: Adapts NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 23894 into risk-management controls for general-purpose AI and frontier model developers.

items.t: Introduction to AI Safety, Ethics, and Society
items.m: A 603-page introductory book consolidating AI risk, safety, ethics and societal impact for non-technical readers.

items.t: LLMs Encode Harmfulness and Refusal Separately
items.m: Finds harmfulness and refusal are encoded separately in LLMs and builds Latent Guard, a latent-based safeguard matching Llama Guard 3.

items.t: Understanding (Un)Reliability of Steering Vectors in Language Models
items.m: Empirical study of when steering vectors reliably change LLM behaviour, linked to activation coherence and geometry.

items.t: Towards Safeguarding LLM Fine-tuning APIs against Cipher Attacks
items.m: Introduces CIFR benchmark and shows activation-based probe monitors detect cipher attacks on fine-tuning APIs with over 99% accuracy.

items.t: LatentQA: Teaching LLMs to Decode Activations Into Natural Language
items.m: Introduces LatentQA and Latent Interpretation Tuning, training a decoder LLM to answer natural-language questions about model activations.

items.t: Probe-based Fine-tuning for Reducing Toxicity
items.m: Trains models against toxicity probes with SFT and DPO, checking whether the probes stay effective detectors afterward.

items.t: Safety is Essential for Responsible Open-Ended Systems
items.m: Position paper arguing that open-ended AI systems that autonomously generate novel artifacts pose underexplored risks to alignment and control, and proposing stakeholder mitigations.

items.t: Partial Identifiability and Misspecification in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
items.m: Mathematically characterises reward ambiguity in inverse reinforcement learning and when behavioural model misspecification yields faulty inferences about human reward.

items.t: Stochastic Parameter Decomposition
items.m: Proposes Stochastic Parameter Decomposition, a more scalable method than APD for splitting neural network parameters into sparsely used components.

items.t: International Scientific Report on the Safety of Advanced AI (Interim Report)
items.m: International expert report synthesising scientific understanding of advanced AI safety risks and how they can be managed.

items.t: Thought Branches: Interpreting LLM Reasoning Requires Resampling
items.m: Introduces resampling over chain-of-thought distributions to causally analyse LLM reasoning, with case studies on alignment faking and unfaithful reasoning.

items.t: Simple Mechanistic Explanations for Out-Of-Context Reasoning
items.m: Mechanistically explains out-of-context reasoning in fine-tuned LLMs, showing LoRA fine-tuning acts like constant steering vectors, including for backdoors.

items.t: Because we have LLMs, we Can and Should Pursue Agentic Interpretability
items.m: Proposes agentic interpretability, where LLMs proactively help humans understand AI concepts through multi-turn conversations, building models of the user.

items.t: What Features in Prompts Jailbreak LLMs? Investigating the Mechanisms Behind Attacks
items.m: Uses probes and causal interventions on hidden states to show different jailbreak families work through distinct non-linear internal mechanisms.

items.t: International AI Safety Report 2025: First Key Update: Capabilities and Risk Implications
items.m: An international report updating assessments of AI capability gains and their risks, including biological weapons, cyberattacks, monitoring, and controllability.

items.t: The Limits of Predicting Agents from Behaviour
items.m: Derives theoretical bounds on inferring an agent's beliefs from its behaviour and predicting that behaviour in new environments.

items.t: General agents contain world models
items.m: Proves that any agent generalizing to multi-step goal-directed tasks must have learned a world model, extractable from its policy.

items.t: Measuring Goal-Directedness
items.m: Defines and proves properties of a maximum-entropy measure of goal-directedness for causal models and MDPs, with small experiments.

items.t: Reasoning Introduces New Poisoning Attacks Yet Makes Them More Complicated
items.m: Shows backdoors can be injected through reasoning-path poisoning in LLMs, though models often recover from them during reasoning.

items.t: Existing Large Language Model Unlearning Evaluations Are Inconclusive
items.m: Critiques LLM unlearning evaluations as inconclusive and proposes two principles for designing better ones.

items.t: Advancing Science- and Evidence-based AI Policy
items.m: Position paper arguing AI policy should rest on scientific evidence and systematic analysis of risks from powerful AI.

items.t: Can Safety Fine-Tuning Be More Principled? Lessons Learned from Cybersecurity
items.m: Argues current safety fine-tuning relies on ad-hoc patches and proposes principled, security-first defenses borrowed from cybersecurity.

items.t: OpenUnlearning: Accelerating LLM Unlearning via Unified Benchmarking of Methods and Metrics
items.m: Introduces OpenUnlearning, a standardized framework benchmarking LLM unlearning methods and metrics across TOFU, MUSE, and WMDP with released checkpoints.

items.t: Recontextualization Mitigates Specification Gaming Without Modifying the Specification
items.m: Proposes recontextualization, an RL training modification that prevents models from learning specification gaming without changing the specification, tested in three settings.

items.t: Two alignment threat models
items.m: Presents under-elicited and scheming threat models of misalignment and argues better elicitation is crucial for evaluations, monitoring, and reward modeling.

items.t: AI Assistants Should Have a Direct Line to Their Developers
items.m: Proposes giving AI assistants a direct communication channel to developers so they can report uncertainty and flag concerning patterns, improving corrigibility.

items.t: MONA: Managed Myopia with Approval Feedback
items.m: Introduces MONA, a myopic RL training method with approval rewards that prevents multi-step reward hacking, shown in test-driven development and steganography environments.

items.t: Request for Proposals: Improving Capability Evaluations
items.m: Open Philanthropy RFP soliciting proposals for GCR-relevant AI agent capability benchmarks, evaluation science, and third-party evaluation access infrastructure.

items.t: Dodging systematic human errors in scalable oversight
items.m: Proposes a modified debate protocol with a 'Bob rejection' mechanism to make scalable oversight robust to systematic human errors on some queries.

items.t: A small number of samples can poison LLMs of any size
items.m: Shows that as few as 250 malicious documents can backdoor language models from 600M to 13B parameters, regardless of dataset size.

items.t: Circuits in Superposition: Compressing many small neural networks into one
items.m: Presents a mathematical framework for compressing many small neural networks into one large network via computation in superposition.

items.t: Detect Goodhart and shut down
items.m: Proposes detecting goal misspecification with validation sets and fact-conditional goals so agents shut down when plans fail validation.

items.m: Introduces Dedicated Feature Crosscoders to diff Llama and Qwen models, finding ideological alignment features that causally control censorship and narrative promotion.

items.t: Agent foundations: not really math, not really science

items.t: Infra-Bayesianism

items.t: We Can Monitor AI's Thoughts… For Now | Google DeepMind's Neel Nanda

items.t: InfAlign: Inference-aware language model alignment
items.m: Proposes InfAlign, aligning language models for inference-time decoding such as Best-of-N, and an algorithm for it.

items.t: Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness of Language Models
items.m: Uses linear probes on Llama-3.3-70B to show models internally distinguish evaluation from deployment, and that safety evals look artificial.

items.t: Alignment Faking Revisited: Improved Classifiers and Open Source Extensions

items.t: A Three-Layer Model of LLM Psychology
items.m: Proposes a three-layer phenomenological model of character-trained LLMs and draws implications for safety research and evaluations.

items.t: The Urgency of Interpretability
items.m: Argues mechanistic interpretability should be prioritized before AI becomes too powerful, to detect deception, prevent misuse, and ensure alignment.

items.m: Shows models can acquire behavioural traits, including misalignment, from semantically unrelated training data generated by a model sharing their base.

items.m: Reports METR's preliminary evaluation of o3 and o4-mini on autonomy and AI R&D tasks, including time horizons and observed reward hacking.

items.m: Presents UK AISI's alignment team research agenda on safety case sketches and scalable oversight with asymptotic guarantees for training honest AI.

items.t: Advancing Gemini's security safeguards
items.m: Describes DeepMind's defence of Gemini 2.5 against indirect prompt injection, using automated red-teaming and fine-tuning on adversarial examples.

items.m: Proposes an algorithm for combining cost-constrained runtime monitors and allocating budget between monitoring and interventions to catch misaligned AI outputs.

items.m: Argues that AI reasoning should be legible and faithful so safety monitoring, deception detection, and prevention of sandbagging and power-seeking are possible.

items.t: Petri: An open-source auditing tool to accelerate AI safety research

items.m: Proposes methods for building and evaluating misalignment classifiers that detect intentional misbehaviour in transcripts, and reports mixed recall results.

items.m: Announces Emmett Shear's startup Softmax, pursuing 'organic alignment' in which agents cooperatively find their role in a greater whole.

items.m: Announces a MATS stream using capture-the-flag games to test whether white-box methods can detect alignment-faking model organisms.

items.m: Announces an October 2025 hackathon pairing lawyers and AI safety researchers to turn alignment risks into legal strategies and risk assessments.
